rationale.rationale: Management's stated reason is that UPL is a conglomerate whose crop protection business is trapped inside a diversified holding structure and is therefore mis-valued: Bikash Prasad said on the May 2026 Capital Markets Day that "even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple" and that UPL carries "a huge conglomerate discount," so separation would make "the sum of the parts... much, much clearer." The Scheme (board-approved 20 Feb 2026) is a three-step composite arrangement: amalgamate UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, India crop protection, 90.91% owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn or 31.15% of UPL's turnover) into UPL Limited; demerge that India crop protection undertaking into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 share entitlement; then amalgamate UPL Crop Protection Holdings Ltd., Cayman (UPL Cayman, the 77.78%-held international crop protection vehicle, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn, net worth USD 1,599 Mn) into UPL 2 at 1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares, with UPL SAS holders getting 1,000 UPL shares per 48 UPL SAS shares. The problems it is said to solve: a split holding structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out that left India and international crop protection in separate vehicles; a single conglomerate multiple and no value visibility per platform; crop protection's cash-flow and capital-allocation needs being, as COO Toshan Tamhane put it in Feb 2026, "very different from that of the seeds business" (he cited Corteva's own crop protection/seeds split); and inability to raise capital or set governance per platform — the filing says the Scheme lets UPL 1 and UPL 2 "raise capital independently" and "optimize its capital structure," and Prasad said platforms with "independent capital structure, independent governance structure... will grow much faster." The demand came from several directions: analysts and investors gave five pieces of feedback that Prasad catalogued (reporting consistency, the four below-EBITDA items worth ~INR 5,000 crore or 60% of FY25 EBITDA, and debt/liquidity), rating agencies and lenders drove the deleveraging that Jai Shroff said had removed the leverage drag on the multiple, and private investors needed exits — KKR (which wrote a "$300-plus million check" into Advanta) and Alpha Wave (USD 350 Mn for ~12.44%, of which USD 250 Mn secondary from UPL Limited), plus The Upswing Trust, the UPL SAS investor that swapped into UPL Cayman and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right. The result is two listed entities: UPL Limited as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform keeping SUPERFORM as its manufacturing arm and incubating new verticals, and UPL Global as what Mike Frank (its CEO-designate) called "the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform" in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate. Shroff framed it as each business needing "a kind of independent life" and said the plan went through advisors and "at least 10 different structures," expected to complete in 12-15 months.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced as an unspecified value-unlock exercise on the 1 Aug 2025 Q1FY26 call, where Prasad said advisors had just been engaged to "explore unlocking value across all platforms" with "no firm decision on any structure," after Jai Shroff's press-release comment on restructuring; before that, on 31 Jan 2025, the only visible step was private monetization of Advanta (Alpha Wave's USD 350 Mn) and a net-debt/EBITDA target of ~2x. On 6 Nov 2025 it broadened to "restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO," explicitly linked to deleveraging, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration. By 2 Feb 2026 it had a timetable and a first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026, described as "the first such step in this direction," with corporate actions for all platforms "within a period of 1 to 3 years" — and management argued seeds and crop protection are fundamentally different businesses. The crop protection scheme itself was announced 20 Feb 2026 (CCI clearance 2-3 Jun 2026, exchange observation letters and the Upswing swap completed 29-31 Jul 2026), and by the 11 May 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted to the structure's fairness, with Old Bridge calling it "fairly detrimental to the current shareholders," Shroff defending it and Prasad promising to take investor feedback "unfiltered to the board" within a month or two.

points.point: Pre-history: value was being unlocked privately, not structurally — Alpha Wave bought ~12.44% of Advanta for USD 350 Mn, USD 250 Mn of it secondary from UPL Limited, the second global investor into Advanta in two years, with proceeds earmarked for debt repayment.
points.quote: We have signed a definitive agreement with Alpha Wave Global under which they will invest US$350 million, US$100 million as primary investment in the company, and US$250 million as secondary through purchase of shares from UPL Limited for an approximate 12.44% stake in the company.

points.point: First mention of structural work: advisors newly engaged to explore unlocking value across all platforms, with no decided structure and no timeline; Prasad tied it to a focus on significantly deleveraging the balance sheet over the next year or two.
points.quote: The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.

points.point: The option set was named for the first time — restructuring, strategic fundraising or an IPO — after the DECCO post-harvest business was folded into Advanta in September 2025.
points.quote: I think we had indicated in our Q1 press release and subsequently also during the earnings call that UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.

points.point: Prasad linked the value-unlock options directly to the debt problem, in the context of USD 500 Mn due March 2026 and ~USD 900 Mn of Q3/Q4 FY27 maturities.
points.quote: We had indicated during Q1 earnings call and press release that we are looking at various options to unlock shareholders' value. And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.

points.point: Advanta's DRHP (filed 19 January 2026) was presented as the first concrete step, within a stated 1-to-3-year window of corporate actions covering every platform.
points.quote: As we have communicated earlier, we remain focused in evaluating various corporate actions for all our platforms, including IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years.

points.point: The Advanta IPO was an offer for sale, not a primary raise — KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8% — with proceeds going to the group, principally to cut debt rather than to fund Advanta.
points.quote: This transaction is offer for sale. It's not a primary transaction. So the cash is not going to Advanta. It is coming to the selling shareholders, which are KKR and UPL Limited in this case.

points.point: The clearest business logic given for separating platforms: crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation profiles, with Corteva's own split cited as precedent and Advanta called the eighth-largest global seeds player.
points.quote: As you would have seen globally, Corteva has also announced a split between crop protection and seeds because just those two businesses are fundamentally different, and we believe Advanta as the eighth largest seeds player globally has a journey and destiny of its own.

points.point: Tamhane conceded the trigger was partly that private-round valuations (KKR, then Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price, so public-market separation was needed to capture it.
points.quote: Because, if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at, at least we feel that the full value of that is not flowing through to UPL Limited.

points.point: The 20 Feb 2026 board-approved Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL Global, to be listed; UPL Limited stays listed as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside simplification of the group structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out and enhanced managerial and board focus.
points.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

points.point: Scale claim for the new entity, with Mike Frank named CEO of UPL Global; promoters hold 71.56% of UPL 2 post-Scheme versus 28.44% public (The Upswing Trust alone 16.78%), and UPL promoters agreed to an 18-month voluntary lock-in from listing.
points.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: The valuation argument stated most bluntly: a single conglomerate multiple is being applied to UPL, and separation is meant to make the sum of the parts visible once each platform has its own capital and governance structure.
points.quote: You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.

points.point: Shroff's framing: brand- and IP-led businesses growing 3x-4x peers need autonomy, and the structure was chosen after extensive tax and structuring advice ahead of the announcement; SUPERFORM stays inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform.
points.quote: All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?

points.point: Shroff said the historic leverage overhang that had suppressed UPL's multiple is gone — gross debt down 40% from USD 3.8 bn (FY24) to USD 2.3 bn and net debt down 48% to USD 1.6 bn, gearing from 4.6x to below 1.6x — clearing the way for the separation to be read as value unlock.
points.quote: We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company.

points.point: An existing shareholder (Old Bridge Asset Management) objected that the announced structure would trigger a HoldCo discount and dilute existing holders, and pressed management on alternate structures; Shroff offered a meeting.
points.quote: But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current structure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount.

points.point: Management said it had run a two-month investor consultation with a tracker of feedback that would go unfiltered to the board within a month or two, and that at least ten structures had been reviewed with advisors before this one was chosen.
points.quote: And very shortly, we will be presenting that unfiltered to the board.

rationale.what_management_expects: UPL Global: pure-play crop protection across 140+ countries, independent capital structure and governance, faster growth, wider investor and lender base. UPL Limited: diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform retaining SUPERFORM, incubating new ventures, deleveraged with net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x. Both: independent fundraising, clearer sum-of-parts valuation removing the conglomerate discount, sharper board and managerial focus.
rationale.gaps: No debt split between UPL 1 and UPL 2, no UPL 2 standalone financials or guidance, no answer to the HoldCo-discount objection, no word on Advanta's IPO post-Scheme.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: UPL 1 remains an existing listed company operating as a diversified platform encompassing agriculture and specialty chemical businesses while incubating and developing new businesses and verticals
other_differences.separated_business: UPL 2 will be a dedicated pure-play crop protection platform consolidating the India Crop Protection Business (UPL SAS) and the Global Crop Protection Business (UPL Cayman), with independent management
other_differences.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure- play crop protection platform. This integrated business will benefit from a strong manufacturing base, advanced research capabilities, a broad portfolio of registered products and brands across multiple geo graphies and independent management.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Turnover of UPL 1 for the year ended March 31, 2025 was INR 53,313 Mn with net worth of INR 120,210 Mn (audited standalone)
other_differences.separated_business: The Demerged Undertaking (India Crop Protection Business) had turnover of INR 24,120 Mn, being 31.15% of UPL 1's turnover; UPL Cayman had turnover of USD 4,187 Mn and net worth of USD 1,599 Mn
other_differences.quote: Turnover of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) (INR Mn) % of Turnover of UPL 1* 24,120 31.15%

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 to raise capital independently and optimize its capital structure
other_differences.separated_business: The Scheme will allow UPL 2 to raise capital independently, build a wider capital and financial base and attract a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders
other_differences.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Group CFO states the structural simplification drives deleveraging, reinforces balance sheet strength and improves return metrics; FY26 gross debt down $850 million to $2.3 billion, net debt $1.6 billion, net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x versus 4.6x in FY24
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Bikash Prasad, Group CFO of UPL, said, "This structural simpliﬁcation strengthens our ﬁnancial foundation and accelerates our journey towards a more eﬃcient an d resilient UPL. By driving deleveraging, reinforcing balance sheet strength, and improving return metrics, we are creating a sharper, more focused organization designed to deliver sustainable long- term value for all shareholders ."

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: UPL Limited consolidated revenue from operations of INR 51,839 crore and EBITDA growth of 18% in FY26; segment revenue FY26 — Crop protection INR 42,399 crore, Seeds & Post harvest INR 6,830 crore, Non agro INR 2,803 crore
other_differences.separated_business: UPL Corp (global crop protection) FY26 revenue growth 11% with contribution margin up more than 250 basis points to 31.5% and EBITDA growth of 20%; UPL SAS India crop protection revenue flat with contribution up 19% and EBITDA up 24%
other_differences.quote: For the full year, we delivered 11% revenue growth year -on-year, driven by industry-leading volume growth across herbicides and fungicides. Contribution margins grew by more than 250 basis points to 31.5% versus FY25.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Separation is expected to enable clearer value discovery and give investors flexibility to choose between the diversified platform and the pure-play platform
other_differences.separated_business: UPL Global is described as creating the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform with a presence in more than 140 countries
other_differences.quote: Mik e Fr ank, CE O of UPL Global, added , "Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure- play crop protection platform.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: An investor at the Capital Markets Day objected that the announced reorganization is detrimental to existing UPL shareholders and could trigger a holding-company discount; management said feedback will be presented to the Board
other_differences.separated_business: Management stated at least 10 different structures were reviewed before arriving at this structure, and that the purpose is to unlock value at each platform level
other_differences.quote: By going to a structure, and before we come to conclusion on this structure, it has been discussed, reviewed by our advisors, and we have looked at least 10 different structures to come up to this structure.

turns: Thank you. Good day, everyone. Thanks for joining us today for the Results for the Quarter and Half-Year Ended 30th September 2023. The “Presentation, Press Re lease and the Financial Statements ” has been made available on the website and we take as having read the Safe Harbor statement. From the Management Team , we have with us today, Vice Chairman -- Rajendra Dara k; CEO of Global Crop Protection business -- Mike Frank ; CFO -- Anand Vora ; Chief Supply Chain Officer -- Raj Tiwari ; Chief Commercial Officer -- Farokh Hilloo ; Mr. Bhupen Dubey and Ashish D hobal, the CEOs of our Advanta business and UPL S AS respectively, and other members of the leadership team. With that, let me now hand it over to Anand.

Having said that, we did see po sitive volume growth in our international crop protection business, which is quite encouraging given the current market scenario. The volume growth in the international business was driven by the good performance of our high margin differentiated and susta inable portfolio, which grew 9% year -on-year, led by strong volume s which were up by 17%. This is quite noteworthy amid st the current industry downturn. UPL Limited October 30, 2023 The share of our differentiated and sustainable portfolio now represents 38% of the crop protection rev enue at the group level versus 30% in the previous year. At the consolidated level, contribution margins declined by 265 basis point s to 39.9% in Q2. This compression in margin s was due to liquidation of high-cost inventory , higher than usual sales return and rebates to support the channel partners. Considering the above factors as transitory, if one were to exclude its impact , contribution margin for H1 would have been higher by approximately 300 basis points versus last year. […] Bulk of the saving for this year will be realized in H2. On the operating profitability front, we reported an EBITDA of INR 1,573 crores in Q2 , representing a decline of 43% for that of the previous year, largely on account of double -digit drop in contribution profits. However, adjusting for the transitory factors impacting the contribution margin, the drop in EBITDA for Q2 and H1 would have been significantly lower. Before we move on to the items below the EBITDA, I would like to briefly touch upon the performance of the two of our platforms UPL SAS, the India Crop Protection platform and Advanta Enterprises , the Global Seeds platform. Advanta continued to see healthy growth in Q2 as revenues grew by 10% to INR1 ,070 crores and the contribution profit grew by 13% over that of the last year. On the whole for H1 , Advanta delivered a strong performance with 17% growth in revenue and 25% growth in co ntribution profit and EBITDA. Looking ahead, Advanta remains on track to achieve its FY24 guidance. Performance of the India Crop protection business , UPL SAS, in Q2 was impacted by high channel inventory, erratic monsoon in August and September month s and higher than usual sales return and also due to the lower acreages for key crops such as cotton and pulses, which form a large part of the UPL SAS revenue . Given the above headwinds, revenue contracted by 36% in Q2 versus last year, while EBITDA declined by 88%. However, led by new launches, a strong product portfolio for the rabi crop s and lower sales return, the performance of UPL SAS in H2 will be much better than that of H1.

Overall , in Q2, our revenue dropped by about 20% while contribution was down approximately 30% with margin compression of 470 basis points. The EBITDA for the same period declined 56% year -on-year. However, if you adjust for one -time impacts as highlighted earlier, our contribution margin is up about 100 basis points versus Q2 of last year which a ugurs well as we refresh our inventory, and the market starts to normalize. Further, I'm happy to share that we have grown our differentiated and sustainable segment by 9% through strong volume increase. The growth has come via newer p roducts such as Evolution and Fero ce. This has also resulted in improved product mix from 27% differentiated and sustainable revenue last year to 36% in this quarter. Additionally, our NPP Biosolutions has grown by 12% in U.S. dollar terms through higher volumes along with improved margins on quarter -over-quarter basis and we expect th e strong NPP Biosolutions performance to continue for the rest of the year. Let us now look at the performance of our reg ions in Q2. In Latin America, our revenue was down by 20% due to significant price decline.

Given that we have revised down our revenue and EBITDA guidance, I think it implies almost like an 18% YoY growth in the second half on the revenue s and also almost like 28 % to 30% growth on the EBITDA. Earlier you alluded to the fact that North America, E urope, LATAM , the high inventory is likely to subside only over the next six to eight months, but on a very gradual basis . And the second half is a more of LATAM and North American , Europe, heavy seasons. So, can you help us to understand the 18% revenue g rowth, does it look like more ambitious and this kind of growth would already be visible in the third quarter or is it more like a fourth quarter loaded growth?

As I mentioned earlier, we are expecting volume growth in Q3 but overall, on a Q oQ basis, we still don't expect Q3 to exceed Q3 of last year. Now , when we get to Q4, obviously we're starting the new calendar year and I think a lot of the destocking is going to be behind us and in Europe and Latin America and US distributors are going to be stocking up for the upcoming season. And so, we would expect very strong volume growth to come back in our Q4 . We don't expect prices to strengthen, but we also expect to see strong performance out of our differentiated and sustainable portfolio. And so, all of that into the mix would mean that we are expecting both revenue growth and EBITDA growth in our Q4 over the Q4 of last year.

So, could you give us some qualitative comments on your relative standing as far as the ot her global integrated producers are concerned, particularly, let's say FMC, Adama, etc., As the market reflects back , we might see higher market share come from those who are projecting higher volumes, but somebody has to lose out. What kind of player do y ou think will lose out and why , I mean, will capital cost , will factoring cost, will debt play an important role and could we see different attitudes by the banks towards which of the weaker players?

Look, I think if you divide our portfolio into the two big segments, firstly , on the post patent side, our volume increases and our share gain in that market is primarily going to come versus the Chinese producers . In that segment , we're not as much head -to-head against the other global companies that you're referring to. I think the market share will come from the Chinese producers based on our portfolio and our superior market access. In our differentiated and sustainable business, again , today it's a smaller part of our business. So, I think from a material standpoint, while we are gaining share as you saw in in the results, our volumes were up in that segment 17% this qu arter and so, considering the destocking, we're definitely gaining share in that segment. But again, based on the siz e of it, I don't think we're taking market share necessarily from one specific player. And so, I don't think about it in those terms in terms of having material impact on any specific other global producer.

Out of that $50 million we are talking about; we have reduced from t he CAPEX number and balance will be primarily coming from the working capital reduction because we are looking at no growth in full year and a very small amount can come from the free cash flow generation in second half . But largely it's the working capita l reduction only which are still in teams to reduce $300 million net debt ?

No, I mean, if you look at what we are talking about the numbers , with a good H2, you should see some good cash realization coming out of H2 besides the working capital also . The margin improvement, the volume growth which we're talking about, all those things, Mike also alluded upon that we are selling more of differentiated and sustainable products which are better margin products. So , all those factors should b ring in the higher EBITDA which we refer to as somebody made a ballpark estimate of 21 % to 23% EBITDA for H2. So , that should generate additional cash, which should help us to also pay off the debt. There are several things we are working on, and this shou ld help us to bring down our gross debt by 500 million.

Thank you, Darwin. Good day, everyone. Thanks for joining us today for the results for the quarter and 9 months ended 31st December 2023. The presentation, press release and the financial statements have been made available on the website, and we take as having read the Safe Harbor statement. From the management team, we have with us today, Vice Chairman, Rajendra Darak; CEO of Global Crop Protection business, Mike Frank; CFO, Anand Vora; Chief Supply Chain Officer, Raj Tiwari; and Bhupen Dubey and Ashish Dobhal, the CEOs of the Advanta business and UPL SAS. We will start with Mike and Anand presenting the performance for the quarter, followed by the Q&A. With that, let me now hand it over to Anand. Over to you, Anand.

Adju sting for one -time transitory impact of higher rebates and returns, the pro forma revenue for Q3 would be INR 10,695 crores, down by 22% versus last year and INR 30,424 crores for 9 months, down by 18%. In particular, the ongoing destocking exercise had a significant impact in our larger markets of North America, Brazil and Europe. However, our rest of the world region buck ed the trend and performed quite well, reporting a double -digit growth in revenues in Q3. The differentiated and sustainable portfolio al so continued to outperform as the share of revenue of this portfolio increased to 32% of the crop protection revenues in quarter 3 versus 29% last year , and 36% in the first 9 months versus 29% last year. Mike will cover details of this portfolio in his rem arks later. The impact of rebates, returns and high cost inventory liquidation on contribution profits was more pronounced as contribution margins contracted by 15% in Q3 versus that of the last year UPL Limited February 0 2, 202 4 quarter 3. If one were to treat these transitory factors as a one -time charge, the pro forma contribution would have been higher by INR 1,532 crores and the contribution margin would have been lower by only 3% versus last year instead of the reported decline of 15% . […] And for the first 9 months, EBITDA was INR 3,583 crores, down by 56%. The decline in EBITDA was driven by the significant drop in contribution profit. Adjusting for the transitory factors impacting the contribution margin, however, the drop in EBITDA for Q3 and 9 months would be significantly lower. I would like to briefly touch upon the performance of 2 of our platforms, UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions, the India distribution business; and Advanta Enterprises, our seeds bu siness , before moving on to the items below the EBITDA. Performance of UPL SAS, the India crop protection platform in Q3 , was also impacted as revenues contracted by 34% while EBITDA declined by 47%. The key factors attributing to the revenue decline were po or Rabi season in Telangana and Karnataka , and low cotton acreage in North India, which led to high sales return. Secondly, the low glufosinate demand due to elevated channel stock and increased competition also impacted the results. […] Furthermore, we are also introducing new products to diversify our crop mix. To give some update on 'Nurture ’, our digital platform, it continues to see good traction on the back of launchi ng exclusive online brands for retailers and in -the-farm services for farmers. We have also brought in significant operating efficiency through cost savings. Moving to Advanta, our global seed platform. rationale.rationale: Astra Microwave is splitting itself into two sector-focused listed companies: the parent (AMPL) keeps Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry, while the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business is demerged on a going-concern basis into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astra Space Technologies Pvt Ltd (ASTPL), which will itself be listed on BSE and NSE. On the May 27, 2026 call MD S.G. Reddy said the board had given in-principle approval and framed the objective as creating 'sharper strategic and operational focus,' enabling dedicated management teams to chase sector-specific opportunities, enhancing governance and accountability, simplifying the corporate structure and creating 'clearer investment propositions to shareholders,' with focused growth, better capital allocation and improved operational efficiency over the medium to long term. The sizing numbers management gave: FY26 standalone turnover INR1,157 crore of which radar was ~60% and space plus meteorology ~16%; the scheme puts the demerged undertaking's FY26 turnover at ~INR157 crore, i.e. 13.58% of standalone turnover; the Dec-2025 order book of INR2,226 crore contained INR249 crore of space and INR369 crore of meteorology/hydrology orders. The scheme's stated reasoning is that space/met/hydro has 'distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile' needing a differentiated strategy, and that a standalone entity would be 'better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests,' thereby unlocking the value of that undertaking for shareholders. Mechanically there is no cash consideration: shareholders get 1 ASTPL share of Rs 2 for every 1 AMPL share of Rs 2, ASTPL's existing promoter-held capital is cancelled, and post-scheme ASTPL mirrors AMPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55%). No investor, lender or partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as management/board-initiated strategic re-alignment, though Atim Kabra had repeatedly argued on earlier calls that the embedded space business was worth far more than the market credited (Aug 2025: 'very, very valuable'; Nov 2025: peers raising at $750-800m valuations with almost no revenue, close to Astra's whole market cap). The move is also backed with people: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy took on oversight of the demerger, stepped down as AMPL MD and director from close of September 30, 2026 to join ASTPL as a director, and Joint MD Dr M.V. Reddy became AMPL's MD from October 1, 2026. As of the last filings, BSE gave 'no adverse observations' and NSE 'no objection' on October 29, 2026, SEBI/NCLT approvals are still pending, and no effect of the scheme has been taken into the Q2 FY27 accounts.
rationale.evolution: Through the Aug 14, 2025 and Nov 13, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk at all, but the groundwork was visible: Astra Space Technologies had been incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary with Bangalore clean rooms and a ~INR230-239 crore space order book, and Atim Kabra argued the space business was being carried inside Astra at far less than standalone peers' valuations. On the Feb 13, 2026 call there was still no mention of a demerger, only Kabra's hint about needing to 'be creative' on financing and 'watch the space.' The board granted in-principle approval on Feb 27, 2026, which surfaced publicly in the April 3, 2026 press release (tied to the MD succession) and was first spoken to investors on the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call, where the detailed scheme was promised 'over the next few weeks.' The board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on June 10, 2026, and the stock exchanges issued their observation/no-objection letters on October 29, 2026; notably, not a single analyst asked a question about the demerger on the May 27, 2026 call.

points.point: Size of the carve-out quantified in the filing: ~INR157 crore of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of the parent's total.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores , representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.

points.point: No cash changes hands; a 1:1 share entitlement mirrors AMPL's register into ASTPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% post-scheme), and ASTPL shares will be listed on BSE and NSE.
points.quote: For the purpose of the demerger of Demerged Undertaking ( as defined in the Scheme ) of Demerged Company into Resulting Company, the Resulting Company shall issue 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each for every 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each held in the Demerged Company ("Share Entitlement Ratio").

points.point: Leadership is being split alongside the businesses: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy was given the demerger and will move to ASTPL, with Dr M.V. Reddy taking over as AMPL MD from October 1, 2026 (April 3, 2026 press release; confirmed in the August 10, 2026 board outcome).
points.quote: In this role, he will lead the adoption of tailored growth strategies and capital allocation frameworks suited to the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology sector, thereby enabling focused management attention, enhanced operational efficiency and the unlocking of value for the shareholders of the Company.

points.point: Status as of the latest filings: exchange clearances in hand on October 29, 2026; SEBI/NCLT and other approvals still pending, with no accounting effect taken in Q2 FY27.
points.quote: AMPL has received observation letter with "no adverse observations" from BSE Limited on 29th October 2026 and observation letter with "no objection" from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on 29th October 2026 in relation to the Scheme of Arrangement.

points.point: Pre-announcement value framing: Kabra argued the embedded space business alone could justify something close to Astra's entire market capitalisation, versus peers raising at high valuations with little revenue.
points.quote: Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit. If I extrapolate these numbers, actually, I got close to my current market capitalization.

points.point: Earliest hint of the value-unlock logic, alongside disclosure that Astra Space Technologies had been set up as a wholly-owned subsidiary with a ~INR230 crore space order book.
points.quote: So our order book, as SG mentioned, is in excess of INR230 crores over there. And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.

points.point: Two weeks before the in-principle board approval, Kabra flagged a need for creative financing for development projects and told investors to watch for options crystallising — the closest the calls come to foreshadowing the restructuring.
points.quote: But as you know, balance sheet for efficiently -- for them to efficiently function, especially when our sales volumes are projected to go significantly higher, we need to be creative as well as ensure that there is enough financing is there so that our NCNC projects, the products being developed and the large blue sky thinking driven projects do not suffer due to inadequate financing.

rationale.what_management_expects: AMPL becomes a radar/EW/telemetry-focused listed company; space/met/hydro becomes a separately listed entity with its own management team, tailored growth strategy and capital allocation, sharper focus, better governance and accountability, a simpler structure, improved operational efficiency, easier access to sector-specific investors, partners and lenders, a clearer investment proposition and unlocked shareholder value. No margin, EBITDA or valuation targets were quantified.
rationale.gaps: No segment margins/EBITDA, asset-debt-employee split, ASTPL standalone financials, listing timeline, transaction costs, or where ARC/MMIC sit; no analyst questioned it; no requesting party named.

deal.size_statement: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores , representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2026 demerger into Astra Space Technologies: "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme, the shareholding of the Resulting Company will mirror the shareholding of the Demerged Company." ASTPL change in shareholding pattern: Pre-Scheme (as on 31.03.2026) Promoters 100.00%, Public 0.00%; Post-Scheme (Indicative) Promoters 6.45%, Public 93.55%. Also: "The post Scheme shareholding pattern of ASTPL will replicate/ mirror the shareholding pattern of AMPL." For AMPL itself: "AMPL: No change". Press release: "Will have mirror shareholding identical to that of Astra ."
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2026 demerger into Astra Space Technologies: "ASTPL will issue and allot 1 fully paid -up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) to the eligible shareholders of the Company, in accordance with Share Entitlement Ratio (as defined under the Scheme) , without any further application, act or deed. After the Scheme has been effected, the issued shares shall be listed on BSE and NSE." Also: "There is no cash consideration being discharged under the Scheme." The entire pre-scheme paid up share capital of ASTPL held by AMPL "shall stand cancelled and reduced".
deal.management_incentives: No stock option, RSU or SAR plan is mentioned in the documents, and no treatment of existing grants in the Scheme is stated. Convertible warrants: "The Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held on May 20, 2025 and the shareholders of the company at Extraordinary General Meeting held on June13, 2025 has approved the allotment of up to 20,13,885 convertible warrants each convertible into, or exchangeable for, one fully paid up equity share of the Company, having a face value of Rs. 2, within the period of eighteen months in accordance with the applicable laws at a price of Rs. 864 aggregating up to Rs. 173.99 crores ("issue proceeds"). During the previous year ended March 31, 2026, the Company has received 25% of the issue proceeds i.e., Rs. 43.50 crores (Upfront monies) on June 23, 2025 and June 24, 2025." Managerial performance bonus is linked to restructuring: for Dr. M. V. Reddy and Mr. Atim Kabra the performance criteria include "Other intiatives of corporate restructuring like merger/demerger 10.0%" weightage. Cash compensation on exit of the outgoing MD: "the consent of the Members of the Company be and is hereby accorded for payment of Rs.1,35,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Thirty-Five Lakhs only) to Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy (DIN: 00003828) in the nature of cash" (Explanatory Statement: recommended "payment of a cash compensation of Rs.1,35,68,889/-" representing "the remuneration payable for the unexpired portion of his tenure as Managing Director"). Director shareholding in AMPL: Mr. P. A. Chitrakar "32,40,830 Equity Shares.", Mr. Atim Kabra "33,56,074 Equity Shares.", Dr. M. V. Reddy "Holds 63,570 equity shares." Insider holdings in the JV: "Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy is holding 0.20% shareholding in ARC", "Dr. M.V. Reddy is holding 0.20% shareholding in ARC", "Mr. Atim Kabra is holding 0.10% Shareholding in ARC", "Mr. Suresh Kumar Somani is holding 0.10% Shareholding in ARC", "Mr. P. A. Chitrakar is holding 0.20% Shareholding in ARC."
deal.insider_actions: No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of shares is stated. Stated intent around the separation: "Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy, Managing Director of AMPL has agreed to take on the additional responsibility of overseeing the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business and thereafter shall join Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL) as a Director subject to the approval of the Board." His resignation letter states: "I am resigning from the position Directorship also with effect from the close of business hours on 30th September, 2026, to oversee the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement." Reason for change recorded with the exchanges: "Has taken responsibility to over see demerger of the Company and focus in establishing resulting Company."

On a standalone basis, 9 months revenue surged to INR 668 crores with the EBITDA at INR 165 crores with a healthy margin of 25%. And the PAT has shown a growth of 6.3% year-on- year with a margin of 10.9%. Our stand-alone order book has crossed the INR 2,000 crores mark and stands at INR 2,226 crores, as of December 2025, providing strong visibility for the upcoming quarters. This includes orders of INR1,477 crores from defence PSUs and DRDO labs, INR 249 crores from space sector, INR369 crores from metrology and hydrology sector and INR130 crores from exports and deemed exports. We continue to focus and execute the modules and subsystems with critical and complex applications in the area of electronic warfare, radar systems, space-based platforms. To mention a few, we have delivered Ashlesha and Rohini modules, expand DWR, AATRU, telemetry products and some more products for QRSAM and SSPA during the quarter. To strengthen our relationship and be a partner in Make in India programs, we signed an MOU with Bharat Electronics to work together on design development and manufacturing of advanced systems with a shared objective of strengthening indigenous design and production capabilities in key defence technologies. Astra Microwave Products Limited February 13, 2026 On the order flow front, we received INR 450 plus crores of orders during the year, which has a mix of defence and other segments. We are on the way to achieve our order guidance for the year. More details about the same will be shared by JMD. Our joint venture, Astra Rafael Comsys has bagged two prestigious orders worth INR300-plus crores during the quarter and is poised to do well in the coming years. From a strategic standpoint, we continue to take steady steps towards becoming an integrated player in advanced electronic modules, subsystems and complete systems for defence electronics and space applications. More business-related updates and future plans will be shared by my other two colleagues. Quick industry updates. When we look at the broader industry landsca pe, it is evident that the defence sector has undergone a structural shift. […] The Indian government now chooses to prioritize the Indian companies that focus on research and development and invest in owning IPR rather than just obtaining technology transfers. Looking ahead, the Union Budget 26-27 provides a strong thrust towards indigenous manufacturing and reduced import dependence, positioning domestic defence industries, including private sector players, as key beneficiaries. The government's continued focus on defence modernization, Make in India and self-reliant is clearly reflected in the budget with allocation towards defence increasing by 15%. Within the aerospace ecosystem, the Space segment is witnessing accelerated momentum, supported by raising investments, expanding capabilities and strong policy backing. The Union Budget 2026 underscores this trend by healthy allocation to the space sector, highlighting government's intent to strengthen India's space capabilities and support long-term ecosystem development. Currently, our order visibility across the industry is strong and backlogs are no longer a constraint. The focus has therefore moved to execution specifically, the ability to meet delivery milestones, while protecting margins and maintaining balance sheet discipline. Additionally, a further support from various global trade engagements is expected to enhance export potential.

We also secured strategically significant wins such as DcPP for EW suites for Su-30 platform and also a few other subsystems, strengthening our role in complex subsystem integration and deepening our participation in mission-critical national programs. Looking ahead, we are even more energized by the strategic opportunities before us. We are strongly positioned in the major programs, which our DPSU customers are expecting contracts in the next couple of quarters. where our competitive edge lies in key subsystems and in-house critical MMIC capabilities. At the same time, as we had mentioned earlier, we are expanding our presence in space domain, which we see as a major long-term growth driver. We partnered with a couple of start-up companies to participate meaningfully in the evolving space ecosystem, combining our RF and microwave strength with advanced propulsion and satellite technologies to capture opportunities in both domestic and global markets. We continue to invest in future-ready technologies aligned with evolving Ministry of Défense requirements and growing export opportunities. Our JVC, ARC overall performance is Astra Microwave Products Limited February 13, 2026 exceptionally well and executed USD18.19 million in Q3. With order book of $80 million and with the visibility of opportunities, which we have today, we are confident of maintaining sustainable growth for the ARC in next 5 to 6 years.

As far as the availability of financing is an issue, for us, it is actually not that big an issue. But as you know, balance sheet for efficiently -- for them to efficiently function, especially when our sales volumes are projected to go significantly higher, we need to be creative as well as ensure that there is enough financing is there so that our NCNC projects, the products being developed and the large blue sky thinking driven projects do not suffer due to inadequate financing. So watch the space. There are a few very interesting options as they crystallize, we'll be letting you know. So the way we look at -- why is the inventory high? The way we look at it, our high inventory is a function of the long gestation product cycles and the lengthy time spans between the quotations we make to the placement of orders and the price negotiations before that, and finally, the lengthy delivery schedules over which the contracted products have to be delivered on contracted pricing.

And sir, just one clarification. On an average, what percentage we are getting as advance in the order book? Management: Generally, for the development orders, we get an advance anywhere ranging from about 20% to 25%. Export orders, we get about 30% advance. Whereas for the production orders, we don't get any advance. Again, the orders from the space application center and metrology sectors, again, there, we get advance in the range of 20% to 25%.

Sir, my question is regarding the space vertical one. We have INR249 crores order like how this order is split like is it unity -- if so these orders are related to payload or payload subsystems or related to launch vehicles, sir? And if you can give us a direction with how we are looking forward to get the order in this vertical on which directions, payloads or the vehicles? Management: Yes. Whatever orders we have in this space as on today, it is all related to the satellite payload electronics and some small portion, I would say, only 5% or 6% of the overall order what we have is related to the launch vehicle electronics. Otherwis e, most of these are part of the payload, which ISRO is trying to build this payload for strategic applications. And going forward, we do have a good visibility to get repeat orders in the same configuration and all. Maybe in the next 2 to 3 years, I think we should have a similar size of order book. And apart from that, as we mentioned, we are trying to build our own satellite with the payload for the -- for future. So that, I think, will take another 2 years to launch the satellite. And then we are also -- we're trying to address the end market.

We continue to proactively invest in development of products and solutions for various defence applications, which is reflected in our increased R&D expenditure on year -on-year basis. These investments are expected to translate into significant business opportunities over the medium to long term and help us to achieve important milestones in revenue and profitability as we move forward. Other key business development happened during the year. On a strategic front, the Board of Directors have in -principle approved demerger of our space, meteorology, and hydrology business. The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments. The proposed structure will enable dedicated management teams to pursue sector - specific growth opportunities, enhance governance and accountability, simp lify the corporate structure, and create clearer investment propositions to shareholders. Furthermore, this restructuring will position us to capitalize on emerging opportunities both in India and globally. Over the medium to long term, we believe this initiative will support focused growth, better capital allocation, and improved operational e fficiency. We will share the detailed Astra Microwave Products Limited May 27 , 202 6 scheme of demerger once it is formally approved by board, which is expected over the next few weeks. I will now hand over the call to Mr. M. V.

Reddy, Joint Managing Director, and thank you for joining us today. I am pleased to share that FY26 has been another strong year for the company. As mentioned, we achieved turnover of INR1157 crore s, delivering at par with the guidance given in the beginning of the year, that shows the strength of the technology portfolio and execution capabilities. Our radar business continued to be a primary growth driver, contributing nearly 60% of our revenue, while space and meteorology segment contributed around 16%, demonstrating our expanding footprint in strategic and high -technology domains. In Q4 alone, we secured fresh orders worth of approximately INR530 crores , taking our total order book to a robust INR2141 crores as on 31st March, and concluded PNC of INR300 crores more orders which are expected to be received in next couple of months. Key orders received during the quarter, which is in Q4, including SDR programs, subsystems of various radar projects from BEL, and the checkout hardware for prestigious Gaganyaan mission from ISRO. I am also proud to share that we h ave successfully completed all our related works in shipborne radar, which we took about couple of years back, and handed over the systems to DRDO for final testing. This marks the successful delivery of one of the nation' s most strategic and technologically advanced defence program during this financial year, further reinforcing our capabilities in complex mission -critical systems. Additionally, we have successfully delivered critical subsystems for one of the nation's unique and strategic defence space program, showcasing our growing technological strength and contribution towards the Indian strategic space capabilities. We also continue to strengthen our future growth pipeline through proprietary products, particularly in MMIC technologies. On th e execution front, we have achieved Q4 billing of INR490 crores , reflecting the strong 16% year - on-year growth. Major programs executed during the quarter included subsystems of radar, EW, and satellite programs, and Doppler weather radar for IMD. Going forward, we have a clear visibility of approximately INR1600 crores plus orders which can be booked in the current year, that is FY27. Around 25% of this expected to come from R&D programs, while balance are basically driven by the production orders. Segment -wise, radar segment is again expected to contribute around 45%, electronic warfare and missile together around 25%, space and meteorology around 25%, and the remaining other Astra Microwave Products Limited May 27 , 202 6 from strategic business areas. So, this provides us strong confidence in sustaining our growth momentum and improving scale in the coming years. Regarding execution front, we have planned to book sales of INR1300 crores to INR1400 crores , that is around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26, covering 40% of R&D and 60% from the production area. As far as ARC concerned, it was a fabulous year for ARC.

I would say the gross margin will be close to about 40% kind of thing in these ex ports. So that is the reason why there is an improved margin from export business as such. I think I have answered your first question Amit. What is the next one?

Management : Your other question Amit, as far as space is concerned, we have deliv ered the subsystems for a defenc e satellite program, which is a very main like complex subsystems which we made in over a period of one year, that would completed in last quarter and that has a decent contribution. And we are expecting similar subsystems going forward as the user is plan ning to go for constell ation of those satellites. So, this will continue as for the orders what we are expecting from both ISR O and as well as from the defenc e side as far as the space business is concerned. And on your other question on the deemed export, yes, we year -on-year we are increasing our value addition in the overall contribution like whatever we've been contributing to our JV as well as the company. Therefore, the reduction in the space order book or overall space contribution to the sales of the company should not have any negative impact in terms of the overall margins .

What would be the growth drivers for this revenue? Management : Yes, the growth drivers, there are many programs are there, both, you know, especially in the radar segment, we have seen clear visibility in to grow in airborne radar, fire control radar and surveillance and tracking radars and medium -range and long -range radars. So likewise in radar segment we have a huge opportunity in the industry. Similarly in electronic warfare segment also, as I've explained just now, I mean we have we been there in the DRDO programs for some few of the airborne platforms which we are DCPP in that. So, we are developing that and once the development and qualificat ion get completed, we expect production orders to come from the services. And also, apart from that, we are part of part and parcel of BEL major programs like Nayan Shakti , Hima Shakti , Shatrughna or some other, there are so many programs which BEL is integrating. So, we are the qualified subsystem supplier for these systems. So that business will continue for next four to five years, three to four years. And in the other segment like in the missile and telemetry also, we are there -- in the some of the active seekers we have developed for couple of missiles. We are expecting few orders in next two to three years. And in space segment, we are expecting repeat orders for the some of the satellite programs from ISRO and also from t he defence satellites. So, these are all our growth drivers going forward. And apart from that, as Mr. Atim had mentioned that in meteorology business also we have developed Doppler weather radars, wind profiler radars, which are, you know, the production orders are yet to come. So, we are we already booked few orders, more orders we are expecting next two to three years.

judge.reason: Segregate asset-heavy hotel ownership/development from the asset-light hotel management and brand platform, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, clearer alignment of business objectives and unlock long-term shareholder value
judge.insiders: Promoters Patanjali Govind Keswani and Spank Management hold 22.28% of LTH, 7.34% directly in Fleur post-scheme; Keswani non-retiring Executive Chairman of Fleur, turns non-executive at Lemon Tree March 2027

rationale.rationale: Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.
rationale.evolution: The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

points.point: Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both.
points.quote: We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.

points.point: He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets.
points.quote: We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.

points.point: The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls.
points.quote: Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.

points.point: All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt.
points.quote: Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.

points.point: Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree.
points.quote: We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .

points.point: Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin.
points.quote: We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.

points.point: Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists.
points.quote: This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.

points.point: He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels.
points.quote: Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.

points.point: Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair.
points.quote: Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.

points.point: Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results.
points.quote: Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.

points.point: On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends.
points.quote: Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.

points.point: Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months.
points.quote: What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.

points.point: Investors pushed for separate reporting: Ashish Kumar of Infinity Alternatives asked for pro forma financials of both businesses while awaiting the listing, and management agreed to publish them from the next quarter.
points.quote: Now that we have decided on the split of the 2 businesses, what might be helpful is if we can add pro forma financials for both of the assets as they look like so that while we are waiting for the l isting, we do get a good sense of what the numbers are looking like.

points.point: Keswani positioned the asset-light entity as a first in India, with fee income from hotels signed three years earlier only now flowing, and Fleur guided to ~Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA by FY28, its first year as a listed company.
points.quote: And keep in mind that Lemon Tree will be the first fully asset -light brand owning tech and distribution and management company in India, the first.

points.point: The demerger was still with Board subcommittees of both Lemon Tree and Fleur, with management hinting that more than the demerger was being negotiated (the Warburg/APG transactions announced two months later).
points.quote: It is not only the demerger of Fleur, but some other even more exciting stuff, but we will talk about it when the time is right.

points.point: First formal disclosure of the structure: committees of directors in both companies to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via demerger and then list Fleur, with Lemon Tree becoming asset-light and focused on management, brand and technology — described as the global trend in the space.
points.quote: You may have also seen that we have said that a committee of directors has been set up in Lemon Tree and in Fleur to evaluate how we can possibly look at a transfer of assets from Lemon Tree into Fleur through a demerger scheme and then automatically look at how we can list Fleur.

points.point: The separation of management was done first and explicitly for this purpose — Neelendra Singh to run asset-light Lemon Tree from 1 October and Saurabh Shatdal to drive Fleur's asset-heavy growth, with Keswani handholding and moving to strategic oversight.
points.quote: The intent of the leadership change was to get 2 very good people who would then run these two companies independently on a day -to-day basis.

points.point: Keswani drew a hard line on mandates — Fleur builds, buys and leases, Lemon Tree only manages or franchises — and noted that the more Fleur dilutes and raises capital, the more Lemon Tree's economic interest rises via fees (Rs 100+ crore this year, potentially Rs 300-400 crore from Fleur in three years).
points.quote: Fleur's mandate will be to focus on, at the right value, building, buying, or leasing hotels. Lemon Tree's will only be to manage or franchise. Lemon Tree will not lease hotels once the Fleur demerger happens.

points.point: The earliest trace in these calls: a Fleur listing was already seen as the accelerator of deleveraging, with Keswani putting an IPO within 2-3 years at most when asked by Prashant Biyani.
points.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free , but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

points.point: The 9 Jan 2026 filing states the Board reviewed the business with a view to segregating the asset-heavy ownership/development undertaking from the asset-light management/brand platform, and that the demerged business is self-sustaining and better housed in Fleur; the demerged division's turnover was Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover.
points.quote: Therefore, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, and clearer alignment of business objectives, it is proposed under this Scheme to (i) amalgamate Transferor Company 3, Transferor Company 4, Transferor Company 5 and Transferor Company 6 with the Transferee Company; and (ii) demerge and vest the Demerged Undertaking (comprising the Demerged Hotel Properties and the Development Capabilities together with the related undertakings, as defined hereinafter) into the Transferee C ompany, while the Company will continue to focus on the asset -light hotel management support, brand and operations including management support of the hotels transferred to the Transferee Company and other properties.

points.point: A stated purpose is market-driven valuation: Fleur ceases to be LTH's subsidiary and lists, so LTH shareholders participate directly in the asset-heavy business through listed shares rather than through a subsidiary.
points.quote: Following the implementation of the Scheme, the Transferee Company will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company , and its shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges, enabling transparent price discovery and market -driven valuation of the asset -heavy business.

points.point: The filing also sets out structural clean-up and partner-flexibility objectives: merging two wholly owned subsidiaries into LTH to remove layering and cost, and creating a structure that lets Fleur bring in investors or co-development partners per project without touching LTH's brand operations.
points.quote: To create a flexible structure enabling the Transferee Company to attract investors or co -development partners for specific hotel projects, without affecting Company's brand operations or control over strategic decisions.

points.point: Continuity is contractually locked: every hotel amalgamated into or demerged to Fleur stays under Lemon Tree Hotel Operating Agreements (existing ones amended/restated and extended from the Appointed Date), and LTH must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur and drop them if Fleur declines.
points.quote: Further, all the hotels amalgamated with or demerged into the Transferee Company will continue to be managed and operated by the Company under Hotel Operating Agreements and, the existing Hotel Operating Agreements with the Transferee Company and its subsidiaries shall be amended and/or restated, inter alia, to reflect the revised terms as detailed in the Scheme, and the Company shall refer new hotel acquisition or development opportunities to the Transferee Company and shall not pursue them if declined, except for hotel operations/franchise arran gements through third parties.

points.point: The Shareholders' Agreement with Warburg gives Fleur the exclusive global right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets, Investor/LTH affirmative consent on reserved matters, up to 3 Investor and 3 LTH directors with Keswani as non-retiring executive chairman, and the right to inject up to Rs 960 crore of primary capital.
points.quote: The Agreement provides Fleur t he exclusive right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets globally, with LTHL being entitled to undertake key money arrangements, in the manner as mutually agreed.

points.point: The 22 Sept 2026 filing records receipt of NSE 'no objection' and BSE 'no adverse observation' letters under Regulation 37, valid six months, with NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals still pending — the gating item management had flagged as the timing risk.
points.quote: In this regard, we wish to inform you that the Company has received the Observation Letter s with 'no objection ' from the NSE and 'no adverse observations' from the BSE on September 22, 2026 vide their respective letters , pursuant to Regulation 37 of the Listing Regulations , in relation to the Scheme .

rationale.what_management_expects: Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.
rationale.gaps: Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.
