other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Listing SBI AMC is presented as capital augmentation / CET-1 accretion for the bank, alongside the mark-to-market unlocking if NSE lists; the bank says it can already fund about Rs 12 trillion of credit growth with current capital.
other_differences.separated_business: SBI Funds Management is the vehicle for that unlocking; only a minority stake is sold and SBI is "not fully exiting".
other_differences.quote: We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET -1.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Bank guidance of 13-15% credit growth for FY27, domestic NIM above 3%, ROA above 1% through the cycles and minimum 15% ROE through cycles (ROE 18.5% at end-Q4FY26, 20.68% at end-Q3FY26).
other_differences.separated_business: The mutual fund business is described as having a large growth runway, with talk of the industry doubling in five years and SBI Mutual Fund as the largest AMC in the country.
other_differences.quote: I see a great opportunity for mutual fund growth and SBI mutual fund will be playing a very, very large role in this.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The AMC contributes to the parent through dividends and trail/cross-sell income: a one-off special dividend of about Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund was a major element of Q3FY26 miscellaneous income (of about Rs. 5,000 crores).
other_differences.separated_business: SBIFM's own Fiscal 2026 total income was Rs. 4,969.09 crores, 0.70% of SBI Group total income; reserves and surplus Rs. 3,533.09 crores, 0.59% of the group's.
other_differences.quote: If I have to talk about one -off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The parent raised Rs 25,000 crores of equity by QIP in Q2FY26 (largest ever in India, oversubscribed 4.5 times) and says neither it nor the listing candidates need capital at this juncture; the listings are for value unlocking and recognition, not funding.
other_differences.separated_business: "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture" — i.e. the AMC (and SBI General) are not being listed to raise money for themselves; the 2026 IPO is a pure offer for sale with no fresh issue.
other_differences.quote: I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.

judge.what_is_spun: Apollo's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, demerged into a separately listed company
demerged_business_names: omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business
judge.reason: Value unlocking via separation and independent listing: sharper strategic focus, operational flexibility, enhanced capital allocation, clearer investor visibility, plus consolidation of pharmacy distribution and a wider capital base
judge.insiders: Promoter group held 4,02,87,130 shares (voted 100% for). Shobana Kamineni to be Executive Chairperson of Resultant Company; Rasmeli-funded upside share agreement (max 9% of upside at 4x MOIC) to her and identified employees; new ESOP to be established
judge.hidden_value: A pharmacy/digital platform at ~INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 6.5-7% targeted EBITDA margin, digital losses near breakeven, Keimed distribution consolidated; promoter and investor incentives concentrated in the spin, not the hospital parent
judge.selling_pressure_why: Shares distributed to all 1.75 lakh AHEL holders in a different industry (pharmacy distribution/digital health) than the hospital parent they own
judge.listing_timeline: On May 21, 2026 management said the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting was called for June 24 and they were "hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier," with "end of December or early Q4 FY27" when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed; NSE's December 23, 2025 observation letter requires trading to commence within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order
judge.read_next: The Scheme's Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio and the Part E abridged-prospectus disclosures for Apollo Healthtech
judge.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long-term value across our integrated health care platform.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

points.point: Earliest reference in the window: integration of the acquired distribution business plus offline pharmacy growth is framed as the path to HealthCo's 'strategic intent' over three years, before any demerger language appears.
points.quote: Transaction integration and healthy growth in offline pharmacy distribution revenues will drive Apollo HealthCo towards its stated strategic intent in the next 3 years.

points.point: The restructuring is still presented as a merger-plus-breakeven story, with Sanjiv Gupta quantifying the FY27 target for the combined entity at INR 25,000 crore of revenue and 6-7% EBITDA, against a then run-rate of ~INR 17,000 crore at 6.5% excluding digital losses.
points.quote: So, we are looking at about INR 25,000 crore of revenue and about 6% to 7% of EBITDA in FY 27.

points.point: Suneeta Reddy's closing remarks on the Q4 FY25 call tie the Keimed merger explicitly to scale and margin durability in pharmacy, not to a listing.
points.quote: The Keimed merger process is also progressing well, which will further enhance scale and margin resilience in our Pharmacy business.

points.point: Sanjiv Gupta gave the margin bridge that underpins the 7% target: removing Apollo 24/7's operating losses and the ESOP charge (INR 100 cr in FY26, falling to a third thereafter) lifts the blended 3.2% to 6.4% even on then-current numbers.
points.quote: If I remove these two things, if I assume these two things even today and remove these losses and the ESOP cost, the new number that comes for the EBITDA percentage is 6.4%.

points.point: First explicit statement on a call of the demerger and separate listing, with the 18-21 month timetable and the INR 25,000 crore / 7% EBITDA end-state for the scheme concluding by FY27.
points.quote: The strategic reorganization of our omni -channel pharmacy and digital health business is proceeding as planned , and we expect to complete all steps within 18 to 21 months, a timeline that we had earlier announced.

points.point: A. Krishnan confirmed the mechanics in answer to an investor: HealthCo in its current form is the entity being demerged and listed by Q4 FY27, by which time Keimed's NCLT merger will also have happened.
points.quote: What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be listed separately by Q4 of FY27.

points.point: Scope limit made explicit — hospital-based pharmacies stay with Healthcare Services; only the ~6,500-store retail chain and the online business leave, alongside Keimed, which supplies about 60,000 third-party pharmacy stores.
points.quote: The hospital -based pharmacies continues as part of hospitals, which I am sure you know, but it is something that , remember, what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online out of that.

points.point: Madhivanan Balakrishnan listed the Keimed synergies: shared technology, data and people, cheaper dark stores (22 at the time) enabling expansion from the top 6 cities to the next 10 and beyond, and private label (then 14.6% of sales) pushed across Keimed's franchises.
points.quote: So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.

points.point: Process update framing the combination as the way to capture scale benefits inside HealthCo; separately Madhivanan said merging Keimed, Apollo Pharmacy and the digital business would release further cost synergies from the next financial year.
points.quote: The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.

points.point: Regulatory progress is reported and the combined-entity target is restated verbatim as INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 7% EBITDA.
points.quote: We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.

points.point: Obul Reddy itemised the approvals obtained (CCI, SEBI) and the NCLT filing, and confirmed Keimed had been cleaned up so that its subsidiaries are 100% owned before the merger.
points.quote: We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.

points.point: The purpose is stated in value terms for the first time in opening remarks — sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform — in the same breath as HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue.
points.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.

points.point: Timeline and end-state confirmed: NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on June 24, 2026, listing of Apollo Healthtech around end-December/early Q4 FY27, annualised revenue of INR 25,000 crore at listing.
points.quote: And hopefully, by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed.

points.point: A second, separate disposal: AHLL's Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr revenue, INR 45 cr EBITDA) go into a Cloudnine-combined platform at INR 1,550 crore — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with INR 750 crore of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics.
points.quote: One is the valuation, which is clearly key to get a valuation of INR 1,500 for EBITDA at a multiple of 35 in this market is something that you cannot ignore.

points.point: The Scheme's stated core problem: the pharmacy/digital undertaking is a different business from hospitals and needs its own strategy, risk posture and growth path; separation gives each side focus, management and control.
points.quote: The Scheme would enable carving-out of the Identified Business Undertaking, which is distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company, necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory.

points.point: Capital-markets rationale: the separated entity is expected to attract its own investors, partners and lenders — i.e. a funding base hospitals cannot supply.
points.quote: The Scheme is expected to enable Resultant Company to build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders, as well as promoting overall business growth;

points.point: The Keimed leg is justified as consolidating pharmacy distribution into a single pure-play vehicle, with the Scheme also citing supply-chain integration, wider assortment, counterfeit prevention, administrative efficiency and board rationalisation.
points.quote: The Scheme would also result in consolidation of pharmacy distribution business of Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2, in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution, enabling synergies;

points.point: Governance package embedded in the Scheme: a 12-member board with 6 independents, the AHL Promoter as Executive Chairperson, three promoter nominees, one AHEL nominee and one nominee for investor Rasmeli Limited, plus the Rasmeli-funded upside-sharing arrangement with Ms. Shobana Kamineni and identified employees.
points.quote: reconstitution of the board of directors of Resultant Company as follows: (i) AHL Promoter (as defined in the Scheme); (ii) 3 (three) directors nominated by the Resultant Company Promoters (as defined in the Scheme); (iii) 1 (one) director nominated by the Demerged Company; (iv) 1 (one) director nominated by Rasmeli Limited; and (v) 6 (six) independent directors;

points.point: June 15, 2026 clarification issued in response to shareholder feedback: the Upside Agreement is investor-funded with no cash outflow from Apollo Healthtech, capped and conditional on a 4x MOIC hurdle, and Rasmeli plus the promoter group will waive nomination rights below 10% shareholding.
points.quote: No minimum amount is guaranteed, with a maximum of 9% of the upside delivered to Rasmeli for achievin g at least 4x MOIC.

points.point: June 19, 2026 follow-up added a sliding scale of promoter nominee caps (nil below 10%, up to 5 at 35%+), an individual 5% waiver per promoter entity, half the board independent while there is an executive chairperson, and a Lead Independent Director.
points.quote: Apollo Hospitals now further clarifies that the promoter and promoter gro up are committ ed to waiving their rights to nominate directors in excess of the maximum numbers set out below, by reference to their aggregate shareholding.

points.point: Shareholder vote on June 24, 2026 passed the Scheme (90.44% of votes polled in favour; 85.71% of public votes), but institutional public shareholders split 85.69% for / 14.31% against — the clearest sign of residual investor discomfort, which no earnings call addressed.
points.quote: the public shareholders of the Demerged Company have approved the Scheme the votes cast in favour of the Scheme are more than the votes cast against the Scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Apollo Healthtech becomes a pure-play pharmacy and digital health company: INR 25,000 cr run-rate revenue at 6.5-7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27 (FY26 exit 4.3%), digital at breakeven, Keimed 3.1%-to-3.5%, offline pharmacy 8-9% on private label, its own investors, lenders and board. AHEL keeps hospitals and AHLL at 25.4% ROCE, redeploying cash into beds, primary care and diagnostics.

The stated promoter/management actions around the separation are: the Upside Agreement dated June 30, 2025 under which Rasmeli Limited shares an agreed portion of its investment upside with Ms. Shobana Kamineni (the promoter of Apollo Healthco) and designated employees; Ms. Shobana Kamineni's proposed appointment as Executive Chairperson of Apollo Healthtech "pursuant to and upon sanction of the Scheme by the Hon'ble NCLT and consequent effectiveness of the Scheme"; and the promoter and promoter group's commitments to waive board nomination rights below the stated 10% aggregate and 5% individual shareholding thresholds, with the Articles of Association of Apollo Healthtech "to be suitably amended, after the Scheme becomes effective, to give effect to these waivers." Promoter and Promoter Group voted 4,02,76,928 shares (99.97% of their holding) in favour of the Scheme at the June 24, 2026 meeting.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Healthcare Services revenues of INR 3,268 crore in Q4 FY26, up 16% year-on-year (Q3 FY26: INR 3,183 crore, up 14%), with 7% volume growth, 5% case mix and 4% from price revisions in Q4 FY26

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "Within the Healthcare Services business, we delivered a ROCE of 25.4% for the year" (FY26); ROCE of 30.3% reported for Q2 FY26
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Within the Healthcare Services business, we delivered a ROCE of 25.4% for the year, supported by balanced performance across our network spanning metro, Tier 1 and Tier 2.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Healthcare services segment assets of Rs. 1,36,651 million at December 31, 2025 (including Rs. 11,405 million of capital employed in hospital projects under construction); recurring capex of around INR 550 crore a year and FY27 growth capex of INR 1,980 crore for 1,000 beds

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "The operating cash flow before dividend that we have generated this year is before the dividend is approximately around at the consolidated SCS level alone, it would be in the region of INR 1,850 crore", about INR 1,550 crore after dividends and recurring capex, fully redeployable for growth capex

entities.name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited
entities.scheme: 2025-26 composite scheme of arrangement amongst Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited (Demerged Company), Apollo Healthco Limited (Transferor Company 1), Keimed Private Limited (Transferor Company 2) and Apollo Healthtech Limited (Resultant Company), approved by the board on June 30, 2025
entities.business: Remains with healthcare services (hospitals), retail health and diagnostics (AHLL); retains a 15% stake in the new entity and one nominee director; CIN L85110TN1979PLC008035
entities.swap_ratio: not stated

entities.net_worth_or_assets: Total assets Rs. 133,722.60 million and net worth Rs. 87,341.90 million for FY ended March 31, 2025 (standalone, Annexure I)
entities.who_runs_it: Dr. Prathap C Reddy, Executive Chairman; Ms. Suneeta Reddy, Managing Director; Mr. Krishnan Akhileswaran, Chief Financial Officer
entities.quote: Demerged Company is one of the leading healthcare service providers in India and is engaged in various healthcare services, including the business activities of the Identified Business Undertaking, which is carried on by Demerged Company directly and through its subsidiary, Transferor Company 1;

entities.name: Apollo Healthtech Limited
entities.scheme: 2025-26 composite scheme of arrangement (demerger of the Identified Business Undertaking of AHEL into Apollo Healthtech, plus amalgamation of Apollo Healthco Limited and Keimed Private Limited into it)
entities.business: Omni channel pharmacy distribution business and digital health platform business (Apollo 24/7 and AHEL's telehealth business), plus the amalgamated pharmacy distribution businesses of Apollo Healthco and Keimed
entities.swap_ratio: "For every 100 (one hundred) equity shares held by an AHEL Eligible Shareholder (as defined in the Scheme) in Demerged Company, such AHEL Eligible Shareholder shall receive 195.2 (one hundred ninety five point two) Resultant Company Shares (as defined in the Scheme)" ("Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio")
entities.turnover: "The turnover of the Identified Business Undertaking I demerged division for the year ended March 31, 2025 was INR 70.13 Crores"; the combined business is stated at "INR -16,300 Crores (-US$1.9bn) of revenue in FY25"
entities.turnover_pct_of_parent: 0.86% ("representing 0.86% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended March 31, 2025")
entities.net_worth_or_assets: not stated for the Identified Business Undertaking; for the Resultant Company the documents state "The Company was incorporated on 15th May 2025 and hence the details are not applicable."
entities.who_runs_it: Ms. Shobana Kamineni, proposed Executive Chairperson of Apollo Healthtech's Board (subject to approvals); board of 12 with 6 independent directors and a Lead Independent Director proposed; AHEL to have one nominee director
entities.quote: The Company continues to believe that the Scheme represents an important step in unlocking value for shareholders by enabling the separation and independent listing of Apollo Healthtech Limited ("Apollo Healthtech").

entities.name: Apollo Healthco Limited
entities.scheme: 2025-26 composite scheme of arrangement - amalgamation of Transferor Company 1 with and into Apollo Healthtech Limited
entities.business: Wholesale trading of pharmaceutical and other products and operating the Apollo 24/7 digital platform; CIN U85110TN2020PLC135839; a material subsidiary of AHEL (AHEL holds 78.88%)
entities.swap_ratio: "For every 100 (one hundred) equity shares held by the Transferor Company I Eligible Shareholder (as defined in the Scheme) in Transferor Company I, such Transferor Company I Eligible Shareholder shall receive 89.5 (eighty nine point five) Resultant Company Shares (as defined in the Scheme)." and "For every 100 (one hundred) compulsorily convertible preference share held by the Transferor Company I Eligible Shareholder (as defined in the Scheme), such Transferor Company I Eligible Shareholder shall receive 32.6 (thirty two point six) Resultant Company Shares (as defined in the Scheme)"
entities.turnover: Rs. 90,930.34 million turnover for FY ended March 31, 2025 (standalone, Annexure I)
entities.net_worth_or_assets: Total assets Rs. 38,096.72 million and net worth Rs. (924.57) million for FY ended March 31, 2025 (standalone, Annexure I)
entities.who_runs_it: Ms. Shobana Kamineni, Executive Chairperson, Apollo HealthCo Limited; Mr. Madhivanan Balakrishnan, CEO of Apollo HealthCo; Mr. Sanjiv Gupta, CFO of Apollo HealthCo
entities.quote: Transferor Company 1 is engaged in the business of wholesale trading of pharmaceutical and other products and operating the Apollo 24/7 digital platform.

entities.name: Keimed Private Limited
entities.scheme: 2025-26 composite scheme of arrangement - amalgamation of Transferor Company 2 with and into Apollo Healthtech Limited
entities.business: Wholesale distribution of pharmaceutical, healthcare and wellness products; CIN U72200TN2000PTC179280; a related party of AHEL
entities.swap_ratio: "For every 100 (one hundred) equity shares held by a Transferor Company 2 Eligible Shareholder (as defined in the Scheme), such Transferor Company 2 Eligible Shareholder shall receive 3045.2 (three thousand forty five point two) Resultant Company Shares (as defined in the Scheme)" ("Transferor Company 2 Merger Share Entitlement Ratio")
entities.turnover: Rs. 15,721.08 million turnover for FY ended March 31, 2025 (standalone, Annexure I)
entities.net_worth_or_assets: Total assets Rs. 10,916.04 million and net worth Rs. 8,413.80 million for FY ended March 31, 2025 (standalone, Annexure I)
entities.quote: Transferor Company 2 is engaged in the business of distributing wholesale pharmaceutical, healthcare and wellness products.

entities.name: Rasmeli Limited
entities.scheme: 2025-26 composite scheme of arrangement - existing investor/shareholder of Apollo Healthco Limited and counterparty to the Upside Agreement dated June 30, 2025, which the Company states is an integral part of the Scheme
entities.business: Investor shareholder of Apollo Healthco Limited; holds board nomination rights in Apollo Healthtech and funds the Upside Agreement
entities.swap_ratio: not stated (as a shareholder of Transferor Company 1 it falls under the Transferor Company 1 Merger Share Entitlement Ratio)
entities.quote: It is important to clarify that the Upside Agreement is entirely investor-funded (Rasmeli) and does not result in any cash outflow from Apollo Healthtech or any of its other shareholders.

entities.name: Apollo Medicals Private Limited
entities.scheme: 2025 related acquisition disclosed with the composite scheme - Apollo Healthco's acquisition of 74.5% of AMPL, whose rights and obligations become binding on Apollo Healthtech on effectiveness of the Scheme
entities.business: Front-end pharmacy business; owns 100% of Apollo Pharmacies Limited; an associate of Apollo Healthco
entities.swap_ratio: not a share-swap; "AHL has entered into definitive agreements to acquire 74.5% (seventy four point five per cent.) shares of AMPL from its other shareholders"
entities.quote: Upon becoming an IOCC, the NewCo also proposes to consolidate the front-end pharmacy business by acquiring the remaining 74.5% stake in Apollo Medicals Pvt. Ltd. (AMPL), which owns 100% of APL.

entities.name: Apollo Health and Lifestyle Limited
entities.scheme: 2026 transaction combining AHLL's Apollo Cradle and Fertility (mother, child and fertility) business with Cloudnine, announced May 20-21, 2026 - separate from the composite scheme
entities.business: Subsidiary holding diagnostics, primary care and specialty care; its Cradle and Fertility verticals go into the combined Cloudnine platform, while Spectra and other AHLL assets remain
entities.swap_ratio: "AHLL's mother and child fertility business are valued at INR 1,550 crore through a combination of cash and 9.9% equity stake in the combined entity."
entities.turnover: AHLL revenue INR 1,865 crore in FY26; "Revenue of the Cradle and Fertility verticals was at INR 450 crore in FY26 with an IGAAP EBITDA of INR 45 crore."
entities.who_runs_it: Mr. Sriram Iyer, CEO of AHLL
entities.quote: AHLL will become the largest nonfinancial shareholder in the combined platform and will have Board representation in the combined entity through a nominee director.

judge.what_is_spun: HUL's Ice Cream Business Undertaking, demerged on a going-concern basis into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited
judge.reason: "Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential"
judge.insiders: Not stated. Entitlement is 1 KWIL share per HUL share, so holdings mirror HUL; KWIL has a dedicated management team (Chitrank Goel, Deputy MD; Prashant Premrajka, Executive Director & CFO).
judge.hidden_value: Cost-of-acquisition split allots only 1.91% to KWIL vs 98.09% to HUL (based on HUL net worth and Ice Cream net assets at 30 Nov 2025), so a very small, cold-chain business carrying Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum is separated from a 23.6% EBITDA-margin FMCG parent.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Tiny relative value (1.91% of cost basis), distributed 1:1 to every HUL holder; distinctive ice cream operating model, different from HUL's FMCG portfolio.
judge.listing_timeline: FAQ dated 29 November 2025: "the statutory timeline for the listing and commencement of trading of shares of KWIL is within a period of 60 days from the receipt of the certified copy of the order of the NCLT sanctioning the Scheme (in or around Q4 of FY26)"; listing and trading approval received 12 February 2026, with "Date of Commencement of Trading: ... 16th February, 2026" for 2,34,95,91,262 shares of Re. 1 each.
judge.read_next: KWIL's first standalone results, and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking at 30 November 2025 underlying the 1.91% allocation.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — brands Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum — demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL) under a Sections 230-232 scheme sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 30th October 2025 (rectified 6th November 2025), effective (and appointed) 1st December 2025. The stated commercial logic in the scheme is creation of a leading listed Indian ice cream company with focused management having 'greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential'; on the Feb 2026 call Priya Nair framed the same point as 'a dedicated management team and singular focus' letting KWIL capitalise on a growing India market. The financial problem it solves for HUL is dilution: management sized Ice Cream at 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' earning 'low single-digit margin' — below HUL average, and even below that in FY26 because of monsoon and investment impacts — so removing it adds 50-60 bps to reported EBITDA margin, which is exactly how the band moved from 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5% (confirmed by Niranjan Gupta as 'the implied number' and restated as the mid-term guide in May 2026). The business was also volatile and seasonal: September quarter 2025 Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition', while March quarter 2025 had double-digit volume-led growth. Execution was a deliberate two-step: demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December 2025 quarter, then list — KWIL allotted 2,34,95,91,262 equity shares of Re. 1 on a 1:1 entitlement to HUL holders of record 5th December 2025, listing and trading from 16th February 2026, with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL based on HUL net worth versus Ice Cream net assets at 30th November 2025. Accounting consequences disclosed were a one-time non-cash gain inside reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) in the December 2025 quarter, and loss of PLI benefit accruals that had flowed through other operating income. Strategically it is presented as one leg of continuous portfolio rotation toward 'fewer, bigger bets' — alongside Pureit divestment (circa Rs 600 crores), Minimalist (90.5%), OZiva (remaining 49% for Rs 824 crores) and the Nutritionalab exit (Rs 307 crores) — with May 2026 citing the Ice Cream demerger as already 'enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio'.
rationale.evolution: On the Apr 2025 call (24th April 2025, March quarter FY25) it was only a progress line — on track with regulatory requirements, completion expected by end of FY26 — bundled with Pureit, Minimalist and OZiva as portfolio rotation. By the Oct 2025 call (23rd October 2025) Ritesh Tiwari hardened both timing and economics: demerger in the December quarter with listing in Q4 FY26, a two-step 'demerger then listing' sequence, Ice Cream at ~3% of business on low single-digit margin, and a quantified 50-60 bps uplift to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22-23% guidance. Filings then closed the mechanics: NCLT sanction 30th October 2025, effective 1st December 2025, record date 5th December 2025, 1:1 allotment of 2,34,95,91,262 shares, 98.09%/1.91% cost apportionment, listing from 16th February 2026 — and on the Feb 2026 call (12th February 2026) Priya Nair declared the demerger complete, reported the continuing business ex-Ice Cream, attributed part of the Rs 6,603 crores reported PAT to a one-time non-cash demerger gain, and reset margin guidance to an implied 22.5-23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30th April 2026) it was retrospective justification — a completed action improving portfolio growth mix, with Foods explicitly kept 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction'.

points.point: Ritesh Tiwari quantified the margin rationale: Ice Cream runs below HUL's average margin, so its exit lifts reported EBITDA margin by 50-60 bps over the 22-23% guided band.

points.point: The plan was explicitly sequenced in two steps — demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December quarter, then list the entity in the March quarter.

points.point: Priya Nair stated the completion and gave the focus argument for KWIL — a dedicated management team with singular focus to pursue India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing set for 16th February.

points.quote: We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.

points.point: Accounting effect disclosed: reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) included a one-time non-cash gain from the Ice Cream demerger recognised per the approved scheme.

points.point: The demerger is retrospectively grouped with the OZiva and Minimalist investments as portfolio rotation that has already improved the quality and growth profile of what remains.

rationale.what_management_expects: HUL: reported EBITDA margin up ~50-60 bps (guidance rebased 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5%), a better growth mix, and capital redeployed into bigger bets (Rs 3,500 crores acquisitions, Rs 2,000 crores premium-format capex). KWIL: dedicated management, singular focus and flexibility for ice cream's distinct operating model to capture a growing India market. Shareholders: direct 1:1 listed exposure.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: HUL delivered 5% Underlying Sales Growth driven by 4% Underlying Volume Growth for FY'26 on turnover of Rs. 63,763 crores, exiting with 7% USG in the March quarter 2026; management guides FY'27 to be better than FY'26.
other_differences.separated_business: The Ice Cream business delivered Underlying Sales Growth of 12.6% CAGR over FY19-20 to FY24-25 but only 4.5% in H1 FY25-26, with Volume Led Growth of 8.5% CAGR falling to 6.5%; KWIL aims to grow ahead of market and the India Ice Cream market is "US$ 2.6 bn market, forecasted to grow at 11% and projected to become US$ 4.4 bn by 2030".
other_differences.quote: Strong Historical performance; Recent performance impacted

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: HUL EBITDA margin was 23.6% for FY'26 and 23.7% in the March quarter 2026, at the higher end of guidance, with mid-term margin guidance "around our current guided range of 22.5% to 23.5%"; the demerger of Ice Cream contributes "a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points".
other_differences.separated_business: Ice Cream EBITDA Margins were 7.1% in FY 24-25 and 0.0% in H1 FY 25-26, with factors impacting H1'25-26 EBITDA being "Cocoa inflation and Strategic Pricing", "Supply chain Investments", "GST transition & Production Linked incentives" and "Standalone entity cost"; in November 2024 the business was described as having "mid to high single digit profitability"; KWIL has a "robust margin improvement roadmap".
other_differences.quote: Ice Cream is a high -growth business with iconic brands such as "Kwality Wall's", "Cornetto" and "Magnum" , operating in an attractive category, and has mid to high single digit profitability .

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: HUL has "signed off a Rs. 2,000 crores planned capex investment to expand capacity in the premium formats" of Beauty and Home Care, and deployed Rs. 3,500 crores into bolt-on acquisitions during FY'26.
other_differences.separated_business: KWIL plans "Rapid Cabinet Expansion" and to "Increase and Regionalize Capacity" with "More Cabinets", "More factories" and "Regionalize mfg. Lines" from 2024-25 through 2030-31; it had "200,000+ Kwality wall's Cabinets & Trikes across India" as at 31 Dec 2024.
other_differences.quote: Prioritizing Capital allocation for growth and productivity

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "Both our ROCE and ROE have improved on year-on-year basis. Together, these metrics reinforce the robustness of our financial growth model."
other_differences.separated_business: KWIL targets "Continuous improvement in ROCE", with ROCE defined as "Profit ( bei) + Interest + Tax / Capital employed".
other_differences.quote: ROCE Continuous improvement in ROCE4

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "Our cash flow from operations stood close to Rs. 10,500 crores, underpinned by strong execution across the business, robust cash conversion, and focus on working capital discipline." Total reserves close to Rs. 49,000 crores at end FY'26; final dividend of Rs. 22 per share taking total dividend for the year to Rs. 41 per share.
other_differences.separated_business: KWIL's value creation framework targets "Cash conversion Improving Free Cash flow", with Free Cashflow defined as "Cashflow from operating activities - net Capital Investments - net interest payment"; "Improving cashflow from operations" is part of its clear path to value.
other_differences.quote: Our cash flow from operations stood close to Rs. 10,500 crores, underpinned by strong execution across the business, robust cash conversion, and focus on working capital discipline.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: HUL cites "focus on working capital discipline" underpinning cash flow from operations close to Rs. 10,500 crores for FY'26.
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Our cash flow from operations stood close to Rs. 10,500 crores, underpinned by strong execution across the business, robust cash conversion, and focus on working capital discipline.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "That there are no secured creditors of the Demerged Company as well as in the Resulting, the same is verified the chartered account in its report." HUL had 2,973 unsecured creditors as on 31st March 2025 with an aggregate outstanding amount of INR 57,68,20,71,497.18, and positive net worth before (INR 49,123 crores) and after (INR 48,163 crores) the Demerger sufficient to meet unsecured creditors' liabilities.
other_differences.separated_business: "There are no unsecured creditors of the Applicant Company 2 as on 31st March, 2025." Creditors of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking are entitled to make claims against the Resulting Company and such claims "shall consequently be entirely borne by the Resulting Company"; "Both Petitioner Companies will service their respective debts/ liabilities post effectiveness of the Scheme".
other_differences.quote: There are are 2,973 (Two Thousand Nine Hundred Seventy Three) unsecured creditors of Applicant Company 1 as on 31st March, 2025 having an aggregate outstanding amount of INR 57,68,20,71,497.18/- (Rupees Five Thousand Sixty Eight Crores Twenty Lakhs Seventy One Thousand Four Hundred Ninety Seven and Eighteen paise Only).

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: HUL shareholders apportion 98.09% of their total cost of acquisition to Hindustan Unilever Limited; the Scheme is in accordance with Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and the Income Tax Department retains liberty to examine any tax payable as a result of the Scheme.
other_differences.separated_business: 1.91% of the total cost of acquisition is apportioned to Kwality Wall's (India) Limited; "as per Section 47(vid) of the Act, the aforesaid allotment of equity shares by KWIL pursuant to the Scheme will not be regarded as transfer" and the date of acquisition of HUL shares is deemed to be the date of acquisition of the KWIL shares.
other_differences.quote: For example, if 1,000 Ordinary Shares of HUL were purchased at Rs 400/ - per share , by a shareholder, the total cost of acquisition would amount to Rs 4,00,000/ - before the Demerger.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The Demerger "will enable the Demerged Company to drive sharper focus in the business as it further accelerates its play in high-growth demand spaces, strengthening its future fit portfolio"; HUL Foods remains "outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction".
other_differences.separated_business: KWIL gets "Access to introduce three more Global Brands" and "Patented global capabilities" "Basis access to global brands and global technologies via a royalty agreement between KWIL and Unilever entities"; Unilever PLC agreed to facilitate a licence with Magnum IP Holdings B.V. for the India IPRs "on substantially the same commercial terms as the existing licence arrangements and until a date no earlier than 1 February 2028".
other_differences.quote: the Resulting Company will have ability to benefit from the portfolio, brand and innovation resources and technical expertise from the largest global ice cream business enabling it to keep winning in the market space;

The net worth of Applicant Company 1 after adjusting the effect of the Demerger, is positive being INR 48,163 crores"; total reserves close to Rs. 49,000 crores at end of FY'26; HUL retains 98.09% of the total cost of acquisition of equity shares

entities.quote: The Petitioner Company No. 1 is one of India's leading private sector companies and is engaged in the business of manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of fast-moving consumer goods.

entities.name: Kwality Wall's (India) Limited
entities.scheme: 2025 demerger of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking of HUL into KWIL under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013
entities.business: Ice Cream Business Undertaking of HUL on a going concern basis - ice creams, frozen desserts, frozen snacks; brands 'Kwality Wall's', 'Cornetto' and 'Magnum'.
entities.swap_ratio: "for every 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- fully paid up held in the Demerged Company, 1 (one) equity share(s) of face value of Re. 1/- credited as fully paid up in the Resulting Company", i.e. in the ratio of 1:1 ("Share Entitlement Ratio"); 2,34,95,91,262 Equity Shares of Re. 1/- each allotted
entities.turnover: INR 1,595 Crores for the year ended 31st March, 2024 (turnover of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking)
entities.turnover_pct_of_parent: 2.7% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st March, 2024
entities.net_worth_or_assets: Kwality Wall's (India) Limited is apportioned 1.91 "% of Total Cost of Acquisition of Equity Shares" versus 98.09 for HUL; "The aforesaid ratio has been determined based on the net worth of HUL and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking, as at 30 November 2025"; HUL net worth falls from INR 49,123 crores to INR 48,163 crores after adjusting the effect of the Demerger
entities.who_runs_it: Chitrank Goel, Additional Director designated as Deputy Managing Director; Prashant Premrajka, Additional (Executive) Director & Chief Financial Officer; Ritesh Tiwari, Non-Executive Director; Independent Directors Ravindra Pisharody, Madhavan Hariharan, Jayaraman Vaidyaraman (JV Raman) and Shukla Wassan
entities.quote: Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL) stands among India's foremost ice cream and frozen dessert companies, offering a powerful portfolio of beloved brands including Kwality Wall's, Magnum and Cornetto, enjoyed by millions nationwide.

judge.what_is_spun: Digitide Solutions (technology/BPM) and Bluspring Enterprises (industrial/facility services) separated from Quess, leaving a pure-play workforce staffing company
judge.reason: Three-way split so each company has "its own focus and its own management"; Quess left "deliberately a pure play business with a single mandate" in workforce management
judge.insiders: not stated
judge.hidden_value: Reveals parent as a thin-margin volume business: FY26 EBITDA margin 2.0% versus ~4–4.5% pre-demerger, since higher-margin skilling and Brainhunter left. Offset by zero debt, ₹271 crore net cash, 20% ROE, ₹11 dividend
judge.selling_pressure_why: Management notes "the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger"; resulting companies sit in different industries (technology, industrial services)
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated as a forward date; at the 19th AGM (August 25, 2026) management said "In FY25, we completed a three-way demerger" and that there are "now three separately listed companies"; the Q3 FY26 call (January 29, 2026) dates the demerger to "since 1st April 2024"
judge.read_next: Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises standalone results — the EBITDA and debt that left Quess
judge.quote: Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.

rationale.rationale: The separation Quess management describes is a completed three-way demerger of the old Quess Corp, effected from 1 April 2024 under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement in which Quess Corp was the Demerged Company and Digitide Solutions Limited (Resulting Company 1, holding the Global Technology Solutions/BPM, platform, foundit and Brainhunter businesses) and Bluspring Enterprises Limited (Resulting Company 2, holding Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage, security, Vedang telecom infra, and the Golden Star facility-management contracts) were carved out, leaving Quess Corp as a pure-play workforce/staffing company in General Staffing, Professional (IT) Staffing, Overseas staffing and the Hamara digital platforms. The stated reason was focus and value unlocking: management repeatedly said the demerger gives each entity 'its own focus and its own management', a 'sharper strategic identity', agility and the ability to unlock value for shareholders, with Quess itself able to concentrate on 'high-margin, high-growth core segments'. The separation was explicitly used as the trigger for portfolio cleaning: in the run-up, Digitide's service lines were rationalised for low-margin/low-efficiency contracts, and at Quess, the Board and management decided to exit non-core, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities, booking INR158 crore of Q4 FY25 exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR26 crore goodwill impairment — INR7 crore Stellarslog and INR19 crore Quess International Services — and INR13 crore of demerger costs, mainly stamp duty), after INR22 crore of demerger expenses in Q3 FY25; skilling alone had been roughly INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin. Management conceded the cost: standalone workforce margins of 2.4–2.5% pre-demerger became 1.8% post-demerger because of newly allocated corporate overheads, and the old 4–4.5% consolidated margin is 'noncomparable' since skilling was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide — so the goalpost was reset to 2% exit margin. The quid pro quo was balance-sheet and capital-allocation discipline: net cash of INR255 crore and gross debt of only INR12 crore at 31 March 2025, consolidated DSO cut from 44 to 37 days, a new dividend policy returning up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, FY25 dividend of INR10 per share, adjusted ROE moving from high teens to above 20%, and no acquisitions planned — investment to go into AI/sourcing technology instead. Strategically, the separated Quess was to tilt its mix from volume to value: profitability from General Staffing fell from 59% (FY25) to 50%, with Professional Staffing (~30%) plus Overseas (~20%) now half of operating profit (42% a year earlier), Professional Staffing margins rising from ~4.5–4.7% in FY20–21 to 12.7% by Q4 FY26, and 'Quess 2.0' targeting 65% of profit from Professional Staffing plus Overseas and dollar-linked revenue from 7% to over 20% in three to four years. By the AGM, Ajit Isaac framed the outcome as value created from the INR1,270 crore of IPO/IPP capital reinvested, with the three listed companies together generating about INR500 crore of EBITDA and employing over 600,000 people, while Quess remained debt-free with FY26 revenue of INR15,305 crore, EBITDA of INR312 crore (up 19%) and 20% ROE. No call attributes the decision to a demand from investors, lenders or partners — only to the Board and management.
rationale.evolution: In the Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) call the demerger was still in flight — first NCLT approval received, shareholder and creditor approvals on 9 December 2024, second-motion NCLT pending, INR22 crore of demerger costs booked, listing of all three companies guided for Q1 FY26 — and Digitide's low-margin contracts were already being rationalised 'as a run-up to demerger'. By the May 2025 (Q4 FY25) call it was done ahead of timeline and framed as Quess's 'first earnings call as an independent entity', with INR158 crore of exceptionals for exiting non-core skilling and utilities projects, a new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a reset margin goalpost of 1.8% to 2%. The Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 calls shifted entirely to execution of the 'pure-play staffing leader' model and the 50/50 profit-mix target, while Feb 2026 used the demerger retrospectively to explain why margins are 2% rather than the old 4–4.5% (skilling discontinued, Brainhunter moved to Digitide) and why the INR120 crore ECL related to demerger-era discontinued businesses. The May 2026 call, 'one year post our demerger', applied the same demerger-era test to exit a further 7,000-headcount, milestone-based project worth about INR200 crore (1.3% of revenue), and the August 2026 AGM closed the arc with the three-company outcome and the 'Quess 2.0' mix targets.

points.point: With the first NCLT approval done and shareholder/creditor approvals obtained on 9 December 2024, Guruprasad framed the pending three-way split as a value-unlocking and positioning exercise for each entity.
points.quote: This transition marks an important step in unlocking shareholder value and positioning each entity for its future success.

points.point: CFO Kamal Pal Hoda described the internal work — internal controls, process streamlining and separate leadership teams — as aimed at creating agile, independently focused entities; demerger-related expenses of INR22 crore were booked in the quarter and more were flagged for Q4.
points.quote: Our aim is to create independent entities that are agile, strategically focused and well positioned to unlock value for all stakeholders in the long term.

points.point: The separation was already being used to clean the portfolio of the entity going into Digitide, by exiting low-margin, low-efficiency service lines to lift long-run operating margins.
points.quote: As a run-up to demerger, with a new entity, Digitide, we are examining our existing service lines and rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts, which would give a sustainable upside to our long-term operating margins.

points.point: First call as a standalone company: the completed three-way demerger was presented as delivering sharper focus, value unlocking and strategic transformation, alongside net cash of INR255 crore, gross debt of INR12 crore and DSO improved by 7 days to 37.
points.quote: This important milestone leads to a sharper focus and unlocking value, strategic transformation, and delivering sustained growth.

points.point: Guruprasad tied portfolio streamlining post-separation directly to profitability, capital efficiency and long-term value creation for the remaining staffing core.
points.quote: Moving forward as we streamline our business portfolios, it will enable a sharper focus on high-margin, high-growth core segments.

points.point: The demerger triggered a comprehensive business review and Board-approved exit of non-core outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities — INR158 crore of exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated ECL, INR26 crore goodwill impairment in Stellarslog and Quess International Services, INR13 crore demerger/stamp-duty costs); skilling had been ~INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: As part of the demerger transformation, we revisited some of our businesses through a comprehensive review, and we will be exiting certain non-core projects in line with the position taken by the management and the Board to discontinue such projects.

points.point: Asked about new geographies, management said the point of the separation was to go deeper in existing core businesses rather than expand, with no acquisitions planned and investment redirected to AI-led sourcing productivity.
points.quote: See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.

points.point: The identity after separation was stated plainly in the closing remarks — a pure-play staffing company with a simplified structure, zero gross debt at quarter-end, and 53%/29%/21% profitability contribution from General Staffing, Professional Staffing and Overseas.
points.quote: So, as we strengthen our position as a pure-play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.

points.point: The post-separation design goal was restated as a 50/50 profit split between scale (General Staffing) and the higher-margin Professional Staffing (11–12%) and Overseas (6%+) businesses — a point management said it had set out two or three quarters earlier and had now reached.
points.quote: I think we had made one point about 2 or 3 quarters ago where we said we would like to have a healthy state where General Staffing on a growing base contributes 50% of the profitability of that company.

points.point: Answering why margins are ~2% versus 4–4.5% historically, new CFO Neeraj Jain explained the pre-demerger comparison is invalid: the high-margin skill development business was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada operations) went to Digitide; Kushal added the demerged balance sheet applies from 1 April 2024.
points.quote: With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brainhunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.

points.point: On the INR120 crore expected credit loss taken in Q4 FY25, Guruprasad confirmed it related to the government skilling receivables of the businesses discontinued as part of the demerger, with collections still being pursued (delayed into Q4 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be a write-back.
points.quote: If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.

points.point: One year after the demerger, the same exit test was applied again: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project was closed down, costing about INR200 crore or 1.3% of revenue, with no further such events known.
points.quote: As you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financial metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization, we will exit and discontinue such businesses.

points.point: AGM (August 2026): Chairman Ajit Isaac described the FY25 three-way demerger as turning one company into three separately listed ones, with the value creation enabled by INR1,270 crore of IPO/IPP capital reinvested; the three now generate about INR500 crore of EBITDA and employ over 600,000 people.
points.quote: Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.

points.point: What shareholders retain in Quess Corp was defined as a debt-free, single-mandate workforce company — FY26 revenue INR15,305 crore, EBITDA INR312 crore (up 19%), net cash INR271 crore, 20% ROE, INR11 per share dividend — with Professional Staffing plus Overseas now half of operating profit versus 42% in FY25, targeted at ~65%.
points.quote: What remains with you is Quess Corp, an independent workforce, talent and technology company, with no debt on its books.

rationale.what_management_expects: For Quess: a pure-play, zero-debt staffing company with sharper focus on high-margin segments — margins rebuilt from 1.8% to 2%+ (2.4% medium term), Professional Staffing 11–12% and Overseas 6%+ lifting their profit share from 50% to 65%, dollar-linked revenue 7% to 20%, ROE above 20%, 80% EBITDA-to-cash conversion and up to 75% of free cash flow returned. Digitide and Bluspring get independent focus, management and technology/industrial platforms.
rationale.gaps: Who initiated or demanded it; sum-of-parts or valuation math; how assets, debt and corporate costs were allocated between the three; Digitide/Bluspring economics or listing details.

A few corporate updates for the year. In line with our leaner structure simplification strategy, implementations o f amalgamation of our wholly owned subsidiaries Conneqt, MFX, Greenpiece post-NCLT approval was completed during the year. You are aware that our Board approved this proposal to demerge the business into three independent listed entities, each one capable of executing its individual business strategies. We believe that this will enable value unlock for our shareholders in medium and long term, scale the businesses to new heights with enhanced management focus, follow -on optimal capital allocation strategy and attract separate investor base. We have filed a scheme of demerger with stock exchange in February 2024, and we are progressing well on our plan. With this, I conclude our financial results and pass it back to the moderator, for taking your questions. Thank you. Quess Corp Limited.

Congratulations team for a great set of numbers. First, on the WFM side , if you look at last four quarters we have been able to maintain our margins at 2.6%. We understand that the IT side of the business is not p icking well. T here are losses in North America which we re likely to turn around by the end of this year , in the fourth quarter. How should one loo k at margins now going forward g iven -- any color on the IT side and the North American operations? If you would like to give us some color on that part? Ques s Corp Limited. Thank you, Chintan, for your question. I request Lohit to give his inputs on this question, please.

Thanks for that question. First and foremost, I'll just take a minute to say that there have been key milestones already achieved this year by our WFM business. And we are proud of the platform that we have created today. We've crossed the 400,000 mark in active hea dcount base. Overall, WFM has crossed the 450,000 mark. We are poised for a long -term growth in WFM which we've already stated as part of our demerger plan to become the world's number one staffing company by volume, by head count and eventually a lso to grow our profitability along with it. In this year, there were challenges that we were facing. There are global headwinds and geopolitical scenarios which have obviously shrunk the business and margins coming out of the IT industry. Particularly wi thin the IT industry also it was the IT services. How that impacts our business and portfolio in WFM is we did two large businesses in Indian IT. One is the contract staffing business, as you know. And the second is the IT permanent recruitment business. IT permanent recruitment business itself on a year -on-year basis has lost around INR 17 crores from where we were one year ago in FY 2023, what we delivered as EBITDA to what we eventually delivered in FY 2024. In spite of that, the core businesses , the staffing businesses , with its focus towards niche digital and predominantly in GCCs as a segment in India has been able to offset some of those losses. To your point on margin pressu res, yes, WFM, especially with g eneral staffing continues to remain a tight margin play. We've been very proud that, in spite of the fact that we 've consistently grown our head count and revenue we've been able to now maintain the margin at about 2.6% as we speak. With no further burn anticipated in U.S. operations for WFM, we feel this would inch upwards by another 20 basis points coming closer to about 2.8% going forward. Medium term to long term we would like to take this to 3% or so.

So, with this I'll now hand ov er to Kamal for financial updates. Over to you, Kamal.

Yes. Thank you for the opportunity. So could you please give a timeline of the demerger details and when will you think the demerger will be completed? And do you expect any hurdle on the way? And secondly, why do you think this demerger will unlock value for Quess Corp. So if you can give some color on that ?

Sure, Aniket, thanks for your question. So on demerger, we have previously also guided that it’s a 12 to 15 months’ process from the date of announcement. So we announced the demerger in the month of February. And the scheme is a mirror sharehold ing scheme and we expect with a simplistic scheme, we should be able to complete this demerger on the timelines that we stated. Obviously, there is lot of external interface on this. There are regulatory approvals, but so far we are on track and hopeful that probably by Q1 of next year we should have the demerger processed. To your question on why or whether it will unlock any value. There a re multiple reasons that we did the announcement of demerger. It does simplify corporate structure and post simplification, there is an opportunity for value unlock. It also leads to an enhanced managerial focus because all these businesses are well scaled , large businesses and industry leaders in each of their respective states, respective lines of businesses. So demerger and running it as a separate listed entity, definitely bringing additional managerial focus and giv ing the competitive edge. Each of our businesses are into different service lines and hence there was also a need of uniquely Quess Corp Limited. So those were some of the reasons the deme rger was announced in the month of February. And like I said, we are on track. Hopeful that by Q1 of next year, we should be able to get this done.

Yes, and thanks for the opportunity. Sir, my first question is on the margins for the WFM segment. So obviously you have provided the clarification. But for my understanding, the margins Y -o-Y has been down and sequentially also it has been almost flat, right? So this is now like despite the increasing contribution of GCC, which is suppose dly at a higher margin. So can you assume that the general staffing, the core general staffing margins have been coming down and still there is no respite to the margins for the core segment within WFM? And also the sourcing component has been going up and the transfer component has been coming down. So in general, if you explain whether the sourcing, higher sourcing can also lead to lower margins?

Sure. Amit, I will start with the margin. We were 2.6% and we've come down to about 2.4%. Again, multiple pointers here. One is, of course, as part of the demerger process we are also Quess Corp Limited . October 29 , 202 4 strengthening each of the platforms. So we are again hiring the capabilities for the back office and all of that for of the platform. Number two, specifically for W FM I spoke about verticalization. We have been investing because investment for future in terms of how each of these vertical s are going to represent and will have its trajectory of growth. Just to give you an example again , for us the manufacturing is about 70,000. We intend to drive this and it has an opportunity in itself to cross over 200,000 associates over a couple of years from now, right. So, to build that you got to get the right structures in place, the processes in place, the challenges between segment to segment is very extremely different. So , we got to make those investments in IR being closer to customers, specifically when I take manufacturing. Then consumer retail hiring is extremely different than what we do for manufacturing. So , from that standpoint we are strengthening the vertical. So verticalization will help us to get the competitive edge as we move forward. So that's the secon d investment post the demerger. Third , hiring for GCC versus hiring for IT services is extremely different. So , in terms of the quality of recruiters, we don't hire freshers here, they are minimum of about three years to eight years of experience. And to hire them in terms of onboarding is something that you need a better quality of recruiters to handle it. The last one here is the international mix , if you take overall WFM EBITDA, 50% comes from general staffing, 50% comes from all other . judge.reason: Green Mobility's risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios are distinct from Ash & Coal handling; it attracts a different set of investors, so the group plans it as a separate listed entity to unlock value.
judge.insiders: Directors/KMP have no interest except directorship and shareholding; RIL holds 100% of RML pre-scheme (cancelled); post-scheme promoter and promoter group hold 56.57% of RML, mirroring RIL 1:1.
judge.hidden_value: Separation leaves parent as high-margin Ash & Coal handling (FY26 PAT ₹247cr, 17% EBITDA, ₹1,721cr orderbook) plus wind; the spin is small and loss-making (segment EBIT −₹38.2cr FY26, ~₹220cr net assets, RGML creditors ₹153cr) but 'progressing steadily towards profitability'.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Tiny (2.5% of revenue, ~₹100cr turnover), loss-making, unlisted new entity in a different industry, distributed 1:1 to 92,973 shareholders.
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated as a listing date. May 27, 2026 call: 'another 60 to 75 days... should get completed in the next 90 days'; Jan 21, 2026 call: 'by April'; Oct 28, 2026 release: 'NCLT hearings are underway... next hearing scheduled for 28 October 2026' and demerger 'awaiting final approval from the Hon'ble NCLT'; NSE letter: trading must commence 'within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT'.
judge.read_next: Annexure 19 — assets and liabilities demerged into RML; then RML's Information Memorandum and the NCLT sanction order.

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of Refex's green mobility (electric-vehicle fleet) business out of Refex Industries Ltd (RIL), whose core is Ash & Coal Handling. Management structured it as a composite scheme in two steps: first merge the wholly-owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Ltd (RGML) into RIL, then demerge the Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a new, separately listed entity, Refex Mobility Ltd (RML), with mirror shareholding (1 RML share of Rs 2 for every 1 RIL share) and, as Dinesh Agarwal stressed, no valuation exercise required because RGML was a 100% subsidiary. The stated reason is investor fit and value discovery: 'the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited,' so a parallel listing is meant to unlock value; the Scheme adds that the mobility business can attract a different set of investors, lenders and strategic partners, and that its risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios are distinct from ash & coal. The second driver is the drag mobility placed on consolidated results — Q1 FY26 showed standalone PAT of about INR33 crore against consolidated INR20.4 crore, with Green Mobility segment margin at minus 50%, prompting an investor to allege 'a miscalculation in your capital allocation'; management had already exited Bangalore airport B2C services to save INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost. Post-demerger RIL becomes essentially a single-business company (Anil Jain: '95% business from ash and coal handling only'), while RML carries its own balance sheet — roughly INR220 crore of net assets and, per Jan 2026, 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity' — and pursues asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led growth toward profitability after crossing about INR100 crore of revenue in three years. Mechanically the appointed date is 1 April 2025, mobility was reported as discontinued operations from FY26, lender NOCs were a gating item, BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters came on 16 March 2026, the NCLT application was filed 26 March 2026, and the NCLT-convened shareholder and creditor meetings on 5 August 2026 approved the scheme unanimously (equity shareholders ~99.999% of value in favour).
rationale.evolution: Through FY25 (May 2024, Nov 2024, Apr 2025 calls) mobility was presented as a growth vertical to scale to 2,000 then 5,000 EVs, with no separation contemplated; the first visible pressure came on the Aug 13, 2025 call, where an investor attacked the capital allocation given minus-50% mobility margins, and Anil Jain replied 'point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses.' The board approved the draft composite scheme on September 22, 2025, and it was first explained to investors on the Nov 6, 2025 call as a two-step merger-then-demerger into a separately listed Refex Mobility Ltd, with a six-to-seven-month timeline and no valuation needed. By Jan 21, 2026 the hold-up was 'final NOCs from the lenders', the net assets moving were quantified at INR220 crore with debt following, and completion was guided to end-April 2026; on May 27, 2026 BSE/NSE approvals were in hand, the NCLT filing done, and 75–90 more days guided. The timeline then slipped: creditor and shareholder meetings were only held August 5, 2026, and the October 28, 2026 press release still shows NCLT hearings pending with the next hearing on 28 October 2026.

points.point: The scheme's own rationale rests on the distinct risk/return character of the two businesses and mobility's ability to draw its own investors, lenders and partners, enabling separate capital-market access.
points.quote: The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.

points.point: Shareholders receive a 1:1 mirror entitlement in RML (appointed date 1 April 2025; RIL's existing 50,000 RML shares cancelled), and the August 5, 2026 NCLT-convened meetings approved it with ~99.999% of equity value and unanimous secured/unsecured creditor support.

rationale.what_management_expects: RIL becomes a near-pure Ash & Coal Handling play (95-100% of standalone revenue) with sharper focus and clearer capital allocation; RML operates independently, carrying its own debt and ~INR220 crore of net assets, pursuing asset-light clean-fuel and enterprise-led growth toward profitability; the 1:1 mirror listing lets a different investor set value the EV business and unlock shareholder value.
rationale.gaps: No valuation, margin or capital-raise plan for RML; no reason given for the merger-then-demerger structure; no debt split detail; repeated timeline slippage never explained.

turns: Today we'd like to intimate you about our performance in the recent quarter and provide insights into our strategic initiatives and future outlook. Before we delve into the numbers, let me take a moment to highlight our core business areas and recent devel opments. Refex Industries was incorporated in 2002 and head quartered in Chennai. It has established itself as a multifaceted company with a diverse portfolio, including ash and coal handling, refrigerant gases, green mobility and power trading. Our involvement and commitment to these sectors places us at the forefront of combating clim ate change and promoting sustainable development. Since our inception, we have been dedicated to refilling refrigerant gases that serve as replacements for harmful chlorofluorocarbons, or CFCs, and hydrochlorofluorocarbons, or HCFCs. We have emerged as a leading supplier of environment -friendly hydrofluorocarbons or HFC refrigerant gases in India. […] To optimize our fleet management, we rely on centralized GPS tracking, partnering with reputable service providers like Loconav, TATA Fleet Edge , and iAlert. Through this innovative tracking system, we can closely monitor volumes, GPS location, and other vital metrics, positioning us as pioneers in this field. In 2022, we venture into power trading and obtain a Category 1 Power Trading license. judge.what_is_spun: The Energy business of Siemens Limited, transferred to Siemens Energy India Limited under a Scheme of Arrangement
judge.reason: not stated — the filings give no rationale; the Dec 2025 analyst meet only describes SEIL as 'now a separately listed pure play energy company'
judge.insiders: not stated — no promoter or management shareholding, stake, or incentive in Siemens Energy India Limited is disclosed anywhere in these documents
judge.hidden_value: Energy left with net assets of Rs 37,846 million including Rs 25,478 million cash; it earned Rs 9,418 million PBT on Rs 61,580 million revenue in FY2024. Parent remains cash-rich (Rs 77,905 million cash and bank, 30 Sep 2026) with a Rs 47,034 crore backlog.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Energy was large, not a stub (FY2024 revenue Rs 61,580 million); management said combined share prices rose ~40%
judge.listing_timeline: not stated as a listing date; appointed date 1 March 2025 and effective date 25 March 2025 (stated 14 November 2025), and at the 12 December 2025 analyst meet SEIL was described as 'now a separately listed pure play energy company'
