deal.size_statement: As per audited standalone financial statements as at March 31, 2024, Tata Motors Limited's ("the Company"/ "TML") total income relating to Commercial Vehicles Business was ₹ 73,116.64 crore, representing ~99% of the total income for FY 2023-24.
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated as a percentage for the parent; the documents state only "TML: No change." in shareholding pattern pursuant to the Scheme, and "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of TML pursuant to the Scheme coming into effect."
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2024 Composite Scheme (CV demerger): "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme, the shareholding of TMLCV will mirror the shareholding of TML." and "The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in creation of two listed companies, forming part of the Tata Group, with identical shareholding (including common promoters) with the Resulting Company housing the Commercial Vehicles Business and the Amalgamated Company housing the Passenger Vehicles Business." TMLCV shareholding (details as on July 26, 2024): Promoters Pre-Scheme 100.00%, Post-Scheme (Indicative) 41.22%; Public Pre-Scheme nil, Post-Scheme 58.78% (*Considering Ordinary and 'A' Ordinary shares). Amalgamation of TMPV into TML: "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of TML pursuant to the Scheme coming into effect." 2024 TMFL–Tata Capital scheme: "TCL will issue its equity shares to the shareholders of TMFL resulting in TML effectively holding a 4.7% stake in the merged entity." 2024 'A' Ordinary Shares scheme: promoter holding after is not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2024 Composite Scheme (CV demerger): "each shareholder of Demerged Company whose name is recorded in the register of members and records of the depository as a shareholder of the Demerged Company as on the Record Date (ie. October 14, 2025) shall be issued and allotted 1 (one) share of the Resulting Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up), for every 1 (one) share of the Demerged Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up) of the same class of shares outstanding and as held by such shareholder in the Demerged Company, without any further application, act or deed ('Share Entitlement Ratio')." Shareholders also continue to hold their existing shares in TML (renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), which "shall continue to be a listed entity". 2024 'A' Ordinary Shares scheme: "As per the Scheme, the Company shall issue 7 (seven) fully paid up New Ordinary Shares of the face value of ₹ 2 each for every 10 (ten) 'A' Ordinary Shares of the face value of ₹2 each, as consideration to the 'A' Ordinary Shareholders of the Company as on the Record Date ('Consideration')." 2024 TMFL–Tata Capital scheme: nothing is received by TML's own public shareholders; "the shareholders of TMFL shall receive 37 equity shares of Rs.10/- each in TCL for every 100 equity shares of Rs. 100 each held by them in TMFL."
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of existing grants under the Composite Scheme is not stated. Resolutions passed at the 79th AGM held on June 24, 2024 (both Special Resolutions): "Tata Motors Limited Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme 2024 and grant of Performance Share Units to the Eligible Employees under the Scheme" and "Extending the Tata Motors Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme 2024 to Eligible Employees of Subsidiary companies of the Company". No new plan in the resulting company, no exercise price or pricing date, and no management or insider shareholding are stated. Related manpower action at JLR: "About GBP 40 million of that was associated with a voluntary redundancy program as we resized our cost base" and "We are taking c.500 employees out of our admin base".
deal.insider_actions: not stated

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Passenger Vehicles Business retained in the listed entity; Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (the amalgamating wholly owned subsidiary carrying the PV business) had total income of ₹51,206.32 crore for the year ended March 31, 2024
other_differences.separated_business: Commercial Vehicles Business demerged into TMLCV with total income of ₹73,116.64 crore, ~99% of TML's standalone total income for FY 2023-24
other_differences.quote: As per audited standalone financial statements as at March 31, 2024, Tata Motors Limited's ("the Company"/ "TML") total income relating to Commercial Vehicles Business was ₹ 73,116.64 crore, representing ~99% of the total income for FY 2023-24.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: 68.85% of a shareholder's total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares is apportioned to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited)
other_differences.separated_business: 31.15% of a shareholder's total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares is apportioned to Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited), being the proportion the net book value of assets transferred bears to the net worth of the demerged company
other_differences.quote: The total cost of acquisition of INR 4,00,000/- would be apportioned in the aforesaid ratio - INR 1,24,600/- (31.15% of INR 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 1,000 Resulting Company shares and INR 2,75,400/- (INR 4,00,000/- less INR 1,24,600) being the total cost of acquisition of 1000 original shares of Demerged Company.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: TMPV group net debt of Rs. 30,000 Cr for the year ending March 2026; net auto debt had moved from a net cash position at end FY25 to ~Rs. 20,000 Cr at Q2 FY26
other_differences.separated_business: Identified Rated, Listed, Unsecured, Redeemable NCDs aggregating ₹2,300 crore transferred from the Demerged Company to the Resulting Company (NCD record date October 10, 2025)
other_differences.quote: The net debt for the year ending March 2026 was Rs. 30,000 Cr, largely representing the Rs. 25,000 Cr of consol cash burn and the Rs. 2,200 Cr of dividends that we paid last year.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: PV remains cash positive at about Rs. 7,000 Cr while JLR net debt stood at Rs. 33,000 Cr (FY26); India business was net cash ~Rs. 5,000 Cr at Q2 FY26
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: PV remains cash positive at about Rs. 7,000 Cr, while the net debt at JLR stood at Rs. 33,000 Cr.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Passenger Vehicles sales in Q2 FY26 of 144,397 units vs 130,753 units in Q2 FY25, robust double-digit year-on-year growth of more than 10%
other_differences.separated_business: Commercial Vehicles sales in Q2 FY26 of 94,681 units vs 84,281 units in Q2 FY25, growth of 12%
other_differences.quote: Overall, in Q2 FY26, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles delivered sales of 94,681 units, registering a growth of 12% over the same period last year.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: TMPV India business ended FY26 with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin; PBT before extraordinary expenses in Q4 of Rs. 1,100 Cr
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: We ended the year with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: TMPV India capex for FY26 of about Rs. 4,300 Cr, about 7.5% of revenues (combined PV and EV); JLR full-year investment of GBP 3.57 billion, of which GBP 2.6 billion engineering
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Capex for the year stood at about Rs. 4,300 Cr that translated to about 7.5% of revenues, well within the guidance range that we gave from the combined Capex for PV and EV.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: TMPV Board approved a dividend of Rs. 3 per share for FY26, cash outflow about Rs. 1,100 Cr; erstwhile Tata Motors paid Rs. 6 in dividends for the last two years
other_differences.separated_business: TMLCV announced Rs. 4 of dividend for FY26
other_differences.quote: The TMLCV has announced Rs. 4 of dividend in the results meeting yesterday.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Cost of acquisition of original shares in the demerged company deemed reduced under Section 49(2D); amalgamation of TMPV complies with Section 2(1B) of the Income-tax Act, 1961
other_differences.separated_business: Demerger complies with Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act, 1961; issue of shares by the Resulting Company is not regarded as transfer under Section 47(vid), and holding period of the demerged company's shares carries over
other_differences.quote: Therefore, the Demerger is not treated as a transfer in the hands of the shareholders.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Reporting boundary split: "Passenger Vehicles (PV) businesses for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026"; the Chinchwad facility in Pune became part of the Company from October 2025
other_differences.separated_business: "Commercial Vehicles (CV) business for the period 1 April 2025 to 30 June 2025", disclosed in Annexure I to the BRSR
other_differences.quote: As per the Demerger Scheme, the CV business was transferred and vested into a separate entity with effect from the appointed date, being July 1, 2025, while the Passenger Vehicle (PV) business continued to remain with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited) (Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles or 'TMPVL' or 'Company').

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is the steel business undertaking of Bhushan Power and Steel Limited (BPSL) — the ~4.5 MTPA integrated plant at Jharsuguda/Sambalpur, Odisha, which JSW acquired out of IBC in 2021 at 2.75 MTPA and then expanded to 4.5 MTPA. The mechanics, approved by the Board on December 3, 2025, were a slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking on a going-concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for Rs. 24,483 crores cash (subject to closing adjustments), with JFE Steel Corporation of Japan subscribing 50% of JSW Sambalpur's holding company JSW Kalinga Steel Limited for Rs. 15,750 crores in two equal tranches of Rs. 7,875 crores — giving a 50:50 JV at an equity value of Rs. 31,500 crores and enterprise value of Rs. 53,000 crores. Management's stated problem was funding growth without stressing the balance sheet: JSW had a 50 MTPA India target by FY31 (raised in May 2026 to 62 MTPA by FY32, plus 16 MTPA across the JFE and POSCO JVs, ~78-80 MTPA in all), and the transaction was 'aimed at securing the Company's growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles,' producing a Rs. 32,000 crore cash inflow and ~Rs. 37,000 crores of deleveraging. The second stated problem was capability: BPSL 'has significant growth potential' and the JV would 'enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products,' building on JFE's partnership with JSW since 2009. A third, separate problem was structure — BPSL sat under Piombino Steel Limited, 82.65% JSW Steel and 17.35% JSW Shipping & Logistics (a promoter group entity) — so a parallel scheme amalgamated Piombino into JSW Steel (10 JSW shares of Re. 1 for every 156 Piombino shares of Rs. 10) so JSW could 'directly hold the investment in BPSL,' giving 'a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL's business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement,' plus 'additional cash to pursue its growth aspirations in a financially prudent manner' and fewer entities/compliances. By May 14, 2026 management reported the JV entity formed by end-March, JFE's first tranche in, ~Rs. 30,000 crores of the Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging done, net debt Rs. 54,000 crores, leverage down to 1.81x and gearing 0.51x, a credit-rating outlook uplift, a Rs. 18,051 crore exceptional gain on the slump sale (largely sheltered by BPSL's carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation), and BPSL deconsolidated into equity accounting. No text in the filings or the one readable call says investors, lenders or partners demanded the separation; JFE is the counterparty and already had a nominee, Mr. Hiroyuki Ogawa, on JSW Steel's board.
rationale.evolution: Nine of the ten supplied transcripts (Jan 2024 through Jan 2026) contain no extractable text, so the call-by-call germination of the idea cannot be traced from these materials; the paper trail starts with the Board approval and signed JV/business-transfer/share-subscription agreements on December 3, 2025, alongside the separate Piombino merger scheme approved the same day. CCI cleared it on January 20, 2026, and the Q3 FY26 results of January 23, 2026 first quantified it (equity value Rs. 31,500 crores, EV Rs. 53,000 crores, Rs. 32,000 crore inflow, Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging), classified the undertaking as held for sale under Ind AS 105, booked a Rs. 1,439 crore deferred tax asset against likely capital gains, and explicitly concluded it was not a 'discontinued operation.' The slump sale completed on March 27, 2026, and on the May 14, 2026 call management reframed it as the foundation of a 'double engine of growth' — JSW Steel to 62 MTPA by FY32 with 16 MTPA more in the JFE and POSCO JVs — while tightening its own leverage caps (3.75x to 3.00x) and gearing caps (1.75x to 1.25x). The Piombino amalgamation then ran its course: shareholder meeting August 21, 2026 (94.86% of valid votes, 97.20% of public votes), NCLT sanction October 16, 2026, effective October 31, 2026 from an appointed date of January 1, 2026.

points.point: Board approval of December 3, 2025 set out the structure: slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking to JSW Sambalpur for Rs. 24,483 crores cash, with JFE buying 50% of JSW Kalinga for Rs. 15,750 crores in two equal tranches.
points.quote: Transfer of BPSL Steel business undertaking, by way of slump sale on a going concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited (“JSW Sambalpur”) for a cash consideration of Rs 24,483 crores, subject to customary closing adjustments as agreed in the transaction documents.

points.point: The stated justification to shareholders was funding a 50 MTPA-by-FY31 growth plan without balance-sheet strain, across cycles.
points.quote: The present transaction is aimed at securing the Company’s growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles.

points.point: The second rationale was technology and product mix: JFE, a partner since 2009, would accelerate BPSL's capacity and push it into high-end value-added steel.
points.quote: JFE has been a long-term strategic partner of JSW Steel since 2009. The BPSL Steel business has significant growth potential and this joint venture will enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products

points.point: Q3 FY26 press release quantified the deal: 50% of BPSL steel at Rs. 31,500 crore equity value and Rs. 53,000 crore EV, with Rs. 32,000 crores of cash in and Rs. 37,000 crores of deleveraging.
points.quote: With this transaction, JFE will take a 50% stake in the BPSL Steel business at an equity value of Rs. 31,500 crores and enterprise value of Rs. 53,000 crores. This transaction will enable a cash inflow of Rs. 32,000 crores, and a substantial deleveraging of Rs. 37,000 crores for JSW Steel.

points.point: Accounting treatment: BPSL's steel assets and liabilities were moved to held-for-sale under Ind AS 105 at December 31, 2025, but the company insisted it was not a discontinued operation.
points.quote: The Group has also assessed and concluded that transfer of BPSL’s steel business undertaking does not qualify as “discontinued operation” as it is not a separate major line of business and forms part of overall steel operations of the Group.

points.point: A Rs. 1,439 crore deferred tax asset was recognised on BPSL's brought-forward unabsorbed depreciation because capital gains on the slump sale made recovery probable.
points.quote: Further, based on the reassessment of unrecognised deferred tax assets, the Group has recognised deferred tax assets (net) amounting to Rs. 1,439 crores as it is probable that carried forward unabsorbed depreciation will be recovered against the likely capital gains on the above mentioned transaction .

points.point: The parallel Piombino Steel merger was justified as removing the 17.35% promoter-group minority above BPSL so JSW Steel could hold and transact on BPSL directly, and would hand JSW extra cash.
points.quote: The merger ensures better alignment of the Transferee Company’s long-term strategic interests by enabling it to directly hold the investment in Bhushan Power and Steel Limited (‘BPSL’). This consolidation provides a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL’s business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement;

points.point: Acharya opened FY26 by framing the BPSL carve-out as the year's defining strategic step and the source of structural deleveraging, with ~Rs. 30,000 of the Rs. 37,000 crores done by March-end.
points.quote: This transaction entails a deleveraging of approximately Rs.37,000 crores for JSW Steel, out of which about Rs.30,000 crores has been completed at March end.

points.point: Balance-sheet outcome cited: leverage 1.81x, gearing 0.51x, net debt ~Rs. 54,000 crores, rating outlook uplift, plus a further Rs. 7,900 crores of deleveraging from JFE's second tranche by end-June.
points.quote: The second tranche of equity investment in JFE is expected by end -June, which will dr ive further deleveraging of Rs.7,900 crores approximately.

points.point: Asked by Amit Murarka (Axis Capital) whether multiple simultaneous projects were the new normal, Acharya said the JV's purpose was dual: faster growth plus deleveraging, run as two balance sheets.
points.quote: So , as we had given you an indication earlier that the idea of the JV was to strategically grow faster in the country, while it helped us to deleverage as well.

points.point: The separation was booked as a Rs. 18,051 crore exceptional gain on the slump sale, inside a Q4 exceptional gain of Rs. 17,888 crores; normalised PAT was Rs. 3,475 crores.
points.quote: This incl udes a gain of Rs.18,051 crores on slump sale of BPSL steel undertaking and Rs.163 crores exceptional charge on implementation of new labor code.

points.point: Swayam Saurabh told Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) that BPSL's carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation made the tax cost of the transaction negligible, including in JSW's own books.
points.quote: So BPSL has had carry forward losses, unabsorbed depreciation. So , the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower.

points.point: Ashwin Bajaj clarified the reporting consequence: BPSL leaves revenue and EBITDA entirely and appears only as income from associates and joint ventures.
points.quote: BPSL has been deconsolidated at March - end. And the n umbers for BPSL will not be part of financials of EBITDA. It would be equity accounting, and there is a line in the P&L, which says income from associates and joint ventures.

points.point: The carve-out also carried a raw-material asset into the JV: the 2 MTPA Netrabanda iron ore mine was commissioned in Q4 inside BPSL and now sits with the joint venture.
points.quote: The 2 mill ion tonnes iron ore mine at Netrabanda, which is now with the joint venture is now part of BPSL is being commissioned in the Quarter 4, increasing the ir on ore availability for the joint venture.

points.point: Management used the freed balance sheet to raise targets to 62 MTPA by FY32 for JSW Steel alone plus 16 MTPA across the JFE and POSCO JVs, and to tighten leverage caps from 3.75x to 3.00x and gearing from 1.75x to 1.25x.
points.quote: So , we'll have a double engine of growth, one which JSW Steel will grow on and the other which the joint venture will grow on.

points.point: Sumangal Nevatia (Kotak) pressed on why a second partner (POSCO) was needed given the already-strong post-JFE balance sheet; Acharya cited technology access plus POSCO's wish to backward-integrate its 2 MTPA Maharashtra cold-rolling plant.
points.quote: I just want to understand better what is the rationale and wha t value does the new JV par tner brings given that we already have a very strong balance sheet after the JFE deal.

rationale.what_management_expects: For JSW Steel: Rs. 32,000 crore inflow, ~Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging, leverage 1.81x and gearing 0.51x, rating uplift, tighter caps (3.00x/1.25x), funding 62 MTPA by FY32 and a Rs. 2,26,000 crore capex programme. For the BPSL JV: faster capacity growth to ~10 MTPA with JFE's best-in-class technology, high-end value-added products, Netrabanda iron ore, equity-accounted. Piombino merger: direct BPSL ownership, extra cash, fewer entities, lower overheads.
rationale.gaps: No BPSL-specific margin, ROCE or valuation basis; no stated originator or investor/lender pressure; no dividend or exit path; nine transcripts unreadable, so pre-Dec-2025 discussion is absent.

deal.promoter_holding_parent: "Promoters 110,82,03,750 45.32" % of equity shares of JSW Steel Limited as on May 12, 2026 (before the BMM Ispat Scheme); Public 133,26,24,392 (54.49%); Non-Promoter and Non-Public 46,25,824 (0.19%)
deal.promoter_holding_after: BMM Ispat amalgamation (2026): "Post Scheme# Promoters 113,79,55,094 45.65 ... Public 135,03,80,791 54.17 ... Non-Promoter and Non-Public 46,25,824 0.19 ... Total 249,29,61,709 100.00", "#post inter se transfer of 4.15% of the issued and paid-up share capital of the Transferor Company, effected pursuant to a share purchase agreement executed between the shareholders of Transferor Company on May 12, 2026." | ARCL/MCL/JRDL amalgamation (2026): "There shall not be any change in the shareholding pattern of JSL pursuant to the amalgamation, as no shares would be issued by JSL to the shareholders of ARCL, MCL and JRSL in connection with the proposed Scheme." | Piombino Steel Limited amalgamation (2026): not stated | JSW One Platforms Limited IPO (2026): not stated (JSW Steel participates only as Promoter Selling Shareholder offering shares aggregating up to Rs. 811 Crores; it held "about 61% equity stake on a fully diluted basis" in the JSW online platform) | Saffron Resources / POSCO JV (2026): "Saffron would become a 50:50 joint venture between the Company and POSCO Group."
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2026 ARCL/MCL/JRDL amalgamation: "As the Transferor Companies are wholly owned subsidiaries of the Transferee Company, no shares of the Transferee Company shall be allotted towards discharge of consideration or in lieu or exchange of the equity shareholding in the Transferor Companies." — nothing is received by JSW Steel's public shareholders, and "There shall not be any change in the shareholding pattern of JSL pursuant to the amalgamation". | 2026 Piombino amalgamation: nothing is issued to JSW Steel's own shareholders; Piombino's shareholders receive "10 (Ten) fully paid-up equity shares of Re. 1 (Rupee One only) each fully paid up of the Transferee Company for every 156 (One Hundred and Fifty-Six) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees Ten) each fully paid up of the Transferor Company." | 2026 BMM Ispat amalgamation: nothing is issued to JSW Steel's existing public shareholders (their stake moves from 54.49% to 54.17%); BMMIL's shareholders receive "1 fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 1/- each of the Transferee Company ... for every 18 fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 10/- each". | 2026 JSW One Platforms IPO: nothing — it is an offer for sale of shares held by JSW Steel Limited, not a distribution to shareholders; "Not applicable, since the transaction is an offer for sale in the proposed IPO." | 2026 Saffron/POSCO JV: nothing — POSCO Group subscribes to new shares of Saffron for ~INR 508.8 crore. | 2024 NSAIL amalgamation: not stated.
deal.management_incentives: 2026 ARCL/MCL/JRDL Scheme, clause 9.5: "It is clarified that save as expressly provided for in this Scheme, the employees of the Transferor Companies who become the employees of the Transferee Company by virtue of this Scheme, shall not be entitled to avail of any Schemes and benefits (including employee stock options) that may be applicable and available to any of the other employees of the Transferee Company (including benefits of or under any employee stock option schemes applicable to or covering all or any of the other employees of the Transferee Company), unless otherwise determined by the Transferee Company. The Transferee Company undertakes to continue to abide by any agreement/settlement, if any, entered into or deemed to have been entered into by the Transferor Companies with any employee of the Transferor Companies." Treatment of existing grants, any new plan in a resulting entity, exercise price or pricing date, and management or insider shareholding: not stated. Directors' interest, 2026 ARCL/MCL/JRDL order: "The Directors of the Applicant Companies may be deemed to be concerned and/or interested in the Scheme to the extent of their shareholding in the Applicant Company, or to the extent the said Directors are common Directors in the Amalgamated Company and the Amalgamating Companies..."
deal.insider_actions: JSW Steel Limited itself is selling down in the JOPL IPO: "the participation of the Company in the proposed initial public offering ("IPO") of JSW One Platforms Limited ("JOPL") as a Promoter Selling Shareholder by offering for sale, such number of equity shares of face value of Rs. 10 each of JOPL aggregating up to Rs. 811 Crores ... held by the Company". | BMM Ispat is bought from the promoter group: "Majority stake in BMMIL is held by JSW Projects Limited, a promoter group entity of the Company, while the remaining shareholding is with Mr. Dinesh Kumar Singhi and Mrs. Snehalatha Singhi." and "#post inter se transfer of 4.15% of the issued and paid-up share capital of the Transferor Company, effected pursuant to a share purchase agreement executed between the shareholders of Transferor Company on May 12, 2026." That scheme raises promoter holding in JSW Steel from 45.32% to 45.65%. | Shareholder vote on the Piombino scheme: "The Scheme was approved by 2,032 equity shareholders holding 2,14,82,88,337 equity shares, representing 94.86% of the valid votes cast by the Company's equity shareholders. It was also approved by 1,982 public shareholders holding 1,06,75,43,004 equity shares, representing 97.20% of the valid votes cast by its public shareholders." | Other promoter/management buying, selling or pledging: not stated.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Leverage 1.81x and gearing 0.51x as on 31 March 2026, net debt ~Rs.54,000 crores; stated maximum cap revised from gearing 1.75x to 1.25x and leverage 3.75x to 3.00x, with comfort below 2.5x; revenue acceptances $2.1 billion
other_differences.separated_business: The BPSL steel business moved into a 50:50 JV with JFE, taking ~Rs.37,000 crores of debt off JSW Steel, of which ~Rs.30,000 crores was completed at March end and a further ~Rs.7,900 crores expected from the second JFE tranche by end-June
other_differences.quote: This transaction entails a deleveraging of approximately Rs.37,000 crores for JSW Steel, out of which about Rs.30,000 crores has been completed at March end.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The Piombino amalgamation is stated to give JSW Steel additional cash and to let it hold the BPSL investment directly, "without minority shareholders' involvement"
other_differences.separated_business: Piombino Steel Limited: paid-up share capital Rs. 5877,36,40,000; its cash is not separately quantified
other_differences.quote: Pursuant to the proposed amalgamation, the Transferee Company will have additional cash to pursue its growth aspirations in a financially prudent manner;

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Effective tax on the BPSL slump sale was significantly lower because carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation were used, on JSW's books
other_differences.separated_business: BPSL had carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation; JSW Retail and Distribution Limited "confirmed that it has no carry-forward losses or unabsorbed depreciation"
other_differences.quote: So BPSL has had carry forward losses, unabsorbed depreciation. So, the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Steel sales ~8 million tonnes in Q4 and ~30 million tonnes in FY26; FY27 guidance of 29.75 million tonnes production and 28.6 million tonnes sales; domestic demand growth of 7% to 9% expected in FY27
other_differences.separated_business: JSW One Platforms (the JSW online platform being taken to IPO) turned profitable for the first time in Q4 FY26, with steel volumes up 50% YoY and GMV up 57% YoY
other_differences.quote: In quarter 4, it turned profitable for the first time. The steel volumes grew by 50% YoY and the GMV reached Rs.6,200 crores, a 57% YoY increase.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Approved growth capex of Rs.1,26,000 crores over the next 4 to 5 years, Rs.22,000–24,000 crores in FY27, plus "another Rs.1,00,000 crores between now to FY33"; capex of Rs.4,612 crores in Q4 and Rs.15,600 crores in FY26; equity of about Rs.4,000–5,000 crores per JV project
other_differences.separated_business: BMM Ispat can be doubled from ~0.9 million tonnes to ~1.8 million tonnes for Rs.1,600–1,800 crores; it was acquired for about Rs.6,500 crores against a net worth of about Rs.2,700 crores
other_differences.quote: Yes. On an expanded basis, you're right that this gives us the additional headroom because we feel the next 1 million or 0.9 million tonne can be expanded between Rs.1,600 crores to Rs.1,800 crores, making the overall investment very attractive.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs.9,713 crores at a 19% EBITDA margin; FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs.32,048 crores; normalised PAT excluding exceptionals ~Rs.8,700 crores for FY26 and Rs.3,475 crores for Q4
other_differences.separated_business: JSW One Platforms: share of profit for FY 2025-26 of (Rs. 90 crores), being (0.35%) of JSW Steel's consolidated net profit after tax; BMM Ispat FY25 production and EBITDA not provided on the call
other_differences.quote: Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs.9,713 crores with an EBITDA margin of 19%, while PAT stood at Rs.19,243 crores.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Exceptional gain of Rs.17,888 crores in Q4 FY26, including Rs.18,051 crores on the slump sale of the BPSL steel undertaking and a Rs.163 crores exceptional charge on the new labor code
other_differences.separated_business: BPSL is deconsolidated at March-end and reported through equity accounting under income from associates and joint ventures
other_differences.quote: It is important to note that there was an exceptional gain of Rs.17,888 crores in Quarter 4.

judge.reason: Consolidate the entire Data Centre Business in one entity and create two dedicated listed companies, enabling independent market recognition and valuation, dedicated management focus and sector-specific funding.
judge.insiders: ARL promoters hold 57.42% of ARL; post-scheme ACPL is 28.14% promoters directly plus 51% held by ARL (79.14% total), public 20.86%. Promoter-group Anish Sarin oversees data-centre rollout.
judge.hidden_value: Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Small (8.96% of turnover), only 20.86% public float in ACPL, and a digital-infrastructure business alien to real-estate holders.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — the July 21, 2026 filings say only that ACPL's demerger shares and ARL's existing ACPL shares "shall be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by seeking exemption under Rule 19(7)", subject to NCLT, SEBI, exchange, shareholder and creditor approvals; no date given
judge.read_next: The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
judge.quote: The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.
rationale.evolution: On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

points.point: An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years.
points.quote: We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.

points.point: Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases.
points.quote: And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.

points.point: Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses.
points.quote: So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.

points.point: The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex.
points.quote: This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.

points.point: An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point.
points.quote: Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.

points.point: The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.

points.point: Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total.
points.quote: In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.

points.point: Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32.
points.quote: And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.

points.point: The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it.
points.quote: The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.

points.point: The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies.
points.quote: The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.

points.point: Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26.
points.quote: the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;

points.point: Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised.
points.quote: the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;

points.point: Consideration is 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2; ARL holders get 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL keeps 51%, so ACPL remains a subsidiary and ARL holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest; listing on BSE and NSE via the Rule 19(7) exemption.
points.quote: Overall, the shareholders of ARL will hold 100% of the ultimate beneficial economic interest in the Resultant Company, ACPL ( direct holding of 49% and indirect holding of 51% throughARL).

points.point: Days before the Scheme, the Finance and Investment Committee funded the shell resultant company: a ₹74,86,45,106 rights issue of 37,43,22,553 ₹2 shares in ACPL (incorporated Oct 11, 2021; nil turnover in FY24, FY25 and FY26) to meet data centre and cloud development funding.
points.quote: ACPL proposes to raise the fund to meet the funding requirement for development of its data centres and cloud business.

points.point: The press release frames the outcome as two independent platforms — ARL in real estate/infrastructure and Ashok Cloud in data centres, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure and DC/DR services — citing separate growth trajectories, operational priorities and capital needs.
points.quote: "Our real estate, infrastructure business and Data Centre & Cloud Services Business have evolved into two distinct platforms, each with its own growth trajectory, operational priorities, and capital needs.

rationale.what_management_expects: Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.
rationale.gaps: Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.

deal.promoter_holding_parent: Promoters 20,66,57,823 shares, 57.42% (Pre-Arrangement Shareholding as on date, per the board-meeting disclosure dated July 21, 2026); Public 15,32,19,107 shares, 42.58%; Total 35,98,76,930 shares
deal.promoter_holding_after: Merger of ARCPL into ARL — no change in ARL: "Post -Arrangement Shareholding : Particulars Post-Arrangement (No. of Shares) Promoters 20,66,57,823 Public 15,32,19,107 Total 35,98,76,930 ... Post-Arrangement (Percentage) 57.42 42.58 100.00"; ARCPL's own capital is extinguished (Post-Arrangement Promoters -, Public -, Total -). Demerger into ACPL — ARL unchanged at Promoters 57.42% / Public 42.58%; in ACPL: "Pursuant to the Scheme, the shareholders of ARL will directly hold 49% in the Resultant Company, proportionate to their shareholding m ARL. Consequently, the shareholding of the Resultant Company shall comprise 28.14% held by the promoters of ARL, 20.86% held by the public shareholders, and the remaining 51 % held by ARL." Post-Arrangement ACPL: "Promoters (ARL: 51%; Promoters of ARL: 28.14%) 58,12,30,376 shares — 79.14%; Public 15,32,19,107 — 20.86%; Total 73,44,49,483 — 100.00%"
deal.public_shareholders_get: Merger of ARCPL into ARL: no shares are issued or allotted, as ARCPL is a wholly owned subsidiary of ARL. Demerger into Ashok Cloud: "Upon the Scheme becoming effective, eligible shareholders of Anant Raj Limited will receive one fully paid-up equity share of face value of ₹2 each in Ashok Cloud Private Limited for every one fully paid-up equity share of face value of ₹2 each held in Anant Raj Limited." Public shareholders end up holding 20.86% of ACPL directly, and "Overall, the shareholders of ARL will hold 100% of the ultimate beneficial economic interest in the Resultant Company, ACPL ( direct holding of 49% and indirect holding of 51% throughARL)."
deal.management_incentives: not stated
deal.insider_actions: Promoter warrant conversion funded ahead of schedule, per the November 12, 2025 earnings call: "prior to doing the Bharat Built from soil to server, the company at that time, the promoters were issued warrants of INR 100 crores for which the promoters were supposed to convert by September '26. Actually, the promoters put in the money in March '25 itself and that additional cash flow of INR 100 crores really helped the company and we converted our share warrants at a price of INR 730 done." Promoter-group management expansion: "the appointment of Sh. Anish Sarin as Additional Director designated as Whole-time Director of the Company w.e.f. May 11, 2026" — "Sh. Anish Sarin forms part of the promoter group of the Company". No promoter buying, selling or pledging of ARL shares around the separation is stated.

judge.quote: A Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement was entered into between the Company ("Amalgamated Company" and "Demerged Company") and Esteem Properties Private Limited ("Amalgamating Company"/"EPPL") and Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly known as Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) ("Resulting Company"/"AHIL) ("Scheme") mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.

listing.text: LISTED — Advent Hotels International Limited (ADVENTHTL) since 2025-11-13 (NSE equity list); record date 2025-07-18

rationale.rationale: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.
rationale.evolution: There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

points.point: The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor.
points.quote: mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders

points.point: Post-demerger Valor is a pure-play real estate company with a single reportable segment, and prior-period hospitality results are reclassified as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105.
points.quote: Consequent to the demerger, the Company is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment.

points.point: Management framed the separation as letting each business pursue its own growth path: Chairman Vinod Goenka tied Q2FY26 progress to completing the demerger and listing of hospitality.
points.quote: We successfully completed the demerger and listing of our Hospitality business, an important milestone that enables each platform to pursue its independent growth path.

points.point: The Q2FY26 press release states the problems the split solves on Valor's side: targeted independent strategies for each business, sharper operational focus, and unlocked long-term value.
points.quote: This development enables each business to pursue a targeted, independent growth strategy, strengthens operational focus, and positions the Group to unlock enhanced long-term value for shareholders.

points.point: Advent's 13 November 2025 NSE/BSE listing was justified on visibility, shareholder liquidity and capital structure, with Advent carved out of Valor and run by its own board and management.
points.quote: The listing will mark a significant milestone in Advent's journey as a dedicated hospitality platform, enabling enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure to support future growth.

points.point: Advent now has independent governance: two operating hotels (313-key Grand Hyatt Bambolim Goa plus 113 keys under development, and a 171-key Hilton in Andheri East, Mumbai).
points.quote: The Company is governed by its own Board and Management team following the demerger.

points.point: Advent quantified the growth the standalone platform is meant to fund: five projects under development including St. Regis and Marriott Marquis at Aerocity Delhi with Prestige Group (FY27), Waldorf Astoria and Hilton at Worli, and a 1,175-key BKC hotel.
points.quote: With five projects under development, the company is on track to expand to 3,100 keys. EBITDA, currently under ₹200 crore, is projected to surpass ₹1,200 crore as these projects mature by FY32, reflecting the company's robust growth and institutional approach.

points.point: Advent's MD & CEO Rahul Pandit cast the separation and listing as a governance and financing fix for an asset-heavy hospitality business; Promoter Director Arshad Balwa targeted mid-teens compounded ROE over the next decade.
points.quote: This listing enhances our financial flexibility, strengthens governance, and enables sustainable value generation for all stakeholders.

points.point: Vice Chairman & MD Shahid Balwa linked the demerger and non-core divestments to deleveraging — consolidated secured debt of ₹730 crore, full redemption of ₹235 crore of NCDs from the ₹262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance.
points.quote: The rationalisation of our project portfolio, combined with selective monetisation initiatives, including the divestment of non-core assets, has enabled us to reduce debt levels, bringing us closer to our medium-term objective of a leaner and more efficient capital structure.

points.point: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy was treated explicitly as a non-core asset being liquidated: the Group went to 76.63% through enforcement of security, then to 100%, and SADPL sold its dairy assets under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees as an exceptional item.
points.quote: As the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets, SADPL has not been consolidated.

points.point: The NCLT order of 29 January 2026 records the benefits claimed for folding dairy-turned-real-estate SADPL into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited, a wholly-owned-subsidiary merger inside the group with appointed date 1 April 2025, effective 12 March 2026.
points.quote: Simplification  and rationalisation  of corporate  struct ure through consolidation;

points.point: The same order lists compliance and overhead reduction as the operating rationale for the SADPL-HVPL consolidation, with the petitioners undertaking not to claim Section 72A tax-loss benefits after the Income-tax Officer objected.
points.quote: Reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances,  reduction in overheads, including administrative, managerial and other administrative costs.

points.point: The Scheme itself restructured Valor's preference capital: Clause 32 cut RPS face value from Rs. 10 to Rs. 9 and consolidated 10 into 9 (KRPL's 7,17,50,000 becoming 6,45,75,000), and Clause 20 allotted 1 AHIL preference share for every 10 Valor RPS (71,75,000 to KRPL).
points.quote: which were reduced and consolidated as per the recent Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench on 12th	June,	2025	(effecting	 the	demerger	 of	Company’s	 hospitality	 business,

points.point: Building on the Scheme, the Board on 14 November 2025 proposed converting KRPL's 6,45,75,000 8% RPS into 0.0001% CCPS convertible into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 (premium Rs. 191.65), to avoid the redemption cash outflow and lift net worth.
points.quote: The conversion of RPS into CCPS is expected to reduce the future cash outflows otherwise required for the redemption of RPS, thereby improving liquidity, conserving cash resources, and enabling the Company to channel funds towards its operational and growth requirements.

rationale.what_management_expects: Valor: pure-play real estate, single reportable segment, leaner and more efficient capital structure, lower debt (secured debt ₹730 crore), greater financial flexibility, unlocked value. Advent: independent board and management, focused hospitality platform, better visibility, shareholder liquidity, stronger capital structure, 3,100 keys and EBITDA above ₹1,200 crore by FY32, mid-teens compounded ROE.
rationale.gaps: No call transcripts supplied; filings never name investors, lenders or partners who asked for it, nor give swap-ratio valuation basis, cost savings, or Advent fundraising plans.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Of consolidated secured debt of Rs 1,328 crores, Rs 839 crores are secured against real estate project cashflows, expected to be repaid in the next financial year
other_differences.separated_business: Rs 489 crores pertains to the borrowing facility for hotel operations (now Advent Hotels), backed by its assets and cashflows, which shall flow into the demerged entity
other_differences.quote: The Group's consolidated secured debt presently amounts to Rs 1,328 crores. Of this, Rs 839 crores are secured against real estate project cashflows, and these real estate project loans are expected to be repaid in the next financial year. The remaining Rs 489 Crores pertains to the borrowing facility for hotel operations (now Advent Hotels), backed by its assets and cashflows which shall flow into the demerged entity upon the hospitality demerger coming through.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Debt-to-equity for real estate among the lowest in the sector at 0.21:1 (Q1FY26); 0.34:1 at FY25, and 0.30:1 including hospitality loans
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: DEBT-TO-EQUITY AMONG THE LOWEST IN THE SECTOR — 0.21:1 (REAL ESTATE)

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Real estate Q1FY26: revenue Rs 840.33 crore with EBITDA of Rs 45.31 crore and PBT Rs 26.55 crore
other_differences.separated_business: Hospitality Q1FY26: revenue Rs 80.43 crore with EBITDA of Rs 25.10 crore, representing 31% of hospitality revenue
other_differences.quote: In Q1FY26, revenue from the hospitality business amounted to Rs 80.43 crores, with an EBITDA of Rs 25.10 crores, representing 31% of hospitality revenue.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Real estate revenue surged 123x to ₹840 Cr from ₹6.79 Cr (Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY25); EBITDA rose 8x to ₹45 Cr from ₹5 Cr
other_differences.separated_business: Hospitality revenue increased by 11% to ₹80 Cr from ₹73 Cr; EBITDA grew by 18% to ₹25 Cr from ₹21 Cr
other_differences.quote: Revenue surged 123x to ₹840 Cr from ₹6.79 Cr.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Real estate recognises revenue only on project completion and issuance of the occupation certificate, so revenue is asymmetrical rather than linear
other_differences.separated_business: Hospitality revenue is operating and recurring — 171-key Hilton Mumbai occupancy 92% and 313-key Grand Hyatt Goa occupancy 81% in Q1FY26
other_differences.quote: Our real estate business recognizes revenue and other profit and loss only upon project completion and the issuance of an occupation certificate by authorities. Consequently, the revenue recognition will be asymmetrical rather than linear, despite project efforts spanning multiple financial years.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Debt-light / asset-light approach to real estate development, capitalising on land acquisition expertise while partnering for construction, branding and working capital
other_differences.separated_business: Asset-heavy, independent hospitality platform with five projects under development, expanding to 3,100 keys and EBITDA currently under ₹200 crore projected to surpass ₹1,200 crore by FY32
other_differences.quote: As an independent, asset-heavy company with marquee partnerships and a strong development pipeline, we are well-positioned to capture the next phase of growth in India's premium and luxury hospitality sector.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Remaining Business — real estate, with differentiated strategy, industry risks, market dynamics, growth trajectory and funding requirements
other_differences.separated_business: Hospitality Business requiring differentiated capital structure, partnerships and management, ready to operate independently as a separate publicly listed entity
other_differences.quote: Each business of the Demerged Company has a differentiated strategy, different industry specific risks and operates inter alia under different market dynamics, growth trajectory, and funding requirements, structure, and timescales.

rationale.rationale: These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement for HDFC Bank, and management never explains one; the question's premise is not supported by the documents supplied. The only business that was partly separated from the Bank is HDB Financial Services Limited (HDBFS), the group's non-deposit-taking NBFC, and that was done by listing it rather than by demerging it: a June 25, 2025 IPO comprising a fresh issue of Rs 2,500.00 crore plus an offer for sale of Rs 10,000.00 crore of the Bank's shares (13,51,35,135 shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740 per share), after which the Bank still held 74.1%. Management gave no reason for the listing at all — no regulatory mandate, no capital need, no valuation argument, no investor or lender demand was cited; Sashidhar Jagdishan only reported that 'we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake' and thanked IPO investors. The only strategic point made about HDBFS was in answer to Pranav Gundlapalle (Jul 2025), who asked about customer conflict between the two entities: management said HDBFS serves a segment 'a notch or two below' the Bank, with 'zero or very minimal overlap' expected to persist, i.e. the two are kept distinct by customer segment and pricing, not separated to fix a problem. Financially the event was treated as a one-off gain — Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated (before tax, net of IPO expenses) — which Srinivasan Vaidyanathan later flagged (Jul 2026) as a base-effect distortion making reported PAT growth 5% versus 9.8% adjusted. Every other corporate action in these texts runs the other way: deepening the 2023 HDFC Limited merger (Apr 2026: e-HDFC home-loan customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA balances up from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 98% of new home loans opening a liability account, 23% carrying active Bank credit cards) and the Apr 16, 2026 board approval to invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in HDFC Life's preferential issue. The closest thing to a forward-looking separation hint is Jagdishan's unprompted remark on surplus capital (Oct 2025): if options arise 'to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so' — unspecified, with no business named.
rationale.evolution: Jul 19, 2025: the HDB Financial Services IPO and the Bank's stake dilution are reported as completed (listed Jul 2, 2025), with no rationale, and management answers only the question of bank-versus-HDBFS customer overlap. Oct 18, 2025: asked by Chintan (Autonomous) what the Bank will do with excess CET1, Jagdishan leaves the door open to unnamed 'other options... to delight shareholders' while stressing capital will be consumed once growth accelerates from FY27. Jan 17, 2026 filings quantify the transaction (Rs 10,000 crore OFS, Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain, 74.1% residual stake); Apr 16, 2026 the Board instead commits up to Rs 1,000 crore of fresh capital to subsidiary HDFC Life. Jul 18, 2026: the HDB gain is referred to only retrospectively, as a prior-year one-timer depressing headline PAT growth to 5% versus 9.8% adjusted — the idea never develops into any separation plan.

points.point: The only partial separation disclosed in any call: HDBFS was listed and the Bank sold down part of its holding, reported as a completed process with no stated rationale.
points.quote: During the quarter, we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake, and which eventually culminated in the stocks being listed on 2nd of July.

points.point: Asked by Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) whether the Bank and HDBFS would end up chasing the same customers, Jagdishan said HDBFS sits a notch or two below the Bank's segment on customer profile and pricing.
points.quote: HDB, we have maintained this. I think the segment that they cater to is about a notch or two below that of HDFC Bank.

points.point: Management framed the two entities as permanently distinct by segmentation rather than as a business being carved out to solve a conflict.
points.quote: There is zero or very minimal overlap at this juncture that will continue to stay for a long period of time.

points.point: On the capital question (CET1 near 20%, draft RWA relief, ECL), Jagdishan said capital will be consumed once FY27 growth exceeds system growth, but left unnamed shareholder-friendly options open — the only forward-looking hint of any corporate action.
points.quote: Having said that, if there are any opportunities that may arise in terms of other options that are available to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so.

points.point: The Jan 17, 2026 filing quantifies the HDBFS sell-down: fresh issue of Rs 2,500 crore plus Rs 10,000 crore offer for sale by the Bank, 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740, producing a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) with the Bank retaining 74.1%.
points.quote: On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to 10,000.00 crore.

points.point: Six weeks before the Apr 2026 call the Board moved in the opposite direction, approving fresh capital into a subsidiary rather than any separation, subject to RBI approval.
points.quote: the Board of Directors of the Bank, at its meeting held today i.e. on April 16, 2026, approved investment of an amount not exceeding Rs. 1,000 crore (Rupees One thousand crore only) in the preferential issue of equity shares to be made by HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited, a subsidiary of the Bank

points.point: Kaizad Bharucha's merger-synergy update shows integration, not separation: e-HDFC mortgage customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 60-65% paying EMIs from in-house accounts, 23% holding active Bank credit cards.
points.quote: Net of attritions, net of acquisitions over this journey, this 36% has come as high as 50% within the last 2.5 years.

points.point: The HDBFS transaction appears only as a prior-year one-timer distorting the growth base, with adjusted PAT growth of 9.8% versus 5% reported — the last mention of it in any call.
points.quote: But last year included certain one-timers like HDB gains and then we had a floating provision counter-cyclical buffer that we added and some contingent provision and so on.

points.point: At the special call on Atanu Chakraborty's resignation, the only structural change hinted at was an internal reorganisation of responsibilities, explicitly not a business separation and with nothing decided.
points.quote: Yes, as I said, as we move forward, we will sort of re-examine our organization structure and with the consent and the advice of the board, we will announce it at the appropriate time.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the one partial carve-out, the HDBFS listing, management claimed no margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit; it cited only a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone one-time gain (later called a base-effect distortion) and segment distinctness — HDBFS one to two notches below the Bank, with minimal customer overlap.
rationale.gaps: Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme exists here. No reason, regulator, lender or investor demand, valuation case, timeline or margin/capital effect for the HDBFS listing is given.

With all humility, we have incorporated most of the feedback, so we are grateful for that. Thank you for that. I may have mentioned in the past, maybe in the last investor conference that I came on, it's important to reiterate that this is a completely new organization. The merger with a nonbank financial entity, the eHDFC Limited and the bank has landed a certain set of day one financials, and so there is a new starting point across all metri cs. This is a new organization. So it will be -- we have to, not only you but even us, we have to desist from having any comparisons vis -a-vis the stand -alone financ ials of either the bank or even the erstwhile HDFC Limited. We are now 9 months into the merger. […] There's a competitive environment that is there. That's a reality. We have done that and probably as we go along, and that will be reflected in some of the financial metrics of the organization. The key to t his sustainable momentum is our enhanced customer engagements and elevated service -first culture. We are not saying that after 30 years, obviously, there's a reason why we have reached this kind of excellence in this deposit mobilization franchise, but we have realized that if you have to be even better, the only way is to elevate the customer service -first culture and we have a lot of measurement and monitoring mechanism in place internally for that. So the intensity of the same is going to be heightened and that's what we're driving and that's somewhere reflected even in this tighter environment that we have seen.

So thank you, Pranav. The fact is that I cannot sort of predict how the competition is going to behave. All I can tell you is we have sufficient history, which suggests that the price -based competition or price -based strategy is not a sustainable strategy, and it's only a short -term strategy at the most. We have seen it in the mid of 2000s on a certain asset product. We see -- we have seen it in multiple products over the years, a nd we have a rich experience to that effect. Frankly, as I said over the last months, we have been witness to this. We have actually experienced rather intensely , the competitive environment, which also borders on some amount of, what should I say, heighte ned rate wars on the liability side because liquidity was tight and probably there were a lot of other compulsions for other competitive players, which force d them to sort of price their deposits higher. But I mean since the most infamous quarter three , where all of you have probably done a lot of research, frankly, Q3 was actually a classical quarter where we chose or elected not to do so.
