rationale.rationale: Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.
rationale.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

points.point: Asked outright about demerging Care and the other subsidiaries from the holdco and about removing the holdco discount, Pratul Gupta said nothing was decided — the board was weighing options and wanted to strengthen the businesses first, after the INR1,500 crore raise, before any capital-market action.
points.quote: On the second question about how the structure will look like in some future time, what I can very clearly assure you is that the management and the Board is evaluating various options which can add value to the shareholders.

points.point: Investors were already framing the choice as Care IPO versus demerger; Dixit Doshi asked it explicitly alongside questions on NBFC yields, showing the separation idea originated with shareholders rather than management.
points.quote: And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can just touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?

points.point: Gupta presented the demerger as a strategic imperative rather than a housekeeping exercise, announced two days after the REL and RFL boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026.
points.quote: It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long -term growth.

points.point: The trigger was three converging conditions — the Burman takeover as promoters, the INR1,500 crore warrant raise covering funding needs for the foreseeable future, and the businesses reaching a scale that demands specialised focus.
points.quote: Each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories.

points.point: Mechanics: lending, broking and ancillary support services move from REL to RFL on a going-concern basis, the Care stake stays in REL, RFL issues one share per REL share and then lists, with a 15–18 month process ending in Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars.
points.quote: The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.

points.point: Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value.
points.quote: I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?

points.point: Gupta positioned this as stage one of a longer restructuring, with a Care reverse merger possible later once unspecified milestones and minimum-shareholding thresholds are met.
points.quote: Well, I think this is -- as I mentioned, this is the first step in that direction.

points.point: The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law.
points.quote: So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.

points.point: Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation.
points.quote: This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.

points.point: Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: Pressed by Vikas Srivastava on whether the scheme could be amended to fold Care in once the promoters reach 26%, Lamba ruled out amending it but left a subsequent scheme open.
points.quote: No, I'll answer your last question first. We don't want to amend the scheme.

points.point: Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted.
points.quote: Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well

points.point: The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding.
points.quote: Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .

points.point: The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.

points.point: Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities.
points.quote: The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28.
points.quote: Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.

points.point: SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them.
points.quote: Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator.
points.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .

rationale.what_management_expects: REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.
rationale.gaps: No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Insurance segment reported a loss of approximately ₹46.8 crore at PBT level for FY26 (segment revenue ₹7,969 crore); Care's combined ratio under Ind AS improved 120 bps to 101.4%
other_differences.separated_business: Financial Services segment reported PBT of ₹152.3 crore for FY26 on segment revenue of about ₹537 crore
other_differences.quote: The profitability for the insurance segment is at INR41 crores for the last quarter, while it reported a loss of approximately INR46.8 crores at PBT level for FY26. For the Financial Services segment, PBT of INR127.5 crores was reported for the last quarter and INR152.3 crores on the annual basis.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Health insurance GWP up 24% YoY to ₹11,417 crore in FY26; retail market share up from 18.8% to 19.7% in SAHI; expected growth "anything between 18% to 24%"
other_differences.separated_business: Broking operating income down 2% to ₹373.4 crore in FY26 with PBT down 31%; RFL core SME book down to about ₹60 crore; RHDFCL AUM down to ₹243 crore from ₹250 crore
other_differences.quote: Consolidated Revenue grew 14.7% YoY to ₹8,493.84 crore in FY26 led by the health insurance business

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: REL repaid its ₹75 crore loan and "REL today is debt free"; Care raised sub debt of ₹100 crore in FY26 and runs investment leverage of 4.07x
other_differences.separated_business: RFL is debt-free with no subsisting default, no cumulative ALM mismatches, CRAR 261.9% and NOF ₹821 crore; RHDFCL managed gearing 0.3 times with 130% CRAR
other_differences.quote: Debt-free; strong liquidity profile with cash balance, including liquid investment of ~₹591 crore as of 31st March 2026

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Capital raise of ₹1,500 crore via convertible warrants at REL, of which ₹600 crore earmarked for Care (₹256 crore infused in September '25)
other_differences.separated_business: RFL holds cash including liquid investments of over ₹591 crore, entirely unlevered; ₹250 crore earmarked for RHDFCL and ₹200 crore for broking
other_differences.quote: RFL reported a profit of INR89 crores in quarter 4 on account of improved recoveries and has a cash balance including liquid investments of over INR591 crores currently.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Care: "Return on equity based on profit before tax increased to 19.9% from 17.7% in the previous year"; mid-teens ROE for the fourth consecutive financial year
other_differences.separated_business: Broking ROE in single digits (6%-7%) with no pathway number worked out; RHDFCL PAT and RoMA of Rs. -18.4 crore and -6.7% in FY2026
other_differences.quote: So basically, we are having 6%, 7% ROE, right? So I wanted to understand, is there a pathway and how quickly can we go to a normal ROE for a broker, which is in the vicinity of 25%, 30%?

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: ₹600 crore of the ₹1,500 crore warrant proceeds allocated to Care Health Insurance to support solvency and business growth
other_differences.separated_business: ₹250 crore to housing finance, ₹200 crore to broking, ₹375 crore general corporate purpose; RFL needs no capital infusion; IT platforms being refurbished across RFL, RBL and RHDFCL
other_differences.quote: Out of the INR1,500 crores, INR600 crores is going to Care, INR250 crores is going to the housing finance company, INR200 crores is going to the broking entity. And there's about INR375-odd crores, which is a general corporate purpose fund, which can be allocated depends on the need of these businesses.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Scheme framed to comply with Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act; details of accounting method to be certified by the Statutory Auditor per SEBI comments
other_differences.separated_business: Scheme framed to comply with Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act
other_differences.quote: in compliance with the provisions of the SEBI Scheme Circular – Equity (as defined in the Scheme) and the Income Tax Act (as defined in the Scheme), including Section 2(19AA) thereof.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: REL continues to be barred from declaring dividends as per RBI letter issued in December, 2019; REL retains a single asset (Care) with a stated holding-company discount concern
other_differences.separated_business: RFL's RBI Corrective Action Plan and the banks' fraud classification have been removed; the NBFC business is set to restart operations
other_differences.quote: Strengthened balance sheet with net worth of ₹898.8 crore and 261.9% CRAR as of 31st March 2026 following RBI's removal of the Corrective Action Plan (CAP) restrictions and withdrawal of fraud classification by banks

entities.name: Religare Enterprises Limited
entities.scheme: 2026 demerger of the financial services business of Religare Enterprises Limited into Religare Finvest Limited
entities.business: Retains the Remaining Business: the insurance business, comprising its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited; becomes a pure play health insurance holding company
entities.swap_ratio: not stated
entities.listing: listed on BSE and NSE (date not stated)
entities.turnover: Consolidated Revenue grew 14.7% YoY to ₹8,493.84 crore in FY26 (₹7,405.47 crore in FY25)
entities.net_worth_or_assets: Other Equity (Excluding Revaluation Reserve) as per Audited Balance Sheet as at March 31, 2024: Rs. 179,344.32 lakhs standalone and Rs. 201,342.00 lakhs consolidated
entities.who_runs_it: Mr. Arjun Lamba, Executive Director, REL (earlier Dr. Rashmi Saluja, Executive Chairperson); Mr. Pratul Gupta, Chief Financial Officer
entities.quote: Under the proposed scheme of arrangement, REL will retain its stake in Care Health Insurance Limited (CHIL) which will continue as an insurance-focused entity.

entities.name: Religare Finvest Limited
entities.scheme: 2026 demerger of the financial services business of Religare Enterprises Limited into Religare Finvest Limited
entities.business: All businesses pertaining to the financial services business activities including lending activities, broking activities, investment activities and ancillary and support services, on a going concern basis
entities.swap_ratio: "1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 10/- each of the Resulting Company ("Resulting Company New Equity Shares"), credited as fully paid-up, for every 1 equity share of INR 10/- each of the Demerged Company"
entities.turnover: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31 March, 2025 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis
entities.net_worth_or_assets: not stated for the Demerged Undertaking; RFL itself reported net worth of ₹898.8 crore and 261.9% CRAR as of 31st March 2026
entities.who_runs_it: Mr. Karthik Srinivasan, Chief Executive Officer of Religare Finvest Limited (also referred to as Mr. Srinivasan Karthik); Mr. Prakash Jejani, Chief Financial Officer
entities.quote: The Financial services business comprising lending activities, broking activities, investment activities and ancillary and support services will be transferred to RFL on a going concern basis.

entities.name: Religare Broking Limited
entities.scheme: 2026 demerger (moves to Religare Finvest Limited as its direct subsidiary); also transferor company in the 2022 scheme of arrangement transferring its E-Governance Undertaking to Religare Digital Solutions Limited
entities.business: Retail-focused broking: equity, derivatives, commodity, depository, insurance and investment product distribution; e-governance services through its subsidiary
entities.swap_ratio: not stated
entities.turnover: Operating income of ₹373.4 crore in FY26 (₹382 crore in FY25); ₹99 crore for Q4 FY26
entities.net_worth_or_assets: Net worth increased by 6% from INR354 crores to INR376 crores (FY26)
entities.who_runs_it: Mr. Vijay Kumar Goel, Managing Director of Religare Broking Limited
entities.quote: On financial services side, while the promoters and public shall continue to hold shares in the ratio as mentioned, the resulting entity RFL shall have Religare Broking as its direct subsidiary.

entities.name: Religare Digital Solutions Limited
entities.scheme: 2022 scheme of arrangement between Religare Broking Limited and Religare Digital Solutions Limited (transfer of the E-Governance Undertaking on a slump sale basis)
entities.status: effective (NCLT order dated June 13, 2025, with effect from the Appointed Date, i.e., April 1, 2022)
entities.business: Receives the E-Governance Undertaking of Religare Broking Limited: e-governance services through a digital platform supported by a nationwide agent network
entities.swap_ratio: not stated (transfer as a going concern on "slump sale" basis; no shares issued to REL's shareholders)
entities.turnover: E-Governance segment revenue (consolidated) of ₹3,965.96 lakhs for the nine months ended December 31, 2024 and ₹4,518.52 lakhs for the year ended March 31, 2024
entities.quote: In this regard, we would like to inform that Hon'ble NCLT, New Delhi, vide Order dated June 13, 2025 received by the Company on July 10, 2025, approved the Scheme between RBL and RDSL, with effect from the Appointed Date, i.e., April 1, 2022.

Thank you, Rahul. Now that we have discussed the quarter gone by, let me get to the other part where we will discuss about reorganization of Religare and demerger of its financial services business. On 14th Feb 2026 this year, the Boards of Religare Enterp rises Limited and Religare Finvest Limited have approved the demerger of financial services and insurance businesses of the group into two focused and independent listed entities. This is not just a structural or reorganization. It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long - term growth. Let me explain the rationale a bit in detail. […] As you see, the promoter group on a fully diluted basis after the conversion of recently issued warrants shall hold 29 .75% in REL, whereas the public continues to hold -- will continue to hold the remaining 70.25%. And as mentioned earlier, we have Care on one side as the insurance segment, and we have NBFCs, RFL and housing, one below the other and broking as Financial S ervices segment. Just to remind, as far as REL is concerned, its stock is listed on BSE and NSE, whereas RFL is an unlisted entity, and it is registered with RBI as a middle layer category, NBFC. Now if you see Slide 37, this demerger is built on 4 pillars. First, streamlined business focus and simplified structure. The segregation of financial services from insurance business is to create a focused entity with specific business model, growth strategy, capital deployment and performance metrics for t he teams. Secondly, unlocking shareholder value through a separate listing. The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation. It will facilitate targeted capital raising for this business and enable more efficient allocation of management resources, thereby supporting sustainable growth and long -term value creation by this newly created company. Third, the focused management attention and talent alignment. Post demerger, each entity will have dedica ted leadership teams. The leadership teams are already in the hiring mode. They'll require sharper operational alignment and clearer strategic mandates. Decision -making has to become faster. […] So with these objectives in mind, there was a need to bring in this clarity. This will also help us set up the objectives for the new incumbents as we hire the senior leadership for different components of the business. Both enhance r isk management and compliance. The demerger enables implementation of spec ific risk management policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to each business segment. This improves monitoring and control of risk associated with them. Now moving to Slide 38. Let me just outline the proposed structure more clearly. This is demerger of Financial Services business from REL to RFL pursuant to proposed scheme of arrangement. The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL. As a consideration for transfer of financial services business, RFL will issue fully paid -up equity shares to the shareholders of REL in a 1:1 ratio. […] As mentioned earlier, we aim to list RFL in the first quarter of FY 2028 after the completion of the process. For the remaining, REL is as it exists today. The listed entity shall continue to hold its entire stake in Care Health Insurance as it do es today. This demerger will be implemented through a scheme of arrangement under sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act 2013 and other relevant provisions of the act read in conjunction with them. The scheme shall also require various regulatory approv als as well as shareholders' and creditors' approval. The company expects the entire process to take 15 to 18 months starting from the current quarter and shall culminate in the first quarter of FY ‘28. The detailed timelines can be referred to in slide 40, which is there before you, with various steps being appended alongside. We believe that during this period there will be no disruption to operations, no impact on customers and no change to employ ee continuity. We are committed to ensuring a seamless transition with complete operational continuity. Just to reiterate, post demerger, each business will have a clarity and focus to pursue its own growth path. This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors. The Board concluded that this particular initiative and option represents the most efficient and future -ready structure for our next phase of growth. Any future fundraisi ng as and when required will be undertaken based on business growth plans, capital requirements and strategic opportunities and will be subject to necessary corporate and regulatory approvals. Just to summarize, we are creating a simplified structure with independent business segments concentrating on their core competencies. We are unlocking shareholder value through separate listing that enhances investor participation and enables targeted growth. We are enabling better management alignment with sector -specific talent acquisition and performance -linked rewards. We are implementing enhanced risk management with tailored compliance frameworks and strengthened governance. And last but not the least, we are executing this transformation backed by a very stro ng commitment from the Board and the promoter group.

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.
rationale.evolution: These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.

points.point: The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India.
points.quote: The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.

points.point: MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering.
points.quote: As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.

points.point: Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals.
points.quote: During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".

points.point: The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.

points.point: Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative.
points.quote: I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.

points.point: The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%.
points.quote: Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.

points.point: A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth.
points.quote: The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.

points.point: Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts.
points.quote: We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.

points.point: The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

points.point: Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim.
points.quote: So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.

points.point: Q1 FY27 (12 August 2026) validates the focused-entity framing: revenue INR 9,707.7 million, up 18.3% YoY, PBT INR 869.2 million at 9.0%, with growth in Wind, General Machinery and Agriculture (Tractors) despite currency and residual demerger costs.
points.quote: In our 3rd quarter as a focused, independent business, SKF India (Industrial) delivered 18.3% year-on-year Sales growth, while maintaining a healthy 9% PBT (in spite of headwinds from currency and demerger-related expenses).

rationale.what_management_expects: For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.
rationale.gaps: No pre-demerger call rationale; no named requester (investors, lenders, partners); no synergy loss, standalone-cost, tax or valuation quantification; nothing on the automotive entity's economics or arm's-length agreement terms.

turns: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. With us, we have SKF India Industrial’s Managing Director, Mr. Mukund Vasudevan, and our CFO, Mr. Ashish Saraf. The purpose of today's call is to share our Q4 results and our overall financial year's performance. Please note that financial information from 17th December 2024 to 31st March 2025 and from 1st April 2025 to 30th September 2025 as reported in the presentation shared has been extracted and may involve some assumptions by the management from the financial information of SKF India Limited pertaining to the demerged industrial undertaking. These are prepared in accordance with the Appendix C of Ind AS 103 Business Combinations by using the financial information maintained by the SKF India Limited demerged company. Before I turn over the call to the management, I would like to remind you that in this call, some of the remarks contain forward -looking statements which are subject to risk and uncertainties and actual results may differ materially. Such statements are based on management beliefs as well as assumptions made by and on the information currently available to the management. The audience is cautioned not to place any undue reliance on these forward -looking statements and making any investment decision. The purpose of today's call is to purely educate and bring awareness about the company's fundamental business and the financial quarter under review. Let me now turn over the call to Mr. Mukund Vasudevan. Over to you.

We had a sales growth of 9.8% with INR 9.5 billion of sales. We had a 1,731 basis points improvement in our profit before tax, that's at 9.5%. Caveat on that, which is the two bullets you can see at the bottom. Due to the demerger, there were some one -time expenses both in the previous quarter and in this quarter. If we remove that, remove the impact of that, this quarter we delivered a margin of 11.5% -- or profit before tax of 11.5%. Again, solid performance given all the changes which were going on in the demerger. And then in net working capital also, we came in strong, reduced our net working capital by 2.8% quarter -on-quarter and delivered 18.7% of sales net working capital. The one -time charges which happened in the previous quarter and in this quarter included, in the previous quarter, it included some IT -related costs related to the demerger, professional services, and a large stamp duty which was paid related to the land transfer from SKF India to SKF India (Industrial ) Limited. That was a total of around INR1.8 billion in the last quarter. In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million. These are all explained in detail in our detailed financials. But overall, very solid performance, proud to say that we had good growth and a solid margin improvement quarter - on-quarter . If I now go on to the economy update and I'll take you to the page titled macro update. […] If I move to the next slide, Slide 10, which is an analysis on margin. As you can see, if you look at, if you compare quarter -on-quarter , year-on-year comparison is not as advisable just because those involved some extractions from SKF India and some assumptions. But if you look at quarter -on-quarter , big jump from negative 7.8% to positive 9.5%. But that involved some demerger expenses both in the previous quarter and this quarter. And so, if you remove both of them, then the previous quarter, that is Q3 '26, would have been 13.1% and the current quarter would have been 11.5%. So that's the difference. alkFalkF SKF India (Industrial) Limited May 13, 202 6 If you ask what specifically caused the decline in margin from 13.1% to 11.5% if you remove the one -off demerger expenses, the biggest reason was the mix change. Our OEM business grew significantly and as a result, the mix of lower margin OEM business compared to higher margin distribution business accounted for most of this drop. Again, we expect that to normalize over the next few quarters. The other reason was a higher employee cost. […] But this quarter, we have seen a significant jump in the cash flow, partly due to the net working capital reduction as well as some t ax adjustments which were made. And then there were other exceptional items -- other items, which include interest incomes and some other current assets and liabilities which accounte d for a higher cash flow in Q4. I'll now move on to discuss our strategy and some success stories which tie well with our strategy. I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial ) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and mak e our business more profitable. We call o ur strategy , the ACES strategy , and our strategy is defined through to 2028. And what we are trying to do here is each one of these ACES has multiple initiatives below it, but I'm highlighting some of the critical ones. The first one is to accelerate localization, which means both we will manufacture more in India for India, but also drive the work with our supplier base to make sure that we get more components also coming from India rather than imported.

Got it. Thank you for this, sir. Sir, just on the question part, just if you can help us understand how is the RM cost inflation happening, sir, and how much price hikes w e have taken from the OEM and distribution level? And also, I mean, the going ahead, sir, with the capacity additions and demerger transition impact, just how do you see the margin, sir, going ahead?

Let me try, let me answer that to the extent possible and then Ashish can add on. Let me answer your second question first, which is on how do we see the margins going ahead. So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%. So, most of those demerger expenses will be done. We will also have some the mix, which we believe OEM is higher right now, we believe the distributor business will come back and the mix will normalize a bit more. So that will also account for some of the growth back to around 13 %. Over the next few years, which is '28 -'29 and '29 -'30, we are looking at more localization, so more production in India for India. We are looking at operational efficiencies as we are looking at how do we build a more local supplier base of our components, but also how do we manufacture, like we showed in the example, how do we manufacture more with less with less cost of manufacturing as well as more less manpower. How do we do that? And then finally, we see more drop down or leverage from our sales on the top from the top line with less S&A involved, Sales and Administration involved. So , all that we think will get us by around by '29 -'30, we believe we should be getting back to the 15 % range. That's the goal. But those kind of are subject to, of course, market conditions. But that's our goal. But near term, we expect to get back to where we were around 13 % after the demerger costs are over. In terms of cost escalations, this is very broad numbers right now. There are two things which have hurt us because which are challenges, but we are passing on price increases. One is the bigger one actually is FX. So , anything we are importing, right, and selling, there is an FX impact with the rupee depreciating. alkFalkF SKF India (Industrial) Limited May 13, 202 6 The second is around escalating costs. The escalating costs we are projecting around 3% to 4% right now, but that is still variable, right? And that involves some assumptions what we are seeing in oil prices right now, but it also involves some assumptions in steel prices going up. We are expecting to pass on most of it through price increases, some both the FX impact as well as the cost escalations. Obviously, with OEMs, it might be it's a little tougher, those are tougher negotiations. We are hoping to pass on most of it. With distributors, we will probably pass on a larger chunk. So that's our overall assessment right now.

Yes. And just to add, I think additionally to what Mumuksh said, we have already undertaken actions as we kind of started this quarter, especially with the distribution business, we have taken some pricing actions already in the market given the cost escalation that we are seeing both on the side of FX as well as raw material. Even with the OEMs, we are actively approaching them to get an appropriate price escalation to offset the additional cost.
Thank you. Thank you, sir, for the answer, sir. I'll come back to the queue, sir. Mod erator: Thank you. We will take our next question from the line of Viraj from SiMPL . Please go ahead.

Yes, hi. Thanks for the opportunity. Just two questions. See, if you look at in quarter 4, while we said that the mix is adverse, our gross margin even Q -on-Q has not seen that kind of a moderation. But actually, even if you adjust for the demerger expense of INR 18 crore s, the jump in other expenses is pretty sharp for us. So just trying to understand, you know, if you can quantify the major line items, you know, which is driving this. And the second part to this question is, see, before the demerger also, you know, in earlier press releases , we used to share the kind of margins industrial used to do. And even with the localization it had at that point in time, the business used to do 13 % to 15 % comfortably. Now with localization which you are targeting to increase, you know, with operational efficiency, ideally one would think that the blended margins for the industrial business would be close to say 16 % to 18 %, you know, by '28 -'29. So , I'm just trying to understand where is that disconnect or the gap coming to you from?

Yes. So, I will answer the second question from my side and then Ashish can answer the first question since I don't have all the details around other expenses. But so, on the second question, one of the reasons for the drag is additional investments which we are making in as we have announced earlier in Pune. These additional investments, including a new plant as we are running out of capacity, is going to add to our expense. So, I would say that is one. The second is we are under, you know, it is a competitive environment and we do face lots of competition. So, while as the especially at the OEMs, I think the competition is intense. Our railway mix has gone up, that has also brought down our margin a little bit. But we see this all recovering, but not before conservatively speaking, not before '29 -'30. So, our aspiration is to get to 16 % to 18 %, but right now up to 2030, both due to slightly higher OEM mix and a little higher depreciation charges, we see this, we have been alkFalkF SKF India (Industrial) Limited May 13, 202 6 conservative here in saying we are going to get to around 15 %. More increase is possible, but we can't commit to it right now.

Yes. Just to elaborate on other expenses, the big components of other expense cost was one was around royalty and trademark. We had we had to pay a royalty and trademark on our sales, on our higher sales to our group company. So that increased by around INR 60-odd million. Apart from that, there were other manufacturing -related costs, which was predominantly around repairs and maintenance, around power and fuel, and stores and spares, which had increased in this quarter compared to previous quarter. And over and above that, we have basically availing some services, manufacturing services from our group company SKF India, on which we have to pay or reimburse a small transfer pricing margin which we basically booked in this quarter. So that kind of led to an increase in the in the overall other expense.

Okay, sir. Just two parts on the first second part again. See, if you look at our white spaces, you know, in the past also, we have kind of vacated some segments in distribution either due to accessibility, affordability, or even in terms of wind, you know, where we have exited certain low margin, low profitability threshold segments for us. Now with localization coming through and you're still guiding a 15 % margin, I'm talking about the EBITDA level, you know, because the comes after that. So , you know, is would it be right to think that the focus would be more on achieving a much more higher rate of growth while margins may be, you know, around what we are saying in the interim? Would that be a right thing to, you know, look at? So that is one. And second is on the Capex, is there any I mean, if you can just confirm the timeline by which we expect it to commission?

Yes. So, you're partially right. Our goal or our strategy is growth while maintaining margin, right? So, if you remove the one -offs, we want to maintain margin, we want to get it back to around 15 %, that's what I mean by maintain, right? But we see a much higher potential for growth. The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we ar e now getting back into it. We did exit some railway business, especially around freight, now we are getting back into it, etcetera , right? So, there are many areas, even the agricultural tractor business, some of it was we exited and now we are getting back into it due to localization. So, we are winning more share, but if you compare it to it comes at the cost of some amount of margin. Our OEM business margin in general is lower, right? So, you can see that. But we don't expect that to kind of sustain, that low margin, that relatively lower margin. We will work both with operational efficiency as well as on pricing to t ry and get back to at least 15 %.
On capex sir? alkFalkF SKF India (Industrial) Limited May 13, 202 6

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business that grew up inside Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly-owned Global Capability Centre, covering life-sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, drug safety and technology-enabled operational services delivered by 400+ subject-matter experts. Management's account is that this began as a captive serving Strides — its FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million explicitly 'including revenues for services rendered to Strides', with EBITDA of ₹169 million, 3% of Strides' turnover and ~1% of consolidated net worth — but that 'as demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers', which it could not remain inside a generics manufacturer's subsidiary. The filings name four specific problems the carve-out solves: supporting the next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — so the vehicle was created first (Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, appointed date April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18, 2026, effective June 1, 2026, making Pivot Path a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides) and only then sold down. The sale values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m post-money: Strides divests a majority for ~₹1,000m (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), Ascent Growth Trust and co-investor Vintage Classic Limited take 65.05%, a 15% ESOP pool is carved for the team, Ascent infuses ₹500m of primary capital, Strides keeps 19.95% and reclassifies Pivot Path as an Associate. Strides frames this as a repeatable playbook rather than a distress exit — 'creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth' — and says it 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet and provides growth capital for Pivot Path', consistent with the three FY26 priorities Badree repeated on the calls (geographic diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength, with net debt at ₹1,437 crores and net debt/EBITDA 1.55x). The stated precedent is the Softgel/OneSource demerger, which Arun Kumar justified in exactly valuation terms — the softgel business was 'adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation' until its 'true value' was discovered through OneSource, with ₹78.8 billion distributed to shareholders. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the Pivot Path separation; pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is stated not to be a related-party transaction.
rationale.evolution: On none of the eight calls (Oct 2024 through May 2026) did management ever mention Pivot Path, Arco Lab's Life Sciences/Digital Innovation business or this Scheme; the only separation discussed was the Softgel-to-OneSource demerger (Oct 2024, Feb 2025, Aug 2025 calls), which established the 'unlock true value outside the generic space' template, and Arco Lab appeared only once, in May 2025, as the wholly-owned subsidiary parked with the retained 1.6% OneSource stake 'for a rainy day'. The Pivot Path track runs entirely through filings: the Scheme was intimated on May 15, 2025 with an appointed date of April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approved it on May 18, 2026 (the very day of the Q4 FY26 earnings call, which made no reference to it), the order reached the portal May 20 and the certified copy May 25, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Twenty-six days later, on June 27, 2026, the Board approved the majority-stake sale to the Ascent Capital consortium plus ₹500m primary infusion, with definitive agreements to be executed before June 30 and the share sale to complete by June 30, 2026 and the infusion by July 31, 2026. So the plan visibly changed shape only once: from an internal reorganisation creating a wholly-owned subsidiary into a control sale leaving Strides a 19.95% associate holder.

points.point: The separated unit is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path Private Limited under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013; on effectiveness Pivot Path became a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides, with the undertaking vesting from the appointed date of April 10, 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).

points.point: The stated reason for the carve-out is four-fold and explicit: next-phase growth, serving global customers, building agentic-AI platforms, and access to external capital — i.e. things the business could not do while embedded in Strides' Global Capability Centre.
points.quote: To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.

points.point: The origin story management gives: a captive capability centre function (life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, technology-enabled operational services) that outgrew its captive role as third-party pharma demand arrived.
points.quote: As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.

points.point: Size and profitability disclosed for the carved-out business for FY26 — and the admission that its revenue still includes intra-group work for Strides, which is why standalone turnover contribution is shown as Nil and consolidated contribution as only 3% of Strides' turnover and 1% of net worth.
points.quote: For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.

points.point: The deal terms: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m to Strides (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), ₹500m primary into the company, and a resultant cap table of Strides 19.95% / investors 65.05% / ESOP pool 15%, with Pivot Path becoming an Associate.
points.quote: The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.

points.point: The corporate-strategy framing: a repeatable incubate-scale-monetise model in which Strides keeps a minority economic interest, with balance-sheet strengthening named as a direct benefit to the parent.
points.quote: The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.

points.point: Badree's stated timing logic: the business needs a partner with capital and expertise that Strides itself does not bring, and the separation is what lets Pivot Path scale independently while Strides still participates.
points.quote: As the business enters its next phase, we believe this is the right time to bring in a strategic investment partner with the expertise and capital to accelerate its growth.

points.point: The buyer's rationale is that independence itself is the enabler — combining technology and agentic AI with 400+ subject-matter experts for compliance, digital transformation and drug safety work for global customers.
points.quote: As an Independent entity, Pivot Path is exceptionally well positioned to combine the power of technology and Agentic-AI with its 400+ subject matter experts in building purpose-built solutions that enable global customers to manage their compliance, digital transformation, and drug safety requirements with greater speed, precision, cost effectiveness and confidence.

points.point: Governance framing: pricing rests on an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation, the buyers (Ascent Growth Trust and BVI-incorporated Vintage Classic Limited) are not promoter/promoter-group/group companies, and the transaction is declared not a related-party transaction and outside Regulation 37A.
points.quote: The transaction has been undertaken based on an independent valuation conducted by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, reflecting the strength of Pivot Path's differentiated capabilities, established customer relationships and long-term growth potential.

points.point: The template for this separation — never applied to Pivot Path on any call, but stated for the Softgel/OneSource demerger: a niche business trapped inside the generics platform was being valued suboptimally, so carving it out revealed its true value.
points.quote: And discussing its true value, while it was adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation, we discovered its true value of a niche business through OneSource.

points.point: Management quantifies the prior unlock as the proof of its shareholder-value method — ₹78.8 billion distributed via demerger and listing — framing further separations as shareholder-value actions rather than disposals.
points.quote: And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.

points.point: The only call reference to Arco Lab, the entity Pivot Path was carved out of: it is described merely as the wholly-owned subsidiary holding the retained OneSource stake, with no hint that a services business inside it was being prepared for separation.
points.quote: So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.

points.point: On the Q4 FY26 call held the same day NCLT approved the Scheme, management restated the three priorities the Pivot Path monetisation serves (diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength — net debt ₹1,437 crores, 1.55x) but said nothing about the demerger or any intent to sell the business.
points.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.

points.point: Sequencing confirms a two-step design: the Scheme was made effective on June 1, 2026 after the certified NCLT order was filed with the RoC, and the stake sale was approved just 26 days later on June 27, 2026.
points.quote: Further, pursuant to filing of the certified true copy of the Order with the Registrar of Companies by the participating entities, namely Arco Lab and Pivot Path, the Scheme of Demerger has become effective from June 1, 2026.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, independence to serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, scale with a 15% ESOP pool for 400+ experts, and access external capital. Strides: ~₹1,000m cash (₹750m now, ₹250m deferred), a strengthened balance sheet, Associate accounting, continued ~19.95% participation in the upside, and sharper focus on its pharma core.
rationale.gaps: Calls never mentioned Pivot Path, Arco Lab's carve-out or the Scheme; no stated investor, lender or partner request; no margin, valuation-gap or post-deal related-party pricing explanation.

deal.size_statement: Delivering Strides' shareholders an embedded value of INR 663 per share for Strides' holding in OneSource, representing a ~82% premium over the previous embedded value of INR 364 per share as per the Scheme of Arrangement announced earlier in September'23. | "The transaction will unlock ~INR 61,000 mn (~USD 725 mn) of value for Strides' shareholders." | For Pivot Path: "Turnover ... Rs. 1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) (Contributes 3% to Strides Turnover)" and "Networth Rs. 100 million (Contributes ~0.3% to Strides Networth) ... Rs. 360 million (Contributes 1% to Strides Networth)"
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated as a percentage; the voting results of the NCLT-convened meeting of equity shareholders held on 10-09-2024 show "Promoter and Promoter Group 2,37,67,542" shares out of a grand total of 9,19,58,214 shares
deal.promoter_holding_after: Not stated for the 2024 OneSource demerger (shareholders of Strides receive OneSource shares in the 1:2 entitlement ratio, i.e. mirror entitlement, but no promoter percentage is given). For the 2025 Arco Lab–Pivot Path demerger: "Pivot Path shall become a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides." After the 2026 stake sale the documents state the holding of Strides, not of the promoters: "Resultant Capital Structure of Pivot Path — Strides' at 19.95%; Investors at 65.05%; ESOP Pool at 15%"
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2023/2024 OneSource scheme: "In line with the Share Entitlement Ratio, OneSource has allotted One Equity Share of Re. 1/- each of OneSource for every Two Equity Shares of Rs. 10/- held by Strides' shareholders." Fractional entitlements "shall be consolidated and held in trust by 'Catalyst Trusteeship Limited' on behalf of shareholders entitled to such fractional entitlements", to be sold within 90 days and the net proceeds distributed. 2025 Arco Lab–Pivot Path scheme: nothing goes to public shareholders of Strides — "Pursuant to demerger, Arco Lab's Investment in Pivot Path shall stand cancelled and Shareholders of Arco Lab (i.e., Strides) shall receive Equity Shares of Pivot Path as per the exchange ratio of 1:1 as a consideration for Demerger."
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of existing grants is not stated. For Pivot Path after the 2026 transaction: "Resultant Capital Structure of Pivot Path — Strides' at 19.95%; Investors at 65.05%; ESOP Pool at 15%". No exercise price or pricing date and no management or insider shareholding is stated.
deal.insider_actions: not stated

turns: And again, the one -offs in Strides with all the work that we are done with network optim ization is complete. A loss picked up from our JV as we guided in Stelis from our associate company, Stelis from H2 will be very negligible. The business in H2 will be EBITDA positive. We continue to add significant new contracts in our CDMO business in OneSource and we expect to close to Syngene transaction as guided in this quarter. Consequently, our targeted debt reduction of about 700 crores between the two companies will fall in place but will also release a significant amount of corporate guarantees of Strides. So, in all, we are very close to achieving everything that we committed to would be our focus and I think we got the company back to a stage of continued growth. You would see significant upsides in terms of new product launches. […] Overall, a good result and we will continue to grow from here. Our focus obviously now is the conversion from EBITDA to free cash and to ensure that the PAT percentages increase, considering the one -offs are all sorted or solved for. That’s the general overview of the quarter. We are excited about t he prospects for the second half, and we continue to be very excited about OneSource that we announced recently. And we Strides Pharma Science Limited October 30, 2023 believe that there will be significant value accretion for all our stakeholders in the coming days. Thank you for your patience, and both Badree and I are very happy to take any questions that you may all have.

My first set of questions is on our GLP -1 portfolio. Sir, in the last call, you mentioned that we had made some solid investments in devices and are a leading drug device player globally. I would like you to elaborate more on this part. Are we saying that we have started manufacturing these self -injection drug delivery systems also, which is r equired for GLP -1?

The GLP -1 is part of Stelis which is an associate company of Strides. We currently have about 15 customers and we partner with several companies worldwide and we have filed all the weight loss and diabetic drugs which are in drug device formats and a lot of other programs too. So, to Strides Pharma Science Limited October 30, 2023 answer your question, we are in a very strong position. But the patterns for this start going off partially in FY25 and the main patterns get off only in 2030. So, commercial supplies will not start quickly. But having said that, we do get a lot of R&D income and we do hold a very large order book for our contract manufacturing opportunities led by GLP in OneSource which in a company that we just announced is a carve-out in the last quarter. Aman V ij: The clarification was left on the comment of leading drug device manufacturer globally. You are saying we have started manufacturing the devices – the drug delivery system self injections – in the subsidiary, OneSource?

Yes, what I am saying is that we have already started manufacturing products for several customers who have made their filings with the regulators, and once their products get approved and when the pattern regime opens up, we would start commercial production. At this time, t heir development and filing batches that we have done for companies.

My question is regarding the other regulated markets ’ performance which has been quite strong. And we had mentioned in our other regulated markets slides in the investor presentation that we have a strong funnel for the European B2B partnerships under the SynergICE to drive growth. Can you please put a little bit of light on this?

SynergIC E is the name of our B2B platform. It ’s a platform that sells capabilities for both OneSource and for Strides under one platform so that we offer multiple services to a customer, and SynergICE is only a logo of the B2B arm of Strides. And we partner with m ajor companies in Europe and out -license our products and that is how we get licensing income, profit shares, and all of that. And SynergICE is the logo that we use for the customers to differentiate our B2B business from our B2C business.

And if I just take that forward, what does it really imply for your E BITDA targets for this business, the ex of the gelatin business that you will dispose of rather divesting to OneSource? If you look at Strides as a business, over the next 2- 3 years, where can net debt to EBITDA levels be for this business?
You are talking about net debt to EBITDA levels?
Yes, net debt to EBITDA levels.

We firmly stand by our guidance that in spite of about 150 crores of EBITDA moving to OneSource, we will still achieve our current EBITDA. So, effectiv ely, we are telling you that like to like, our EBITDA will be closer to 950 crores in the next year. So, in spite of 150 crores of that moving away, we would still achieve our current EBITDA and revenues. There will be no drop in revenues and EBITDA. And we believe that in the next 2 years, our debt to EBITDA therefore will be much below 2 given the strong performance that we are now achieving through our reset.
Sir, if you can talk about where do we see our CDMO business in the next 2 years?

The CDMO business, once OneSource is up and running, we had put up a detailed presentation. We said that the business will be about $160 odd million at the launch year which is next year after t he NCLT process is complete, and we expect the business to hit $400 million in FY27.

And this is nothing to do with Sputnik. We have already written off all the inventories related to Sput nik in Stelis. Having said that, we had several consumables that can be used for many years in our other plants . But we have provided for them such that we operate once they are listed as OneSource of pure-play CDMO. We have provided for all those inventories and there are no more onetime pickups of Stelis going forward. Q4, as you can see, Stelis has grown its business significantly. Last year, we had revenues of only INR 5 crores to now INR60 crores and we would have even a stronger quarter in Q4. […] And we have now -- our partners now received approved status or close to receiving approvals for the first GMP, and we have already received our first commercial order for a significant value in FY'25. Second thing is the objective has been to maintain the gross margins. And that is what we have done consistently, you can see all the 8 quarters, we have demonstrated the gross margins between that 58% to 60%, and we wil l continue to work on it to get to that range.
