rationale.rationale: Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).
rationale.evolution: In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

points.point: First call of the separated entity: management confirmed the demerger took effect 1 October 2025 and that the CV business was listed as Tata Motors Limited under ticker TMCV on both exchanges, describing it as a commitment delivered.
points.quote: We successfully completed the demerger with Effective date of 1st October.

points.point: Comparatives had to be derived because the resulting company only came into existence in June 2024 — a direct consequence of the scheme structure.
points.quote: the prior period financials in this presentation, they reflect the impact of the demerger as it has just been effective since the Company’s incorporation that happened in June 2024.

points.point: The newly separated CV entity immediately tied up its own acquisition financing for Iveco through a bridge loan, with refinancing options (equity or debt) left open.
points.quote: On the Iveco acquisition, the regulatory approvals are underway and the initial funding through bridge loan has been secured.

points.point: The separation carried an explicit one-time cost of ₹960 crore, booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 within ₹1,500 crore of standalone exceptionals (with ₹603 crore labour code and ₹82 crore Iveco acquisition cost).
points.quote: Demerger cost has been around ₹960 crore.

points.point: Management flagged the demerger and labour-code charges as non-recurring, separating transaction cost from underlying performance.
points.quote: And both these are going to be one-time for us. We don't expect this on a recurring basis.

points.point: The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case.
points.quote: The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.

points.point: The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented.
points.quote: Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.

points.point: The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity.
points.quote: Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.

points.point: Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability.
points.quote: This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.

points.point: The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%.
points.quote: EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.

points.point: Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated.
points.quote: Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.

points.point: Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business.
points.quote: Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.

points.point: Mechanics of the separation as disclosed in every filing: NCLT Mumbai-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, with the resulting company renamed and listed.
points.quote: As per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench—amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the Company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited—the Company’s name was changed to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025), and its equity shares are listed on the BSE Ltd and the NSE Ltd.

points.point: Employee incentives were carried across the split one-for-one: outstanding PSUs of the demerged company entitle holders to a matching PSU from the CV entity, implemented via a new scheme for up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution).
points.quote: the unexercised performance share units (“PSUs”) (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company’s Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme.

points.point: The separated CV entity's strategic use of its independence — the Iveco combination is justified on scale, no overlap, operating leverage and dampening CV cash-flow volatility; ~EUR 21 billion combined revenue, ~590k units, Europe 46%/India 32%.
points.quote: The new company will be able to drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector.

points.point: Iveco was pursued as an all-cash EUR 14.10 (later EUR 14.40) offer valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, funded by a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Exor (27.06% of shares, 43.19% of votes) irrevocably committed.
points.quote: TML CV HS signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing to be used in connection with the Transaction, which was subsequently implemented through a facility agreement entered into by the Offeror for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00.

points.point: Structural simplification continued after the demerger: the CV entity is absorbing its own wholly owned financing subsidiaries TMF Holdings and TMF Business Services under a further NCLT scheme.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the merger of Amalgamating Company 1 and Amalgamating Company 2 (being direct and indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company respectively) with the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.
rationale.gaps: Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

deal.size_statement: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2025 demerger: not stated. 2026 Composite Scheme of Amalgamation (TMF Holdings / TMF Business Services into Tata Motors Limited): "The proposed scheme will not result in any change to the shareholding of TML and is subject to receipt of the necessary creditors, regulatory and other approvals." and "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of TML pursuant to the Scheme coming into effect." 2026 Iveco tender offer: "The Offeror and Iveco believe that having Iveco operate as a wholly privately owned subsidiary is key to the sustainable success of Iveco's business and long-term value creation" — percentage held by promoters not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2025 Composite Scheme of Arrangement (demerger of the commercial vehicles business): "3,68,23,31,373 Equity shares of face value and paid up value of ₹2/-each amounting to ₹736 crores has been issued to the shareholders of TMPVL on October 15, 2025 and difference between the face value of the Equity shares issued and carrying value of the assets and liabilities and other components of equity of the Demerged Undertaking has been recognised in the appropriate reserves in other equity." 2026 Composite Scheme of Amalgamation (TMFHL and TMFBSL into TML): "No consideration shall be paid by TML for the mergers. It is clarified that no new equity shares shall be issued by TML in consideration of the amalgamation." 2026 Iveco tender offer (for Iveco's shareholders, not TML's): "Shareholders tendering their Offer Shares under the Offer will be paid a cash amount of EUR 14.10 (cum dividend) per Offer Share in consideration for each Offer Share validly tendered and transferred to the Offeror", later increased to "an aggregate amount of EUR 14.40 (cum dividend) per Common Share".
deal.management_incentives: "Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited (presently Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited) ("Demerged Company"), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (presently Tata Motors Limited) ("Resulting Company" or "the Company") and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated w.e.f. October 1, 2025) and their respective shareholders under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ("the Scheme of Arrangement"), the unexercised performance share units ("PSUs") (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company's Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme." "the Board of Directors of the Company, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, at its Meeting held today, i.e., March 11, 2026, has, inter alia, approved the adoption of Tata Motors Limited Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme ("TML SLTI Scheme" or "the Scheme"), in accordance with the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits & Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, for issuance and allotment of not exceeding 23,07,647 Equity Shares of the Company." "The aforesaid allotment of Equity Shares may result in a maximum dilution of 0.062% of the total issued share capital of the Company." Pricing formula: "Exercise Price shall be ₹2/- per PSU, i.e., at the face value of the underlying Equity Share of the Company". "The Exercise Period would commence from the date of vesting of PSUs and will expire at the end of twelve months from the date of vesting of PSUs." "The maximum number of Equity Shares that may be issued/allotted pursuant to exercise of PSUs granted to an Eligible Employee, in aggregate, shall not exceed 23,07,647 Equity Shares of the Company of the face value of ₹2/- each fully paid -up representing 0.0.62% of the issued share capital of the Company. The TML SLTI Scheme shall be implemented and administered directly by the Company." PSUs vested, exercised, money realised and shares arising: "N.A". Management or insider shareholding in the Company: not stated.
deal.insider_actions: 2026 Iveco tender offer: "Exor N.V. ("Exor"), Iveco Group's largest Shareholder, has irrevocably committed to support the Offer and tender its shareholding representing approximately 27.06% of the Common Shares and 43.19% of all voting rights"; "Subject to settlement of the Offer, Exor has agreed to transfer its Special Voting Shares back to Iveco for no consideration."; "Iveco Group has agreed to use its best efforts to procure that all Iveco Board members holding in aggregate approximately 0.14% of the Common Shares , subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, tender all Common Shares held by them in the Offer and vote in favour of the resolutions to be proposed at the EGM." Third-party stake build-up raised on the Q4 FY26 call: "How are you looking at the acquisition of a 6 -7% stake in Iveco by an activist hedge fund from the market?" — answered: "On the second part of the question, on the investor, I think we are confident that the Iveco investor would see value in our offer and would support the deal." Also: "in the period between the Date of the Offer Document (i.e., 4 September 2026) and the date hereof, the Offeror has not purchased Common Shares outside the Offer". No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging in Tata Motors Limited stated.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited (commercial vehicles, post-demerger): EBITDA margin expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crores to ₹10,200 crores; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 13.9% (11th consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA margin) and EBIT margin 12.1%; double-digit EBIT margin crossed for the first time at 11% for FY26
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: While I'm really pleased with the margin story, EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited (commercial vehicles): Auto ROCE 72% for FY26; ROCE 53% for Q3 FY26 versus 38% in Q3 FY25; 45% in Q2 FY26
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: free cash flow approximately ₹9,200 crores in FY26 (about 12% of revenue); net cash ₹7,500 crores standalone at March 31, 2026 and approximately ₹13,700 crores consolidated (versus ₹4,000 crores in FY25); net cash ₹3,900 crores (domestic) and ₹6,100 crores (consolidated) at December 31, 2025
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Cash PAT almost entirely translated into free cash flow. With disciplined working capital management for the full year , free cash flow was ₹9200 crores. It is 12% of revenue. This led to a year -end net cash position of ₹7500 crores as of March 31st, 2026.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: trade receivables ₹376 crores, inventory burn ₹690 crores, payables and acceptances release ₹2,057 crores in FY26; current ratio 0.68 times and debtors turnover 21.73 times for the nine months ended December 31, 2025
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: Our cash conversion cycle best -in-class at negative 31 days. It means the business continues to be self -funding on working capital.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: FY26 investment spending approximately ₹3,000 crores (R&D approximately ₹1,700 crores; capital expenditure and other investments approximately ₹1,100 crores), guided range 2% to 4% of revenue, expected to stay in a similar range for FY27
other_differences.separated_business: Iveco Group: "Iveco Group's business shall remain substantially intact and contractual capital expenditures (CAPEX) commitments shall be respected."
other_differences.quote: Our investment spends has been consistent with the guided range of 2% to 4% of revenue, and growth and tech investments have always been prioritized.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: FY26 revenue approximately ₹77,000 crores, up 11% YoY; FY26 volumes 4,28,329 units, up 14%; Q2 FY27 sales 1,35,114 units, up 42.7% YoY; international business up 54% in FY26
other_differences.separated_business: Combined Tata Motors CV business and Iveco: "sales of over c.590k units per year" and combined revenues of c.EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000Cr+)
other_differences.quote: For the full year (FY26), sales volumes grew by 14 % from 3 ,76,903 to 4, 28,329 YoY, showcasing broad -based growth across product lines, customer segments and markets.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: standalone Debt Equity Ratio 0.29 times at December 31, 2025 (0.54 at September 30, 2025; 1.50 at December 31, 2024); consolidated Debt Equity Ratio 0.48 times; total debts to total assets 0.08 times standalone
other_differences.separated_business: Iveco acquisition financing: bridge facility agreement for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00; "our initial plan for financing is going to be through a bridge loan and subsequent refinancing at this point of time, all options are open. So we've kept both equity and debt still open."
other_differences.quote: Significant reduction in interest charge as a result of deleveraging, our interest cost has been kind of coming down, and you will see that quarter -on-quarter.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: nine months ended December 31, 2025 — profit before tax ₹1,790 crores with a tax charge of ₹834 crores standalone (₹2,039 crores PBT and ₹803 crores tax consolidated), because the impairment/fair value provision is not allowable and deferred tax assets were not recognised; current tax computed on a nine-month effective tax rate from July 1, 2025 as there were nil operations prior to the demerger
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: For the nine months ended December 31, 2025, while there is profit before tax of ₹1,790 crores which is after considering provision for investment in subsidiary and associate companies; there is a tax charge of ₹834 crores as the above provision is not an allowable expenditure under Income Tax.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Tata Motors Limited: one-time separation and acquisition costs charged as exceptional items in Q3 FY26 — new Labour Code ₹603 crore, demerger ₹962 crore (stamp duty on transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme) and acquisition cost ₹82 crore; ₹1.5K crore in standalone and ₹1.6K crore in consolidated financials; nine-month standalone exceptional items ₹3,920 crores including ₹2,355 crores impairment of investment in subsidiary and associate companies
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: The exceptional items include impact on account of the New Labor Code (₹603 Cr), demerger ( ₹962 Cr) and acquisition cost (₹82 Cr) .

rationale.rationale: TVS Motor is carving its consumer finance and related business undertaking — the lending, investment, leasing and ancillary/support activities it runs directly and through subsidiaries, principally the NBFC TVS Credit Services — out of the listed automotive company into Harita ARC Limited, a shell wholly-owned subsidiary bought from TVS Credit Services for Rs 25,000 on 28th October 2026, with TVS Motor shareholders getting 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 TVS Motor share (47,50,87,114 shares, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP, fairness opinion by JM Financial), and the resulting company to be listed; the same Composite Scheme also amalgamates the dormant wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited (total assets Rs 251.44 Cr, net worth Rs 198.93 Cr, nil turnover) into TVS Motor 'to streamline the group corporate structure', after which it is dissolved without winding up. Management's stated problem is that finance has outgrown its host: the demerged undertaking already turned over Rs 3,921 Cr of TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated revenue in H1 FY27, and the Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of assets and Rs 33,288 Cr of liabilities against Automotive's Rs 23,868 Cr, which is why consolidated net debt/equity sits at 2.90x versus 0.37x standalone. The Scheme says the consumer finance business 'needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path', that 'the nature of, and competition in, the consumer finance and related business differ from those of the other businesses', and — the capital-structure crux — that 'a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth'. The second stated problem is investor mismatch: a standalone entity 'can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business', and the demerger will 'unlock the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'. Chairman Sudarshan Venu framed it as 15 years of sustained investment reaching scale — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India serving 'more than 45 million customers across 100,000 touchpoints', plus the Varthana education-finance acquisition and the Jana Small Finance Bank stake — so the platform should now allocate capital to its own priorities while TVS Motor 'remain[s] focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally'. It follows the August 2026 step in which the group's NBFCs approved merging STPL Trading and Services into Home Credit India Finance (155.79 shares per 200) and then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance into TVS Credit Services (9.94 per 180), expressly for 'consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions'; alongside the demerger the board also bought STPL outright for Rs 530.08 Cr to pick up ~2.4% more of TVS Credit post-merger. No lender, partner or named investor is cited as having asked for the split.
rationale.evolution: Strikingly, the separation is absent from all seven earnings calls in the window (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026): management discussed TVS Credit only as a performance line — book Rs 26,647 Cr and PBT Rs 1,027 Cr in FY25 (28 Apr 2025 call), Rs 30,631 Cr and Rs 1,248 Cr in FY26 (13 May 2026), Rs 32,053 Cr and 2.6 crore customers in Q1 FY27 (21 Jul 2026) — while repeatedly describing fresh equity infusions into it (Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26 per the 28 Jan 2026 call, Rs 200 Cr across FY26, Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the filing). The only hint of structural intent came from an analyst on the 31 Jul 2025 call asking about monetising or IPO-ing TVS Credit, which CFO Gopala Desikan shut down as 'not yet even discussed at the Board level'. The plan then surfaces entirely in filings: the 5 Aug 2026 NBFC-consolidation scheme (STPL → Home Credit India Finance → TVS Credit Services, citing RBI directions), then the 28 Oct 2026 board approval of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement that demerges the undertaking into Harita ARC Limited 1:1 and folds TVS Motor Services into TVS Motor, with the press release calling the demerger 'the next step in this strategic process'.

points.point: The 28 Oct 2026 Composite Scheme demerges the consumer finance and related business undertaking from TVS Motor into Harita ARC Limited and simultaneously amalgamates wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited into TVS Motor.
points.quote: The Scheme, inter alia, provides for: (i) the amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company; and (ii) the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) from the Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, in consideration for which the Resulting Company shall issue its shares to the shareholders of the Company in proportion to their shareholding in the Company.

points.point: Stated rationale #1: structural simplification into two independent standalone platforms, each with its own strategy and capital plan.
points.quote: The demerger will simplify the group structure and create focused businesses, with a clear segregation of the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business.

points.point: Stated rationale #2: the lending business has risk, competitive and growth characteristics unlike the vehicle business, so it needs its own strategy.
points.quote: The consumer finance and related business needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path;

points.point: The capital-structure crux — an NBFC can run far more balance-sheet leverage than a manufacturer; consolidated net debt/equity was 2.90x at 30 Sep 2026 against 0.37x standalone.
points.quote: a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth .

points.point: Investor/lender mismatch is named explicitly: a pure-play finance entity can draw capital providers who want finance exposure, and this unlocks value for existing holders.
points.quote: the independent company can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business .

points.point: Size of the carve-out: the demerged undertaking produced Rs 3,921 Cr of revenue in the period ended 30 Sep 2026 against TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated turnover; shareholders get 1:1 shares and the new entity will be listed.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921 Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .

points.point: Press release frames the trigger as scale reached after 15 years of investment — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India at 45 million customers and 100,000 touchpoints, plus Varthana and Jana Small Finance Bank — needing a dedicated structure for capital allocation.
points.quote: The consumer finance and related business have expanded in scale and scope and a dedicated st ructure will provide greater strategic focus, flexibility in capital allocation and the ability to pursue opportunities across the consumer finance and related sector s.

points.point: Chairman Sudarshan Venu's framing: full value realisation for the finance platform while TVS Motor concentrates on global mobility leadership, with shareholders participating in both.
points.quote: It positions them to realise the full potential of their assets and capabilities while enabling TVS Motor Company to remain focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally .

points.point: The precursor step (5 Aug 2026): STPL merges into Home Credit India Finance, then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance merge into TVS Credit Services — partly driven by regulator-led NBFC consolidation; TVS Motor separately paid Rs 530.08 Cr for STPL to gain ~2.4% more of TVS Credit.
points.quote: consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions.

points.point: The only investor-side prod in three years of calls: an analyst asked about earlier plans to monetise or IPO TVS Credit Services, and the CFO said the board had not taken it up — no mention of a demerger.
points.quote: And as far as the question is all about IPO, not yet even discussed at the Board level.

points.point: Scale of the business being separated, as management last described it on a call: book up 19% to Rs 32,053 Cr, PBT Rs 283 Cr for the quarter, ~2.6 crore customers, ~62,000 touchpoints.
points.quote: The book size of TVS Credit grew by 19%. Now it is at INR 32,053 crores as against INR 26,898 crores last year.

points.point: FY26 record finance earnings quantified on the call — the profit stream now leaving the listed automotive entity.
points.quote: PBT has grown by 22%, INR 1,248 crores as against INR 1,027 crores during last year.

points.point: TVS Motor was repeatedly injecting equity into the finance arm while it sat inside the parent — Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26, and Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the quarterly filing — the capital drain the separate structure is meant to re-route.
points.quote: Now coming back to the second question on INR 900 crores, the delta this quarter has been TVS Credit Services, we have invested about INR200 crores.

rationale.what_management_expects: For the finance platform: strategic autonomy, sharper capital allocation, freedom to run higher NBFC-style leverage, a dedicated investor/lender/partner base, and value unlocked via a 1:1 listed entity. For TVS Motor: a simplified group structure, operational synergies from absorbing TVS Motor Services, and undiluted focus on automotive/mobility leadership globally. Shareholders participate in both.
rationale.gaps: No call ever discusses the demerger; no margin, ROE, capital-release, cost, tax, debt-allocation or timeline numbers for either entity; no promoter-control or future-stake-sale intent disclosed.

deal.promoter_holding_after: 2026 demerger into Harita ARC Limited: "Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the Resulting Company will issue and allot its fully paid -up equity shares to the eligible shareholders of the Company, in proportion to their respective shareholding in the Company as on the Record Date (as defined in the Scheme)  such that the shareholding pattern of the Resulting Company will mirror that of the Company." Amalgamation of TVS Motor Services Limited: "There will not be any change in the existing shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the proposed Scheme." 2025 bonus NCRPS scheme: "Thus, there would be no change in shareholding of TVSM." 2026 NBFC amalgamation: "Not applicable. TVS Motor Company Limited  is not a party to the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and consequently, there will be no change in the shareholding pattern of TVS Motor Company  Limited."
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2026 Composite Scheme of Arrangement: "Under the proposed Scheme, shareholders of the c ompany will receive equal number of shares in the resulting company  as in TVS Motor , enabling them to participate in the future growth of both the mobility and consumer finance  businesses" — i.e. "1 (One) fully paid -up equity share of face value of INR 1/ - (Rupee One only) each of the Resulting Company for every 1 (One) fully paid -up equity share of face value of INR 1/ - (Rupee One o nly) each of the Company". 2025 Scheme of Arrangement: "the Company shall issue and allot, by way of bonus, 4 Preference Shares of face value of INR 10 each fully paid up to each equity shareholder of the Company holding every 1 equity share of INR 1 each fully paid up" (6% Cumulative Non-Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares, redeemed 1 September 2026 for Rs. 2,014.36 Cr including dividend). Amalgamation of TVS Motor Services Limited and of Sundaram Auto Components Limited: no consideration, both being wholly owned subsidiaries.
deal.management_incentives: not stated as to treatment of grants in the Scheme or any new plan in the resulting entity. The only related disclosures are financial: "Share based payment expense 4.33" (standalone) / "5.59" (consolidated) for the half year ended 30.09.2026, and "Changes in treasury shares by ESOP Trust 1.46" in financing activities.
deal.insider_actions: The Company acquired 100% of Harita ARC Limited (2,500 equity shares of Rs. 10 each) for Rs. 25,000/- in cash from TVS Credit Services Limited, a material subsidiary: "Yes, the proposed transaction is a related party transaction.  The Company has  acquire d shares  of TVSM WOS  from TVS Credit Services Limited, a material subsidiary of the Company." The Board also approved acquiring 100% of STPL Trading and Services Private Limited (18,89,47,551 equity shares) for Rs. 530.08 Cr in cash: "The shares are acquired  from various stakeholders  who are related parties." and "The transfer of shares will be done at “arms -length” based on a valuation report." No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of TVS Motor shares is stated.

listing_resolution.quote: IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has filed the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2026 (“DRHP”), on 7th November 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Offer (“IPO”).

listing.short: IPO DRHP filed — IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited
listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO DRHP FILED — IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited; date not fixed

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.
rationale.evolution: The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

points.point: The capex need that later drives the separation starts here: the Korea Circuit HDI/substrate JV is on hold pending the ECMS scheme, with a likely Rs1,000cr-plus minimum investment and 70-75% of it only reimbursed later by MeitY and the states.
points.quote: So, on Korea Circuit we are waiting for Government to finalize the incentive scheme.

points.point: With an INR3,000cr PCB application planned and subsidies spread over 5-6 years, management says the Electronics division is itself seeking third-party funding — the first hint of capital being raised at the subsidiary rather than at Amber.
points.quote: So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.

points.point: Two funding routes are named — an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and private equity money targeted specifically at the electronics arm; the same call sets the constraint that drives it, a board cap of 2x debt/EBITDA and a goal to be net-debt-free by FY27.
points.quote: Second direction is a lot of private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division.

points.point: The separated entity is given its own standalone ambition and margin identity — $1bn revenue in three years at 11.5-12% EBITDA, versus ILJIN's 2.8% EBITDA on INR300cr when acquired in 2018.
points.quote: With all the add -ups, we intend to take Electronics division to $1 billion by next 3 years with target EBITDA of 11.5% to 12% range.

points.point: The raise happens at two levels simultaneously: INR1,750cr into ILJIN (mostly CCPS; INR370cr in September, INR280cr in October, ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr pending CCI) and a separate INR1,000cr QIP at Amber used mainly to cut debt.
points.quote: We secured funding of INR1,750 crores from marquee investors.

points.point: ILJIN's raise closes in full and Amber's stake stays at 90% only because the instrument is CCPS; the same call adds the ECMS approvals (Ascent-K HDI, Shogini) and 116 acres at Jewar that the money has to fund.
points.quote: On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.

points.point: The outside investors' economics depend on a valuation event: no dilution has occurred yet because CCPS convert off a future multiple, with auditors provisioning roughly 30% maximum dilution in non-controlling interest. FY27 capex is guided at INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash), net debt INR511cr rising to INR700-800cr.
points.quote: It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation.

points.point: The ILJIN cap table already limits group structuring — management cannot say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business (8m units year one, 13-15m year two, sub-INR50cr capex, 1.5-2% industry EBITDA) will sit inside ILJIN or directly under Amber.
points.quote: But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .

points.point: April 2026: Amber pre-funds ILJIN again, subscribing INR296.02cr of a INR328.12cr rights issue (12,46,430 shares), taking its holding from 89.58% to 89.72% — capital in before the listing, not a stake sale.
points.quote: Further, pursuant to the allotment of equity shares under the rights issue by IL JIN on 21st April 2026, which has resulted in an investment of Rs. 296.02 Crore, Amber Enterprises India Limited (“Amber” or “the Company”) has subscribed to and been allotted 12,46,430 equity shares.

points.point: July 2026: ILJIN is mechanically prepared for listing — Rs10 to Rs5 share split, authorised capital to Rs250cr, 25:1 bonus, conversion from private to public limited, registered office moved Pune to Greater Noida, and a board resolution to explore fund-raising modes including a public issue.
points.quote: Evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives.

points.point: 7 November 2026: the separation becomes a formal partial listing of the electronics arm — a DRHP for ILJIN's IPO filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, Amber retaining ~90% pre-offer.
points.quote: IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has ﬁled the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2026 (“DRHP”), on 7th November 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Oﬀer (“IPO”).

points.point: The rest of the group is being simplified in the opposite direction: wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast (cross-flow fans) is merged into Amber — no shares issued, NCLT dispensed with meetings, appointed date moved to 1 April 2026 — for compliance savings, scale synergies and cleaner peer comparison.
points.quote: more absolute and profound comparison with industry peers ie. benchmarking business performance with industry; and

points.point: Portfolio pruning runs alongside: the 49% Shivaliks/Titagarh Firema stake is impaired (INR94cr in Q3, INR112cr FY26 including JV losses) and then sold in March 2026 to JP Fincap for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85, ending Italy export ambitions while keeping the Titagarh commercial relationship worth ~INR700cr of visibility.
points.quote: And to curtail future losses, on etime exceptional impairment loss has been recognized during this quarter.

rationale.what_management_expects: Electronics: self-funded ECMS PCB capex, $1bn revenue in ~3 years, margins from 2.8% (2018) toward 11.5-12%, double digits from FY27, ~26% ROCE, stickier high-entry-barrier industrial/defence mix. Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.
rationale.gaps: Calls never discuss the IPO itself: offer size, fresh issue versus OFS, use of proceeds, valuation, Amber's post-listing stake, CCPS conversion terms, or why listing rather than demerger.

deal.size_statement: From the 7 September 2024 filing, for AmberPR only: "The amount and percentage of the turnover or revenue or income and net worth contributed by such unit or division or undertaking or subsidiary or associate company of the listed entity during the last financial year" — "Turnover FY 2023-24" "12,092.63" and "Net Worth FY 2023-24" "2,923.57" (Amount in Lakh); "% of Turnover or Revenue or Income and Net Worth contributed by AmberPR of the Company" "2.68%" and "1.71%". No size statement is given for IL JIN relative to Amber.
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated (the documents state only that "The Transferee Company has 1,15,647 equity shareholders as on September 30, 2025" and a paid-up capital of 3,51,91,667 equity shares of Rs. 10/- each)
deal.promoter_holding_after: For the IL JIN IPO: not stated. On Amber's own holding in IL JIN before the IPO, Q2 FY26 call: "So as of now, should we assume that the stake remains at 90% only and it will go down only once the CCPS converts in the future?" — "Yes, right." And Q4 FY26 call: "So nothing is being considered as a dilution on CCPS. Nothing -- no dilution has still now happened due to CCPS. It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation. So currently, on a conservative side, the auditor has considered the diluted percentage and calculated the NCI." / "I think they are considered around 30-odd percent." For the AmberPR amalgamation: "In terms of clause 18 of the Scheme, the Transferor Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Transferee Company, accordingly, upon the Scheme becoming effective, all the equity shares as held by the Transferee Company in the Transferor Company either by itself or through its subsidiaries/nominees shall stand cancelled and extinguished." For the 2024 slump sale: "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the proposed slump sale."
deal.public_shareholders_get: For the 2026 AmberPR amalgamation, nothing: "No shares are to be issued by the Transferee Company in lieu or in exchange of its holding in the Transferor Company as consideration, and therefore, there is no reorganization in the paid-up capital structure of the Transferee Company" and "the proposed Scheme will not result in any dilution in the Shareholding of the Shareholders of the 'Transferee Company'". For the 2024 slump sale: "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the proposed slump sale." For the IL JIN IPO: not stated — the documents disclose no entitlement, reservation or shareholder quota for Amber's public shareholders.
deal.management_incentives: Existing grants: "Subsequent to April 01, 2025, the Transferee Company has issued and allotted shares under Amber Enterprises India Limited - Employee Stock Option Plan 2017 on April 18, 2025, June 05, 2025, August 02, 2025, November 06, 2025, and February 25, 2026." Reporting treatment: "For clarification, operating EBITDA is before impact of ESOP expenses and other nonoperating income and expenses." The documents do not state how existing grants are treated in any scheme, do not disclose any new plan in IL JIN, and do not give an exercise price or pricing date. On management of the new mobile-phone business: "Certainly, it requires a very dedicated efforts. And certainly, there will be a senior most management dedicated to this sector only". On where it will sit: "we'll give a clarity on that, whether it will come directly under Amber or it will go in IL JIN... But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table."
deal.insider_actions: No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of Amber shares is stated. The documents do state, on the Ascent management shareholding: "We have taken our -- earlier, we acquired 60%, now we own 98.5%. Yes, because of the arrangement in the agreement, Mr. Manjunath had to step down because he's no more a shareholder in the Ascent." Third-party capital raises around the separation: "ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors" (CCPS plus a small portion of equity; tranches of INR370 crores in September, INR280 crores in October and ChrysCapital's INR1,100 crores) and "Amber Enterprises raised equity fund of INR1,000 crores from marquee investors through QIP". Also "share of loss of Shivalik JV is INR64 crores from 1st January '26 till 30th March '26, the date of sale of Shivalik shares." On an earlier demerger report, the Company told NSE on 24 December 2024: "As on date, there is no such event that triggers the disclosure obligations under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations."

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consolidated revenue grew 22% to INR12,186 crores in FY26; Consumer Durable division grew 14% to INR8,383 crores; Railway Systems and Defence grew 19% to INR535 crores
other_differences.separated_business: Electronics division (IL JIN and its subsidiaries) revenue grew 49% to INR3,268 crores in FY26 and is guided to grow around 40% in FY27
other_differences.quote: Revenue for financial year '26 increased to INR3,268 crores compared to INR2,194 crores in financial year '25, reflecting a strong growth of 49% year-on-year, driven by strong PCBA business along with bare PCB and the addition of new businesses.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consolidated operating EBITDA INR970 crores on revenue of INR12,186 crores in FY26; Consumer Durable operating EBITDA INR593 crores, up 6%; Railway operating EBITDA INR90 crores, up 8%, with margins expected at 16% to 17%
other_differences.separated_business: Electronics division operating EBITDA INR287 crores in FY26, up 89%; guided to 9.5% to 10% in FY27; within it PCBA about 5%, PCB about 12%-13%, Power-One about 15%
other_differences.quote: Operating EBITDA for the year recorded growth of 89% year-on-year and stood at INR287 crores compared to INR151 crores in financial year '25.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "Our net working capital days stood at 29 days as of March '26 compared to 9 days in March '25."
other_differences.separated_business: The new mobile phone business is described as structurally low on working capital intensity, at 4 to 5 days, maximum 10 days
other_differences.quote: It's very, very minimal working capital requirements. Normally, this sector operates on a net-working capital days of almost 4, 5 days, maximum 10 days.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "On the balance sheet front, net debt stood at INR511 crores as of March '26 against INR780 crores in March '25." Expected to rise to around INR700 crores to INR800 crores by FY27 year-end
other_differences.separated_business: IL JIN raised INR1,750 crores, predominantly compulsorily convertible preference shares with a small portion of equity, from marquee investors, part kept "in the war chest for the future expansion"
other_differences.quote: On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Overall FY26 capex around INR1,070 crores, of which capitalized capex only INR550 crores; FY27 overall capex INR1,800 crores to INR2,000 crores with cash outflow of around INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores; Railway capex only around INR50 crores to INR60 crores
other_differences.separated_business: The electronics/PCB businesses are the asset-heavy part: Ascent around INR1,200-odd crores in FY27, Ascent-K Circuits first phase INR1,200 crores (total INR3,200 crores), Shogini INR500 crores application with INR55 crores to INR60 crores in the coming year; ECMS approvals of more than INR4,500 crores total investment
other_differences.quote: See Dhruv, I'll add to what Sudhir has answered. These are all asset-heavy businesses where the capex is going, largely the printed circuit boards. This is exactly like OSAT and ATMP business where asset turns are about 0.8 to 1x.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: not stated as a parent-level figure; on the component side "if we talk about the component side where our goal is the PCB, we work in the range of 15% to 16%"
other_differences.separated_business: The new high-volume mobile phone assembly business is said to be ROCE accretive on a stand-alone basis
other_differences.quote: And -- but we see a very, very good ROCEs. Generally, these are very ROCE accretive. If you take this on a stand-alone basis, I mean, the ROCEs will be more than 30%, 35%.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consumer Durable is a pass-through, quarterly-lag business with fixed margin per unit: "we have a fixed price margin per unit. So overall, fixed margin will remain same in terms of value"; Indian Railway contracts are fixed price contracts
other_differences.separated_business: The bare PCB business is a Tier 2 supplier with a longer pass-through lag; mobile phone assembly runs at industry EBITDA of 1.5% to 2%
other_differences.quote: But in the PCB business, we are Tier 2. We don't supply directly to Maruti or Hyundai, we supply to Tier 1 guys, and that's where the inventory has to be taken care at 2 levels. And hence, the lag in the PCB business to increase the cost is about 2 quarters.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Under the AmberPR scheme the authorized share capital of the Transferor Company transfers to Amber "without any liability for payment of any additional fees ... or stamp duty"; the scheme was certified as complying with accounting standards under section 133

turns: Hello and good morning , everyone on the call I'm joined by Mr. D aljit Singh – Managing Director; Mr. Sudhir Goyal – our CFO ; Mr. Sanjay Arora – Whole-Time Director of IL JIN Electronics ; and Mr. Sachin Gupta – CEO of R AC Division. We have uploaded our Results , Presentation on the exchanges and I hope everybody had an opportunity to go through the same . This year has been a year of transformation at Amber . […] Firstly, we shifted towards supply of components to room air conditioner customers with our goal of maintaining our share of business in this sector of 28 % to 29% in value terms . We are glad to announce that we have been able to maintain our share and are hopeful to continue maintaining it. Furthermore, we opted for going for non -room air conditioner components , like components for telecom, smart meters, automobiles, refrigerator compressor parts, washing machine parts, Amber Enterprises India Limited February 12, 2024 microwave parts, etc. , Today, our room AC contribution has come down from 72% in 2018 to 38% and will further reduce in the coming years to come. We also diversified our electronics PCBA portfolio to different applications apart from consumer durables . We added hearable and wearable sector, telecom sector , auto, smart metering and now further expanding into defense and industri als, plus, we acquired Ascent circuits for expanding our portfolio into PCB boards for various applications. Furthermore, we strengthen ed our railway portfolio . Apart from supplying air conditioners, we entered into doors and gangways and pantry systems and further now expanding into couplers, interiors, toilets, pantograph s and p assage through our recently announced JV with Titagarh . […] However, we are very strongly confident of maintaining our growth trajectory in our bottom line in the next financial year and years to come. Also, we are confident of maintaining our guidance of ROCE levels of 19 % to 21% range in the next three years, i.e. FY'27. I would now like to take you through Highlights of Recent Announcements made in Electronics and Railway Division . Ascent Circuits: Amber Group has acquired 60% stake in As cent Circuits Private Limited through IL JIN Electronics for consideration of Rs.311 crores subject to adjustments as stipulated in definitive agreements . This acquisition will aid us in manufacturing of printed circuit boards and help us develop capacities and capabilities for single -sided , double - sided, multi -layered and RF PCBs . Through this acquisition, we will be able to cater diverse set of customers for various applications that is aerospace and defense, medical, energy solutions, automotive, telecom, data centers, consumer electronics, IT, lighting , etc., Further , Amber via Ascent Circuit s also signed an MOU with South Korea ’s Circuit, which is a YoungPoon g Group Company, to manufacture Flex , HDI, semiconductor substrates , PCB s, thereby enhancing PCB manufacturing in India . Korea Circuit is the pioneer of Korean PCB industry and has pioneered various PCB solutions including HDI , flex, semiconductor substrates, multilayer double -sided and single -sided PCB s in the last 45 -years. These solutions find applications across diverse sectors such as mobile industry , IT industry, semiconductor industry, home appliances, consumer electronics, aerospace and defense, medical, energy solutions, automotive, telecom, data centers and more. Amber Enterprises India Limited February 12, 2024 The recent acquisition of a majority stake in Ascent C ircuits, followed by signing of this M oU with Korea Circuit , places Amber in a unique spot and positions it as a leading player in the electronic EMS space, thereby opening a myriad of new business opportunities. Moreover , it enhances Amber's EMS portfolio by increasing local value addition and fostering backward integration into passive components of PCB assemblies. This aligns seamlessly with the Atmanirbhar Bharat Vision of Government of India and is consistent with the group strategy of strengthening backward integration for its EMS play across diverse applications. We clearly see our electronics division becoming Amber 2.0 strategy that has exponential growth opportunities in the year to come. Now , I'll talk about Sidwal and Titagarh Announcement. Further, Amber through Sidwal has posed a strategic partnership with Titagarh Rail Systems Limited to enter the train components and subsystem business in India and Italy via a 50 :50 joint venture SPV named Shivali k. Titagarh Rail stands as a front runner in the railway rolling stock domain excelling in both freight and passenger rolling stock. […] Consequently, although it may seem that our revenues in these divisions have experienced a 3% and 5% YoY decline for the nine months and Q3 respectively, it's crucial to consider the context, namely the decline in finished goods sale compared to the previous fiscal year. Typically , orders for finished goods commence in late October to prepare for the upcoming business season, while orders for components usually kickstarts in January to February to minimize inventory holding period. We expect margin expansion in this division due to our shift of strategy towards components and we expect to maintain our share of bus iness of 28 % to 29% in value terms in this division . Shifting gears to the “Electronics Division ,” it has reported total revenue of Rs.757 crore s for the nine months FY'2 4 and Rs.241 cr ores for Q3 FY'24. Operating EBITDA increased to Rs.36 crores versus Rs.30 crores in the nine months as compared to the nine months FY'23. Despite witnessing a 7% Y oY increase in the revenues for the nine months FY'2 4, there was an 8% decline in Q3 FY' 24. Amber Enterprises India Limited February 12, 2024 As previously mentioned, we have recently done two strategic onboarding in Amber’s ambit ; Ascent Circuits and Korea Circuit which will significantly contribute to the top line and bottom line of the division going forward.

I have two questions. One is on the mobility business I want to know . We are talking about the opportunity on Vande Bharat, know through Titagarh , but on the metro, do we have tie -ups with the likes of B EML, Siemens, Alstom, Bombardier? That's the first question. The second question is on the CAPEX side. We've spent over Rs.2,000 crores in the last 10 years and we are looking at the significant CAPEX given that we've spent almost Rs.260-odd crore s in the first nine months. You did indicate in the opening remarks , you want to get to ROC E of 19 % to 20% from Amber Enterprises India Limited February 12, 2024 single digit. Can you just take us through how will you reach from single digit ROCs given the CAPEX intensity that we can see in the next couple of years ?

To answer your first question, Rahul, we already are suppl ying to B EML, Alstom, then CR RC and now onboarded Titagarh plus, all the three railway manufacturing facilities, ICF Chennai , RCF Kapu rthala, MCF Raebareli and plus all the sub -divisional parts on the DCW and all , plus we are also supplying to locomotives as well , both Siemens and G E. So, on the customer front, we are already approved there. We just need to expand the product offering by increasing our wallet share. To answer the question on the second part on the CAPEX intensity, since all these new initiatives are higher margin businesses with a high ROC E businesses like Sidwal per s e today is sitting at about 22% of EBITDA margin with close to 40% of ROC E business , Electronics again is at about 27% of ROC E business. And furthermore, by the initiatives which we have taken, we are going to increase the margins in the business , and on the consumer durable side also because of our strategy shift on the component side, the margins are expanding. So , because of higher margin businesses and high growth plus the operational leverage on the plants, we will reach to the ROC Es level of what we guided.
Isn’t consumer and electronics both are close to 5%-odd because that's what we've seen in the nine months numbers.
Consumer has now come to about 7.3% and electronics by next year will cross 7%.

On these two inorganic initiatives that you have taken right, so just wanted to understand what kind of revenue potential and margin that we can see in terms of improvement ? And if you could even talk about Ascent' s nine month s performance and how should we think about it in the next two or three years? And just one clarification there , on the electronic side, you mentioned that Amber Enterprises India Limited February 12, 2024 you will go to about 7%, 7.5% margin. So does this include the Ascent because we understand that the margins there are much higher ?

So Ascent , nine months is performing fine ; they have done Rs.206 crore s with almost Rs.42 crores of EBITDA, almost about 19 % to 20% of EBITDA levels which is very high for this kind of business sector. Yes, it will be consol of electronics division will reach to 7%, 7.5% moving forward, both PCB A as well as the Bare PCB Board put together , will be there on an EBITDA level.

My second question is of your new initiative on the Ascent and Tita garh, you' ve tie up with them . What is the kind of upside , very approximately that we can expect? Management: On Ascen t, we have done two things. One is we have acquired 60% in Ascen t, and secondly, we have also signed M oU for partnering with YP Group Korea C ircuit of South Korea. It is a $12 billion group and they are one of the leading players supplying to mobile industry as well as semiconductor in dustry there and a specialist in HDI board . So they are very keen . With both of them put together , we have opened up a good opportunity for this business sector . Right now this bare PCB board is largely getting imported and nobody is making mobile PCBs here and nobody is making semiconductor substrates here , plus you must have heard anti -dumping duty has been levied and the file is just awaiting the final notification to be out. Already, DGFT has recommended 30% anti -dumping duty on these products from single layer to six layer basis. We expect that notification should be up and out by March . So that will open up this whole complete import substitution for us . Currently , if you see , almost about $3.8 billion worth of bare PCB boards are getting imported, p lus, ongoing growth in electronics sector, where every sector is having more content of electronics, be it automobile , be it consumer durables, defense, aerospace, aviation, whatever sector you see , the content of electronics is increasing on yearly basis. So today, if we see, there's a lot of opportunity, which opens up because of As cent Circuits and our association with YP Group .

I have got two questions. First is on electr onics division . Can you help us understand what prop ortion of the revenue as you report today is from R AC-related electronics and what is non - RAC related electronics, just to understand what kind of decline that we have seen in electronics can be attributed to ? Management: So, electronics basically contribute about 19% in the total con sol revenue and in that almost about 25% is air conditioner PCB boards.

Any guidance on that , if you can quantify exactly you're looking in terms of margins, although you are looking to double the revenue for your electronics and also if you can guide on that what sort of margin are you looking for FY'26?

Well, all the divisions are at a different margin profile. I think we are at almost 7.2 % in the consumer durable division , we will be touching 7% plus in the electronics division by next year , and railway mobility is at about 20 % plus. So all divisions are at different stream and at good growth prospective . Like in railways , I've exp lained that by this announcement , we have opened a good TAM for us . If you see on the Vande Bharat Express, very few Vande Bharat Express will be delivered next year. But next -to-next year, the numbers are going up, and by FY '27 the numbers are exponentially going up. So our revenues in that stream also will go to in line with the requirement of the Indian Railways.

Now that you are focusing more on the non -AC part, whe n do we see the growth in the top line , do we have a better sort of growth than earlier , are you envisaging some stronger growth than earlier or do we see some slowdown in that now that the AC part is coming down in the proportions ? Management: It's very difficult to predict on the top line basis because on the component side also we have some sub -assemblies where customers do take sub -assemblies, sometimes they don't take sub- assembl ies. Similarly , in electronics division we have seen similar kind of a trend. So predicting and guiding on top line will be very difficult. But yes, as guided earlier , on the bottom line basis, we see a very, very strong growth moving forward .

JASBIR SINGH – EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN & CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER , & WHOLE -TIME DIRECTOR , AMBER ENTERPRISES INDIA LIMITED MR. DALJIT SINGH – MANAGING DIRECTOR , AMBER ENTERPRISES INDIA LIMITED MR. SUDHIR GOYAL – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER , AMBER ENTERPRISES INDIA LIMITED MR. SANJAY ARORA – WHOLE -TIME DIRECTOR , IL JIN ELECTRONICS Disclaimer: E&OE -This transcript is edited for factual errors. On the call, I'm joined by Mr. Daljit Singh, Managing Director, Mr. Sudhir Goyal, our CFO, Mr. Sanjay Arora, Whole -time Director of IL GIN Electronics and our Investor Relations Advisor, SGA. We have uploaded our Results, Presentation on the exchanges and I hope everybody had an opportunity to go through the same. FY'23 -24 has been a year of resilience and growth for Amber. And in this one year we have strengthened our portfolio and market offerings with strategic diversifications in new growth segments. […] Mass production from the new plant will commence from H2 second half this year, where we expect around 40,000 washing machines to be produced in this year, which will further take it to 1,25,000 in next financial year. We have already onboarded a couple of customers and the trials are currently going on. Through this JV , we gained access to manufacturing washing machines, thereby allowing us to offer wider range of high quality products to our customers.
