rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

points.point: Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years.
points.quote: Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.

points.point: The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae.
points.quote: The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.

points.point: Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself.
points.quote: This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima

points.point: Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given.
points.quote: And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?

points.point: Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation.
points.quote: Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.

points.point: The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation.
points.quote: We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.

points.point: Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26).
points.quote: With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.

points.point: Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged.
points.quote: With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.

points.point: Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations.
points.quote: Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.

points.point: Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%.
points.quote: In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.

points.point: The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated.
points.quote: As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.

rationale.what_management_expects: Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.
rationale.gaps: No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.

deal.size_statement: Swara Baby (2026 IPO): "If we refer to the summary of restated consolidated Profit and Loss account of Swara Baby as disclosed in page no. 75 of the DRHP, the revenue from operations of Swara Baby for FY 26 is Rs. 11,639 Million. Further, post adjustment of the inter-company transaction between Swara Baby and Brainbees of Rs. 2,634.61 Million as disclosed in the Risk Factor No. 2 on Page No. 23 of Swara Baby's DRHP, the revenue from operations is Rs. 9,004.39 Million which got consolidated in the revenue from operations of India Multi-channel business of Brainbees." | Solis Hygiene (2025 restructuring): "Solis Hygiene Private Limited (“Solis Hygiene”) has contributed Turnover of Rs. 240.7 Crore and Net Worth of Rs. 84.8 Crore amounting to 3% and 2% of the Consolidated Turnover and Net Worth, respectively of the Company, during the financial year 2024-25." | Mush (2026 sale): "Amount: Rs. 11.34 Crore Percentage Contribution: 0.13%" of turnover and "Amount: Rs. 2.09 Crore Percentage Contribution: 0.04%" of net worth for financial year 2025-26.
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated as a percentage — "The Company does not have any identifiable promoters or controlling shareholders and accordingly, there is no requirement to provide an exit offer" (AGM Notice dated August 13, 2026); "The Company does not have identifiable promoter or promoter group" (filing dated October 7, 2026); "The Company doesn't have any identifiable promoter" (filings dated August 13, 2025 and May 26, 2026)
deal.promoter_holding_after: Swara Baby 2026 IPO: "Brainbees currently holds 76.59% shareholding in Swara Baby. Brainbees continue to remain invested and supportive of the business of Swara Baby and Swara Baby will continue to remain as Subsidiary Company of Brainbees. This is only a partial monetization of our investment in Swara Baby." Also: "Brainbees is a Promoter of Swara Baby and Mr. Supam Maheshwari and Mr. Gautam Sharma have been appointed as non-executive directors on the board of directors of Swara Baby." The percentage after the IPO is not stated. | 2025 Solis Hygiene restructuring: "the shareholding of the Company in Swara Baby will be increased from 75.92% to 76.59% and Swara Baby will hold 100% stake in Solis Hygiene. Solis Hygiene will become step-down subsidiary of the Company and consequently, the indirect control of the Company in Solis Hygiene will be 76.59%." | 2026 Mush sale: "GlobalBees, a Subsidiary of the Company, has today, i.e. October 07, 2026, entered into a Memorandum of Understanding for the sale of its entire 51.54% shareholding in its Subsidiary viz. Mush"; the Company states it has no identifiable promoter or promoter group.
deal.public_shareholders_get: not stated — none of the schemes on file is a demerger that issues shares to the parent's shareholders. The Swara Baby transaction is an IPO: "an IPO aggregating up to Rs. 10,000 million, comprising of a Fresh Issue ... aggregating up to Rs. 5,000 million and an OFS ... aggregating to Rs. 5,000 million", with Brainbees selling up to Rs. 3,000 million of its own holding; the Solis Hygiene restructuring is "a part of intra-group restructuring"; and the Mush transaction "is being undertaken outside the scheme of arrangement".
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of existing grants in the IPO / schemes: not stated. New plan in the new entity: not stated. Documents state: "Mr. Sanket Hattimattur did not receive any remuneration from the Company during the financial year 2025-26. However, the ESOP Cost of options already granted to him was Rs. 2,01,15,927/-, for the financial year 2025-26."; his "Shareholding in the Company 6,34,780 Equity Shares of Rs. 2/- each (as at the date of this Notice)"; for the four Non-Executive Independent Directors, "Details of shareholding in the Company Nil". "It is further clarified that the Company, while calculating the limits under Section 197 of the Act for the managerial remuneration, has also considered the ESOP cost towards the ESOPs granted to Executive Director(s)." Consolidated "Employee share based payment expense 485.65 ... 2,236.13" (quarter and year ended March 31, 2026, INR million); among steps for improvement: "Reduction in ESOP cost." For the entity being listed: "A further adjustment of Share based payment expenses of Rs. 3.42 Million (as disclosed on Page No. 75 of Swara Baby's DRHP) gives an EBITDA of Rs. 1,445.7 Million". A "Brainbees ESOP Trust" is consolidated as a controlled trust. Exercise price or pricing date: not stated.
deal.insider_actions: Parent selling down into the IPO: "the Board of Directors of the Company has today i.e. July 01, 2026, considered and approved the participation in the Offer for Sale up to such number of equity shares of face value of Rs. 2/- each of Swara Baby, a Subsidiary of the Company, for an amount aggregating up to Rs. 3,000 million, held by the Company". Stated intent: "Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." and "We continue to remain invested and supportive of the business of Swara Baby and Swara Baby will continue to remain as Subsidiary Company of Brainbees." Buyers in the Mush sale: "Mr. Nihar Gosalia, existing shareholder of Mush and Mr. Vaishvik Brahmbhatt (“Proposed Buyers”) have agreed to acquire 13.45% and 38.09% shareholding, respectively." On buybacks (Q4 FY26 call, May 26, 2026): "Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions." No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of the parent's shares is stated; the Company states it has no identifiable promoter or promoter group.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Brainbees remains a multi-channel retailer of baby, kids and maternity products (India multi-channel, International, Globalbees, pre-schools), with IPO proceeds reallocated towards new leased warehouses in India, FirstCry-format modern stores, technology and sales & marketing
other_differences.separated_business: Swara Baby is contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with a global vision and "different capex and working capital needs", and will "bridge their own capital requirement" through the IPO
other_differences.quote: With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Brainbees is a declining share of Swara Baby's customer base; terms of trade between the two "has always have been at arms-length and will continue to remain the same post listing of Swara Baby"
other_differences.separated_business: Swara Baby's revenue dependence on Brainbees fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, having become the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in India's hygiene manufacturing industry
other_differences.quote: It has become the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in the fast-growing hygiene manufacturing industry in India, including baby diapers, adult diapers and sanitary napkins with a reducing proportion of revenue from operations coming from Brainbees as is evident from the disclosure made in Page No. 23 and 24 - Risk Factor No. 2 in the DRHP wherein the % of revenue from operations derived by Swara Baby from Brainbees has reduced from 27.03% in FY 24 to 22.64% in FY 26.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consolidated Brainbees: Profit before finance costs, depreciation, amortisation, exceptional items and tax expense of Rs. 4,466.71 million on revenue of Rs. 85,479.44 million for the year ended March 31, 2026, with a consolidated loss for the year of Rs. 2,036.58 million
other_differences.separated_business: Swara Baby FY26 EBITDA of Rs. 1,927.70 million (Rs. 1,442.28 million excluding other income; Rs. 1,445.7 million after adjusting share based payment expenses) on revenue from operations of Rs. 11,639 million
other_differences.quote: As disclosed in page nos .435 of the Swara Baby's DRHP, the EBITDA of Swara Baby for FY 26 is Rs. 1,927.70 Million. However, post adjustment of the other income (as disclosed on Page No. 75 of Swara Baby's DRHP) from the EBITDA, the EBITDA (excluding other income) becomes Rs. 1,442.28 Million.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Brainbees holds substantial cash and bank balances (consolidated cash and cash equivalents Rs. 2,462.83 million plus other bank balances Rs. 11,562.71 million as at March 31, 2026) and chose to monetise rather than fund the business from its own books
other_differences.separated_business: Swara Baby raises a fresh issue of up to Rs. 5,000 million in its own IPO to fund its capital requirements
other_differences.quote: Holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions. Even when a company has sufficient cash, management must periodically evaluate whether capital is optimally deployed.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: "The members are also informed that as on the date of this notice, the Company does not have any secured creditor and it has neither taken any loan from any bank or public financial institution, nor issued any debentures" (standalone); consolidated non-current borrowings Rs. 1,790.10 million and current borrowings Rs. 4,157.08 million as at March 31, 2026
other_differences.separated_business: not stated for Swara Baby
other_differences.quote: The members are also informed that as on the date of this notice, the Company does not have any secured creditor and it has neither taken any loan from any bank or public financial institution, nor issued any debentures, in view of the same, there is no default in payment of dues to the aforesaid parties.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Brainbees consolidated total tax expense of Rs. 374.31 million for the year ended March 31, 2026; standalone deferred tax credit of Rs. 134.03 million
other_differences.separated_business: On the Mush disposal, GlobalBees will recognise a capital gain and pay capital gains tax
other_differences.quote: The sale consideration receivable by GlobalBees from the transaction is in excess of the cost of acquisition of the GlobalBees' investment in Mush. Accordingly, GlobalBees shall recognise the resultant capital gain and discharge the applicable capital gain tax thereon.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consolidated revenue grew 12% year-on-year in FY26 with adjusted EBITDA up 24%; India multi-channel revenue grew 9% in FY26
other_differences.separated_business: Swara Baby turnover history: 2022-23: INR 537.29 Crore; 2023-24: INR 686.50 Crore; 2024-25: INR 545.14 Crore; FY26 revenue from operations Rs. 11,639 Million
other_differences.quote: Revenue for FY26 has grown by 12% year-on-year and adjusted EBITDA has increased by 24% year-on-year for the full year.

judge.what_is_spun: The Bio Pharma (Biopharma) Undertaking — bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses, plant-based APIs, nutraceuticals and nicotine derivatives
demerged_business_names: Ennature Biopharma division of India Glycols Limited
Ennature Bio Pharma Private Limited (former name)
judge.reason: "The demerger will result in the creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus," giving each dedicated management oversight and capital, investments and resources managed to its own business requirements.
judge.insiders: Promoter family controls it: Pragya Bhartia Barwale Managing Director 5 years (ran the division to Rs 200 crore revenue); father U.S. Bhartia and sister Pooja Jhaver non-executive directors; promoters held 3,99,67,854 of 6,70,26,765 IGL shares, voted 100% in favour.
judge.hidden_value: Tax cost apportionment assigns Ennature 20.61% of value on only ~2% of group revenue (FY26 segment revenue Rs 207.77 crore, EBIT Rs 7.23 crore, 3.5%, down from 20.76 crore EBIT in FY25), with segment assets Rs 426.42 crore versus liabilities Rs 92.49 crore — a depressed-margin, asset-heavy business management says is being rebuilt into branded nutraceuticals.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Smallest of three entities, only 2,23,42,255 shares on a 1-for-3 ratio creating odd lots; pharma/nutraceuticals unrelated to chemicals or spirits holders bought.
judge.listing_timeline: Per EBPL's letter dated 2 November 2026: listing and trading approvals received from BSE and NSE on November 02, 2026 for 2,23,42,255 equity shares of Rs 5/- each, with "Date of Commencement of Trading: November 04, 2026"; earlier, the 1 September 2026 news release said only that "The management of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will apply to BSE and NSE for listing of its shares on the respective bourses."
judge.read_next: Ennature Bio Pharma's Information Memorandum (board-approved 8 September 2026) — standalone balance sheet, debt allocation and segment margin trend.
judge.quote: Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.

Rupark Sarswat: A very good afternoon to everybody and thank you for joining us for this call. We have several topics on the agenda to talk about today. And of course, we will talk about the business performance and the nine-month highlights as well as highlights for the quarter. But equally importantly, we will also talk about the initiation of the scheme, which proposes to restructure IGL into three de-merged identities. So, what I will do to start off is to give you a little bit of highlights in terms of the business and we will come to the details later on. And a very high level view of the restructuring in terms of getting the gist of it. Then I will request my colleague, Mr. Anand Singhal, to take you through the details about the scheme, the demerger and how it's going to be implemented and the mechanisms that we will adopt to achieve that and so on. And then we will have some more commentary on various businesses. And after that, we will be happy to take your questions. So, let me, as usual, start with how our performance has been. I recognize that what we shared with you, our EBIT numbers

right now, and also taking the Bio Polymers business, which is a small business, from chemicals and putting it into Ennature Bio Pharma. They have slightly different priorities, different markets, different drivers, and therefore grow these businesses independently to create more value. I will pause now and I will request Mr. Singhal to brief you on the details of the scheme. Anand Singhal: Thank you, sir. So, now the board in its meeting on 4th February 2025 has largely approved two proposals. One is the merger of Kashipur Holdings Limited, which is a holding Company for India Glycols Limited and demerger of the business into two separate entities. One is the IGL Spirits, and the other one is Ennature Bio Pharma. So, presentation is already with everybody, so now everybody can see, but I will largely give you the brief on what is the proposal. Although CEO Sir has already given main things. So, now for the new companies, the India Glycols, which is the Chemical business largely, for 9MFY25 this Company has a turnover of Rs. 1,079 crores with an EBITDA margin of 13.6%. IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin. The Ennature Bio

The Ennature Bio Pharma, which has the biopharma, means the herbal division, plus the biopolymer, which is the Guar gum business, is having the turnover of Rs. 178 crores for the 9MFY25 with having an EBITDA margin of 14.9%. So, this is what the proposal for de-merging these three companies. The merger of Kashipur Holdings, holding Company with India Glycols, is largely keeping in mind that the promoters will have the direct shareholding of IGL in their names. The main benefits of the proposed scheme will be that the demerger will enable independent growth for each businesses. Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others. Will create a potential to unlock value for the shareholders by drawing focused investors. rationale.rationale: Management presented the separation as a focus-and-investor-base argument, not a rescue: India Glycols was running four structurally different businesses under one listing — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, including the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV into which IGL sells ethylene oxide), Potable Spirits (country liquor/IMIL plus IMFL, with the Amrut and Bacardi tie-ups), Bio-Fuel/ethanol-ENA sold at government-administered prices to OMCs, and Ennature Biopharma (thiocolchicoside, nicotine, nutraceuticals) with biopolymers. On 4 February 2025 the board approved splitting these into India Glycols (chemicals, glycols, bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the Clariant JV), IGL Spirits (spirits + bio-fuel/ENA) and Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymers), all three to be listed via the NCLT route. CEO Rupark Sarswat said the purpose was to run the companies differently with much more focus and to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors have different appetites; CFO Anand Singhal listed the benefits as independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, unlocking value by drawing focused investors, and clearer focus leading to improved management and resource allocation — while insisting the structure would not unduly increase the cost base. Scale was quantified with 9MFY25 numbers: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% (against FY24 BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, Bio-Fuel Rs 512 cr, Potable Spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross). Capital allocation was the hard constraint: big capex was frozen until after the demerger, long-term debt was pre-allocated with the SBI-led consortium (about Rs 500 cr chemicals / Rs 700 cr liquor out of Rs 1,200 cr in May 2025, restated to Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr out of about Rs 1,400 cr in November 2025), the Rs 467 cr preferential allotment at Rs 915/share in November 2025 went entirely into prepaying debt, and the credit rating was parked on watch-list with no upgrade possible until the demerger completed. Management simultaneously defended keeping bio-fuel with spirits rather than with chemicals, arguing captive multi-feedstock ethanol/ENA gives backward integration, quality control, scale and resilience even if it dilutes percentage margin, and that plant proximity and the EO-to-JV link preserve synergies. By FY26 the residual chemicals business was pitched as under-earning for want of focus and in-house cost streamlining, with the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 expected to make the chemicals entity debt-free. The scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad on 17 July 2026, became effective 1 September 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), with IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma listing and trading from 2–4 November 2026.
rationale.evolution: First disclosed on the 6 February 2025 call as a composite scheme that also folded promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL directly; by the 21 May 2025 call it was accompanied by a Rs 500 cr/Rs 700 cr debt split, and the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the KHL amalgamation to pursue the demerger alone. The 11 August 2025 and 18 November 2025 calls hardened the mechanics — three named entities, capex deferred to the post-demerger companies, debt restated to Rs 600 cr/Rs 800 cr, and a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-associates preferential issue to cut debt — while an investor on the August call openly questioned demerging a unit in degrowth. The 12 February 2026 call added that the credit rating would stay on watch-list and no sizeable capex would be sanctioned until completion, and the 18 May 2026 call was spent waiting on the NCLT hearing of 21 May. Shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes) and unsecured creditors (100% by value) approved on 24 March 2026; NCLT sanctioned on 17 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026, record date 2 September 2026, with trading in both new entities from 4 November 2026.

points.point: Rupark Sarswat first unveiled the three-way restructuring, initially to sit inside the IGL group before listing.
points.quote: So, essentially what we are trying to do is to restructure these businesses into three separate companies, for the time being within the IGL group.

points.point: The core stated reason: different businesses need different strategies and attract different pools of capital.
points.quote: And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.

points.point: CFO Anand Singhal framed one benefit as ring-fencing contagion between segments (relevant given Ennature's margin collapse and the chemicals/EO price squeeze).
points.quote: Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.

points.point: Anand gave the pro-forma 9MFY25 size and margins of each proposed entity — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6%, spirits+biofuel Rs 1,628 cr at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%.
points.quote: IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.

points.point: Anand confirmed the NCLT route, a 12-15 month timetable, 1 April 2026 appointed date and listing of all three entities.
points.quote: So, this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.

points.point: Investors pushed on listing of the biggest piece, noting over 75% of the business would sit in IGL Spirits.
points.quote: Sir, my first question regarding post restructuring, more than 75% of business comes from IGL Spirits. Is there any plan to list that entity?

points.point: Lender involvement: working capital and term loan allocation across the three companies had to be negotiated with the SBI-led consortium and was not yet confirmed.
points.quote: Rohit, regarding the working capital allocation to each Company and the term loan allocation, we are talking to the term lender, mainly the State Bank of India, who is the leader in our consortium banking.

points.point: Rupark stressed the split must not create duplicate overheads; corporate resources would stay shared with an allocation mechanism.
points.quote: The principle of demerger to start with is to continue to run the businesses under one umbrella, but differently as in separately from a strategic perspective, but not unduly increasing the cost base.

points.point: Asked by Saket Kapoor whether clubbing government-priced bio-fuel with liquor would dilute the IMFL valuation, Rupark defended it as backward integration, quality control and scale.
points.quote: Well, percentage margin is one factor, but the overall profitability and resilience of the business also improves.

points.point: First debt allocation disclosed: Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt split roughly Rs 500 cr to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (spirits) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals).
points.quote: Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.

points.point: Rupark restated the rationale and the exact clustering — spirits with ethanol/bio-fuel into IGL Spirits, chemicals with the Clariant JV, Ennature with biopolymers.
points.quote: The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.

points.point: Growth capex was explicitly deferred to the post-demerger entities; FY26 limited to rollover and Rs 40-50 cr maintenance capex.
points.quote: And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.

points.point: Investor pushback: a long-term shareholder challenged unlocking value by demerging a unit whose net margin had fallen from ~33% (2021) to ~2.4%.
points.quote: We are planning to unlock shareholder value by demerging our business units when there is extreme degrowth in that business.

points.point: Entity-level debt restated: of about Rs 1,400 cr long-term debt, Rs 600 cr to India Glycols and Rs 800 cr to IGL Spirits, with the Rs 467 cr raise plus Rs 180 cr scheduled repayment cutting both proportionately.
points.quote: INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.

points.point: The Rs 467 cr preferential issue at Rs 915/share to promoters, friends and relatives was earmarked entirely for debt reduction ahead of the split.
points.quote: So, this is the update, and the money which whatever we will receive out of this preferential will be utilized for the reduction of the term loan.

points.point: Rupark tied the restructuring to the broader strategy of focusing on bio-based ingredients and consumer/lifestyle value capture.
points.quote: And one of the outcomes of that is in the last few years and now once again, how we've been reorganizing and restructuring our businesses to bring the necessary focus.

points.point: Rating agencies had placed IGL on watch-list because of the demerger; no upgrade (and hence no full benefit of the Rs 582 cr debt reduction) until completion.
points.quote: So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens.

points.point: Capex remained gated on the demerger even after the Rs 467 cr raise and planned FY26 closing term debt of about Rs 1,100 cr.
points.quote: Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.

points.point: Rupark argued the chemicals business (FY26 net revenue Rs 1,203 cr, down 10.4%, EBIT Rs 141 cr, margin 11.7%) is understated and needs in-house cost streamlining and dedicated focus.
points.quote: Now, there is, if you look at EBITDA without adjusting the other income and probably some streamlining that is required in-house, we will start to see that the quality of the Chemicals business is probably going to be better than this going forward.

points.point: Anand said the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 would fund term-loan repayment and leave the chemicals entity debt-free.
points.quote: So, in '28-'29, I'm hopeful that the Chemical business will be totally debt-free.

points.point: Investors were tracking the NCLT timetable; management expected the sanction order around 21 May/early June 2026, then ROC filing.
points.quote: 21st May, we are hopeful that we will get the order for the demerger of the division.

points.point: Plan change: the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the amalgamation of promoter vehicle Kashipur Holdings Limited and pursued the demerger alone, with appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: The earlier proposal for the amalgamation of KHL into the Company will no longer form part of the Scheme being pursued.

points.point: The 1 September 2026 news release stated the benefit as dedicated focus and better oversight and resource allocation for each of the three companies.
points.quote: Each company will have a dedicated focus, enabling improved management oversight and more efficient allocation of resources towards growth.

points.point: The release made the capital-allocation argument explicit — each entity sizing its own capital and investment needs.
points.quote: In addition, each company will be able to manage its capital, investments and resources based on its specific business requirements, thereby enabling more efficient utilisation of capital.

points.point: Share entitlement: 1 IGL Spirits share for every 1 IGL share, and 1 Ennature Bio Pharma share for every 3 IGL shares (6,70,26,765 and 2,23,42,255 shares of Rs 5 allotted on 8 September 2026).

rationale.what_management_expects: Chemicals: cost streamlining, higher-value performance chemicals, improving EBIT (11.7% FY26), JV stake sale funding a debt-free unit by FY29. IGL Spirits: premiumisation toward ~22% EBIT margins on captive ENA, geographic and CSD expansion. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals margin recovery. All three: dedicated focus, own capital allocation, focused investors, value unlock.
rationale.gaps: Never quantified: value unlock, standalone corporate costs, inter-company ENA/EO transfer pricing, shared Kashipur utilities, debt-covenant consents; no investor, lender or partner was named as having requested it.

"Pre and post-shareholding pattern of EBL upon demerger": Promoters Pre-Scheme 10,000 (100%) → Post-Scheme 62,97,011 (61.01%); Public Nil → 40,23,489 (38.99%); Total 10,000 → 1,03,20,500. "Pre and post-shareholding pattern of ISL upon demerger": Promoters Pre-Scheme 10,000 (100%) → Post-Scheme 1,88,91,032 (61.01%); Public Nil → 1,20,70,468 (38.99%); Total 10,000 → 3,09,61,500 (Scheme of Arrangement intimation, 16th May 2025; shares then of INR 10 face value, later updated to INR 5 after the stock split). For the parent: "Pre and post-shareholding pattern of IGL": Promoters 1,88,91,032 (61.01) → 1,88,91,032 (61.01); Public 1,20,70,468 (38.99) → 1,20,70,468 (38.99). Under the withdrawn 2025 Composite Scheme the corresponding post-scheme promoter holdings were 60.27% in IGL, EBL and ISL. "There will be no adverse implication on the existing public shareholders of Transferee Company as they will continue to own the same percentage of shares in the Company."
deal.public_shareholders_get: "Each Shareholder of India Glycols on the record date of September 2, 2026, will be enƒtled to receive one equity share of IGL Spirits Limited for every one equity share held in India Glycols Limited, and one equity share of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited for every three equity shares held in India Glycols Limited." "As a result, a Shareholder holding 300 India Glycols shares on September 2, 2026, will be enƒtled to receive 300 equity shares of IGL Spirits Limited and 100 equity share of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited, resulƒng a total of 700 shares across the three enƒƒes, including the 300 equity shares held in India Glycols Limited." Under the withdrawn 2025 Composite Scheme, KHL shareholders were additionally to receive "1 (One) Equity Share having face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each, for every 1(one) equity share held by KHL in IGL to shareholders of KHL in proportion to their shareholding in KHL."
deal.management_incentives: not stated
deal.insider_actions: Preferential issue to promoters: "IGL has, on 24th November, 2025, successfully allotted, on preferential basis 51,03,765 Equity Shares of Face Value Rs. 5/- each, at an issue price of Rs. 915/- per Equity Share (Including a premium of Rs. 910/-per Equity Share), aggregating to Rs. 466.99 Crore, for cash consideration, as approved earlier by the Board of Directors in its meeting held on 16th October, 2025 and subsequently by the Members at their Extraordinary General Meeting held on 12th November, 2025." "Of the newly issued Equity Shares, Kashipur Holdings Limited (KHL), part of the Promoter Group, was allotted 21,85,790 Equity Shared and 29,17,975 Equity Shares have been allotted to various funds and other investors belonging to the Non-Promoter category." "The funds raised from this preferential issue will be used to reduce IGL's overall debt including term loans and working capital by 31st March, 2026." On the Nov 2025 call: "the company has decided to come out with the preferential allotment to the promoters, friends and relatives." Promoter consolidation: "Acquisition of additional 37,79,819 equity shares by Kashipur Holdings Limited, Promoter Company representing 12.21% of the total paid-up capital of the Company from below mentioned Promoter group entities." — "Consequently, Kashipur Holdings Limited has become the Holding Company of India Glycols Limited w.e.f. 2nd December, 2024." Scheme vote: Promoter and Promoter Group cast 3,99,67,854 votes, 100% in favour, at the court-convened meeting on 24th March 2026. No promoter sale or pledge is stated.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: India Glycols Limited (remaining entity): revenue from operations 354.64 and EBITDA 40.22 for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (INR Crores); Chemicals net revenue INR1,203 crores in FY26, down 10.4%
other_differences.separated_business: IGL Spirits Limited: revenue from operations 2,541.89, EBITDA 120.10; Ennature Bio Pharma Limited: revenue from operations 90.39, EBITDA 9.98 for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (INR Crores)
other_differences.quote: Further, Key details of 3 companies for the quarter ended June 30,2026 are as under:- Company Name Revenue from operations EBITDA India Glycols Limited 354.64 40.22 IGL Spirits Limited 2,541.89 120.10 Ennature Bio Pharma Limited 90.39 9.98

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Chemicals (Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals, the remaining business): "net revenue of INR1,203 crores in FY26, which is down 10.4%, but our EBIT at INR141 crores is up 12.5% and our EBIT margins are up to 11.7%"
other_differences.separated_business: Potable Spirits FY26 EBIT margin materially higher (EBIT INR285 crores on INR1,331 crores, Q4 EBIT margin 22.1%); Bio-Fuels FY26 EBIT margin 7.8% with EBIT up 103.3%; Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure (Q3 FY26 EBIT margin 4.1%, 9M FY26 2.9%)
other_differences.quote: As far as the Potable Spirit business is concerned, we posted a top-line of INR1,331 crores in FY26, up 14.4% and an EBIT of INR285 crores, which is up 11.1%.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: About INR 600 crores of long-term debt allocated to India Glycols Limited; management expects "the Chemical business will be totally debt-free" in FY28-29 after the planned sale of a further 24% of the joint venture equity
other_differences.separated_business: About INR 800 crores of long-term debt allocated to IGL Spirits Limited; of FY26-27 normal term-loan repayment of INR 268 crores, "in liquor, it is INR168 crores, and INR100 crores in Chemical"
other_differences.quote: So, in these two companies, India Glycols and IGL Spirits, the segregation what we have done as of date is about INR 600 crores and INR 800 crores. INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Chemicals capex described as incremental and modular: "we are talking about in the range of maybe INR 10 crores to INR 50 crore kind of CAPEX to start with"; plant shutdown 17th March to 2nd April 2026 for catalyst change reduced production and sales
other_differences.separated_business: Of roughly INR830 crores of FY26 capital expenditure, about INR 400 crores was the two grain distilleries (Gorakhpur and Kashipur) that sit in the Spirits and Biofuel Undertaking
other_differences.quote: Actually, there are two distilleries largely, which are the main capital expenditure. One is the grain distillery in Gorakhpur, and one is the grain distillery in Kashipur.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: The Income Tax Department "is permitted to retain recourse for recovery in respect of demand and any other future liabilities of the Demerged Company in respect of the assets sought to be transferred under the Scheme"; counsel noted "the Petitioner Company No.1 which is a demerging company and remains in existence post approval" would be bound by any outstanding demand (Rs.27,890/- outstanding per demand raised on 06th May, 2026)
other_differences.separated_business: Tax liabilities, pending appeals and compliances relating to the Biopharma Undertaking and the Spirits and Biofuel Undertaking transfer to the respective Resulting Company from the Appointed Date, 01.04.2026
other_differences.quote: The respective Resulting Company shall be responsible for paying any tax liability of the Demerged Company relating to the respective Demerged Undertaking, if any, pending on the Appointed Date, i.e., 01.04.2026 or determined by the Income Tax Department after the Appointed Date, i.e., 01.04.2026.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: INR 466.99 crore preferential issue proceeds plus internal accruals used to prepay about INR804 crores of debt in Q4 FY26, saving about INR20 crores of interest; other income of the remaining business includes the Clariant joint venture share (INR20.60 crores for the quarter ended 30 June 2026)
other_differences.separated_business: not stated
other_differences.quote: So, this INR804 crores include the long-term debt, the working capital, and the short-term loans resulting in INR20 crores saving in the interest cost, which is already there in the results.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Consolidated India Glycols Limited before the demerger; management also notes debt-to-equity down from 0.7x in FY23 to 0.5x in FY26 and interest coverage up from 2.3x to 3.0x
other_differences.separated_business: not stated (no separate return-on-capital figures given for the demerged undertakings)
other_differences.quote: And if you look at ROCE over the last few years, it has gone from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.9% in FY26, and RONW has gone up from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.3% in FY26.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Segment assets as at 30.06.2026 (standalone): Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals 3,514.26; segment liabilities 577.54 (INR Crores)
other_differences.separated_business: Segment assets as at 30.06.2026 (standalone): Potable Spirits 632.16, Bio-Fuel 1,538.06, Ennature Biopharma 417.28; segment liabilities Potable Spirits 385.41, Bio-Fuel 100.20, Ennature Biopharma 107.57 (INR Crores)
other_differences.quote: Segment assets -Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals 3,514.26 -Potable Spirits 632.16 -Ennature Biopharma 417.28 -Bio- Fuel 1,538.06 -Unallocated 44.35 Total 6,146.11

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: not stated
other_differences.separated_business: IMFL expansion within the Spirits business is described as working-capital heavy, which is why the company prioritises government-corporation markets where payment is secure
other_differences.quote: We are very cautious about giving credit. So, our first focus is on the corporation-led markets in particular where the money is secure, because the working capital required for IMFL is very high.

The challenge of cost pressures like our chemical business has continued on the joint venture. And by and large, the joint venture has been focusing on formulated products, indigenizing products in India, and also looking at exports from India for bio-based products, fetching us some premium. So, there is some pressure there, but the joint venture is functioning well. And, we believe that as we do think about improving ethanol costs, including going back to the softened ethanol prices of internationally imported ethanol, that should help the joint venture. In terms of headlines for our business units, if you talk about bio-based specialties and performance chemical, I think we are moving towards, calling it, chemicals and biofuels, as biofuels becomes a significant part of what we do in the space, so this will continue to drive top line. As I said, we have been somewhat, let’s say, being doing business in the sense that we have done business, which was not profitable, which we had to do for various reasons. And things like reduction in freight, reduction in coal costs have also helped improve our margins. And, yes, it is an important sector for us in bio-based MEG. Bio-based MEG has been, kind of flat or has been under pressure in terms of volumes. But the development that we go seeing into the future is that the market for bio-based MEG will continue. Bio-based MEG goes into manufacture of polyester or PET, there was a feeling that recycled PET will replace a lot of bio-based MEG. We see that recycled PET has its own challenges, including the number of recycles that you can do. So, we will continue to see some traction for bio-based MEG in its own way. World is also working on 100% bio-based PET, which include bio-MEG and, bio-based PTA, we are engaged with those people who are working on those projects and as those materialize in the next maybe couple of years that will be another interesting growth period. I have already spoken about what has happened in the portable space. In the Ennature Biopharma space, it is a relatively smaller segment for us. The headline is that, whilst we've been under some pressure for sales, largely because there's a lot of competition in nicotine and there's a lot of cost pressure there, which has also eroded our margins. However, we continue to maintain our position in Thiocolchicoside. We have our sourcing of raw materials well covered over there. And there is a push for data quantities and demand in the market. And as far as the Kashipur facility where we were converting some of our given assets that were concerned, it is looking at the demand scenario. What we are also doing for nicotine is working with and because it is in the pharma space and similar space, et cetera. So, we are expecting a good traction in those products. And we have already established an office in Houston, America. And the person who is already there, is in the contact of the many agents to have the better turnover in the next coming quarters.

So Saket, just to add to what Manish said, as you see, nicotine sales have started to increase. In terms of branded ingredients, Gingeren and asparagine have been launched in supply chain in U.S. with clinical data, and I think that will strengthen NHS's global market presence. Maxicuma NOP organic certification and Korea registration is underway, which will also help enhance sales and positioning across key markets. I mentioned to you about some of the challenges. In this business, we are dependent on how the developed markets are picking up, but the efforts are on to build standardized ingredients, improved quality, better certification, better registration, including markets like Taiwan, etcetera. So, all in all, we are focused on the strategy, we realize we are going through a bit of a challenging time. But as you know, the nutraceuticals and the herbal by fundamentally, it's a good business as long as you continue to innovate, give differentiated products, build a brand around it, get your registrations and get your products into good formulations across the world.
Rating is in process. Shortly, you will get. But only thing is because of the demerger, the rating is in watch list.

So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens. So, any improvement in the rating you will see only after the completion of the demerger. Till that time, the rating will be the same, and we will continue to be in watch list.

Yes, good afternoon, Nitin, and thank you for hosting this call. Also, my apologies for us starting a little late. And I'm also joined by one of our other colleagues, Akshay Bansal, who Heads the Ennature Biopharma business, and Ankur due to some emergency is not here. So, nevertheless, I think I have a good year to report, because we are talking about the annual performance. So, as you have probably seen the numbers, we have had gross revenues of INR9,827 crores, which is up 8.7%. Net revenues of INR4,211 crores, which is up 11.8%. Now, the revenue growth has been led to a large extent by the growth in Potable Spirits and Bio- Fuels, and we will talk about these segment a little bit subsequently. EBITDA has been INR654 crores, which is up 24.5% over last year. And the EBITDA margin itself is up to 15.5%, up 162 basis points. And we have seen EBITDA growth more or less across the business. The significant segments of Potable Spirits, Bio-Fuels, as well as Chemicals have driven the margin improvement, particularly led by Chemicals and Bio-Fuels. At a PAT level, we are posting INR293 crores, which is up 26.8%, and the PAT margin at 6.9% is also 84 basis points up. So all in all, a strong operating performance, and therefore, also resulting in a good increase in profitability. If you look at the quarter, we have a net revenue of INR976 crores, which is up 13.1% for the same quarter prior year. […] In Chemicals, we've seen a bit of a dip in sales, but having said that, I think we saw significant uptick in terms of the margin percentages as well as growth in overall margin. Now, that's based on some readjustments in the business, and letting go of some low margin businesses, but we continue to focus on higher value-added Chemicals. In short, our performance Chemicals portfolio has started to do well, though it's a smaller part of the overall Chemicals business, but our pipeline is strong and we expect that it will continue to drive good growth in Chemicals. In Ennature Biopharma, you would hear later as well, the top-line by and large has been stable despite a relatively challenging global and macroeconomic environment, as well as cost pressures. But the silver lining is that we've been acquiring new customers and the progress that has been made in terms of launching of branded nutraceuticals, getting more standards and certificates, etcetera is good, and we expect that the business will recover and do well in the times to come. Now, as I report this year, I may like to point out that we've had an interesting journey over the last few years. So, I’ll talk about some ratios, our EBITDA in the year FY22 was 9.6%, in FY23 it became 11.9%, in FY24 it became 12.9%, in FY25 it became 13.9%, and in FY26 it became 15.5%. […] Now, there is, if you look at EBITDA without adjusting the other income and probably some streamlining that is required in-house, we will start to see that the quality of the Chemicals business is probably going to be better than this going forward. As far as the Potable Spirit business is concerned, we posted a top-line of INR1,331 crores in FY26, up 14.4% and an EBIT of INR285 crores, which is up 11.1%. For the Bio-Fuels business, an excellent year with the 40.9% growth delivering a top-line of INR1,470 crores in FY26 and an EBIT of INR115 crores, which is nearly double, which is up 103.3% and an EBIT margin of 7.8%. Ennature Biopharma, as I mentioned, top-line has more or less been similar to last year, but margins have been under pressure. And we will talk about the actions, which we are taking and India Glycols Limited May 18, 2026 making good progress on, which should see this business becoming stronger in this year, as well as the years going forward. For the quarter, the net revenue for Chemicals is up 18.8% at INR301 crores. The EBIT is at INR37 crores, is up 37.4%, and EBIT margins are 12.2%. And this is given some of the factors that I spoke about, the business, in my opinion, will start to look better going forward. In Potable Spirits, we posted a top-line of INR306 crores for the quarter, up 7.9%, whereas, margins for the quarter were somewhat under pressure, but that was a bit of an odd quarter in the last year, at INR68 crores. Overall, EBIT margins were very good at 22.1%. For Bio-Fuels, for the quarter, 11.6% growth posting a top-line of INR305 crores and an EBIT of INR30 crores, which is up 90.0% with an EBIT margin of 9.9%. Ennature Biopharma saw a turnaround as far as the top-line is concerned with a 23.2% growth in the last quarter, but an EBIT of INR3 crores, as I said, the margins have continued to be under pressure. Talking about a few other things, I spoke about one of the things that we often talk about, which is the EO price and the ethanol price and the relative price of EO to Reliance's EO price, because it impacts several of our businesses. So, we saw a period and for the last couple of months, we have been competitive as far as Reliance's EO price is concerned and that is because of rising crude prices and also ample availability of ethanol within India. And we'll talk about the ethanol capacity and the fact that we have now a little more than the capacity that Bio-Fuels consumed in India. […] Now, the reason I say this is that we have seen a period of lower crude prices and if you go back before 2021, for a period of 15 years, we were equal or less than Reliance's EO price. So, I do not know, which period to call abnormal, but we did see significantly lower crude prices for a period of time. India Glycols Limited May 18, 2026 Related to this is also the ethanol price trend that we monitor. It is important to several of our businesses; Chemicals, Potable Spirits, Bio-Fuels. Because of a number of factors including freight and others, the imported ethanol prices in India went up quite significantly, whereas, the domestic prices have more or less been stable or maybe even saw a bit of a dip. Now, given the fact that we have good ethanol capacities in-house, we talked about a 3x3 strategy and the fact that we have grain, molasses-based, as well as the option to import, it allows us to also use in-house ethanol for our Chemicals as an intermediate without worrying too much about excess ethanol capacity. So, I think that strategy, which allowed us to tide over some of the difficult times, also is helping us right now because we've toned down our imports quite significantly and we've been able to support our Chemical business to a large extent by ethanol produced in-house. So, talking about the segment, which is in higher spirits these days, which is definitely Potable Spirits, to start with, continued to have a very good year with 14.4% top-line growth. As I mentioned, 11.1% EBIT growth and improvement in EBIT margin as well. So, we've made a strong entry in the CSD business, Bunty and Bubbly continues to remain the highest selling brand in India. We've maintained our market leadership position, as far as Indian Made Indian Liquor is concerned in UP and Uttarakhand. […] We saw some growth in the glycol space and we've maintained our market in Southeast Asia despite the challenges. I don't even think that I should talk about those as separate challenges right now, because the Reliance MEG, we don't compete with. I think the point here is that the niche customers have continued to buy glycols from us and have continued to grow. Then coming to Ennature Biopharma, we spoke about the numbers in terms of growth being steady, in terms of top-line, a nominal degrowth is what we saw, however, margins being under pressure. So, the Q4 revenue performance saw a strong comeback as I mentioned driven by certain increase in Thiocolchicoside prices, recovery of the nicotine business, and strong nutraceutical numbers. We've strengthened our branded nutraceuticals portfolio through global certifications, clinically backed ingredient launches. And we expect that the business will come back given the actions that we are doing in the times to come both in terms of volume as well as profitability.

Okay, sir. Secondly, sir, on the Potable Spirit segment, the EBIT is down Q-o-Q. We say we are continuously moving towards premiumization, and so sir, my first question is what is the split between country liquor and IMFL, and how do you see it going forward? But we have definite focus to improve the IMFL part of it without losing focus of the IMIL part. With the result that, you know, we are now, I would like to tell you what the steps are we are taking for increasing the IMFL segment, particularly premium segment. First of all, we take satisfaction in mentioning that two of our key brands, that is Soulmate Whisky, which is a Millionaire Case Brand, also our Zumba Lemoni, which is very popular in India Glycols Limited May 18, 2026 the market have been introduced in the CSD and we've already started supplies in the entire country. For the benefit of those who are not very much familiar with CSD details, this is a lifetime registration, and which is obtained after a lot of screenings by the armed forces, because it is meant for the consumption of the Indian military. So, this is one. And also, a third brand of ours, that is Zumba Black, which is the mainstay business, the rum, black rum of the military, also has cleared the preliminary screening committee, PSC we call it, which consists of the entire board of the administration of CSD. In other words, in principle, they have accepted our third brand also, of course, final board approval will be awaited. It will take little time, but this is also very positive news. Now, our growth, as our CEO rightly said, has been very strong in the IMFL, particularly premium segments. And we expect to continue to grow rapidly in the IMFL premium segment. Now, how this is possible is in two ways. The first point is that we are taking more geographical coverage. We started with Kerala market. We are very cautious about giving credit. So, our first focus is on the corporation-led markets in particular where the money is secure, because the working capital required for IMFL is very high. So, we want to go steadily but with very firm grounding. So, Kerala has given us very good response. We introduced our new brandy in Kerala, and we used a French blend, which took us lot of time, lot of research was done. We don't introduce brands off the cuff. We do a lot of research, and we do it both internally and externally. So, the brand is well-accepted in the market. Then we have started business in our other states and very soon we will be doing in Andhra Pradesh and other markets like Rajasthan. So, one, is geographical coverage. And second is with new brands. As our CEO rightly said, we have introduced brands like Jamun and Cranberry Vodka, which are in demand, or if I may use the word, which are in vogue. So, because of we being a tropical country, Jamun and Cranberry are well-accepted. We have two more brands in the offering, but for obvious reasons we cannot disclose at this stage, but very soon they will see the light of the day. So, both geographically, as well as new brands wil l stem the growth to high double digits, and we expect to consolidate our position in the markets like Delhi, UP, Uttarakhand, Kerala, and other markets very soon. Most important is that we have inbuilt capacity, see as opposed to competition, if I may say, we have an inherent advantage where we do not use even one liter of ENA for our brands and we have enough inbuilt capacity to use our ENA. For the benefit of those who may not be aware, our ENA goes to top multinational companies including Radico and Tilaknagar and Diageo for now, and Bacardi, which is our partner since over 15 years. So, there is no reason why we should not be able to make our brands as good or better than competition. So, our ingredients are good, we have laid the foundation of our new India Glycols Limited May 18, 2026 brands, and I'm sure in times to come, we will have a very strong double-digit growth. So any other questions?
Raju ji, can I just add to it?

So, just to share some data with you, UP is one of the largest liquor market where for IMFL, if I am not wrong, Manish correct me, our top-line growth last year was 25%, that's it. As, you know, we are also the first company ever to start doing third-party bottling for Bacardi in Kashipur. In addition to that, I think the fact that we've got a strong base in terms of Indian Made Indian Liquor is a good way for us to make our presence felt and graduate some of our customers. In addition, I think our approvals in CSD, as well as paramilitary, we think would be growth drivers. And the traction that we have seen with the inorganic growth in terms of acquisition of Amrut brand is also good, which allows us to state with some confidence that we will continue to drive premiumization in our portfolio, which will not only drive growth but also make the business richer in terms of margins.

Yes. If I may just add and supplement to what our CEO said. See, now we are poised for growth, because now we've got the entire range of brands. Our Soulmate Whisky, which is our flagship brand, is a Millionaire Case Brand. We've got our Vodka, which is Amazing Vodka with various Flavors including Cranberry and Jamun, which are doing very well, which are a challenger brand to the leader brand. We've got our Zumba Lemoni, which is again number two brand in that segment. And now it is in public domain, so I can clearly say that we've got in few states of the north, we've got the distribution rights of our Amrut luxury malts, which are world famous and loved India Glycols Limited May 18, 2026 all over the world. There was unmet demand for these brands. So, it is slightly more than distribution, but for obvious reasons I cannot disclose, but we have got the entire range now. So, when our sales guy goes, he has a regular range brand up to th ese single malts. The future is in premiumization, so we are in a good position to attend to the needs of all segments.

Right, sir. If I may just add one more point and join the queue is about the Ennature Biopharma. So that segment also the profitability has improved, and also in your presentation, sir, the outlook is mentioned that the segment is expected to perform well in future on account of good customer addition, volume growth, and price realization. So if you could just throw some more color, and when will this segment achieve, sir, earlier when we used to post a higher EBITDA profitability, I think the environment has changed significantly in our product profile. How is this segment going to perform?

So, Saket, this is Akshay here. So, basically, the division was originally dependent on one of the products, which has the highs and downs of the price in terms of the total contribution to the net margin, and as well as the top-line. But as a company, what we have done in last three years, we have diversified the business. So, more focus has come to the highly growing market in nutraceutical, which is basically the branded nutraceutical segment. And we have invested very significantly on some of the clinicals, for the highly growing indications of women's health and some other indications. So already we have completed some of the studies in last one year and there are a couple of more studies, which are ongoing and that is likely to be completed by this financial year. And then we have a target focus on multi-geography presence in terms of right now we already have a strong presence in Asia Pacific, but we are also trying to get hold of US market, which is one of the biggest markets. And then we also have opened our office very recently for us to have that trajectory and momentum in US. So, this is broadly in terms of Ennature Biopharma, we are on the right trajectory. We are investing in higher growth component both in terms of our manufacturing capability, and also the customer acquisition in various market, and so we'll continue to remain in that.

Only on the profitability front, can you give some more color, how will the profitability shape, I think so last time, because of some products and some new plants were also commissioned, because of which the realizations were down and so were the profits. So, broadly, if you look at where we started this business, we had some of the customers, which are from the commodity side, but again they are volume-based driven customers and that has given a good top-line. But strategically we have taken a very strategic shift in last three years for us to shift to more value-added customers to sustain for the long-term growth and to contribute on the profitability. So, this is broadly in terms of nicotine, I mean, I would say, the business right now is in the focus, but in terms of the EBITDA improvement, we may not see the significant improvement in this financial year, but definitely the investment and the growth and the customer acquisition what we're doing right now is going to contribute towards more of EBITDA and the profitability of the particular this Ennature Biopharma segment.
Okay, sir. So, my second question on the scheme of arrangement is submitted by NCLT. I think the hearing is expected, 21st of May. Is there any expected timeline for the completion of demerger?

21st May, we are hopeful that we will get the order for the demerger of the division. And another hope is that in first 10 days of the June we will get the order. So, once we get the order, we will start working for filing that in ROC and the other matters, which is related.
Okay. Got it, sir. Thank you.

judge.what_is_spun: The Power Evacuation Business (substation/evacuation infrastructure undertaking) of Inox Green, demerged into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited
demerged_business_names: Resco Global Wind Services Limited (formerly known as)
Resco Global Wind Services Private Limited
judge.reason: Segregation of distinct business verticals with separate risks, rewards and investors; consolidation of Power Evacuation Business into IRSL to unlock value and lend enhanced focus; establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, creating two listed entities
judge.insiders: Inox Wind Limited, promoter and holding company, directly holds 51.13% of Inox Green; IRSL shares issued pro-rata to the same shareholders. Director/KMP stakes tiny (Bindu Saxena 12,640 shares). No separate incentive scheme stated.
judge.hidden_value: Removing ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation leaves Inox Green a pure-play O&M business with ~50% EBITDA margins, tax shield and FY27 EBITDA guidance above Rs 600 crore; IRSL holds the capital-heavy, leveraged evacuation assets, losses and a Rs 96.8 crore tax demand
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held - small odd-lot stakes; 4,89,82,030 shares spread to O&M holders; different industry (EPC/power evacuation), loss-making, heavily indebted
judge.listing_timeline: Feb 13, 2026 call: NCLT approval 'should come in a month or so' and 'Post receiving of the NCLT approval, it is 1 to 1-1/2 month process for the listing of the company... within 3-odd months, 2-3 months, it should get on the process' - 'but don't take it as a commitment'. May 29, 2026 call: 'IRSL will be automatically listed on the stock exchange post receipt of all the approvals.' Aug 24, 2026: after allotment of 4,89,82,030 shares, 'IRSL is taking necessary steps for crediting the aforesaid equity shares to the respective demat accounts... and for obtaining the listing and trading approvals for the said equity shares from the Stock Exchanges.' No completed listing date stated through the latest filing (Oct 7, 2026).
judge.read_next: IRSL listing/trading approval intimation and its standalone financials - secured/unsecured debt and the Rs 96.80 crore AY2023-24 tax demand
judge.quote: Such consolidation in a single entity will lend enhanced focus to the Power Evacuation business.
