rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of Inox Green Energy Services Ltd's (IGESL) power evacuation / substation and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services), leaving IGESL a pure-play renewable O&M company and consolidating all evacuation/EPC infrastructure in IRSL, which gets automatically listed. Management's core explanation is historical and structural: when IGESL was spun out of Inox Wind, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco, but the already-commissioned substations and transmission lines could not be moved because, as Devansh Jain said in Aug 2024, shifting them 'would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business'; so IGESL's balance sheet stayed 'unnecessarily inflated' with assets on which it is 'actually the trustee', while all new substations were being built in Resco anyway ('no future CapEx under Inox Green at all', Feb 2024). The financial fix they repeatedly quantified: a gross block of ~INR 1,000 crore (net block ~INR 750 crore, Aug 2024) leaves IGESL, annual depreciation of ~INR 50-55 crore (~INR 13-17 crore a quarter) is eliminated, PBT rises by that amount, and only ~INR 3-5 crore a quarter (~INR 10 crore a year, Feb 2026) of revenue goes out with virtually no cost and no interest moving — Akhil Jindal put the benefit at '~INR 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis' (Nov 2024), turning reported PAT of ~INR 6 crore into ~INR 18-20 crore. They stressed the evacuation assets are not needed for O&M ('not required for O&M services per se... that is required for further providing a turnkey solution'), so IGESL becomes a zero-capex, asset-light annuity business where EBITDA equals PBT and cash PAT, helped by a ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax-loss shield that stays at company level, with 'significant improvement in ROE and ROCE' (Jun 2026). The Scheme's own rationale adds that risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are 'separate and distinct' for O&M versus power evacuation, that the evacuation business 'is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders', that consolidating it into IRSL (which already does the same business) unlocks value and lends enhanced focus, and that the result is two listed entities each free to pursue its own strategy. On the IRSL side, management argued the infrastructure is itself a high-value platform — INR 175 crore raised at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation (Sep 2025), ~10 GW of 'plug and play' evacuation infra made more valuable by the CERC hybridisation amendment — and that listing it 'will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green' (Nov 2025). The push came from the promoters/board (valuers appointed Aug-Nov 2024, scheme approved 13 Nov 2024) with investors on calls repeatedly asking about rationalising subsidiaries and value unlocking; Akhil Jindal framed the purpose as giving shareholders optionality — 'a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business' — and shareholders, warrant holders, secured and unsecured creditors all approved it before NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned it.
rationale.evolution: On the Feb 2024 call the idea did not exist yet; management only explained that all future common-infra capex would sit in Resco, not Inox Green, while legacy depreciation ran on. By the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Oct 25, 2024) calls the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business, pitched as a 'cleaner and asset-light balance sheet' worth ~INR 12 crore a quarter to the bottom line, and the board approved the Scheme on 13 Nov 2024; in Feb 2025 (Jan 31, 2025) Akhil Jindal said exchange approvals were due in February and NCLT would take 6-9 months, with IGESL holders getting ~20% of the renamed Inox Renewable Solutions. By Sep 2025 (Sep 1, 2025) stock-exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad (approval expected in 2-3 quarters), IRSL had raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the CERC hybridisation ruling made its infra far more valuable; Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) reported shareholder and creditor approval, and Feb 2026 (Feb 13, 2026) said hearings were in final stages with listing 2-3 months out. NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 13 Mar 2026, it became effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 (May 29, 2026) call management confirmed approval and booked the benefits as done — INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore depreciation gone, ROE/ROCE improved — while refusing to give IRSL's standalone top line or EBITDA until listing; the record date was 1 Aug 2026 and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares were allotted on 24 Aug 2026.

points.point: Pre-demerger baseline: management explained IGESL carries legacy substation gross block (4 GW capacity, 3 GW commissioned) with ~INR 13 crore quarterly depreciation, while all future common-infrastructure capex is being incurred in Resco Global, a 100% subsidiary of Inox Wind.
points.quote: So, no future CapEx under Inox Green at all. So, whatever is the depreciation which is being incurred on a quarterly basis will continue until and unless our net block gets consumed.

points.point: Board appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger; Mathusudhana framed it as producing a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet whose main benefit is eliminating depreciation.
points.quote: The proposed demerger will significantly add value through depreciation elimination.

points.point: Devansh Jain gave the historical reason the assets were stranded in IGESL: at the time of the EPC slump sale to Resco, only uncommissioned assets moved, and commissioned substations could not be shifted without re-opening contracts with over 200 customers.
points.quote: We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.

points.point: He added that IGESL's balance sheet was inflated by assets it merely holds as trustee (net block ~INR 750 crore), and that the remaining business is a zero-capex annuity with no land bank or future evacuation capex.
points.quote: Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.

points.point: Akhil Jindal quantified the P&L effect for Pritesh Chheda: the whole depreciation goes, only INR 3-4 crore of quarterly revenue leaves, and IGESL shareholders receive Resco shares in lieu, with valuation yet to be fixed.
points.quote: Excluding the substation business, the revenue would be down by around Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores on a quarterly basis, and the whole depreciation will go away. So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.

points.point: Mathusudhana answered Bhavik Shah's objection that the transferred assets would come back as opex: the evacuation and common infrastructure is not needed to run O&M at all, it belongs to the EPC/turnkey business, so margins are unaffected.
points.quote: So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se. That is required for further providing a turnkey solution to the customers.

points.point: Jindal described the post-demerger entity as an asset-light balance sheet with no depreciation, so EBITDA is the benchmark for PAT; the ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company, not asset, level.
points.quote: So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it means is that our profitability will be far more stronger.

points.point: Asked by Hansal Thakkar whether the subsidiaries would be rationalised into IWL shareholders' hands, Jindal said the whole intent of separating the businesses was shareholder optionality, and that no further corporate action is needed.
points.quote: And I think from a shareholder's perspective, a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business. He can hold the O&M business, he can hold the infrastructure business, he can hold the entire value chain together under Inox Wind.

points.point: Mathusudhana restated the balance-sheet numbers (INR 1,000 crore gross block off, INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, PBT up by that amount, ROE/ROCE up), with exchange no-objections received and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crore will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: Sanjeev Agarwal gave the value case for the receiving entity: IRSL had just raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the new CERC hybridisation rules multiply the value of its site infrastructure (Devansh: ~10 GW of plug-and-play infra).
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: With shareholder and creditor approval obtained, Devansh Jain framed the separation as a value-unlocking event for both the parent and IGESL, with IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: Answering Prit Nagersheth on how much revenue comes off, management sized the revenue leakage at only ~INR 10 crore against ~INR 50 crore of depreciation removed, i.e. no material impact on the INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA math.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.

points.point: Mathusudhana confirmed NCLT Ahmedabad approval and booked the benefits as realised: INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, profitability and returns up; Devansh said remaining steps were administrative, 1-2 months.
points.quote: It has also led to significant improvement in ROE and ROCE of Inox Green.

points.point: Management declined to disclose IRSL's top line or EBITDA profile until the demerger dates are announced, and tied the post-demerger IGESL story to ~INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA converting almost fully to cash with no depreciation, no finance cost and a INR 700 crore tax shield.
points.quote: We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.

points.point: The Scheme's stated rationale is segregation of two verticals whose risk-reward and financial profiles differ, consolidation of the evacuation business into IRSL which already runs it, and establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, producing two listed entities.
points.quote: Further, the Power Evacuation Business is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: Consideration to IGESL shareholders was fixed by registered valuer Finvox Analytics (fairness opinion from Marwadi Chandarana) at 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares; appointed date 1 Oct 2024, NCLT sanction 13 Mar 2026, effective 4 May 2026, record date 1 Aug 2026, 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares allotted 24 Aug 2026.
points.quote: 122 equity shares of Resco of face value of INR 10 each fully paid up to be issued for every 1,000 equity shares of Inox Green of face value of INR 10 each fully paid up

rationale.what_management_expects: Inox Green: asset-light pure-play O&M — Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation gone, only ~Rs 10 crore revenue lost, EBITDA≈PBT≈cash PAT, better ROE/ROCE. IRSL: separately listed EPC/evacuation arm with its own investors, lenders and ~10 GW plug-and-play infra; IGESL holders get 122 IRSL shares per 1,000.
rationale.gaps: Never quantified IRSL's evacuation revenue/EBITDA, who pays IGESL's common-infrastructure contract revenue post-transfer, lender/customer consent mechanics, or whether IGESL now rents the substations back.

As per the Scrutinizer's Report, all the participating warrant holders voted in favour of the resolution approving the proposed Scheme of Arrangement and none voted against the same." Under the Scheme the IGESL warrants held by them are repriced/substituted from an issue price of Rs. 145 each to Rs. 120 each, with 122 IRSL warrants at Rs. 205 each per 1,000 IGESL warrants. Earlier group issuance: "the company has issued number of 2,89,85,503 equity shares and 4,48,27,582 convertible warrants having face value Rs.10/- each of the group at price of Rs. 138/- per equity share and Rs. 145/-per convertible warrants respectively (including premium Rs.128/-per share and Rs. 135/ per share respectively) fully paid up", and allotment of equity shares on conversion of 27,58,620 warrants into 27,58,620 equity shares at an issue price of Rs. 145/- per share. Intra-group sales: Inox Clean Energy Private Limited, Aliento Wind Energy Private Limited, Flurry Wind Energy Private Limited and Flutter Wind Energy Private Limited were sold to "a related party controlled and owned by significant beneficial owners of the Company". No promoter buying, selling or pledging of IGESL shares around the separation is stated.

Post valuation of reports and subject to board approval, the demerger process will be initiated. Demerger of power infrastructure facilities currently on the balance sheet of Inox Green will result in a cleaner and asset light balance sheet. Thanks for the opportunity. First of all, I would like to congratulate Devansh and team for a successful fundraise of INR1,000 crores. In an era where a lot of promoters are selling the stake in the company, it's very encouraging to see promoters pumping in INR400 crores. So m y first question is relating to the demerger of the power evacuation infra. In the presentation, you have mentioned that the depreciation which is appearing right now will g o away. So I just wan ted to ask that with the demerger , will only the depreciation go from the P&L or there will be an impact on revenue and interest cost as well?
So Bhavya, to be very precise, there would be no impact on the interest cost as such, but a little bit of the revenue will go away, which is a very miniscule number.

Okay. Devansh, in the presentation, we have mentioned that there's an opportunity of 10 gigawatts of such inactive players, but one of the peers who made an equation right now in a TV interview said that the opportunity size is of 50 gigawatt s. So, can you just reconcile what would it be? Does the 50 gigawatt include solar?

So, Bhavya, Mathu, you add to it, but I think, Bhavya, what he mentioned, the peer was, currently we have a 46 gigawatt installed base, and in the next three to four years, they see the wind base expanding to 100 gigawatt. So, effectively, the O&M service opportunity is a 54 gigawatt opportunity. Now, naturally, the OEM who controls common infrastructure and the OEM who survives is doing O&M himself. No IPP wo uld ideally go out and give O&M to a live and kicking solid OEM, because the headaches are just too much. And the proprietary information and supply chain and spare parts are very complex. What we say when we say 10 gigawatts are the assets which are avail able in the domain, in the public domain where OEMs have either gone bust, or which are currently being serviced by unorganized, small, so -called ISPs. That is what we are talking about. Otherwise, it's like saying, by 2032, Modiji has targeted 175 gigawa tts of renewable energy. We are currently at 46 gigawatts of wind. So, actually, it's a 129 gigawatt opportunity in the next eight years.
Okay, okay, got it. Thanks for answering. Thank you.
Okay. And you want to separate out t he green also has some power evacuation ass ets which you want to separate and bring it to?

If you go back to Inox Green, Inox Green was effectively the company which owned the EPC arm and the O&M arm. Prior to the listing of Inox Green were shunted out or deemed or slump sold the EPC business to a 100% subsidiary of Inox wind called Resco. At that point in time the assets which were uncommissioned or which were being built is what went out. What was already commissioned or which were only a trustee, we have already been paid for by customers but it still resides on our balance sheet. We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and scre wing the entire O&M business. What's happening now is going forward, all the substations transmission lines are anyways being built under Resco. Inox Green Energy Services Limited August 09, 202 4 Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee. So, we are now demerging this from our balance sheet and merging it into Resco. That's what we are doing. Otherwise, there are no land banks and there is no future power evacuation under Inox Green. It's a zero - capex model business. It's an annuity service business.

At INOX Green, motivated by the philosophy of the INOX GFL Group, we are constantly working on ways and means for cost and quality control. We have indigenized several critical spare parts and equipment s, including control system, gearbox , etc., by developing in -house capabilities and tying up with local ized v endors . This significantly reduces the supply chain r isk and timelines for maintenance activities, resulting in significant cost savings. The Board of INOX Green has appointed consultants and registered value rs for valuating demerger of power evacuation business from INOX Green. Post valuation of reports and subject to Board approval , the demerger process will be initiated . The demerger of power infra facilities currently on the balance sheet of INOX Green will result in a cleaner and asset -light balance sheet. The proposed demerger will significantly add value through depreciation elimination. Our Vayuveer program launched recently to create highly trained, skillful manpower with six months of dedicated technical and on -job training, has b een a success. After the successful completion of the first batch of Vayuveers , we are in the process to induct the second b atch. This will further help the Company to create sustainable business operations and control costs to achieve our desired results . As we are significantly and rapidly scaling up our operations across several locations, the program helps in creating job opportunities for local youth and also meeting our social commitments. INOX Green remains strongly committed to almost doubling its O&M portfolio in revenue terms from current levels to 6 gigawatts by FY ‘ 26 and 10 gigawatts in the next three to four years. The macro outlook for the renewable sector, especially wind power, continues to be very strong . In FY ‘25 , around 12 gigawatts of hybrid FDRE wind capacities have already been awarded . And we expect the pace of awarding and subsequent commissioning of wind capacities to continue strongly. This will provide large multi -decadal opportunities for O&M service providers like us.

And obviously, we are continuously evaluating multiple opportunities for acquisitions of such businesses, either through NCLT route or the direct acquisition and also the portfolio of the existing ISPs. The financial position of the company, as you would have noticed, has improved significantly. It is in terms of the higher cash b ack, in terms of the EBITDA, which is a true profitability reflection of the Inox Green business. As you would know, at this juncture, the Resco demerger has not taken place, it's in the process. There is a significant amount of depreciation charges that is being reflected in our current numbers, which would be transferred to Resco as assets get transferred. So practically, whatever number you are seeing, you should look at our EBITDA number as a benchmark for our PAT numbers, because in absence of de preciation, everything will flow back to the profitability, to the bottom line. And that's where I guess the cash flow is a very important number for you to analyze as our company -- and Mathu said that our cash side is roughly INR23 crores on a quarter -to-quarter basis. And that is growing significantly as we are acquiring new businesses. The scheme for the demerger is also under process. The Resco, which my colleague mentioned in my previous call also, so we are awaiting the regulatory approvals the BSE, NSE approvals are likely to be available to us in the first week to 15 days of February. Once the regulatory approval comes in, the demerger will be done through NCLT and that would take, say, another 6 to 9 months as the case may be. We are hopeful that within this calendar year we will have the demerger of the business. And to that extent, the Resco will also be merged -- will be listed. So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset - light balance sheet. A nd it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it INOX Green Energy Services Limited January 31, 202 5 means is that our profitability will be far more stronger. Post the demerger, the shareholders of Inox Green will also receive the shares of Resco, which is renamed as Inox Renewa ble Solutions Limited. And where the -- so as a shareholder, they would also be a partner in the growth of the substation business, which is also getting merged through the same scheme. I would just reflect on the inorganic growth initiative s of the company, as I mentioned in the beginning, we are looking at a number of possibilities in this sector. There are many companies which are going through the bankruptcy route, and we are evaluating many of them.
Okay, and then my second question is how the Resco demerger will help the company in terms of revenue and EBITDA going ah ead?

So in terms of the Resco demerger, obviously -- yes, the demerger of substation business and merger with Resco Global, Inox Green shareholders will be benefit by in two ways. One, they will get the shares of Resco, broadly 10%. Broadly 20% of the Resco would be owned by the Inox Green shareholders. That is one. Secondly, after this merger, demerger will get completed, the complete depreciation will be go away from the financial numbers, and our EBITDA would be as Mr. Akhil has said will translate to PAT and P BT.

Okay. And second question is on this demerger of the substation from Inox Green. So while it will take away depreciation from our books, will it also take away any of the tax losses that we have accumu lated.
No. So the tax losses would be on a company level, not on an asset level. So the tax losses will remain in this company.
Okay. And what is the current accumulated tax loss.

Just one clarification on how much of cranes are expected to be operationalized in the next quarter? And also, you mentioned that the transformer capacity would be operational. So what capacity would begin, let's say, Q4. And I do understand that the Resco is targeted to be demerged from the Inox Green and it's capacity, my understanding is it would come on the Resco, but would it still have any kind of a margin impact on Inox Green for FY '26 numbers?

So on your first question on the cranes, obviously, it is unrelated to Inox Green related to Inox Wind because Resco is a subsidiary of Inox Wind. But still two cra nes will become operational, and we are starting with that and then additional claims will come in the subsequent months. INOX Green Energy Services Limited January 31, 202 5 And there will be no impact on the transfer of the business -- the substation business from Inox Green in terms of the EBITDA margins. We don't see -- feel that there'll be any impact.

We executed 146 megawatt during this quarter. We have very well diversified order book of 3.1 gigawatt , comprising of marquee clients across the spectrum, and a healthy mix of turnkey and equipment supply contracts. Our endeavour over the past year has been to build on our existing relationship to get more repeated orders, and in case of new customers, to get our first orders , however small or large it may be, as it is important to break through to build a long -term relationship and ensure repeat orders in the future. We expect to gain a fair share out of the opportunities coming in from our existing and potential customers, most of whom have very ambitious renewable additional plans. Currently we have a multi -gigawatt order pipeline and expect to convert a substantial portion into firm orders over the coming months. Inox Wind Limited and Inox Green Energy Services Limited September 01, 202 5 To achieve our target both in terms of execution and margins, we are continuously ramping up in the critical areas. We have recently operationalized our new 1200 megawatt capacity nacelle and Hub manufacturing unit near Ahmedabad, Gujarat. We have also deployed the first few set of cranes at our project sites and have commenced our transformer manufacturing facility as well, all under Inox Renewable Solutions. We are confident that these initiatives will aid faster execution and deliver higher than industry average margins. With that we are raising our margin guidance to 18% to 19% for the full year FY '26 from 17% to 18% earlier. Further we are strategically expanding our blade manufacturing capacity and are in process of setting up another facility in south part of India. This will improve our access to the sites in the southern states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores. Further the scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green and subsequent merger into Inox Renewable Solutions has received no objections from the stock exchanges and we have filed the scheme in NCLT as well. We expect the approval to happen within next two to thr ee quarters. On the macro side, the outlook remains strong. I believe the government continues to stand firmly behind the wind industry. This is not just desirable but a necessity given the thrust to replace conventional fossil fuel based power with renewable sources. While solar will continue to lead this space, wind will continue to play a significant role in giving its complementar ity to solar and generation during non -solar hours and wind role in grid balancing and making efficient usage of the transmission network . There is also some sort of a myth that solar plus B ESS will completely replace the conventional power without much role of wind. However, this is not right understanding as B ESS is only a storage resource and not a generating resource. 16 hours of B ESS is still not financially viable which is why wind ’s role in RTC set up is critical and will remain critical.

During the quarter, the machine availability for entire portfolio averaged around 95.6 %. Inox Green added approximately 1.6 gigawatt peak of solar O &M contracts to its portfolio in the month of April to May 2025. Our move into solar O&M has been strategic given that one of our group companies has recently commenced solar module manufacturing and the imminent large scale opportunities for hybrid, RTC, FDRE projects. Our total renewable O &M portfolio stands at approximately 5.1 gigawatt. Additionally, we signed an agreement for the comprehensive O &M of 182 megawatt of wind projects of one of India's largest diversified conglomerates as well. Inox Green is rapidly expanding its portfolio through both organic and inorganic means. On acquisitions, we are continuously working with multiple parties on large scale opportunities. We have made investments in an entity around 2 gigawatt of O &M assets and shall keep on looking for such opportunities to expand our portfolio inorganically as well. Further, we are participatin g in multi -gigawatt scale wind and solar O &M tenders of IPPs as many of the large companies have now changed their strategies and are now moving out of capital O &M to outsourcing model where we believe Inox Green has an edge given its strong credentials. Finally, with a scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green, its subsequent merger into Inox Renewable Solutions receiving no objection from the stock exchanges, we have now filed the scheme in NCLT Ahmedabad. Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated , thereby increasing the PBT by that amount. It will also lead to significant improvement in the ROE and ROCE of Inox Green. We expect the approval in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

While wind manufacturing is on a very solid growth platform built over the years, Inox Green is where I am extremely bullish on in terms of exponential growth which should start kicking in from this financial year as we ramp up our portfolio multiple times from 5 gigawatt currently to about 17 gigawatts over the next two years. While 17 gigawatts will have a mix of both solar and wind assets, wind will form the majority of the pie. As promoters, our motivation is to create and enhance value across our group companies and always be mindful of all our minority shareholders, case in point being the merger of IWEL with IWL. Our IPP arm and the solar manufacturing business under Inox Clean are also shaping up very well and the synergies between Inox Clean 's businesses with Inox Wind, Inox Green and Inox Renewable Solutions are quite unique and beneficial for all. Backed by the large capacity targets of Inox Clean , we expect further orders for Inox Wind, EPC opportunities for Inox Renewable Solutions and long -term O&M service opportunities for Inox Green, both across wind and solar. Today I can proudly say INOX GFL Group is one of the deepest and most integrated energy transition groups in the country with a presence across wind, solar, EVs, energy storage and a large IPP play now. Our renewable arm is extremely solid, capitalizing on opportunities and capable to withstand any challenges, regulatory or macro, if they were to come. I believe our group's renewable arm , and particularly Inox Wind , continues to be strongly positioned to capture the mega opportunities which lie ahead of us and will continue to create enormous value for all our stakeholders. Given that the industry is moving towards round -the-clock RE projects, at INOX GFL Group , we have strongly positioned ourselves to be a one -stop-shop for all our customers, offering solutions right from plain vanilla to the most complex projects across wind, solar, desk, infrastructure development and O&M services. We can now open the floor for Q&A.

First of all, congratulations on the successful completion of the merger of IWEL into IWL and a very successful rights issue. It is also very encouraging to note that the recent demerger of the evacuation business from IGESL into IRSL has seen no objection s. And given that our company has experienced so many corporate actions, I have a specific query regarding our subsidiaries, which are Inox Green Energy Services and Inox Renewable Solutions , formerly Resco. Sir, as I recall, Mr. Jindal had mentioned in the past that the management will demerge these two subsidiaries, albeit those proposals were at a nascent stage. So my question is, on a longer term strategic view, what is the management's stance on the possibility of rationalizing these subsidiaries via demergers into the hands of the IWL shareholders? So Inox Wind Limited shareholders will likely get IGESL and IRSL via demerger. I wanted to know the management's view on this. And what circumstances would thi s step be considered?

Thank you for firstly recogni sing and understanding the achievements of the company so far. As I mentioned to you last time, the attempt was to de -merge the substation business and the connectivity and common infrastructure from INOX Green into Inox Resco. As we call it now, INOX Renewable Solutions Limited. Under that, there would have been an automatic listing of Resco . And to that extent, the shareholders of INOX Green would be getting the shares of INOX Resco also. So when we mentioned about the de -merger of the businesses, it was de -merger of the infrastructure assets and getting into that INOX Resco. And that Resco in turn will get listed. That's the attempt and which is what now we have got all the necessary approvals. The NCLT process has started and we hope that within two to three quarters, this all will be achieved and the shares could be issued for INOX Resco also.

Sir, in opening remark s you said about , there is some notification from CERC . Can you throw some light on that amendment with respect to the industry, how it would be helpful to the industry and our company ? Management: So it just came out yesterday in which they allowed the hybridization of the existing transmission beyond 50 megawatt at a particular location. How it helps us as a company is across all Inox Wind , Green, Inox Renewable Solutions as well as one of our companies under Inox Clean , which is Inox Solar , everyone benefits due to this because a large part of the project infrastructure which we have built is currently evacuating only wind power. Now we can hybridize it and this gives us multiple times evacuation ready plug and play infra to set up the upcoming projects. So the execution then expedites because we don't have to build new infra. Infra is already there. It's now hybridized. So it's very good. I would say it has been Inox Wind Limited and Inox Green Energy Services Limited September 01, 202 5 coming. Some of the states had already declared it , the likes of Gujarat and Rajasthan . But now that it has come on a pan -India basis , it helps us expedite the project execution much faster.

I think it -- also just to add , I think it gives us access to almost 10 gigawatts of plug and play infrastructure across wind and solar , which is huge. I don't think anybody in India , barring maybe one or two massive PSUs and a large Indian conglomerate , have access to this kind of plug and play common infrastructure. It should be game changing for us. Kailash?

I just wanted to add on what Anshuman said that this is -- other way also that there are a lot of solar -alone projects and people will look for wind along with that. So that is another boost for Inox Wind.
I think it will be fantastic for us and the whole industry.
I mean certainly for us given our common infrastructure , the industry . Those who control infrastructure will certainly benefit out of it.

Yes, Yes. Hi, congratulations on a great set of numbers. Just two questions from my end. Number one, I understand that we are sold out for the next 2 years, which is a great thing. But is there some sort of opportunity loss in terms of loss of customers to a competitor? Second question is in the lines of GST. So there is a lot of news going around about the GST rates in the renewable sector being cut from 12% to 5%. I understand the meeting is going to happen sometime this week. So, do we see any sort of tailwinds due to the rate cuts, GST rate cuts?

Look, with respect to your first question, with respect to our saluting orders, I think Sanjeev reiterated it multiple times. Kailash reiterated it. I think we are growing it both horizontally and vertically where we are building on our existing relationships and we are diversifying to newer customers. And that's true across NTPC, CESC, Ampless, Multiple Orders, First Energy, Hero, Continuum, NLC. So that will continue to be the strategy. Some orders, I mean we cannot be the sole supplier to any one customer. So some orders we take, some competitors take. In certain new accounts, customers, existing suppliers lose and we enter. And I think that's how it is. As I mentioned, we have a very diversified book today of 10 -12 large customers whom we are supplying to. The team continues to work on newer names. So I think we are very, very solid on that. With respect to the GST rates being cut, yes of course it's a tailwind because your capital costs will go down. As a result, investment costs will go down. So returns could go higher or the cost of energy could go lower. Whichever way it is, it benefits the nation.

Inox Green's portfolio stands at 12.5 gigawatts, including the investment which we have made to acquire 6.5 gigawatts of operational wind of asset of two companies. With the financial expected to consolidate into Inox Green's books in FY '27 post -statutory approvals. We expect our profitability to grow manifold in FY '27 over FY '26. We will continue to be benefic iaries of our parent company, Inox Wind's rapid execution growth, a dditionally, large - scale plans of our group IPP company and solar module vertical will also benefit us going ahead. I be lieve Inox Green is well on track to become India's largest renewable O&M company in the very near future. I will now hand over to our Executive Director, Mr. Devan sh Jain , for his remarks, after which we will open up the floor for the Q&A. Thank you.

Yes, hi. So I just wanted to first of all congratulate everybody here. Especially on Inox G reen side to achieve a 12.5 gigawatt portfolio. That's just amazing. My question is that given that the assets that could have been acquired have been acquired. And I remember in the last call being said that there is also a chance to add more asset s via taking o ver the O& M portfolios of existing players. So is that a strategy that we still are on? Look, so when we set out at Inox G reen, if you recall the overall ambition was to eventually make it a 10 gigawatt company o ver the next 2-3 years ahead of where we are today, frankly speaking, we've already become 12.5 gigawatt. We've acquired two large a ssets directly, indirectly, whichever way you want to put it. rationale.rationale: These texts announce no separation: the only board-approved reorganisation is the opposite — a consolidation. On 29 September 2026 the boards of JSW Cement Limited (JCL) and its 66.23%-owned listed subsidiary Shiva Cement Limited (SCL) approved a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232 read with Sections 52 and 66, amalgamating SCL into JCL with appointed date 1 April 2026, no cash consideration, and a swap of 5 JCL shares of ₹10 for every 41 SCL shares of ₹2 (JCL's own SCL equity cancelled; the ₹100 crore of 1% OCCRPS it holds also cancelled). The problems management says it solves are: dependence on third-party clinker — SCL's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh (Odisha) clinker plant becomes backward integration, 'avoiding third-party purchases and associated mark-ups'; split funding — a single entity can raise funds on 'more favorable terms' and inter-company guarantees disappear; two listed entities' duplicated administration, record-keeping, consolidation effort and legal/regulatory compliance; a broken balance sheet at SCL (FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore, net worth negative ₹30.08 crore versus JCL's ₹5,995.28 crore and ₹7,029.47 crore), whose ₹133.92 crore accumulated losses are written off against its securities premium, while JCL's amalgamation adjustment deficit is set against its own premium account (left at ₹4,335.67 crore) — described as 'right sizing' the financial statements; and SCL's illiquid minority float, whose 33.50% public holders move into a larger, institutionally-held stock. Structurally it is tiny and non-dilutive: shares rise from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537, promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%, public from 27.03% to 27.67%. No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for the Shiva merger; valuation was by PwC Business Consulting and BDO Valuation, with fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets (JCL) and DAM Capital (SCL), JM Financial as exclusive financial advisor and Price Waterhouse & Co as tax adviser; closing is guided at 12-14 months subject to stock exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation. The genuine separations in these texts are different and smaller: the ₹191.63 crore cash sale of Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd (a Gujarat power plant) to Nuvoco Vistas (SPA 17 November 2025), and JCL selling up to ₹123 crore of JSW One Platforms shares as Promoter Selling Shareholder in that company's IPO (board 13 August 2026, alongside JSW Steel's up to ₹811 crore).
rationale.evolution: The Shiva amalgamation never appears in any of the four earnings calls supplied — the consolidation theme surfaces only around the UAE clinker JV: on the 3 September 2025 Q1 FY26 call Kamlesh Bagmar (Lotus Asset Managers) argued holding Fujairah clinker through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders', and CFO Narinder Singh replied the financial investors would exit over time and it would become a full subsidiary; on the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call Raghav Maheshwari (Equirus) asked directly about merging the JV and was told 'not as of now', maybe in 2-3 years once the financial investor is given an exit, while the new 1.65 MTPA Fujairah grinding unit was instead placed in a wholly owned subsidiary at USD 39 million. The 13 February 2026 investor presentation disclosed the only completed carve-out — the Nuvoco SPA for Vadraj Energy Gujarat at ₹191.63 crore — and footnoted Shiva's 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit built under a commercial arrangement with Bhushan Power and Steel. The Shiva merger then arrives fully formed in the 29 September 2026 board outcome and press release, and is restated as a 'Key Business Update' in the 27 October 2026 Q2 FY27 press release; the November 2025 call transcript is unreadable, so any discussion there cannot be checked.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of the listed 66.23%-owned subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement, appointed date 1 April 2026, explicitly to create one unified platform rather than to separate anything.
points.quote: Creating a consolidated cement platform supports Transferee Company's strategy, enabling category leadership, increased competitiveness, enhanced market share and efficient resource utilization.

points.point: Core industrial logic is backward integration: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa clinker plant at Sundargarh, Odisha stops being a third-party-style supply and becomes internal, cutting external procurement and mark-ups.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in backward integration of clinker manufacturing with the Transferee Company's cement manufacturing business.

points.point: Financial rationale is single-entity borrowing capacity and the removal of inter-company guarantees between parent and subsidiary.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will lead to greater ability of the consolidated entity to access and raise funds within a single entity on more favorable terms, leading to elimination of inter company guarantees and facilitate more efficient funding arrangements.

points.point: Running two listed companies is called out as duplicated cost and compliance — two sets of records, two consolidations, two regulatory burdens.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in a simplification of the existing corporate structure and eliminate administrative functions and duplications, reducing regulatory and legal compliances of two listed entities, eliminating multiple record keeping and reducing time and efforts for consolidation of financials at the group level,  consequently reducing the administrative costs of maintaining separate companies, while reducing the multiple legal and regulatory compliances.

points.point: Shiva is financially impaired: paid-up equity ₹159.00 crore, FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore and net worth negative ₹30.08 crore at 31 March 2026, against JSW Cement standalone turnover ₹5,995.28 crore and net worth ₹7,029.47 crore; ₹133.92 crore of accumulated losses are extinguished against its securities premium.
points.quote: With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the debit balance of Retained Earnings and SPA in the books of Transferor Company is likely to be  INR (133.92) crore and Nil respectively.

points.point: The parent's amalgamation deficit is absorbed into its own securities premium, which is left at ₹4,335.67 crore — the 'right sizing' of both balance sheets.
points.quote: With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the balance of Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account is likely to be Nil. The balance of SPA in books of Transferee Company is likely to be INR 4,335.67 crore.

points.point: Shiva's 33.50% public float is given liquidity: 5 JSW Cement shares of ₹10 per 41 Shiva shares of ₹2, lifting JSW Cement's count from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537 and promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%.
points.quote: The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization.

points.point: CEO Nilesh Narwekar framed it as integration and simplification, with completion guided at 12-14 months subject to exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation.
points.quote: The proposed merger is a strategic step towards creating a more integrated and efficient business.

points.point: The only consolidation pressure voiced by investors concerned the UAE clinker JV, not Shiva — Kamlesh Bagmar of Lotus Asset Managers argued holding Fujairah through a JV was poor for shareholders; the CFO said the financial investors would exit and it would become a full subsidiary, timeline undecided.
points.quote: So lastly, like, doesn't it make a bigger sense to have, like, say, clinker capacity of Fuj airah under our own hold entirely?

points.point: Asked again about folding the Fujairah JV in, management deferred it to 2-3 years because a financial investor must first be given an exit — while the new 1.65 MTPA UAE grinding unit was put in a wholly owned subsidiary (USD 39 million) that consolidates into the parent, with the JV selling clinker to it at arm's length.
points.quote: Not as of now. Probably going forward in next 2 -3 years, we will have a look because there is a financial investor sitting there, we'll have to provide exit to him.

points.point: The actual disposal in the period was non-core: Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd, owning a Gujarat power plant, sold to Nuvoco Vistas for cash; the November 2025 filing confirms the division contributed nothing to turnover, income or net worth.
points.quote: Entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd. for the transfer of Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd. (owning a power plant in Gujarat), for a consideration of Rs. 191.63 crore

points.point: Because Shiva is a subsidiary, the deal is a related-party transaction under LODR; arm's length rests on independent registered valuers (PwC Business Consulting, BDO Valuation) and a category 1 merchant banker fairness opinion, with no cash moving.
points.quote: Additionally, the consideration to be discharged for the Scheme of amalgamation is determined by independent registered valuers on which a fairness opinion has been issued by an independent category 1 merchant banker, the transaction therefore is at arm's length.

rationale.what_management_expects: For JSW Cement: in-house clinker (1.32 mtpa) replacing third-party purchases and mark-ups, lower costs, single-entity funding on better terms, no inter-company guarantees, simpler compliance, category leadership and market share; securities premium of ₹4,335.67 crore absorbs the amalgamation deficit. For Shiva holders: shares in a larger, more liquid, institutionally-held entity; ₹133.92 crore of losses written off.
rationale.gaps: No quantified synergy, cost-saving or clinker-volume numbers; no EPS or margin impact; no analyst Q&A on the merger (Nov 2025 transcript unreadable); Fujairah JV buyout timing unexplained.

deal.promoter_holding_after: 2026 amalgamation of Shiva Cement into JSW Cement — "Promoter/ Promoter Group 98,18,46,640 (72.02%) [Pre-Arrangement] ... 98,19,43,497 (71.39%) [Post-Arrangement]"; and "Public Shareholding 36,84,98,380 (27.03%) ... 38,05,50,123 (27.67%)"; "Non Promotor-Non Public 1,30,19,916 (0.95%) ... 1,30,19,917* (0.95%)", total 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537, with the note "*Note: Includes one equity share towards fractional entitlement. Actual number of equity shares to be issued towards fractional entitlement will be determined based on the shareholding pattern as on the record date." 2026 JSW One Platforms IPO — promoter holding after the IPO: not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2026 amalgamation of Shiva Cement — a public shareholder of Shiva Cement receives "5 (Five) Equity Shares of the face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten only) each fully paid-up, for every 41 (Forty One) equity shares of the face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two only) each fully paid-up held by such member in the Transferor Company", and "The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization." A public shareholder of JSW Cement (the parent) receives no new securities; "Shareholders in the Transferee Company get direct access to the economics of the Transferor Company." 2026 JSW One Platforms IPO — nothing is distributed to shareholders; "the transaction is an offer for sale in the proposed IPO" by JSW Cement as Promoter Selling Shareholder; what public shareholders of JSW Cement receive: not stated. 2025 Algebra Endeavour sale — cash consideration to the Company; "There is no scheme of arrangement, hence the same is not applicable."
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of existing stock options / RSUs / SARs in the Scheme: not stated; no new plan in a new entity is stated. ESOP cost disclosure only: "Employee costs included ESOP expense of Rs. 6.9 crore, Rs. 3.4 crore and Rs5.2 crore in Q3 FY25, Q2 FY26 and Q3 FY26 respectively". Pre-IPO conversion of preference capital: "On 24 July 2025, prior to the IPO of the Company, 160,000,000 CCPS of face value Rs. 100 each were converted into 235,662,477 equity share of face value Rs. 10 each". Management or insider shareholding: not stated. Exercise price or pricing date: not stated.
deal.insider_actions: 2026 JSW One Platforms IPO — JSW Cement Limited's Board "considered and approved the participation of the Company in the proposed initial public offering ("IPO") of JSW One Platforms Limited ("JOPL") as a Promoter Selling Shareholder by offering for sale, such number of equity shares of face value of Rs. 10 each of JOPL aggregating up to Rs. 123.00 Crores ... held by the Company"; JSW Steel Limited's Board approved the same for shares "aggregating up to Rs. 811 Crores ... held by the Company"; both "subject to applicable law, market conditions, receipt of necessary approvals/ regulatory clearances and other considerations." 2026 amalgamation — "Further, the Equity Shares held by the Transferee Company in the Transferor Company shall stand cancelled and extinguished and no Equity Shares of the Transferee Company shall be allotted in lieu or in exchange of the same", and on the reserve reorganizations "There shall be no consideration involved ... Thus, there will be no benefit to any promoter/ promoter group/ group companies". 2025 Algebra Endeavour sale — "None of the buyers belong to the promoter / promoter group companies." No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of JSW Cement shares is stated.

judge.what_is_spun: The Sugar Business — white crystal sugar, allied and food products — demerged into wholly owned Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited
judge.reason: Separating the Sugar Business lets both companies give focused attention to core businesses and attract investment, unlocks value through price-discovery of individual entities, and makes PAIL a pure-play alco-bev company.
judge.insiders: Not stated as a percentage; shareholding proportionate — no change in PAIL's pattern; PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no consideration. Promoter converted 6,36,942 warrants into PAIL shares, listed November 2025.
judge.hidden_value: Parent becomes pure-play alco-bev: FY26 distillery segment result Rs 23,658.72 lakhs vs sugar's Rs 494.79 lakhs on 20.53% of turnover; sugar segment liabilities Rs 22,166.79 lakhs exceed its assets Rs 10,553.97 lakhs, so leverage leaves with the stub.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Entitlement is only 1 PFEL share per 9 PAIL shares; sugar is a different, seasonal industry premium-spirits holders did not buy.
judge.listing_timeline: Press release and earnings call (28–29 April 2026): demerger scheme filed with SEBI, "expects completion by the end of FY27"; NSE observation letter (14 August 2026): listing/trading must commence "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; shares frozen in depositories till trading permission.
judge.read_next: Scheme explanatory statement: value of assets and liabilities transferred to PFEL, plus PFEL's abridged prospectus/Information Memorandum.

rationale.rationale: Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.
rationale.evolution: Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

points.point: Sugar was the main reason standalone Q4 EBITDA margin fell about 300 basis points, its quarterly EBITDA margin dropping from 11% to 2% — the dilution the demerger removes.
points.quote: That is one of the major factor is because of sugar drop in business, sugar margins drop, which was 11% EBITDA margin last year and last year same quarter and 2% this year quarter.

points.point: Management contrasted sugar's drag with Alco-Bev EBITDA margins of about 31.5% (and IMFL margins of 45–50%), which it expects to maintain or improve with premiumisation.
points.quote: I would like to highlight one more point here that if you look at our Alco-Bev business EBITDA margins, which is in the range of, let's say, current year about 31.5%, which is one of the highest margin in any Alco-Bev competition.

points.point: Sugar seasonality was also cited as what makes quarter-to-quarter margin comparison unreliable for the consolidated entity.
points.quote: So as I said, that as you rightly said that overall our EBITDA margins are same on year-over-year basis, but quarterly one factor is a sugar because of seasonality of the sugar business.

points.point: The April 28, 2026 Board outcome states the scheme demerges the Sugar Business into wholly owned subsidiary PFEL under Sections 230–232, creating two listed companies with proportionate shareholding — sugar in PFEL, distillery in PAIL.
points.quote: “The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.

points.point: Sugar's scale is disclosed as INR 233.05 crore of FY26 turnover, 20.53% of the listed entity's total turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31% March 2026 is as follows:

points.point: Scheme rationale: separating the undertaking lets each company give focused attention to its core business and attract the investment that business needs.
points.quote: Demerger of the Demerged Business and Undertaking and transferrmg it to a separate company would enable both the Demergéd Company and. the Resulting Company to provide focused attention for growth of their core businesses and attract required investments for growing that business;

points.point: Scheme rationale: value unlock via separate price discovery for each entity for existing shareholders.
points.quote: The Scheme would unlock value for the overall-business portfolio through price-discovery of the individual entities for existing shareholders;

points.point: Scheme rationale: the right operating architecture, sharper individual business strategies and clear capital allocation for each company.
points.quote: The Scheme could lead to the right operating architecture for both companies with sharper focus on, their individual business strategies and clear capital allocation, in alignment with the respective value creation journeys;

points.point: Scheme rationale: two separately listed companies each attract their own investor set, gain financial flexibility and better capital market outcomes.
points.quote: Separately listed companies to attract specific set of investors for their’ business profile, achieve financial flexibility and consequently, encourage stronger capital market outcomes.

points.point: Scheme rationale: better, more efficient conduct of each business by using its own financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, and greater business focus enhancing shareholder value.
points.quote: The Scheme will be conducive to better and more’ efficient and effective conduct of: business. and operations of the respective . companies, by utilizing the financial resources, managerial talents, technical skills and marketing resources and services delivery

points.point: Mirror listing, no cash: one PFEL share of INR 10 for every nine PAIL shares, PFEL's existing capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, ratio set on sugar's turnover and assets.
points.quote: The Share Entitlement Ratio is fixed keeping in view the turnover of Sugar Business Undertaking and assets of the Sugar Business.

points.point: The April 28, 2026 press release frames the end state as a pure-play alco-bev company with sharper focus, better capital allocation and value creation, scheme filed with SEBI and completion expected by end-FY27.
points.quote: Post-demerger, Piccadily Agro will transition into a pure-play alco-beverage company, enabling sharper strategic focus, improved capital allocation, and enhanced value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: CFO's press-release quote ties the demerger directly to unlocking value in core operations alongside Chhattisgarh monetisation from May 2026.
points.quote: With the strategic demerger of our sugar division, we are now sharply focused on unlocking value in our core operations.

points.point: On August 17, 2026 the company intimated receipt of no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 from BSE and NSE (following SEBI's August 13, 2026 comments), enabling the NCLT filing; the letter is valid six months and PFEL's listing is at the exchange's discretion.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Company has received the No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, in respect of the aforesaid Scheme from the BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“Stock Exchanges”).

points.point: SEBI's comments require the company to spell out, to NCLT and shareholders, the need for and rationale of the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, swap-ratio basis, assets and liabilities transferred, risks and the financial implications for promoters and public shareholders — disclosure not yet made in these documents.
points.quote: Need for the demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Alco-Bev PAIL becomes a pure-play premium spirits company: sharper focus, pooled human and capital resources, better capital allocation, and 31.5% alco-bev / 45–50% IMFL margins no longer diluted by seasonal sugar; 60–70% FY27 growth and 3–4x revenue in 3–4 years. Sugar, housed in PFEL, gets focused attention, its own investor set, price discovery, financial flexibility and ability to attract investment.
rationale.gaps: No sugar standalone P&L/debt split, lender or creditor consents, demerger costs, PFEL management, dividend or sale intent beyond listing; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it.

turns: On a standalone basis, revenue grew by 33% year-on-year basis from INR270 crores to INR364 crores. Our PBT grew by 17% from INR54 crores to INR63 crores and our PAT grew by 14% from 40 crores to INR46 crores. A couple of announcements also, we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio. And we've been discussing this and with management approval and Board approval yesterday, now we have filed our scheme of demerger of our sugar business, into a new entity. rationale.rationale: Thomas Cook (India) Ltd (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management business — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand, which it had itself absorbed from Nature Trails Resorts Pvt Ltd by slump sale for Rs 522.5 mn (appointed date 1 March 2025) — and demerging it into its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd (SHRL), which will then be separately listed on BSE and NSE. Management's stated logic is twofold: operationally, the resorts "would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry" (SHRL ran 75+ resorts/3,700+ rooms at scheme date, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms across 65 destinations by FY26-end, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA INR 1,701 mn at 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn at 21%, 25 straight profitable quarters, debt-free with ~INR 3,400 mn cash); and financially, the split is meant to "unlock value" and "attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment," leaving TCIL to "concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business." The demerged undertaking is tiny in revenue terms — INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone turnover — so the driver is structural, not scale: SHRL's board says it "has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry," with two listed entities each pursuing "growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics." Bolted onto the same composite scheme are three capital-structure fixes aimed squarely at EPS and optics: consolidating four Re 1 shares into one Rs 4 share (47,69,50,562 shares becoming 11,92,37,641) to "better reflect the true market value" and "convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics"; absorbing three dormant subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — that are "incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs"; and cutting face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payout to "right size the balance sheet and capital structure." Consideration is 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1, with no cash; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%), promoters end at 65.55% of SHRL and public at 32.30%. The initiative came from the Board on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and an Independent Directors Committee — no lender, partner or named investor demand is disclosed anywhere in the calls or filings, though analysts had repeatedly pressed management on deployment of the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash pile and on Sterling's EBIT failing to scale with its room additions.
rationale.evolution: Across the May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no hint of a separation: the only structural move discussed is the opposite direction — the March 2025 slump sale pulling Nature Trails' three Mumbai-area resorts (80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) into TCIL — while analysts push on cash use and on why Sterling's EBIT stayed flat at ~INR 129 crores despite adding 1,200-1,300 rooms, and on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer still says "there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition." The Board then granted in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 and the full composite scheme (demerger, 4:1 consolidation, merger of three dormant subsidiaries, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 capital reduction) was announced that day. It was discussed on an earnings call for the first time on 13 May 2026, where Iyer framed it as a "strategic divestment"/value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed "the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated," and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected by Q1 FY28. Execution then tracked that guidance without the plan itself changing: BSE no-adverse-observation on 31 August 2026, NSE no-objection on 1 September 2026, SHRL's registered office shifted from Tamil Nadu to Maharashtra effective 13 July 2026, and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order dated 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing TCIL shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings.

points.point: First earnings-call disclosure of the March 2026 board approval, framed as a strategic divestment of the resort business into Sterling that unlocks shareholder value.
points.quote: Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.

points.point: Iyer's stated benefit for the remaining TCIL: a cleaner capital structure and resources concentrated on Travel and Financial Services (forex, corporate travel, MICE, DMS).
points.quote: For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.

points.point: The face-value consolidation plus absorption of the three dormant subsidiaries is pitched explicitly as an EPS and corporate-structure simplification measure.
points.quote: The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries, further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share, directly benefiting our shareholders.

points.point: Lalvani places the demerger alongside Sterling's own next phase — brand re-architecture and expansion to 95 resorts/4,500 rooms in 2027 — as process already under way.
points.quote: In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.

points.point: Nandy gave the only timeline guidance: 12-15 months from board approval, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, completion expected Q1 FY28.
points.quote: So when we took the Board approval for this particular demerger project, we said that it will take us 12 to 15 months.

points.point: Sterling's readiness argument on the call: FY26 as an inflection year with revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT margin 21%, 25 consecutive profitable quarters and a debt-free balance sheet with ~INR 3,400 mn cash.
points.quote: FY '25-'26 marks a defining year for Sterling, a decisive inflection point where scale, profitability and balance sheet strength have expanded simultaneously, not sequentially.

points.point: Core operating rationale: the resorts belong with Sterling because Sterling has the hospitality operating expertise, catering to a different demographic with more curated experiences (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways).
points.quote: TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.

points.point: Sterling is presented as having outgrown subsidiary status and ready for its own listed existence in a fast-growing sector — the justification for subsequently listing SHRL on BSE and NSE.
points.quote: Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.

points.point: The value-unlock case is explicitly about attracting different investor bases to travel/financial services versus leisure hospitality, with each entity pursuing sector-specific growth strategies with agility.
points.quote: Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment

points.point: Segregating verticals is expected to improve operating efficiency and profitability at both entities because each faces different industry dynamics.
points.quote: In this manner, the two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.

points.point: Scale of what is actually moving: the demerged undertaking's turnover was only INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — six Nature Trails resorts.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.

points.point: Consideration is all-paper at 81:100, no cash; TCIL retains its existing SHRL stake, leaving promoters at 65.55% (including 7% held by TCIL) and public at 32.30% of SHRL.
points.quote: for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up ("Share Entitlement Ratio").

points.point: Three dormant shells (TC Visa Services, Jardin Travel Solutions, Borderless Travel Services — FY25 turnover Rs 1.2 cr, nil and nil) are folded into TCIL purely to cut compliance and overhead and free management attention.
points.quote: TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non-operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.

points.point: The Rs 4-to-Rs 3 face-value reduction involves no payout to shareholders and no change in share count; it is a balance-sheet right-sizing aimed at EPS, and is stated not to prejudice creditors.
points.quote: The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.

points.point: The 4-into-1 share consolidation is justified on ratio optics — making reported per-share metrics reflect intrinsic value and signal financial stability.
points.quote: The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will result in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios.

points.point: Six weeks before the announcement, management told investors asking about the ~INR 1,000 crore gross cash pile that no cash-return or acquisition discussions were live — no separation was signalled on this call.
points.quote: But currently, there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition.

points.point: The opposite-direction precursor: in March 2025 TCIL bought the Nature Trails resorts business into itself by slump sale (three resorts near Mumbai, 80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) — the very undertaking now being demerged out to Sterling.
points.quote: We completed this, the slump sale in March. Now this actually includes 3 resorts close to Bombay.

points.point: Analyst pressure on Sterling's standalone performance versus listed hospitality peers, which Lalvani answered by citing the completed transformation from vacation-ownership to a hospitality model.
points.quote: But if you see, if you see the revenue, we are quite underperforming the industry.

points.point: Standing investor concern the separation does not address: Sterling's EBIT stayed around INR 129 crores for two years despite roughly 1,200-1,300 extra rooms, attributed to membership-revenue sunset, resort ramp-up lags and ROU depreciation.
points.quote: But our EBIT continues to actually be steady in terms of INR 129 crores over the last 2 years, in fact, a decline from FY '24.

rationale.what_management_expects: TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources focused on travel and financial services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger, lower admin cost. SHRL: separate listing on BSE/NSE, own growth path in fast-growing hospitality, hospitality-expert ownership of the resorts. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sector-aligned strategies, improved operational efficiency and profitability.
rationale.gaps: No valuation methodology or derivation of the 81:100 ratio, no quantified value unlock or SHRL financials post-demerger, no accounting treatment of the capital reduction, no shareholder-vote or listing-date specifics.
