judge.quote: Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: NSE letter dated May 15, 2026: "Lloyds Realty Limited shall ensure that steps for listing of specified securities are completed and trading in securities commences within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; listing "is at the discretion of the Exchange" and subject to SEBI approval. Chairman, 9 July 2026: "our real estate business will be listed". Scheme still pending NCLT (applications filed; Observation Letters received 15 May 2026, valid six months).

rationale.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of Lloyds Enterprises Limited's (LEL) Real Estate Business Undertaking into a new, separately listed vehicle, Lloyds Realty Limited (LRL), carried out inside a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 read with Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 that the Board approved on 22 December 2025; the same scheme first merges Lloyds Realty Developers Limited (LRDL, Transferor 1) and Indrajit Properties Private Limited (IPPL, Transferor 2) into LEL, so that all realty assets sit in one place before being carved out into LRL. The only rationale management itself states is in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): the merger-and-demerger scheme means 'our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders', set against a realty platform spread across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane with 'nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development' — i.e. a capital-hungry pipeline that needs its own currency and price discovery. For the parallel group merger the Chairman gives the generic benefits: 'enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders'. The filings show why real estate sat awkwardly inside LEL: for 9M FY26 the Real Estate segment did only ₹53.30 crore of revenue and ₹0.88 crore of segment result (down from ₹11.26 crore) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, while Steel (₹492.80 crore revenue, ₹255.60 crore result) and Engineering (₹795.75 crore, ₹151.08 crore) carried the group, and subsidiary LRDL itself ran a ₹1.26 crore net loss; consolidated FY26 total income was ~₹2,200 crore against ~₹800 crore standalone, with LEL otherwise functioning as a holding/trading company (stakes of ~4.13% in Lloyds Metals and Energy, ~31% in Geomysore, and material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works with a group order book of ~₹8,000 crore and 44% PBT growth). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only parties on record demanding anything are the regulators — SEBI, NSE and BSE required LEL to disclose to shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio', synergies, minority impact and a cost-benefit analysis, plus lender NOCs and 'Conditions imposed by lenders, if any'. The same unlock-by-listing logic recurs twice more in the group: LEWL's absorption of Lloyds Infra, Metalfab and Techno Industries to end 'silos' and create a ₹6,150 crore-order-book design-to-execution entity, and the SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore), where a DRHP within 30 months is meant to 'facilitate independent price discovery', market visibility and access to capital.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings. It surfaces fully formed on 22 December 2025, when the Board approved the Composite Scheme (LRDL + IPPL into LEL, real-estate undertaking out into LRL) and filed it with BSE and NSE the same day; a week later (29 December 2025) the group announced the separate LEWL merger of LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries, and the 9 February 2026 results notes restated the Scheme verbatim alongside a ₹500 crore NCD approval, the ₹361 crore Tata Capital/Bajaj Finance/Jio Credit borrowings and the block-deal sale of LEWL shares to Thriveni Earthmovers. On 15–16 May 2026 LEL received NSE's 'No objection' and BSE's 'no adverse observations' (with LRL's listing left to exchange discretion, an Information Memorandum, frozen shares and a 60-day post-NCLT listing timetable), followed on 18–19 May 2026 by exchange NOCs and CCI clearance for the LEWL merger; by the 9 July 2026 AGM the Chairman described the scheme as approved, an NCLT application filed, and the realty business as one that 'will be listed'.

points.point: Board approval on 22 December 2025 of the Composite Scheme: LRDL and IPPL merge into LEL, and LEL's Real Estate Business Undertaking is demerged into Lloyds Realty Limited; filed with BSE and NSE the same day.
points.quote: The Scheme is filed with Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) & National Stock Exchange (NSE) on December 22, 2025.

points.point: The only explicit purpose management gives for the demerger, in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): a separate listing of the real estate business to unlock value, against a pipeline of nearly 14 million sq ft across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane.
points.quote: Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.

points.point: For the group merger leg, the Chairman offers only structural benefits, noting approvals from NSE, BSE and SEBI and an application filed with the NCLT.
points.quote: This strategic merger is expected to enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders.

points.point: NSE's 15 May 2026 observation letter confirms the demerger is a route to a new listed realty entity, but conditions it on an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, and listing within 60 days of the NCLT order.
points.quote: However, the listing of shares of Lloyds Realty Limited  is at the discretion of the Exchange.

points.point: The parties actually demanding an articulated rationale are the regulators: SEBI and both exchanges ordered LEL to put the need, rationale, swap ratio, synergies, minority impact and cost-benefit analysis in the shareholder explanatory statement.
points.quote: Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the minority shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.

points.point: Lenders are referenced only as a consent/disclosure requirement imposed by SEBI — NOCs from lending banks, FIs and debenture trustees, plus any lender-imposed conditions — not as instigators of the separation.
points.quote: Conditions imposed by lenders, if any, may be disclosed to the public shareholders along with the impact of same on the scheme.

points.point: The mirror-image transaction at material subsidiary LEWL (announced 29 December 2025) consolidates LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries into one vertically integrated design-to-execution entity with a ~₹6,150 crore combined order book, ~38.1 crore new shares and equity rising from 147.42 to 185.52 crore shares, appointed date 1 April 2025.
points.quote: By bringing Lloyds Infra, Metalfab, and Techno Industries under one banner, we are eliminating silos.

points.point: The same unlock-by-separate-listing logic is applied to the June 2026 SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore; FY26 turnover ₹816.87 crore, net profit ₹43.42 crore), with a DRHP promised within 30 months of Stage 1.
points.quote: The proposed listing of SISCOL is expected to facilitate independent price discovery of its business, enhance its market visibility and access to capital, and unlock value for all its stakeholders, including the Company as a significant shareholder.

points.point: The filings' own numbers show the real-estate leg was the group's weakest earner before separation: 9M FY26 segment revenue of ₹53.30 crore and segment result of ₹0.88 crore (vs ₹11.26 crore a year earlier) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, with LRDL itself loss-making.
points.quote: We have not conducted a review of the Subsidiary (Lloyds Realty Developers Limited) included in the unaudited consolidated financial results. whose financial information reflects total revenues of <53.30 and total Net Loss after tax of t1.26. crores.

rationale.what_management_expects: For the realty entity: a separate listing of the ~14 mn sq ft Mumbai-region pipeline, 'unlocking its true potential' and greater shareholder value. For the retained LEL group: enhanced operational efficiencies, optimised resource utilisation, a stronger business structure and sustainable long-term value, leaving a holding/trading company around LEWL (~₹8,000 crore order book, 44% PBT growth), Lloyds Metals, Geomysore and SISCOL.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts on file; no swap ratio, valuation, debt or asset split for LRL, no margin or capital targets, no timeline, no named investor or lender demand.

deal.size_statement: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2025-26 Scheme of Merger by Absorption into Lloyds Engineering Works Limited: "Post-merger, Mr. B Prabhakaran and Family & along with his controlled entities will hold a significant stake of 21.03% in the expanded LEWL entity, reinforcing their long-term commitment to the company's growth trajectory." and "Mr. B. Prabhakaran & family: 21.03% stake — Reinforces long-term promoter commitment" (General Announcement dated 29 December 2025). 2025 Composite Scheme of Arrangement / Lloyds Realty Limited: not stated — the NSE observation letter only requires the company to disclose "Details of shareholders of Transferor companies and their classification as Promoters and Public shareholders in Transferee Company, post scheme" and "There shall be no change in the shareholding pattern or control in Lloyds Realty Limited between the record date and the listing which may affect the status of this approval." 2026 SISCOL acquisition: not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2025 Composite Scheme of Arrangement (demerger of the Real Estate Business Undertaking into Lloyds Realty Limited): not stated — no entitlement or share exchange ratio for Lloyds Enterprises Limited's shareholders is disclosed in these documents; the NSE observation letter states only that "The shares allotted pursuant to the Scheme shall remain frozen in the depositories system till listing/trading permission is given by the designated stock exchange." 2025-26 Scheme of Merger by Absorption into Lloyds Engineering Works Limited: shares are issued to the shareholders of the transferor companies — "Lloyds Infra (LICL): For every 1500 shares of LICL, 1798 shares of LEWL" and "Metalfab: For every 5 shares of Metalfab, 94 shares of LEWL"; nothing is stated as being received by Lloyds Enterprises Limited's own public shareholders. 2026 SISCOL acquisition: not stated (cash and preferential share swap by LEWL to SISCOL's sellers).
deal.management_incentives: "Further, the Company introduced an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) for employees and its subsidiaries/associates. This initiative reflects our focus on building a performance-driven culture and aligning employee growth with the long-term success of the Company." (Chairman's speech, 40th AGM, 9 July 2026). Treatment of existing grants under either scheme, any new plan in Lloyds Realty Limited, exercise price or pricing date, and management/insider shareholding: not stated. Related insider holding stated only as: "Post-merger, Mr. B Prabhakaran and Family & along with his controlled entities will hold a significant stake of 21.03% in the expanded LEWL entity".
deal.insider_actions: On 9 February 2026 Lloyds Enterprises Limited sold 60,34,299 fully paid-up equity shares of Lloyds Engineering Works Limited at Rs. 49.65 each, amounting to INR 29,96,02,945.35, i.e. 0.41% of LEWL's equity share capital, to Thriveni Earthmovers Private Limited, the investment arm of Mr. Balasubramanian Prabhakaran, through a Block Deal; the buyer "does not belong to the promoter/ promoter group/group companies" and "No specific agreement was executed by the Board of Directors and the Shareholders of the Company." During FY26 the Company subscribed to 75,00,002 share warrants of Lloyds Metals and Energy Limited, which were converted into equity shares, funded by loans of ₹361 crore from Tata Capital, Bajaj Finance and Jio Credit. The Company completed its Rights Issue of partly paid-up equity shares and made the First and Final Call of ₹19.50 per share on 25,44,25,324 partly paid-up shares (Rights Issue Committee, 8 January 2026). Under the SISCOL transaction LEWL will "issue and allot 7,06,74,554 equity shares on a preferential basis to the sellers/ shareholders of SISCOL at a price of INR 71.25 per equity share", and Mr. B Prabhakaran and family with controlled entities are stated to hold 21.03% of LEWL post-merger. No promoter pledging of Lloyds Enterprises Limited shares is stated.

rationale.rationale: This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

points.point: Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.

points.point: Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.

points.point: The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started.
points.quote: Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years.
points.quote: Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins.
points.quote: Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality.
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring.
points.quote: The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.

points.point: The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%).
points.quote: This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.

points.point: The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000).
points.quote: Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.

points.point: An investor asked outright about demerging or selling the rig business post-May 2025; management confirmed intent but no board discussion and no valuation expectation.
points.quote: It is something which we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval.

points.point: After an investor said the rig arrangement (MSL renting the rig to group company Jindal Drilling, which sub-contracts to ONGC) looked out of line with MSL's governance clean-up, management personally agreed and promised a communication once board approvals came.
points.quote: You are right, and I personally agree with you, but once suitable decisions and Board approvals are received, we will send communication on this.

points.point: Management confirmed a rig exit had been contemplated but that the board had given no update, while re-committing to pipes only — the rig had just been recontracted to Jindal Drilling at ~$35,000/day L1, with MSL to get ~$17,000-18,000/day.
points.quote: There was a view of getting out of the rig business, but we've not received any update from the Board in the Board meeting, which concluded yesterday.

points.point: A five-year shareholder explicitly demanded the company be split so investors could choose the pipe business over the treasury/holding activity, arguing the merged picture was unclear; management offered no response.
points.quote: Either divide the company in two parts. One should be a holding company, one should be a seamless company.

points.point: Six months before board approval, an analyst asked specifically about getting the Jindal Explorer rig off the books and was told there was no update, with the rig about to start a new ONGC contract.
points.quote: There is no update on the proposal that you mentioned.

points.point: On the last call before the first board approval, management described the future as cash conservation and opportunistic distressed acquisitions, with no mention of any restructuring, while defending the INR3,500 crore treasury against shareholders noting ~50% of market cap was cash.
points.quote: We are conserving cash as of now and we are on the lookout for any inorganic opportunity that may arise, but that inorganic opportunity should be at a cost level at which we are comfortable.

points.point: The same call set out the economics of the Telangana asset that now forms United Seamless Limited: INR477 crores purchase plus INR73 crores reactivation, INR100-200 crores of EBITDA a year, and ~INR375 crores of tax saved from USTPL's INR1,500 crore-plus accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation.
points.quote: We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill.

rationale.what_management_expects: Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.
rationale.gaps: No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

turns: Sir, just one last question . We have also indicated long back that , eventually , Maharashtra Seamless is holding one rig , and we may look to sell this rig off basically . So, any, since the oil prices are already good at a good level , so any progress on that regard or given our cash flows are very strong , so we have dropped this plan ?
No, we have not dropped , but we are looking for the right time to hive off.

My question again comes on the total liquid cash that we have in our hand. Since there is no serious kind -- look out for a company to -- outright purchase. And secondly, with so much cash, our ROEs are getting impacted and dividen d -- paying dividend eventually, the investor has to pay tax at 30%, right? And also the promoter is quite interested in increasing the stake. So you can, at current cash level, easily go for a 5% of your total float as a buyback. I mean with promoter not participating, automatically, their stake will increase to almost 70%, 71%. So why is management, as of Maharashtra Seamless Limited 30 January 2024 now, not considering it? I mean it is helpful in every way, right? All your attributes are going to improve on the financial point of.

So when you make the statement that there is no serious effort in place, I take issue with that statement. That is not the case. We are actively on the lookout for opportunity. But we cannot create opportunity out of thin air just because one doesn't exist . When we make that statement, please note that United Seamless was an acquisition which we identified and that generated significant benefit for the company. We have also put in a lot of efforts to look at other assets such as ISMT and OCTL, but they did not materialize for no fault of the company because there are other factors in place which are beyond our control. As of now, we have enough cash for such an opportunity, and we want to conserve that cash going forward because we are taking a long -term vi ew rather than a short -term view of just trying to improve market capitalization. What we believe is if we take a long -term view, and we are able to set up more manufacturing units at a price that is comfortable for us and is inherent of our competitive ad vantage, then we'll be able to generate long -term sustainable shareholder value creation.

Yes, surely, United Seamless was one of the very brilliant acquisitions, I would say, because the EBITDA per ton, etcetera, that generates on the product is quite high. Also, sir, on this 1 lakh capex -- 1 lakh ton capex that is going to kick in by Decembe r, is the product anything different from -- nature of the product different from what we are doing right now?
No. It is the same product.
Additional products will also be there in addition to our existing product.

Okay. Okay. And with respect to the ISMT turnaround as well as increasing our own utilization at United Seamless, sir do you see these ramp -ups to create a situation of oversupply in the industry? Kaush al Bengani: No, no, no.

Okay. And sir, just you said you have the INR 1,800 -plus crores cash and you have INR 800 crores capex plus dividend increase. And you said you are looking for inorganic growth acquisition. In which geography you're looking for acquisition or any company that -- which geography you are mostly focused?

Earlier, we were looking within India. We were looking to acquire one of our competitors, but that did not happen. We were looking at United Seamless, and that happened successfully. We can look at any geography as long as the equipment is as per our requirement and t he cost of the equipment is also as per our requirement. Geography is not so important for us because we have the ability to dismantle equipment overseas, pack them into boxes, ship them to India and assemble them and commission them within India. Moderato r: We have our next question from the line of Afzal -- is fro m the line of Richa from Equitym aster.

All right. Also on the rig business that you have, I understand that you are planning to demerge or sell it post May '25. So what is the kind of expectation that you have in the terms of realization from that sale of business? And how long will this process actually take like once you start it in May '25?

We don't have an expectation figure right now because that matter has not yet been discussed at Board level. It is something which we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval. When we reach that stage, suitable communication will be given.
So, how much is exports in the order book? And is there a delta between domestic and exports margin in the United States?

As of now, exports is less than 10% of the total order book , and there is definitely a delta because if there is no d elta on the exports front, then the Maharashtra Seamless Limited 28 Januar y 2025 risk we are carrying is the risk of anti -dumping duties being imposed upon us on pe tition by the domestic manufacturers of the country in which we are exporting because then they would petition their government that we are selling our product at lower margins in the export market.

And lastly, sir, when we have merged the United Seamless in our Company at that time we were receiving some tax in cidence advantages of carry forward losses and all so have we got all the benefits of tax outgo of that and if we could share the number of how much the advance tax has paid of the last nine months ?

That number I cannot share right now immediately but whatever tax benefits we had everything has been utilized by March 2024. After that whatever tax provision we have almost that amount of advance tax has been paid.
Sir, as you mentioned now, some of the competitors have gone bankrupt , is there any opportunity for acquisitions , one of them ? And second, is any of your competitors adding any capacity as of now?

Yes to both questions. We acquired United Seamless Tubula ar Private Limited from the IBC process in 2020 and amalgamated that entity with our company. So that was one competitor which we had taken over. There aren't any other opportunities right now in India. On the capacity expansion front, like the way we are going ahead with ca pacity expansion, one of our competitors is also doing so.

Okay. Sir, secondly, according to the Seamless Tubes Manufacturers Association of India, the seamless capacity in India is currently 1.9 milli on tons, whereas the demand is 1.3 million tons. So if we say 20% to 25% of the industry size, so is it the right number if you take 20% to 25% of the 1.3 million ton demand that they have stated recently? Maharashtra Seamless Limited 05 N ovember 2025

Those numbers are not correct because they refer to nameplate capacity, which is different from actual capacity. Actual production of seamless pipes in India is around 9 lakh tons. So the 20%, 25% is linked to the actual production of 9 lakh tons annually.

Sir, in recent IIP numbers, the base metal sector has seen a good growth. And in the press release also written that ste el tubes market is -- growth has been encouraging. So what are your comments on that and how that impacts our company?
Who has given this view? I couldn't...

I have a question regarding as we are hearing and seeing the reports like the shale gas and the oil, and the peak oil output has ju st passed and now more means more drilling is required to get the same amount of oil and gas. Sir, can you please throw some light on your acquisition about the United Seamless Tubulaar that was done some time back? And how are you getting the feelers in t he market? Or do you see that capex is coming by large global conglomerates in this space?
Regarding United Seamless Tubulaar, what is it that you would like to know?

Sir, I would like to understand the means -- like we acqu ired it on some basis. Is the thesis playing out? Are we getting some traction in North American or the European market where we wanted to compete with the other large players? Maharashtra Seamless Limited 29 January 2026

I am confused. We never said that we want to compete in Europe an and North American markets from our mill in United Seamless Tubulaar. That mill is working very well. We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill. So against a total capital expenditure of INR550 c rores, that mill generates between INR100 crores to INR200 crores of EBITDA every year depending on the margin profile. In addition to that, there were accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation in excess of INR1,500 crores in United Seamless Tubulaar Private Limited. Subsequent to merger of that company with Maharashtra Seamless, we were able to set off the profits of Maharashtra Seamless with the unabsorbed depreciation and accumulated losses of United Seamless Tubulaar, thereby saving tax of around INR375 crores. So the entire project was paid back in maybe two years. So yes, the thesis did play out, and that is the position today.

rationale.rationale: No earnings-call transcripts were supplied ("no transcripts on file"), so this reconstruction rests solely on Raymond Limited's filings. Management's own framing, set out in the EGM explanatory statements of May 25, 2026 and September 8, 2026, is that the separation is already executed — "the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business" — leaving Raymond Limited as "a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries," namely JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (precision engineering and auto components) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (aerospace / new-age industrial and technology-led businesses), while Raymond Lifestyle Limited (branded textile, branded apparel, garmenting, high-value shirting, emerging) and Raymond Realty Limited (100-acre Thane land ~₹25,000 cr revenue potential plus asset-light Mumbai JDAs ~₹27,000 cr potential) trade separately. The problem the structure is said to solve is focus and clean capital allocation: the Q2/H1 FY2027 group update (filed November 2, 2026) titles the result "Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms" across three listed entities, each with its own ~75%-independent board (vs a ~50% top-100 Indian average), its own ring-fenced audit/pay/risk/related-party committees, its own CARE/CRISIL ratings (RLL AA/A1+, Raymond Realty and TenX A+/A-, JKMPTL A+/A1+, JKMGAL A/A1 within ₹9,476 cr rated debt) and its own balance sheet — group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x on TTM EBITDA of ₹1,738 cr and revenue of ₹13,115 cr, liquidity up from ₹571 cr in FY20 to ₹2,791 cr, and short-term debt cut from 74% of gross debt in 2020 to 38% in 2026 with 4.24-year average maturity. It also de-concentrates earnings: non-lifestyle verticals now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), with engineering Raymond Ltd. posting H1FY27 income of ₹1,311 cr (+17%), EBITDA ₹203 cr (+22%), PBT ₹84 cr (+69%), aerospace & defence revenue ₹262 cr (+56%) and a ₹77 cr net cash surplus, against FY21 engineering revenue of just ₹141 cr and EBITDA of ₹22 cr. The separated, residual listed company is then being funded as an acquisition vehicle described as being "at a pivotal inflection point": ₹330.88 cr of 18-month warrants at ₹497 to promoter-group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited (29.83% to 35.91% diluted; ultimate beneficial owner Gautam Hari Singhania), then ₹214.71 cr at ₹645 to Minerva Ventures Fund (0% to ~4.31%, ultimate beneficial owner Ghanshyam Hurry), with 75% earmarked for Indian and international acquisitions in aerospace, automotive and defence including acquisition-debt repayment or bridge funding, and 25% for general corporate purposes, CARE Ratings appointed monitoring agency. Nobody outside is named as having demanded the separation: no investor campaign, lender covenant or JV partner appears in the texts; the visible external pressure is from the stock exchanges, whose queries forced a June 10, 2026 corrigendum and an October 22, 2026 restatement of the allottee's diluted stake. Running the other way, the January 27, 2026 Scheme folds wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover) back into Raymond Limited "to enable simplified structure and greater management focus," so the pattern management describes is separation of the big consumer and property platforms combined with re-absorption of small subsidiaries into the listed engineering holdco.
rationale.evolution: The idea is presented as already settled rather than emerging: by the January 27, 2026 Everblue Apparel amalgamation filing, Raymond Limited is described as holding "investment in Engineering and Aerospace business through its subsidiaries" with standalone turnover of only ₹289 lakh, and the scheme's stated logic is simplification and management focus. The May 25, 2026 board outcome and May 27, 2026 EGM notice first spell out the post-separation rationale — demerger done, engineering holdco now raising ₹330.88 cr of promoter warrants for a multi-sector growth strategy through JKMPTL and JKMGAL — and that framing is repeated verbatim in the September 8/11, 2026 notice for the ₹214.71 cr Minerva Ventures Fund issue. The plan changed under exchange pressure: the June 10, 2026 corrigendum deleted "Capital expenditure and capacity expansion at subsidiary companies" and recast 75% of proceeds as acquisitions "including repayment of acquisition debt," the June 18, 2026 EGM passed with 31.72% of public-institution votes against, and the June 24-25, 2026 rumour verification on a German target (Deharde) was answered as speculative. By the November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update the separation is marketed as three "Pure-Play Platforms" with per-entity boards, ratings and balance sheets, and the second raise (approved October 3, 2026 with 99.998% in favour) was granted exchange in-principle approval on November 6, 2026.

points.point: The May 27, 2026 EGM explanatory statement states the separation is complete and defines what the residual listed company now is — an engineering holdco operating through JKMPTL and JKMGAL.
points.quote: Raymond Limited ("Company") is a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries and has consistently invested in building world-class capabilities across its business verticals.

points.point: The same statement (repeated in the September 11, 2026 notice) gives the explicit cause-and-effect: because lifestyle and real estate were demerged, the remaining entity can pursue a focused multi-sector engineering strategy.
points.quote: Having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities in recent years — including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business — Raymond is now positioned to pursue an accelerated, multi-sector growth strategy through its subsidiary companies, including:

points.point: Management frames the moment created by the separation as requiring fresh growth capital, which is what both warrant issues (₹330.88 cr to promoter group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited at ₹497, ₹214.71 cr to Minerva Ventures Fund at ₹645) are for.
points.quote: The Company is at a pivotal inflection point in its growth trajectory.

points.point: The November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update brands the outcome of the demergers as three single-focus listed platforms: Raymond Lifestyle Limited, Raymond Realty Limited and Raymond Limited (Aerospace & Defence plus Precision Technology and Auto Components).
points.quote: Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms

points.point: The same update argues the separation de-risks group earnings by removing reliance on the lifestyle business, quantifying the shift precisely for H1FY27.
points.quote: Non-lifestyle verticals (Realty + Raymond Ltd.) now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), signalling an increasingly balanced, multi-engine growth profile.

points.point: Governance is presented as a deliberate consequence of splitting into three listed vehicles — independent boards and independently chaired audit, pay, risk and related-party committees at each entity, above what LODR requires.
points.quote: This is not a statutory response to LODR, LODR would allow far less. It is a deliberate architecture.

points.point: Each separated entity carries its own leverage, liquidity and rating profile: group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x, ₹1,738 cr TTM EBITDA, ₹3,382 cr cash, with Raymond Limited at -0.34x and Raymond Realty at 1.70x; the engineering arm reports a ₹77 cr net cash surplus.
points.quote: Net cash surplus of Rs77 Cr as of September 2026, backing disciplined growth investments.

points.point: Who actually put up money: the promoter group, not an outside activist or lender — the May 2026 issue is justified on promoter conviction and on speed versus a QIP or rights issue, given time-sensitive acquisition targets.
points.quote: Promoter participation in the fund-raise demonstrates a strong personal commitment and conviction in the Company's strategic direction.

points.point: The stock exchanges, not investors, forced disclosure changes: NSE (June 3, 2026) and BSE (June 8, 2026) queries produced a corrigendum that dropped subsidiary capex/capacity expansion and re-labelled 75% of proceeds as acquisition funding including acquisition-debt repayment.
points.quote: Funding acquisitions of businesses in India and internationally across targeted growth sectors either directly or through subsidiary entities for organic and inorganic growth including repayment of acquisition debt upto 75% of the aggregate proceeds of the issue; and

points.point: Public institutions were not uniformly convinced by the promoter-funded step: 31.72% of institutional votes polled went against the June 18, 2026 resolution (overall 96.36% in favour), whereas the October 3, 2026 Minerva resolution passed with 99.9978% in favour and institutions 100% in favour.
points.quote: Whether promoter/promoter group are interested in the agenda/resolution? Yes

points.point: Asked on June 24-25, 2026 about a reported German engineering acquisition (Deharde), the company neither confirmed a target nor denied the programme, pointing back to the stated objects of the warrant issue.
points.quote: The Company evaluates various strategic opportunities in the ordinary course, for growth and expansion of its business.

points.point: The January 27, 2026 Scheme of Amalgamation runs opposite to the demergers — wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover, ₹376 lakh net worth) is absorbed into Raymond Limited with no shares issued, purely for structural simplicity and focus.
points.quote: To enable simplified structure and greater management focus on the business, it is imperative for the Transferor Company to be merged into the Transferee Company.

points.point: The amalgamation rationale lists the specific benefits claimed from collapsing subsidiaries into the listed holdco, the same vocabulary used for the larger separation.
points.quote: Simplification of overall group structure by fully integrating EBAL's garmenting operations directly into RL and creating efficiencies through amalgamation;

rationale.what_management_expects: Three focused listed platforms, each with its own board, ratings and balance sheet. Lifestyle: premiumisation, net cash of ₹69 cr. Realty: ~20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, ~20% ROCE, 9-10% PAT margin, debt/equity below 1.0x. Engineering Raymond Ltd.: aerospace scale-up at ~21% segment margins, operating leverage (PBT margin 6.4% vs 4.4%), and warrant capital for acquisitions without pre-funding dilution.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts were provided; filings never explain demerger mechanics, ratios, record dates, costs, who requested it, or why garmenting sits under the engineering holdco.

deal.size_statement: "This strategic move comes as Raymond's Real Estate Business has achieved scale, reporting revenue of INR 1,593 Cr. (43% YoY growth) and EBITDA of INR 370 Cr. in FY24, positioning it well to chart its own growth path as a separate entity." (Press Release, July 4, 2024). The turnover table in the same board disclosure states: "Turnover of Real Estate Business Undertaking as on 31 March 2024 — 1,59,265 [INR in Lakhs]; Percentage to the total turnover of RL as on 31 March 2024 — 24.16%". Apportionment of cost of acquisition of equity shares (May 13, 2025): "Raymond Limited 60.92%" and "Raymond Realty Limited 39.08%".
deal.promoter_holding_parent: Raymond Limited shareholding pattern in the July 4, 2024 board disclosure: "Promoters 3,26,26,525 — 49.01%" (both pre-Scheme and post-Scheme); "Public 3,39,24,906 — 50.96%"; "Non Promoter – Non Public 22,300 — 0.03%". The Q2/H1 FY2027 group presentation (reporting benchmark 30-Sept-2026) states only a range across the three listed entities: "PROMOTER STEWARDSHIP 48.87% – 59.62% PUBLIC FREE FLOAT 40.36% – 51.10% REPORTING BENCHMARK 30-Sept-2026".
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2024 real estate demerger — mirror shareholding; pre and post shareholding of RRL as disclosed on July 4, 2024: pre-Scheme "Promoters 16,50,000 — 100.00"; post-Scheme "Promoters 3,26,26,525 — 49.01 / Public 3,39,24,906 — 50.96 / Non Promoter – Non Public 22,300 — 0.03"; "Upon the Scheme coming into effect on the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme), on demerger, RRL shall issue 6,65,73,731 (Six Crores Sixty Five Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty One) Equity Shares of RRL having face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each to the equity shareholders of RL." 2024 engineering composite scheme — "Post Scheme, RPAL & MPPL will cease to exist and shareholding in JKTTL & RGCEL will change from 100% to 66.3% as subsidiaries of Raymond Limited."; CARE Ratings (July 4, 2025): "Post the process, MPPL and RPAL will cease to exist, and RL & its promoters will hold 67.40%, MPPL promoters 28.5%, and balance will be with the others and minority shareholders of the new companies." 2023 lifestyle demerger — promoter holding in Raymond Lifestyle Limited not stated (shares issued to all RL shareholders in the ratio 4 RLL shares of INR 2 for every 5 RL shares of INR 10).
deal.public_shareholders_get: Real estate demerger (2025): "In accordance with provisions of the Scheme, RRL shall issue and allot 1 (One) fully paid-up equity shares of RRL having face value of INR 10/- each for every 1 (One) fully paid up equity shares of INR 10/- each of RL to the shareholders of the Company whose names are recorded in the register of members and / or records of the depository as on the Record Date (i.e., Wednesday, May 14, 2025)." Lifestyle demerger (2024): "Each equity shareholder of Raymond Limited as on the Record Date, will be issued and allotted 4 (four) fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each of Raymond Lifestyle Limited for every 5 (five) fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each of the Raymond Limited." Engineering composite scheme (NCLT order 2025): shareholders of Raymond Limited receive nothing — "No. The shares issued by JKTTL and RGCEL would not be listed on any of the stock exchanges." and "Not applicable, since the Scheme is between subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries of the Company." Fractional entitlements under the lifestyle scheme: "Fractional entitlement, if any, shall be consolidated and allotted to the Trustee (as defined in the Scheme), who shall hold such shares in trust on behalf of the relevant security holders entitled to such fractional entitlements, for the specific purpose of selling the same in the market and on such sale, distribute to the relevant security holders in proportion to their respective fractional entitlements, the net sale proceeds of such shares (after deduction of applicable taxes and costs incurred and subject to withholding tax, if any)."

This fiscal, we announced our ethnic portfolio by acquiring TCNS to complete the gap in premium ethnic space that the portfolio had. Additionally, we run our TMRW business with a strong portfolio of digital first brands. These were key additions to make our portfolio more comprehensive in line with the long -term strategy of the company. Pursuant to that, we have also reclassified our segmental reporting this quarter, and we'll continue to share the financials in a similar way till demerger becomes effective. The two proposed entities now are Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited consisting of Lifestyle brands, You th Western Wear, Innerwear and Sportswear, while Aditya Birla Fashion and R etail Limited consists of Masstige and Value retail, Ethnic, Super Premium and Digital First Brands. This strategic demerger of ABFRL is paving the way for the creation of two separate growth engines, each with a clear capital allocation strategy and uniq ue path for value creation. rationale.rationale: The business being separated is the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle / western-wear branded-apparel business — Louis Philippe-type premium lifestyle brands plus Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear and the (exited) Forever 21 — demerged out of ABFRL into a separately listed Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), leaving in ABFRL the Pantaloons/OWND (ex-Style Up) masstige-value play, the ethnic portfolio (Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil, Tasva, Jaypore, TCNS/W-Aurelia), luxury (The Collective, Galeries Lafayette) and digital-first TMRW. Management's stated reason is a capital-allocation and focus problem inside one company: ABLBL is a mature, high-margin, cash-generating platform (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, EBITDA margin 16.2%, up 100bps; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 17%, +200bps; brands at 19.3% FY25 margin, retail LTL 9-12%) whose growth lever — an 'aggressive' net 300+ store rollout, 200 of them own-capex — was 'underleveraged in the combined entity', so the demerger was explicitly designed to 'leave that cash for allowing that business to soar' and let it invest through downcycles when franchisees cannot. Conversely the retained ABFRL is a portfolio of loss-making/investment-phase businesses (TCNS, Tasva, Style Up/OWND, Galeries Lafayette, TMRW) that needed a clean, cash-rich balance sheet: ABFRL raised USD 490 million via QIP plus preferential issue (promoters paying a significant premium) to make demerged ABFRL 'debt-free' with gross cash of INR2,350 crores at consolidation, versus ABLBL starting with ~INR700-781 crores net debt to be repaid in 2-3 years. Dikshit framed the underlying problem as too many simultaneous growth bets starving each other of attention — 'Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us' — i.e. separation is about focus, differentiated capital structures (dividend-paying ABLBL vs. investment-funding ABFRL) and separate value-creation journeys. The same philosophy is applied one level down: TMRW was built as a separate company from 2021 precisely so it would raise its own capital (INR437 crores from ServiceNow Ventures for ~11%, INR440-450 crores equity in FY26, INR500 crores NCDs, ~INR800 crores cash) and eventually have 'its own public market journey'. Mechanically the demerger was Board-approved 19 April 2024, shareholder-approved 21 January 2025, NCLT-sanctioned 27 March 2025, effective 1 May 2025 with an appointed date of 1 April 2024, a 1:1 share entitlement (1,22,02,94,773 ABLBL shares allotted 26 May 2025) and ABLBL listed 23 June 2025; it also reset intercompany accounting, producing a one-off INR97 crore gain from ending inter-division elimination on Madura stock sold through Pantaloons and INR148 crore of depreciation not charged on discontinued operations. Targets attached to the split: ABLBL to 'double in scale' and expand margins over five years and pay dividends at the earliest opportunity; ABFRL to deliver 3x revenue and 2x margin over five years, with most of that margin uplift coming from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from EBITDA-negative to profitable.
rationale.evolution: The demerger was Board-approved on 19 April 2024 and by the Feb 17, 2025 call was 'progressing well', with NCLT listed for the third week of March 2025, the USD 490 million QIP/preferential raise just closed, and guidance that ABLBL would open FY26 with INR700 crores debt while demerged ABFRL held ~INR1,300-1,500 crores cash; in that call the rationale sharpened from generic 'unlock value' into the specific point that Lifestyle Brands' store expansion had been 'underleveraged in the combined entity'. By the May 26, 2025 call it was 'successfully completed' — two 'focused fashion power houses', ABLBL shares allotted 1:1, ABFRL carrying INR2,350 crores gross cash, with the first explicit five-year targets (ABLBL to double in scale and pay dividends; ABFRL 3x revenue, 2x margin) and the clearest statement of cause, that a combined ABFRL with '5 or 6' growth opportunities starved businesses like Innerwear of attention. The Aug 14, 2025 call confirmed completion and listing on 23 June 2025 and extended the same logic to TMRW raising its own external capital, and by the Nov 2025/Feb 2026/May 2026 calls the demerger survives only as an accounting comparability footnote (the INR97 crore base-quarter gain) while the structural work shifts to simplification inside ABFRL — the Feb 5, 2026 Scheme amalgamating wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor into ABFRL, NCLT-sanctioned 2 July 2026 and effective 1 August 2026.

points.point: First formal framing of the separation: the western-wear brands business is being carved into a separate listed entity, ABLBL, with NCLT scheduled for the third week of March 2025 and completion expected in 2-3 months.
points.quote: First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months.

points.point: The USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue was raised inside the pre-demerger company specifically so the retained ABFRL would emerge debt-free with enough cash to fund its loss-making businesses until self-sustaining.
points.quote: The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its balance sheet by making it debt-free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sustainable.

points.point: Capital structures were deliberately split asymmetrically — debt with the cash-generating lifestyle entity, cash with the investment-phase entity.
points.quote: We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.

points.point: The sharpest stated rationale: Lifestyle Brands' store-expansion opportunity was under-exploited while inside the combined company, and the demerger was designed to free its own cash for that expansion (300+ stores, ~200 own-capex).
points.quote: And one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar.

points.point: A second, cyclical argument: as a standalone entity ABLBL can self-fund store rollout when franchisee partners pull back in weak demand periods.
points.quote: Lifestyle Brands particularly also will have access to their own cash. So their ability to grow even in downtimes, when franchisees sometimes are not in a position to invest during the low time, the business will be able to sort of short circuit that and invest deeper.

points.point: The umbrella justification offered to investors was value unlock via two independently capitalised, independently growing entities.
points.quote: The completion of these steps in the next 2, 3 months will enable us to unlock value through 2 independent entities, both with attractive growth potential and a strong balance sheet through a resilient growth-oriented business model sharpened over time.

points.point: Completion announced: demerger done, 1:1 entitlement, ABLBL shares allotted to ABFRL shareholders and listing targeted by end-June 2025.
points.quote: We successfully completed the demerger, creating two focused fashion power houses, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, ABLBL; and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited, ABFRL, both now set on independent high-growth trajectories.

points.point: The underlying diagnosis stated plainly in answer to a question on why Innerwear had stagnated at ~INR500 crores since 2016 — one company carrying five or six growth bets could not give each the management attention and capital it needed, hence restructuring into separate entities.
points.quote: I think as it becomes part of a company which is fundamentally profitable free cash flow generator and it's an important part of its growth journey, Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us.

points.point: Same answer gives the structural logic for the split: multiple growth opportunities in one company required separate capitalisation and structure.
points.quote: ABFRL, the combined ABFRL business had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively.

points.point: Both halves were shown as independently healthy at separation — ABLBL Q4 margin +200bps (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% margin), demerged ABFRL Q4 EBITDA more than doubled to INR199 crores comparable.
points.quote: Both entities delivered robust profitability, ABLBL clocking 200 basis points margin expansion, while demerged ABFRL more than doubling its EBITDA.

points.point: ABLBL is positioned as the self-funding, net-debt-INR781-crore, dividend-paying mature platform with a 300+ store FY26 pipeline, to double in scale over five years.
points.quote: ABLBL shall be a dividend-distributing company at the earliest appropriate opportunity.

points.point: Retained ABFRL's post-demerger ambition quantified; management added that most of the margin uplift must come from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from EBITDA-negative to profitable.
points.quote: ABFRL with a sharpened brand portfolio, a comprehensive diversified play across high-growth segments and a gross cash balance of INR2,350 crores is set to unlock the next phase of growth, targeting a 3x revenue scale up and 2x margin expansion over the next 5 years.

points.point: Accounting consequence of separating the two: the inter-division elimination on Madura brand merchandise sold through Pantaloons ends, producing a one-off INR97 crore inventory write-up gain, alongside INR148 crore of depreciation not charged on discontinued operations.
points.quote: Reported EBITDA includes gain of INR97 crores on account of discontinuation of interdivision elimination post demerger as company's financials get reset to report on independent and stand-alone basis going forward.

points.point: Process closed out and ABLBL separately listed, completing the separation.
points.quote: On demerger, as previously communicated, all requisite processes have been successfully completed, culminating in the creation of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited.

points.point: The same 'separate entity, separate capital' philosophy is applied one level down to TMRW, created as a separate company in 2021 so it would raise external capital (INR437 crores from ServiceNow Ventures for ~11%) and eventually list on its own rather than consume ABFRL's cash.
points.quote: And over the next 8, 10 years, build a company which can find a very digital native path to this industry, which is fashion industry and have its own public market journey as we go forward from private to public.

points.point: A year on, the demerger persists only as a comparability adjustment in reported numbers; underlying ABFRL is now at standalone EBITDA breakeven and ex-TMRW consolidated pre-Ind AS loss narrowed to INR33 crores.
points.quote: It is important to note that last year included a onetime gain of INR97 crores relating to inventory write-up and accounting treatment relating to demerger, which was explained in detail during Q4 results of last year.

points.point: Leverage guidance is explicitly carried across both the pre-demerger combined company and the post-demerger entities, at 2-3x for any of the group's fashion companies.
points.quote: We are very far, but that's the guidance we gave 5 years back and 3 years back.

points.point: The later corporate action runs the other way: wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor are amalgamated INTO ABFRL (Board 5 Feb 2026, NCLT order 2 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026, effective 1 August 2026) with no consideration or share issue, purely to simplify structure and cut administrative cost.
points.quote: Seamless integration and better financial strength and flexibility for the Amalgamated Company, which would result in maximizing overall shareholder value.

points.point: Stated benefits of that simplification step are legal/operating structure and cost, not value unlock — a contrast with the ABLBL demerger rationale.
points.quote: Streamlining of business & administrative operations consequently reducing administrative & other operating costs;

rationale.what_management_expects: ABLBL: own cash flows fund 300+ net stores, scale to double and margins expand from 16.2%, INR781 crore net debt repaid in 2-3 years, dividends paid early. Demerged ABFRL: debt-free with INR2,350 crore cash to fund OWND, Tasva, TCNS, luxury and TMRW; 3x revenue and 2x margin in five years, chiefly by turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW profitable; sharper focus and attention per business.
rationale.gaps: No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded it; no tax, dis-synergy, cost-allocation, brand-royalty or transition-service detail; no reason given why INR700-781 crore debt stayed with ABLBL.

deal.size_statement: The turnover of the MFL Business of the Demerged Company as on March 31, 2023, was Rs. 7,607 crores and forms 64.81 % of the total standalone turnover of the Demerged Company  as on March 31, 2023.
deal.promoter_holding_parent: Promoter and promoter group: 52,75,17,139 shares, 46.28% pre-issue (pre-issue shareholding includes 6,85,83,059 equity shares allotted on January 21, 2025 pursuant to Qualified Institutional Placement) and 56,83,51,129 shares, 46.58% post the preferential issue, per the Corrigendum to the EGM Notice dated February 4, 2025 (EGM held February 13, 2025). Of this, Indian individuals/HUF 21,56,877 (0.19%) and bodies corporate 52,53,60,262 (46.09%).
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2024 demerger into ABLBL — mirror shareholding: "Upon effectiveness of the Scheme, the entire existing equity share capital of the Resulting Company shall stand cancelled and new equity shares (as mentioned in point (e) below) shall be allotted by the Resulting Company to the equity shareholders of the Demerged Company on the Record Date in accordance with the Scheme. Thus, the equity shareholding in the Resulting Company would m irror the shareholding of the Demerged Company." 2024 TCNS amalgamation and 2026 Jaypore/TG Apparel amalgamation: no promoter holding in a new entity arises — for the 2026 scheme "the shares held directly by the Amalgamated Company in the Amalgamating Companies along with nominees, will stand cancelled and no consideration whatsoever shall pass from the Amalgamated Company."
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2024 demerger into ABLBL: "ABLBL shall issue and allot 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of ABLBL having face value of Rs 10 (Rupees Ten) each for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of Rs 10 (Rupees Ten) each of the Company to the shareholders of the Company whose names are recorded in the register of members and / or records of the depository a s on the Record Date (i.e., Thursday, 22nd May 2025)." — in addition to their existing shareholding in ABFRL: "the shareholders of ABFRL will get one share of ABLBL for every one share in ABFRL, in addi tion to their existing shareholding in ABFRL." 2024 TCNS amalgamation: ABFRL's own public shareholders received nothing; TCNS shareholders received "11 fully paid-up equity shares of the face value Rs. 10 each of ABFRL for every 6 fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Rs. 2 each held in TCNS." 2026 Jaypore/TG Apparel amalgamation: nothing — no consideration passes and no new shares are issued.
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of stock options / RSUs / SARs in the schemes is not stated. Insider and employee-trust shareholding is disclosed in Annexure A of the EGM Notice (Corrigendum dated February 4, 2025): "Directors and their relatives (excluding independent directors and nominee directors)  7,08,556  0.06 ... Key Managerial Personnel  1,24,564  0.01" and "Non - Promoter Non - Public Shareholders (Employee Benefit Trust)  44,06,334  0.39" (post-issue 0.06%, 0.01% and 0.36% respectively). The standalone financial results "include the financial information of ABFRL Employee Welfare Trust". On intent to subscribe to the preferential issue: "Other than above, none of the promoters, directors, key management personnel or senior management of the Company intends to subscribe the offer." New ABLBL management appointments were made (Ashish Dikshit as Managing Director, Vishak Kumar as Deputy Managing Director and CEO, Dharmendra Lodha as CFO, Rajeev Agrawal as Company Secretary, and senior managerial personnel Puneet Kumar Malik, Jacob John and Narahari N), but no incentive plan, exercise price or pricing date is stated.
deal.insider_actions: Promoter group subscribed to the pre-demerger capital raise: "The board of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited ("ABFRL") in its meeting today approved raising of USD 500 Mn through a combination of preferential issuance and Qualified Institutional Placement ("QIP") of equity shares. The Preferential issuance of USD 275 Mn will be led by the promoter group investing USD 150 Mn. and Fidelity Investments investing USD 125 Mn. The promoter participation is at a significant premium of 17.5% over yesterday's closing price, signalling strong conviction in the value creation potential of ABFRL." Specifically: "Pilani Investment and Industries Corporation Limited, part of Promoter Group of the Company intends to subscribe up to 4,08,33,990 equity shares in the proposed Preferential Issue" at ₹317.75 per share aggregating up to ₹12,97,50,00,521, taking its holding from 0.35% pre-issue to 3.67% post-issue. At announcement of the demerger: "ABFRL plans to raise ~ Rs. 2500 Cr equity capital within 12 months of demerger with promoter participation" and "The company's promoter group will fully support t he proposed equity raise." Promoter and promoter group voted 52,75,17,139 shares (100%) in favour of the Scheme at the NCLT-convened meeting, and "Whether promoter/ promoter group are intere sted in the agenda/resolution? NO". No promoter or management selling or pledging is stated.
