rationale.rationale: There is no separation, demerger or spin-off of a business by ICICI Bank in these texts — the question's premise is not supported by the transcripts or the filing, and the dominant direction of travel is the opposite: consolidation of group entities into the Bank. The nearest things management actually described are four entity-level reorganizations. (1) Pension funds: the Board on July 19, 2025 approved acquiring 100% of ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, moving it from a step-down subsidiary of ICICI Life to a direct wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; the share purchase agreement was executed January 12, 2026, and on the Jan 2026 media call Sandeep Batra said the rationale was that 'the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion,' i.e. 'synergising with the banking set of customers'; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on the sale, which was part of why its FY2026 PAT rose 34.6% to Rs. 16.00 billion (25.0% excluding the sale). (2) ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC, completed with ICICI Prudential AMC managing the transferred funds effective April 1, 2026; the stated purpose was 'offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity,' while ICICI Venture keeps only 'certain advisory activities' and 'certain residual funds' — ICICI Venture's PAT jumped to Rs. 1.5 billion in FY2026 from Rs. 0.2 billion in FY2025. (3) A small divestment of the Bank's entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV (set up around 2006), which Batra on Apr 2025 called 'a very small amount' done to 'rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.' (4) Closure of the Offshore Banking Unit in the SEEPZ, Mumbai, for which RBI gave a no-objection letter in May 2026 (a prior OBU closure had already pushed Rs. 3.40 billion of negative foreign currency translation reserve into the Q4-FY2024 P&L). Against these, the Bank was pulling businesses in, not pushing them out: ICICI Securities was delisted on March 24, 2025 and became wholly owned (56 million ICICI Bank shares issued at a 67:100 swap, which Anindya Banerjee cited as the main reason net worth rose about Rs. 20,000 crore sequentially, 'while it's capital neutral'); the Bank bought ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% more of ICICI Life, explicitly 'towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding' against stock-based compensation dilution; it infused Rs. 5.0 billion (including Rs. 500 crore in Q3-FY2026) into ICICI Home Finance, which Batra justified as meeting 'the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view'; and it acquired the remaining equity of I-Process Services. The only genuine ownership separations described are at the partner/JV level, not the Bank's: ICICI Prudential AMC listed on BSE and NSE effective December 19, 2025 following Prudential Corporation Holdings' February 2025 announcement of a 'potential listing and partial divestment of its stake,' and after PCHL agreed on May 17, 2026 to buy 75% of Bharti Life, ICICI Life applied to IRDAI to reclassify PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor' and to rename itself 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' (IRDAI approved the name change August 7, 2026).
rationale.evolution: No separation idea ever surfaces as such: on Apr 2025 (call of April 19, 2025) the only disposal discussed is the small NIIT Institute JV stake sale, framed as portfolio simplification, in the same quarter ICICI Securities was delisted into the Bank (March 24, 2025). The ICICI Venture PE/VC/real-estate fund management transfer was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 and the pension-fund acquisition on July 19, 2025 — the same day as the Jul 2025 call, where neither was mentioned and no analyst asked. By Jan 2026 (call of January 17, 2026) Batra confirmed the pension step-down subsidiary had been brought under the Bank, noting 'we explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision,' and the Oct 2025 transcript is unreadable so any interim discussion is unverifiable; the Apr 2026 call (April 18, 2026) contains no mention of any of it, and only the September 18, 2026 Annual Securities Report records the ICICI Venture transfer as effective April 1, 2026 and the PCHL promoter-to-investor reclassification.

points.point: Batra confirmed the Bank had taken over the pension fund business from ICICI Life, explaining it was a step-down subsidiary and that the decision had been disclosed about two quarters earlier.
points.quote: It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision.

points.point: The stated rationale for moving the pension fund manager under the Bank was synergy with the Bank's customer base and faster expansion, not value unlocking or capital release.
points.quote: We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.

points.point: Asked directly whether the pension business had been acquired from the subsidiary, Batra confirmed it in one word; no numbers, consideration or targets were given on the call.
points.quote: Yes, we have.

points.point: The only outright exit discussed on any call — the entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV set up around 2006 — was framed as immaterial portfolio simplification, with no consideration disclosed.
points.quote: And over the period, we are just wanting to rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.

points.point: The one real carve-out of a business line in the texts: ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC on May 8, 2025, with ICICI Prudential AMC managing those funds from April 1, 2026.
points.quote: On May 8, 2025, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited's Board of Directors and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Board of Directors, in their respective meetings, approved, in principle, a proposal to transfer the private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business of ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.

points.point: The purpose of that transfer was to give ICICI Prudential AMC a complete asset-class platform, leaving ICICI Venture with only advisory work and residual funds.
points.quote: The transaction enabled the offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity, by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.

points.point: The pension transaction was a Board-approved intra-group purchase to convert a step-down subsidiary into a direct wholly owned subsidiary, conditional on RBI and PFRDA approvals; the SPA was executed January 12, 2026.
points.quote: The Board at its meeting held on July 19, 2025 approved the acquisition of 100% shareholding in ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited to make ICICI PFM a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank, subject to the Reserve Bank of India, PFRDA and other necessary approvals.

points.point: The seller side quantified it: ICICI Life's FY2026 PAT of Rs. 16.00 billion (up 34.6%) included a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on selling the pension subsidiary; growth was 25.0% excluding it.
points.quote: The profit after tax of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited grew by 34.6% year-on-year from Rs. 11.9 billion in fiscal 2025 to Rs. 16.0 billion in fiscal 2026, primarily driven by higher investment income from Shareholders' funds, which includes a gain of Rs. 1.1 billion realized from sale of 100% equity shareholding in ICICI PFM.

points.point: Direction of travel was consolidation, not separation: ICICI Securities was delisted and absorbed as a wholly owned subsidiary on March 24, 2025, with Bank shares issued to its public shareholders at a 67:100 swap.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement amongst ICICI Bank Limited and ICICI Securities Limited and their respective shareholders, ICICI Securities Limited has been delisted from stock exchanges on March 24, 2025 and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank.

points.point: Banerjee attributed the ~Rs. 20,000 crore sequential jump in net worth to the shares issued to ICICI Securities' minority holders, describing it as capital neutral rather than value creating.
points.quote: So, we would have issued shares to the minority shareholders of ISec that would have, while it's capital neutral, it would have increased the net-worth by a substantial amount.

points.point: Stake increases in the listed subsidiaries were defensive against stock-compensation dilution, not steps toward separation: ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% of ICICI Life (taking it to ~52.8%).
points.quote: This purchase was primarily for the purposes of maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited were it to grant stock-based compensation.

points.point: The only partner-level separation: Prudential Corporation Holdings signalled a partial exit from the AMC, which listed on December 19, 2025, and after agreeing to buy 75% of Bharti Life it is being reclassified from promoter to investor in ICICI Life, which is renaming itself.
points.quote: Consequently, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited has applied to IRDAI for the reclassification of PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor', along with a proposal to change the name of the company from 'ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited' to 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited'.

points.point: Capital was being pushed into subsidiaries rather than freed from them — Rs. 500 crore into ICICI Home Finance in Q3-FY2026 (Rs. 5.0 billion in FY2026), with Batra committing to fund it further.
points.quote: We are happy to infuse the capital to meet the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view.

points.point: The only operational unit being shut is an offshore branch, not a business: RBI issued a no-objection letter in May 2026 for closing the SEEPZ Mumbai Offshore Banking Unit.
points.quote: In May 2026, the Bank received the no-objection letter from the Reserve Bank of India to close the Offshore Banking Unit located in the Santacruz Electronic Exports Promotion Zone, Mumbai.

points.point: The most recent call contains no mention of any separation, demerger, carve-out or subsidiary restructuring — management's framing of strategy is entirely about growing PBT excluding treasury within one integrated bank.
points.quote: At ICICI Bank, our strategic focus continues to be on growing profit before tax excluding treasury through the 360-degree customer centric approach and by serving opportunities across ecosystems and micro-markets.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the moves that were made: the pension business gains Bank-customer synergies and faster expansion; ICICI Prudential AMC gains a full asset-class platform including private equity; ICICI Venture keeps only advisory and residual funds; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain. No margin, capital-release, valuation-unlock or focus claims were offered.
rationale.gaps: Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger exists. No consideration for NIIT or ICICI Venture's transfer, no pension AUM/economics, no lender, investor or partner demands, no analyst questions, and Oct 2025's transcript is unreadable.

deal.size_statement: not stated
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated (the documents state no promoter or promoter group holding for ICICI Bank; they note "Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas holds 1,149,973,715 equity shares of the Bank constituting 16.0% of the equity share capital of the Bank at June 30, 2026" as depositary for ADSs)
deal.promoter_holding_after: 2025 listing of ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited: "We had 53.0% interest in the entity and PCHL owned 34.6% at March 31, 2026." — after the Bank's purchase of 2.0% from PCHL. 2023 Delisting Scheme: "with effect from March 24, 2025, ICICI Securities Limited has become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank". 2025-2026 pension transaction: "the Bank acquired 100% shareholding in ICICI PFM. Accordingly, ICICI PFM is now a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank." ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited: "Following this, the Bank's shareholding in ICICI Life stands at approximately 52.8%."
deal.public_shareholders_get: not stated for the 2025 listing and partial divestment of ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited — no distribution or entitlement to ICICI Bank's own public shareholders is described (the divestment is of PCHL's stake). Under the 2023 Delisting Scheme the Bank issued its shares to the subsidiary's public shareholders, not to its own: "On March 26, 2025, the Bank allotted its equity shares to the public shareholders of ICICI Securities as of the record date, in accordance with a swap ratio of 67 to 100, as provided in the Delisting Scheme." The 2025-2026 pension and ICICI Venture business transfers were intra-group; nothing is stated as received by public shareholders of the parent.
deal.management_incentives: "In June 2025, the Board approved the purchase of up to 2.0% additional shareholding in the ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited. Following the receipt of requisite approvals, the Bank purchased 2.0% additional shareholding from PCHL. This purchase was primarily for the purposes of maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited were it to grant stock-based compensation." For the life insurer: "The Board, at its meeting held in February 2026, approved purchase of up to 2.0% additional shareholding in its subsidiary, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited... This purchase was primarily towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in the event of exercise of stock-based compensation of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited." Parent capital includes "capital and reserves and surplus including employees' stock options outstanding at year-end fiscal 2026, were Rs. 3,630.6 billion". No treatment of existing grants under a scheme, no new plan in a new entity, and no exercise price or pricing date are stated.
deal.insider_actions: "In February 2025, the Bank's joint venture partner, PCHL, made an announcement regarding a potential listing and partial divestment of its stake in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited, subject to market conditions, requisite approvals and other considerations." "Following the receipt of requisite approvals, the Bank purchased 2.0% additional shareholding from PCHL." For the life insurer: "the Bank has, through multiple tranches executed between July 22, 2026 and September 2, 2026, completed the purchase of approximately 2.0% of ICICI Life's equity share capital at June 30, 2026, through the stock exchange mechanism." "PCHL entered into definitive agreements on May 17, 2026, pursuant to which PCHL has agreed to acquire a 75% stake in Bharti Life Insurance Company Limited" and "ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited has applied to IRDAI for the reclassification of PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor'". No pledging is stated.

entities.name: ICICI Securities Limited
entities.scheme: 2023 Delisting Scheme under Regulation 37 of SEBI (Delisting of Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021 — a share-swap delisting (not a spin-off); completed March 24, 2025
entities.status: effective (delisted from the stock exchanges and now a wholly owned subsidiary)

entities.listing: not to be listed — delisted from the stock exchanges with effect from March 24, 2025
entities.turnover: not stated (consolidated profit after tax of Rs. 17.1 billion in fiscal 2026 compared to Rs. 17.5 billion in fiscal 2025)

entities.name: ICICI Pension Fund Management Limited
former_names: ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited

entities.status: effective (now a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank)
entities.business: Registered pension fund manager under the National Pension System and approved 'point of presence' for distribution and servicing through physical and online channels.

entities.name: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited

entities.name: ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited

rationale.rationale: Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd. (TEIL) put through a single composite scheme of arrangement that does two things: it amalgamates its ~61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Ltd. (SSEL, the Shamli sugar/distillery unit) into TEIL, and it demerges TEIL's Power Transmission Business (PTB — high-speed/turbo gearboxes at Mysuru, plus the incubating defence business) into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd. (TPTL) for separate listing, which management described on the Feb 2026 call as being done 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' and in Feb 2025 as 'value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.' The problem being solved is that PTB's economics look nothing like the rest of TEIL: PTB ran PBIT margins above 34% in FY25 (PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, on turnover up 27%, order booking ₹475+ crore), about 36% in H1 FY26 and 41% in Q2 FY26, against sugar and alcohol businesses whose output and input prices are both administered (SAP up ₹300/tonne in UP, no ethanol price revision for two years, maize at ₹20–26/kg, MSP unrevised), and whose FY25 segment profits fell on a 69bps recovery decline. Investors made exactly this point on the call: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers told management that 'barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes,' the other businesses 'produce a very mercurial kind of an outcome,' and Tarun Sawhney conceded TEIL had not met its return profile on ethanol capital. Separation is also meant to let PTB fund and run its own growth: a board-approved capex of ₹340 crore in three tranches (taking gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, with just over ₹100 crore sanctioned for the defence facility and ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore on defence), an export-led order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%), a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, acquired 100% by TPTL), aftermarket at ~40% of gears, and a global addressable high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million. Crucially, TEIL deliberately did not do a clean 100% separation: it retains roughly 30% of TPTL, and Sawhney justified this by the defence business — 'we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for,' where establishing pre-qualifications and the ability to bid involves 'balance sheet considerations… from a Group perspective,' plus the precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, which he called 'actually quite a positive one for the Company.' Post-approval TEIL said ICRA reaffirmed its long-term rating at AA+ Stable, lifting it off watch, and that TPTL goes out 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet' to fund its capex and opex.
rationale.evolution: The board approved the composite scheme on 10 December 2024, and the Feb 2025 (5 Feb) call was the first investor call after it — there Sawhney framed it as value unlocking, guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year,' and defended the retained ~30% stake against Resham Jain's push for a clean structure; Bharat Shah's 'mercurial' critique of the commodity businesses came on the same call. By Jun 2025 (28 May) the scheme was stuck with SEBI with NCLT next, guidance slipped to 'middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year,' and Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure ahead of listing, which Sawhney accepted as a 'welcome suggestion'; on Aug 2025 (30 July) approvals were still pending with SEBI and stock-exchange queries, with Sawhney allowing it 'could add another 30-odd days.' Nov 2025 (7 Nov) reported stock-exchange approval (observation letters 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings set for late November/early December, plus TPTL's 100% acquisition of Swiss step-down subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH; Feb 2026 (2 Feb) reported shareholder/creditor approval in December 2025, an NCLT hearing in February, systems work to let TPTL 'hit the ground sprinting,' and Sawhney's line that 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.' On Jun 2026 (4 June) he confirmed the scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval (orders 7 and 18 May), appointed dates of 1 April 2025 for the amalgamation and 1 April 2026 for the demerger, the SSEL record date of 3 June 2026, and guided to a TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate results and earnings calls for both companies — in the event the demerger record date was 22 July 2026, 7,34,54,338 TPTL shares were allotted on 28 July 2026 (TPTL thereby ceasing to be a subsidiary and becoming an associate), and TPTL listed and began trading only on 12 October 2026.

points.point: First call after the 10 December 2024 board approval; Sawhney introduced the composite scheme — amalgamation of ~61.77%-held SSEL into TEIL and transfer of the PTB undertaking to wholly-owned TPTL — explicitly as a value-unlocking exercise by the Board.
points.quote: I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.

points.point: Resham Jain of DSP Asset Managers challenged the structure, arguing TEIL's retained ~30% stake in TPTL would re-import a holdco discount and that a clean separation was needed for value to be unlocked.
points.quote: It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have happened in a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.

points.point: Sawhney's two reasons for keeping ~30%: the positive precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, and — decisively — that the incubating defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and be allowed to bid, since defence is co-located with gears in Mysuru.
points.quote: The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.

points.point: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers made the investor case for separation directly — PTB is the predictable, brick-by-brick business while the regulated sugar/ethanol/water businesses swing unpredictably — and Sawhney conceded the ethanol capital had not met its return profile.
points.quote: On a shorter-term basis, interplay of the other businesses always produces a very mercurial kind of an outcome, sometimes to delight, but other times to depress.

points.point: Same call quantified why PTB deserves its own listing: incremental board-approved capex of ₹60 crore taking gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026 from ~₹400 crore, order book at an all-time-high ₹377 crore, and a global high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million.
points.quote: The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business. This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.

points.point: Initial timeline guidance: NCLT sanction expected by the end of calendar 2025.
points.quote: As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.

points.point: Q4 FY25 call showed the margin gap the demerger exposes — PTB turnover up 27% with PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%) and PBIT margins above 34%, record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore and PBIT ₹46.5 crore — while the scheme itself sat pending at SEBI, with separation guided to Q4 FY26.
points.quote: So we're expecting that by the middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year, we will have the separation of the PTB business.

points.point: Resham Jain asked management to begin disclosing PTB in granular detail — customers, industry mix — precisely because it was about to be separately listed after being buried inside a much larger company; Sawhney accepted.
points.quote: And since it was a part of a much larger company, the understanding of this business from the very granular perspective was much lower.

points.point: Q1 FY26: approvals still outstanding, with continuous follow-up at SEBI and stock-exchange queries answered; slippage of about 30 days flagged but Q1-calendar-2026 timing maintained. PTB closing order book was a record ₹423 crore (+38%), with engineering order book just under ₹2,000 crore.
points.quote: The amalgamation with Sir Shadi Lal and the demerger of the Power Transmission business. We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.

points.point: Stock exchanges had cleared the scheme (observation letters of 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for late November/early December; separately, TPTL bought 100% of Triveni Power Transmission GmbH in Switzerland, building the export engine inside the entity being listed.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.

points.point: PTB PBIT margins improved more than 400bps YoY on product mix and cost optimisation (about 36% PBIT for H1, 41% in the quarter), and TPTL was equipped with its own CRM, digital-factory/digital-twin and SAP HANA systems ahead of standing alone.
points.quote: Triveni Power Transmission Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, has acquired a 100% stake in Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, a Swiss company.

points.point: Shareholders and creditors approved in December 2025 with an NCLT hearing in February; management stated the twin purpose as unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies, and said PTB was being equipped with the systems and skills to run as an independent company.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Sawhney signalled the split was imminent and thanked participants for years of feedback, saying the next call would be with two separate companies; a lot of systems work was underway so TPTL could start at full speed with TEIL-level efficiencies.
points.quote: I think the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.

points.point: Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2025 and demerger appointed date 1 April 2026; SSEL record date 3 June 2026, TEIL record date within four weeks, and listing of TPTL anticipated by end-August 2026 with separate board meetings, published results and earnings calls for both entities.
points.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

points.point: Management argued the separated entity is self-funding: of the ₹340 crore board-approved capex in three tranches (output of about ₹700 crore of gears, excluding defence), ₹231 crore was spent by 31 March 2026 including ₹78 crore on defence, with ₹109 crore left to September 2026 — all fundable by TPTL itself.
points.quote: Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.

points.point: A balance-sheet benefit of completion was cited: ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable and removed the under-watch status that the pending scheme had caused, restoring Triveni's historical highest rating.
points.quote: I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long-term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.

points.point: Asked about post-demerger margins, CFO Suresh Taneja said PTB's own dynamics support continuation of the roughly 35% PBIT level it had been delivering inside TEIL; Sawhney also guided that exports of original equipment should exceed half of PTB sales in the near future.
points.quote: As regards to the PTB business, it has got its own dynamics, as a matter of fact. So far, we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT. I think the same trend is expected to continue in future also.

points.point: Entitlement terms: TEIL shareholders receive 1 TPTL share of ₹2 face value for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1; SSEL shareholders received 100 TEIL shares of ₹1 for every 137 SSEL shares of ₹10, with 4,308 consolidated fractional shares sold by a trustee and ₹12,24,787 net distributed to 6,064 shareholders by 9 September 2026.
points.quote: For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company

points.point: Demerger record date was 22 July 2026 and 7,34,54,338 TPTL shares were allotted to TEIL shareholders on 28 July 2026, at which point TPTL ceased to be a subsidiary and became an associate of TEIL — confirming the deliberately retained residual stake (3,13,00,000 locked-in shares of the 10,47,54,338 total).
points.quote: Accordingly, the Company ceased to be a subsidiary and become an associate of TEIL.

points.point: TPTL was staffed as a standalone listed company on 28 July 2026: Tarun Sawhney as Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Dhruv M. Sawhney as Non-Executive Chairman, Raman Kumar S. as CFO, Rakesh Kumar Yadav as Company Secretary, EY as internal auditor, with Geeta Bhalla and Suresh Taneja resigning as TPTL directors because of the scheme's implementation.
points.quote: I Suresh Taneja, hereby tender my resignation from the directorship of the Company with effect from closing of business hours on 28th July, 2026, due implementation of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement and the consequent reconstitution of the Board of Directors of the Company.

points.point: For tax purposes the cost of acquisition was split 86.60% to TEIL and 13.40% to TPTL — the only quantified indication in these documents of the relative value attributed to the demerged power transmission business.
points.quote: Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 86.60% 13.40% Triveni Power Transmission Limited

points.point: TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares received BSE and NSE listing and trading approvals on 8 October 2026 and began trading on 12 October 2026 (BSE 544824, NSE TRIVENIPT) — roughly six weeks later than the end-August listing guided on the June 2026 call.
points.quote: Accordingly, the equity shares of the Company shall be listed and admitted to dealings on BSE and NSE with effect from October 12, 2026

rationale.what_management_expects: TPTL: independent listing of a ~35% PBIT, export-led gears and defence business, self-funding its ₹340 crore capex toward ~₹700 crore of gears output, exports above 50%, aftermarket-led margins. TEIL: a cleaner sugar-distillery-water commodity platform with SSEL absorbed, AA+ Stable restored off watch, and cash flows for brownfield/greenfield expansion. Both: unlocked value, operational efficiencies, separate reporting.
rationale.gaps: No valuation basis for the 1:3 ratio, no standalone PTB balance sheet or financials, no quantified dis-synergies, demerger costs, TPTL dividend policy, or why exactly 30% was retained.

turns: The overall performance of the Company during the half year ended September 30, 2023, has been satisfactory. As you all know, H1 is generally muted as off -season expenses in the Sugar business are expensed off during this period. Our Alcohol business has grown very well , due to capacity expansions during FY 23 and the stabili sation of all operations since then. The Power Transmission business is charting new heights, contributing both in size and growth to the Company as a whole. We're all set for the new sugar season and an overall crop that seems healthier due to favourable climatic factors as well as due to the rigorous sugarcane development activities that has been undertaken by the Company 's teams. For the half year, revenue from operations stood at ■ 2,606 crore , an increase of 1.4% and Profit Before Tax stood at ■ 130.2 crore , an increase of 15%. While comparing profitability, we should note that Q2 / H1 FY 23 includes ■ 11 crore of dividend income received from the erstwhile associate company, Triveni Turbine Limited. As you may be aware, Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited has completely divested its stake in Triveni Turbine Limited last year. As such, there is no dividend income in the results under review. Furthermore, the profitability of the quarter at half year considers additional liability against levy molasses, which has impacted profitability of Q2 & H1 FY 24, by ■ 12.1 crore . The total impact being approximately ■ 18.2 crore for the full year. […] So pretty early start, not just compared to last year, but also compared to the last few years . And I think that is primarily to do with fantastic climatic factors, especially in West ern Uttar Pra desh. Turning to the Engineering business es. Q2 FY 24 saw the highest ever quarterly revenue and highest ever profitability in the Power Transmission business , which drove robust half year results. The order booking of the Power Transmission business was ■ 155 crore approximately during the quarter, an increase of 36.1% closing the order book at ■ 282 crore approximately , compared year -on-year it's an increase of 15%. During the quarter, the Water business has also won an important bid at RUDSICO , which is Greater Jaipur and the Letter of Intent (LOI) has been received after the end of the quarter. The outstanding order book for the Engineering businesses combined stood at ■ 1,573 crore . Looking at the financial performance on a consolidated basis . The net turnover increased by 4.7% and 1.4% in Q2 FY 24 and H1 FY 24, primarily driven by higher turnovers in the Alcohol and Power Transmission business. The sales volume in sugar, including exports were lower by 5.9% in Q2 compared to the previous fiscal year. However, the blended reali sations were higher by approximately 6%. Consequently, the turnover was flat during the quarter. Sales volumes for the current half year also include approximately 14,500 tonnes of sugar that was exported in Q1 of this fiscal year. The Alcohol business turnover, net of excise duty increased by 19.8% and 20.5% in Q2 and H1 FY 24. And this was due to higher sales volumes driven primarily by operational efficiencies achieved in the post stabili sation period of the new distilleries and an increase in activities in the Indian Made Indian Liquor (IMIL) business. The combined Engineering turnover increased by 8.7% in the quarter and this performance was boosted by a 28.4% increase in revenues in the Power Transmission business for the quarter under review. The Profit Before Tax and exceptional items increased by 60% in Q2 FY 24 to reach ■ 130 crore for the half year milestone. The gross debt on a stand -alone basis as of the 30th of September is approximately ■ 295.66 crore as compared to ■ 825 crore as on March 31, 2023. Considering operational surplus funds that have been held in fixed deposits tota lling ■ 285.5 crore , the net debt on September 30 th, 2023, stood at ■ 10 crore only and this is a major milestone for the Company . […] And of course, one can independently have the tender floated as well. And we ’re hoping that all of this will be resolved very soon by the Central Government. I’d like to turn now to the Engineering businesses. For the Power Transmission business, the increase in H1 FY 24 turnover and profitability was 44.8% and 58.2%, respectively, driven by high domestic sales across all the OEMs. The Defence business received an order recently of ■18 crore for the supply of propulsion gearboxes for fast patrol vessels of the Indian Coast Guard. This marks an entry of this business into the Marine Gearbox segment. The first entry into the Marine Gearbox segment. These gearboxes need to be highly engineered , compact and lightweight to meet the specific requirements of vessels and the Company would be undertaking this project with its own design, in -house manufacturing and testing and with over 90% indigenous content, which is a major step in line with Make in India policy of the Government of India. With this, the defence business will also be well placed to support the nation ’s future shipbuilding projects of similar nature with completely indigenous solutions. With that, ladies and gentlemen, I'd like to open up the floor for questions.
Thank you. My questions are pertaining to the Power Transmission Business. If I just look at the business that is a part of.

Okay. I'm going to answer the question in terms of the way that we actually disclose data. It is slightly different with the way that you've asked the question. But I do appreciate how you've asked it. It is the way that one should actually look at sales, frankly speaking. We don't typically give out data to segment between original equipment sales as well as replacement sales of original equipment. Okay? Because, I'l l tell you why. The customer of ours is typically the same. For a new projec t, if we are selling to either a Siemens or a Mitsubishi or a Triveni Turbine s, or to Atlas Copco or a BHEL, and the list can go on. Typically, it is our OEMs that are securing the overall order with the end customer for a new gearbox. For aftermarket, the end third -party users, like a said cement company, contacts us and asks us for replacement. It could be of something that we had installed 20-30 years ago, even earlier. It could also be of a replacement of somebody else's make. The vast majority are other people's makes. If I look at FY26 , actually the percentages, typically about in previous years, historically, it has just been above 30 -odd% that has been the aftermarket share. However in FY26 , the aftermarket share was about 40% of overall gears. So that is part of the reason why even with slightly lower revenues, our profitability margins, et c are very good and remain unabated despite a slightly lower revenue and higher overheads, obviously as time has elapsed. That's one. Looking at this particular market globally, it remains exactly the same. You mentioned resellers and retailers. So u nlike low -speed gearboxes, which are catalog unit products are sold on an axis, frankly speaking, and can be stocked etc. Ours are heavily engineered gearboxes, which are customi sed to a particular requirement and a set of conditions, and therefore it has to be engineered and then supplied uniquely. So w e can't operate within the same type of retail type system that other companies within the industrial landscape comply. How ever how we operate this, and it's a very good question, I'm happy to answer it, is through a different type of structure. The first thing, of course is that our OEMs are the same, broadly speaking. So if we are selling to the said OEMs, be it Triveni Turbine s, Siemens, Atlas Copco, Mitsubishi, Sulzer, I'm giving you a smattering of names. The list is very , very extensive. It is the same OEMs that will buy in Germany, in France, in the U.K., in the United States, in Korea, in Japan. Wherever their offices are, wherever their plants are, they will be buying. So it is about marketing to the supply chain teams in said geographies. That is something that we do aggressively, and we do that internally. We don't outsource that. That is a critical part of our value proposition and something that actually creates a lot of s tickiness. Why does it create stickiness? Because we are able to give responses to enquiries in the shortest possible time. And a huge part of our IT development continuously is about reducing the time it takes to give very complex quotations so that an OEM of ours has that comfort that they can get it so much faster than anybody else that this is the firm to partner with going forw ard. That has been part of our USP. Now g etting on to third -party AVLs is very important, especially when we look at the oil and gas segment. People who buy on A merican Petroleum Institute compliance norms. That, of course, is an ongoing process. We have had a huge amount of success. In the last 3 years, it has been massive, much more than I personally anticipated. However w e are not fully there. There are still some critical companies around the world. We don't disclose names, but I would just assure you that we are working on, and we expect even more success this year. Hopefully the next couple of years, we should be covered with pretty much everybody of note around the world or anybody of importance around the world. Having said that, our aftermarket business globally is one where we can work with partners. And w e have accelerated agencies, so having agents in local countries that can go out and do. These are small mechanical companies that have engineers, et c that can go out, do dimensions, have relationships with third-party users, and secure aftermarket business for us because a ftermarket business needs proximity. It needs somebody to be at the site, take dimensions and convince end users that Triveni is the solution provider for any problem, especially when it's a gearbox of somebody else's make. That is a program me that is ongoing. That is a program me that needs a lot of strategic attention by the business and by the marketing teams. Yes, we've had successes, but there is a long way to go as far as that is concerned. Domestically, our aftermarket business is handled by a very professional and strong te am in Mysore, which has decades of relationships with OEMs. So w e don't need anybody else to be able to do that. In fact, we're the first port of call for not just our gearboxes, but everybody's gearb oxes pretty much across the country. I hope that answers your question. Lakshminarayanan K .G.: Yeah, that's helpful. Just one more question. If I just do a cursory glance across some of the results by steel companies, cement companies, and paper companies, et c, I get a mixed view that some of the cement companies are reducing their CapEx, even the large ones, and some of the steel companies want to sharpen their CapEx, and they want to actually debottleneck and things like that. How much of that is actually, whic h from your vantage point you are seeing, that potentially would g ive some kind of a pathway into one or two years ahead?

Yeah, thanks. I just had one question on the aftermarket business. I just broadly wanted to understand why are the OEMs, why are the other manufacturers we are competing with letting this business go and letting us kind of replace or refurbish their gears? Is it just a question of cost or are there some other factors at play?

I'll answer your question in detail. It really depends on what the aftermarket solution is , okay . So w hat exactly is aftermarket solution? It could be, and it's not limited to, is a gearbox that fails , okay . What you do is you get the exact same gearbox with the same dimensions and replace it. A second solution could be that your bull gear or some of your gear teeth get chipped off, and during the annual maintenance, you do some replacement of parts, or perh aps the entire gear train, or you d o a bearing replacements, et c., or wear and tear. That's the second. The third could be a speed upgrade and a speed downgrade. The fourth could be a complete refurbishment because the footprint of where the gearbox actually sits does not change. It adds value, and you can go out and put in a much bigger gearbox in the same footprint designed by a company like Triveni, for example. It's part of our compelling value proposition. And t hen there are other variants of aftermarket sales and service. What distinguishes us in each one of these various segments is different . In the classical aftermarket that you probably were thinking about, there, what our value proposition is that we can deliver much faster than anybody, anywhere in the world. Even if we have to ship this 3,000 miles, 4,000 miles, we can do it delivered fas ter than anybody, which means our time to manufacture sometimes, because of our supply chain initiatives, because o f our stocking policies, et c., can be 2-3 months. We have the capacity. We are able to do it. For global firms, I am led to understand by my teams that this could be as high as 12 months. So there's a substantial difference in terms of the time period. To get mission -critical, as you can appreciate, a gearbox is tied to a turbine or a compressor or a pump or an alternator. It is a much smaller value than what it is coupled to at either end, but it is just as mission -critical. So if a gearbox goes down, a plant goes down. It's just as bad as if a compressor goes down or a turbine goes down or an alternator goes down, the plant goes down. So it is the same type of criticality, frankly speaking. And t herefore, for a customer that has broken gear teeth, for example, for them to find a time, an appropriate solution is very very important. We have some other tricks of the trade in terms of how we do dimension ready sites, and we do a lot of pre -activity work, and we work with our third -party users in helping them with predictions, et c. All of these things are more on the relationship side, and they work very beautifully, which is why domestically we have such a fantastic market share because of the service that we can provide. That is not product. Now I'm coming to the service side of i t. Internationally, it's going to be a challenge. Obviously, because we're based in India. We don't have somebody sitting in Arg entina. We don't have somebody sitting in South Korea. I'm just taking two countries' names as examples. And h ow we're going to develop solutions around that will be with local partners, and then as the business progresses with other Triveni staff that sit in international locations, et c. But t hat is something that we will have to bridge. Not just on the product side, but also being able to add the service, which then leads into guaranteeing product orders. But it's a complex arrangement. I think the fact t hat we can do it at a lower price point also plays a very significant part of the value proposition. Sometimes we are a fraction of what is usually offered by the original equipment gearbox manufacturer to a client. A fraction and y et, it's a highly profitable business for us.

Ladies and gentlemen, thank you very much for joining us for this earnings conference call. I think we've had a productive discussion. We're at a very important inflection point for Triveni. The growth trajectory for TPTL looks extremely robust. We're very excited about the new journey, as that company and that business also completes its 50th year, a year worth being celebrated. As far as Triveni Engineering is concerned, there's a lot of excitement in both the commodities parts of the business. I think it's unfortunate that El Ni no has such a devastating impact, but for the sugar industry, it can only be considered positive in some respects. As far as the distillery business is concerned, we've seen with what's happened with oil prices, with the rupee, and with the government's ren ewed push and look at higher blends and more ethanol. I'm personally very excited about the next path of that business as well. Our water business, too, continues very , very well in terms of its progress as well. I look forward to discussing both Triveni Engineering and Triveni Power Transmission with you separately in August. Thank you very much. rationale.rationale: On the documents supplied, the business being separated is ITC's IT services arm, ITC Infotech India Limited (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary that is to be carved out of the unlisted group structure and listed on BSE and NSE through a strategic combination with listed Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (31 Aug 2026 filing). The mechanics are two-step: ITCI buys 3,36,61,700 shares (22.106% fully diluted) from promoters Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP for ~Rs 1,330 crores cash in two tranches (11.00% at Rs 390/share, 11.106% at Rs 400/share), funded by a Rights Issue of Rs 1,330 crores, after which Happiest Minds amalgamates into ITCI at 25 ITCI shares per 81 Happiest Minds shares (1:3.24) — implying Rs 405/share or Rs 6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and Rs 1,312/share or Rs 11,920 crores for ITCI pre-rights — leaving ITC with ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders ~26.6%, and ITCI listed. The stated problem it solves is sub-scale: management says '> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management office radar' and gives the 'Right to Hunt' and 'Right to Win' large deals, so the combination targets US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis versus ITCI's FY26 IT services revenue of Rs 4,718 crores (PAT Rs 510 crores adjusted, 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 13,000+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 14%) and Happiest Minds' FY26 Rs 2,315.11 crores (FY25 Rs 2,060.84 crores, FY24 Rs 1,624.66 crores, 6,500+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 25%). It also fixes portfolio gaps: Americas mix rises from 27% to 38%, BFSI from 12% to 20%, Build:Run moves to 50:50, and Hi-Tech, EdTech and Healthcare verticals plus 800+ clients and 19,000+ professionals are added, against an industry backdrop of a ~$400 Bn AI-driven TAM by 2030, compression of ~$350 Bn of legacy services, cost-takeout deals at 30-40% savings and vendor consolidation. For ITC shareholders the explicitly stated benefit of separation itself is that it 'Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility', alongside ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion and EPS accretion in the first full year. Nobody is recorded as having demanded it: ITCI's board moved under its own 'Orbit Next' strategy, ITC's board merely 'endorsed' it, and the only external party is the counterparty-seller Ashok Soota, who frames it as Happiest Minds finding 'a welcoming new home'; approvals needed are CCI/anti-trust, stock exchanges/SEBI, shareholders, creditors and NCLT, over ~15 months.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so the idea is traceable only through filings: ITC had already demerged its Hotels business (visible as discontinued operations with Rs 15,163.06 crores of exceptional items in FY2024-25 and ITC Hotels Limited now an associate), establishing the separation template. The IT separation surfaces fully formed on 31 August 2026, when ITCI's board approved both the 22.106% promoter-stake purchase and the Happiest Minds amalgamation that will list ITCI, endorsed the same day by ITC's board. Housekeeping then followed in the opposite, consolidating direction: on 1 September 2026 step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan Technologies and Cloudlytics were dissolved into ITC Infotech (appointed date 1 October 2024), tidying the entity to be listed, while on 2 November 2026 ITC moved the other way at the parent by absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar) to 'reduce the number of operating entities'. The plan's indicative sequencing was set at board approval in Aug'26, Tranche 1 and exchange/SEBI no-objection around Q3FY27-early Q4FY27, shareholder/creditor meetings Mar-Apr'27 and ITCI listing in Q2-Q3 FY28.

points.point: The separation vehicle is disclosed in the 31 August 2026 filing: ITC Infotech acquires 22.106% of Happiest Minds for cash and then amalgamates it, with ITCI's own shares to be listed on both Indian exchanges.
points.quote: The shares of ITC Infotech are proposed to be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited.

points.point: Transaction summary states the listing is the consequence of the merger, not an IPO or a demerger to ITC shareholders; ITC retains ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders get ~26.6%.
points.quote: Thereafter, Happiest Minds to merge with ITC Infotech pursuant to which ITC Infotech will be listed

points.point: The value-creation case for ITC shareholders names independent price discovery as a benefit of having the IT business separately listed.
points.quote: Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility

points.point: Regulation 30 disclosure frames the deal as the execution of ITCI's existing standalone expansion strategy, aimed at a step change in revenue scale and competitiveness.
points.quote: ITC Infotech's 'Orbit Next' strategy envisages rapid global expansion through capability led strategic partnerships.

points.point: The industry slide gives the explicit scale threshold problem the separation-and-combination is meant to clear — being below US$1bn keeps ITCI off large buyers' vendor lists.
points.quote: > $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management  office radar

points.point: Media statement sets the quantified target for the combined, listed entity: US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis, AI-first, with 19,000+ professionals.
points.quote: ITC Infotech (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited and a leading global technology services player, today announced the proposed strategic combination with Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (Happiest Minds) to create a scaled, future-ready, AI-first global technology services enterprise.

points.point: Synergy slide quantifies what the combination is expected to deliver financially: roughly 10% revenue synergies, about 100 bps of margin expansion, and EPS accretion in year one.
points.quote: Expected to be EPS accretive in first full year of combined entity operations

points.point: ITC's Chairman Sanjiv Puri justifies it on complementarity of capability and culture rather than on any investor, lender or partner demand.
points.quote: The coming together of our complementary strengths, deep domain expertise and future-ready capabilities will further enhance our ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions across geographies.

points.point: The only external party pressing for a change of ownership is the Happiest Minds promoter selling the 22.106% stake, who wanted a larger home for his company.
points.quote: We believe that ITC Infotech is the best partner for Happiest Minds to fulfil its destiny and we are pleased that our team will have a welcoming new home .

points.point: ITCI's CEO Manas Chakraborty positions the rationale as capability completeness — full-stack AI-led transformation — rather than financial engineering.
points.quote: Integrating Happiest Minds' Digital Engineering, Data, AI, and Cybersecurity capabilities with our deep domain expertise, cloud and engineering capabilities will enable us to serve as a full stack AI-led transformation partner.

points.point: At the parent level ITC is simultaneously simplifying in the opposite direction, absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar; FY26 turnover Rs 451.71 crores, total assets Rs 150.07 crores) on 2 November 2026.
points.quote: Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to simplify the corporate holding structure.

points.point: The 1 September 2026 filing shows pre-listing entity cleanup: step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan and Cloudlytics were merged into ITC Infotech with appointed date 1 October 2024.
points.quote: Accordingly, with effect from 1st September , 2026, BTPL and CTPL stand  dissolved without winding up and have cease d to be subsidiaries of the Company.

points.point: Completion is conditional and long-dated — about 15 months — with CCI, exchange/SEBI, shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals, and the two firms operating independently until then.
points.quote: The compani es expect the transaction to be completed within the next                     15 months and will continue to operate independently until all approvals have been obtained.

rationale.what_management_expects: ITC Infotech: step change to ~US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from Rs 4,718 crores FY26), Americas mix 27%→38%, BFSI 12%→20%, Build:Run 50:50, ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion, EPS accretive in year one, 19,000+ people, 800+ clients. ITC: a separately listed IT platform giving independent value discovery and strategic flexibility, while retaining ~73.4%.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts supplied; filings never explain ITC's intent for its 73.4% stake, any ITC-shareholder entitlement, carve-out/dis-synergy costs, valuation basis, or the earlier hotels demerger's rationale.

deal.size_statement: "For example, if 1,000 Ordinary Shares of ITC were purchased at ` 400/- per share by a shareholder, the total cost of acquisition would amount to ` 4,00,000/- before the demerger. Based on the Share Entitlement Ratio, 100 shares of ITCHL would be allotted to the said shareholder. The total cost of acquisition of ` 4,00,000/- would be apportioned in the aforesaid ratio - ` 3,45,960/- (86.49% of ` 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 1,000 ITC shares and ` 54,040/- (13.51% of ` 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 100 shares of ITCHL." (apportionment table: ITC Limited 86.49%, ITC Hotels Limited 13.51% of total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares of ITC Limited)
deal.promoter_holding_parent: not stated as a percentage; the Voting Results for the Court-convened Meeting of Ordinary Shareholders held 6th June, 2024 show "Promoter and Promoter Group" with No. of shares held 0, No. of votes polled 0, % of Votes Polled on outstanding shares 0.0000, and "Whether promoter / promoter group are interested in the agenda / resolution? Not Applicable"
deal.promoter_holding_after: For the 2025 Hotels demerger (no promoter/promoter group; stated in terms of shareholders): "ITCHotels toissue equity shares directly totheshareholders ofITCinamanner that about 60%stake isheld directly byITCshareholders proportionate to their shareholding inITCand remaining about 40%stake tocontinue with ITC -Overall, existing ITCshareholders willhold 100%ofITCHotels, i.e.about 60%directly and balance ofabout 40%through their shareholding inITC". ITC retained about 40% and "ITCHL has ceased to be a subsidiary of the Company effective 11th January, 2025" (ITC Hotels Limited subsequently shown as an Associate of ITC). For the 2025 Scheme of Amalgamation of Sresta Natural Bioproducts Private Limited and Wimco Limited with ITC: not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: 2025 Hotels demerger: "ITCHL has allotted 125,11,71,040 Equity Shares of ` 1/- each to the shareholders of ITC whose names were recorded in the Register of Members of ITC or in the Register of Beneficial Owners maintained by the Depositories as on the Record Date (i.e., January 6, 2025) in the ratio of 1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of ` 1/- (Rupee One) each for every 10 (Ten) fully paid-up Ordinary Shares of ` 1/- (Rupee One) each held in ITC ('Share Entitlement Ratio')". Also: "as per Section 47(vid) of the Act, the aforesaid issue of Equity Shares by ITCHL pursuant to the Scheme will not be regarded as transfer". 2025 Scheme of Amalgamation of Sresta Natural Bioproducts Private Limited and Wimco Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) with ITC: not stated.
deal.management_incentives: Treatment of existing stock option grants under the demerger Scheme, any new plan in ITC Hotels Limited, exercise price and pricing date, and management/insider shareholding: not stated. ITC Board on 6th February, 2025: "Limit for Equity Settled Stock Appreciation Rights: Recommended for the approval of the Members, a limit of2% of the issued and subscribed Share Capital of the Company to be earmarked for issue of shares from time to time under a new Employee Stock Appreciation Rights Scheme." Segment note: "As stock options and stock appreciation linked reward units are granted to align the interests of employees with those of shareholders and also to attract and retain talent for the enterprise as a whole, the charge thereof do not form part of the segment performance reviewed by the Corporate Management Committee." Shares issued under ITC's Employee Stock Option Schemes: 41,11,690 Ordinary Shares (quarter ended 31st December, 2024), 24,09,390 (quarter ended 31st March, 2025), 34,22,360 (quarter ended 30th June, 2025), 18,29,340 (quarter ended 31st December, 2025). On employees: "Employees engaged in/ related to Hotels Business being transferred to ITC Hotels - Employment terms to be no less favourable than their existing terms of employment with ITC - Transferred employees to become employees of ITC Hotels with continuity of service".
deal.insider_actions: No promoter or management buying, selling, pledging or stated intent is stated. The documents record only intra-group transactions around the separation: ITC on 24th October, 2024 approved and on 18th December, 2024 completed acquisition of 1,52,32,129 Equity Shares of ` 2/- each of EIH Limited and 34,60,829 Equity Shares of ` 2/- each of HLV Limited from Russell Credit Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, at book value (fair value gain of ` 527.96 Crores as an Exceptional Item; post acquisition holdings 16.13% in EIH and 8.11% in HLV), and on 29th November, 2024 acquired the entire share capital (4,20,60,166 Equity Shares of ` 10/- each) of Greenacre Holdings Limited from Russell Credit Limited; "Financial Investments (EIH Ltd.&HLV Ltd.)and non-operational investments (Logix Developers Pvt.Ltd.)not being transferred, asenvisaged intheScheme".

listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited trades since 2025-06-02 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps 44%

rationale.rationale: Across these texts Aegis is not demerging a division to its own shareholders — one filing states plainly "Yes, transaction is outside the Scheme of Arrangement" — it is carving its port terminalling business out of Aegis Logistics Ltd (ALL) into the Royal Vopak joint venture Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd (AVTL), IPO-ing it, and then migrating terminal assets into AVTL and its subsidiaries by slump sale; ALL retains Mumbai Liquid, Mumbai LPG, LPG/ammonia Distribution, Infrastructure Development (EPC), Sourcing and treasury. Management's stated reason is capital: the group is funding roughly USD 1.2 billion of gross capex (about INR 10,000 crores) by FY27 and a USD 5 billion pipeline to 2030 (including a non-binding INR 20,000 crore Vadhavan MoU, INR 1,675 crores at JNPA/J2, INR 525 crores per ammonia terminal), and Murad Moledina said the AVTL IPO's "primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy" — GATI being Gateway Access to India. The dilution problem is answered two ways: in Nov 2024 he argued equity infused into the JV "will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies," so rising minority interest is offset by interest savings; post-listing he called it EPS accretive because reinvested proceeds more than compensate for profit shared with minorities. The split is engineered so cash returns to the parent: ALL (or a 100% subsidiary) builds the assets and bills AVTL at arm's length with a ~20–25% margin — 30% on signing the framework agreement (INR 500 crores of the INR 1,675 crore J2 project) and 70% on completion — so "we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash," eliminated on consolidation but real at the standalone level, while ALL also keeps 44.71% of AVTL and management control, so AVTL is still consolidated line by line. Partner structure, not lender pressure, shapes it: Vopak dilutes equally alongside ALL; SEBI rules legally oblige a Phase-II equity infusion within three years; Itochu has taken 10% of Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Ltd with intent to reach 25%; L&T (Kandla green ammonia) and Hindustan Zinc (15-year ammonia take-or-pay) sit on the project side. Consolidation of stragglers followed — Haldia's Hindustan Aegis LPG (25,000 MT, HPCL contract to 2038) moved 75% into AVTL, with 51% sold by Aegis Gas for INR 701.6 crores, and the Pipavav ammonia terminal transferred to ATPL for INR 525 crores — and performance has been strong throughout: FY26 revenue INR 8,333 crores (+23%), normalised EBITDA INR 1,599 crores (+36%), PAT INR 1,107 crores (+41%), EPS 25.59, cash and investments ~INR 5,939 crores versus INR 150 crores in FY22, consolidated debt-to-equity 0.04 and no net debt.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced only as press speculation: on the Aug 2024 call (Jul 31, 2024) Murad Moledina refused to engage on an AVTL fundraise news item — "nothing finalized as of now" — and Anil Sarin used that call to lobby against it on behalf of minority holders, asking that capital instead be raised in the Holdco; the Nov 2024 call (Nov 19, 2024) opened by disclosing the DRHP had been filed the previous day, with Moledina declining detail ("We are not at liberty to talk as of now") beyond saying proceeds would repay debt and that dilution would be shared equally by both partners and done in two phases. By the Aug 2025 call (Aug 8, 2025) AVTL was listed (June 2025, INR 2,800 crores raised, ALL at 44.71%) and the rationale was given formally — debt reduction, GATI, EPS accretion, Phase-II infusion legally due within three years — plus the first slump sales (Sea Lord's Mangalore terminal, business transfer agreements of Jun 19, 2025) and the rule that "most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak." Thereafter it became mechanical: Nov 2025 (Nov 7) and the Oct 28–29, 2025 filings moved Hindustan Aegis LPG and Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) into AVTL (INR 701.6 crores for 51%; ALL retaining 34% indirectly, offset by ~INR 700 crores cash), Feb 2026 (Jan 30, 2026) defined the parent's remaining six businesses, the Mar 26 / Aug 24, 2026 filings assigned and executed the INR 525 crore ammonia BTA to ATPL, and the Jun 2026 call (Jun 9, 2026) plus the Sep 28, 2026 board approval of INR 6,000 crores of borrowing limits and INR 6,000 crores of fundraising confirmed the steady state: ALL builds and funds, AVTL owns.

points.point: Investor Anil Sarin explicitly lobbied against separately listing AVTL, saying minority holders would be confused about which entity to own and that capital should instead be raised in the listed Holdco; management called the discussion premature.
points.quote: it would be so much better if you retain that in the consolidated hold and raise money in the Holdco.

points.point: Asked directly about press reports of an AVTL IPO, the CFO would not confirm it, framing it only as one of several ways to fund the capex programme.
points.quote: As far as the second news item is concerned, I can tell you, we always explore many possibilities of funding our capex program and nothing finalized as of now.

points.point: On the day after the DRHP was filed, the CFO gave the core defence of the structure: equity raised in the subsidiary repays infrastructure debt, so interest savings offset the increase in minority interest and the holdco is left unaffected.
points.quote: We have already said earlier that the equity infusion into the JV will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies.

points.point: The Chairman stated the stated use of IPO proceeds — debt reduction plus general corporate purposes — while an investor asked whether the listed parent would simply become a holdco since the bulk of the business was moving into the JV.
points.quote: The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.

points.point: Post-listing (AVTL listed June 2025, ALL holding 44.71% with management control, so still consolidated line by line), the CFO gave the formal rationale and said reinvested proceeds would more than compensate for profit now shared with minorities.
points.quote: The primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy.

points.point: The Chairman tied the separation to a regulatory obligation: a second equity infusion into AVTL is mandated within three years under SEBI rules, which he said largely funds the USD 1.2 billion-to-USD 5 billion capex plan at 0.6x gearing capped at 3.5x EBITDA.
points.quote: With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.

points.point: The allocation rule between parent and AVTL was stated: standard port terminals go into AVTL under the GATI strategy, while other assets (e.g. the INR 250 crore Mumbai liquid expansion) stay in the parent, decided case by case on where value is maximised and whether partners are involved.
points.quote: But yes, most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak, for sure.

points.point: Explaining the Haldia/Hindustan Aegis consolidation into AVTL, the CFO quantified the trade: holding drops from 51% to an indirect 34%, but roughly INR 700 crores of cash more than offsets the 17 points, and it lifts the subsidiary's EPS.
points.quote: The 17% that drops is compensated by the surplus INR 700 crores, whatever is going to come in our hands.

points.point: The cash mechanics of the two-entity structure were spelled out for a shareholder worried that the USD 5 billion capex benefits only AVTL: the parent builds at ~25% margin, is reimbursed in full plus margin, and also earns via its AVTL stake.
points.quote: So, for AVTL, if we develop, then obviously, AVTL pays for the entire amount, including our margin. So, we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash.

points.point: Asked what is left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL, the CFO enumerated the retained perimeter — and added that ammonia distribution is being added to it alongside LPG.
points.quote: So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.

points.point: The steady-state operating model was confirmed: capex is incurred and the asset built at Aegis Logistics standalone (or a 100% subsidiary), billed as EPC, then transferred to Aegis Vopak, with consolidation capitalised at ALL's billed cost.
points.quote: So, we will be doing capex at the Aegis level, the Aegis Logistics. And then after creating the asset, will we then transfer it to Aegis Vopak, am I right?

points.point: The Aug 24, 2026 Business Transfer Agreement transferred the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited by slump sale for INR 525 crores, and states the transaction sits outside any Scheme of Arrangement and is a related-party transaction at arm's length.
points.quote: The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.

points.point: The Oct 29, 2025 board approval priced the Haldia step: 6,21,146 shares (51%) of Hindustan Aegis LPG sold by wholly-owned Aegis Gas (LPG) Pvt Ltd to AVTL, an entity contributing 2.49% of turnover and 10.07% of net worth in FY25.
points.quote: The consideration to be received by AGPL against the sale of 6,21,146 Equity shares held by AGPL in HALPG from AVTL is  INR.7,01,60,71,920/-

points.point: A year after the AVTL IPO the parent itself moved to raise capital: the Sep 28, 2026 board approved raising borrowing limits to INR 6,000 crores and a fundraise of up to INR 6,000 crores via equity, FCCB/ADR/GDR, debentures or QIP, subject to shareholder special resolution.
points.quote: raising of funds for an amount aggregating up to Rs. 6,000 Crores, for cash, in one or more tranches

rationale.what_management_expects: AVTL: debt repaid, balance sheet strengthened, ~25% EBITDA on matured assets, terminals consolidated for operational synergy, partner capital from Vopak and Itochu. Aegis Logistics: upfront 20–25% EPC margin returned in cash, 44.71% of AVTL plus management control and line-by-line consolidation, high-return distribution/sourcing/treasury retained, EPS accretion, 0.6x gearing, and funding for USD 5 billion of capex to 2030.
rationale.gaps: No stated valuation of retained versus transferred businesses, no answer to the which-entity-to-own dilution objection, no Phase-II infusion size, terms or timing, no lender rationale.

other_differences.quote: The company remains in a strong financial position with a low debt to equity ratio of 0.04 and no net debt on 31 March 2026 on a consolidated basis.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Cash and investments of approximately INR6,000 crores (INR5,939 crores) at FY26, up from INR150 crores in FY22; held in Aegis Logistics standalone plus its 100% subsidiaries.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Aegis Logistics standalone (or a 100% subsidiary) does the EPC / infrastructure development and bills AVTL at arm's length with roughly a 25% margin, receiving 30% on signing the framework agreement and 70% on completion; the capitalised value in consolidation is at which ALL bills.
other_differences.separated_business: The terminals built are housed in AVTL, which pays the full amount including the parent's margin; AVTL and ALL together target aggregate gross capex of USD1.2 billion by FY27 and a USD5 billion pipeline by 2030.
other_differences.quote: So, we do the infrastructure development at arm's length basis. Generally, the margins are 25%. And in consolidation gets eliminated.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: Business left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL: Mumbai liquid, Mumbai LPG, distribution, infrastructure development, sourcing and treasury, plus the new ammonia distribution.
other_differences.separated_business: AVTL houses the terminalling assets; "if it is a terminal, yes, every chance that it will be housed in AVTL."
other_differences.quote: So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.

other_differences.parent_or_remaining: FY26 group: LPG segment revenue INR7,689 crores with EBITDA INR1,131 crores (up 68%); distribution margin around INR7,000 per ton versus INR4,000-odd in the previous year.
other_differences.separated_business: Liquid (terminalling) segment delivered FY26 revenue of INR644 crores with EBITDA of INR472 crores, down 5%; Q3 FY26 liquid segment EBITDA margin expanded by 674 bps to 77%.
other_differences.quote: Liquid business delivered revenue of INR644 crores broadly stable year-on-year with EBITDA of INR472 crores, down 5%, reflecting phasing of capacity additions.
