turns: Perfect. I mean the stabilized levels, where do you see the margins at for the liquids like up to where we can reach? We are at around 52% this quarter.

You also wonder. So we reach as much as possible. But it's like the more value -added products you do by doing small tweaking in your infrastructure and that's an exercise ongoing at all the sites, all the time. So we'll keep looking at new products, big cl ients, complex products and try and get those we have the technical expertise of Vopak. And of course, we ourselves are having those expertise with us. So we are confident. I think the product mix and the improvement on EBITDA on that accou nt should also keep happening going forward.

So maybe if you could shed some life on the industry dynamics sort of consolidation that you see in the space for the next 5 years, and your perspective on getting higher market share and initiatives that we would like to have to do that?

Yes. Good question, and I'm glad you asked that. Look, market dynamics and industry dynamics and consolidation I think I've mentioned this in the past. I think with the combination of Aegis Aegis Logistics Limited February 02, 2024 and Vopak coming together, we have noticed that in every port that we are operating, we are now -- with our joint venture, Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd., is essentially becoming the market leader -- unquestioned market le ader with maximum market share. And we have become the price leaders and the volume leaders in every single port. In Kandla, we are the unquestioned leader. In Pipavav, we are done unquestioned leader. In Mumbai, obviously, we are the unquestioned leader. We've just entered into JNPT. I could say that we are not the market leader, we have yet to commission the terminal, but please watch this space. In Mangalore, we are the market leader. In Kochi, we are the market leader, and in Haldia, we are the market leader. So I would say that there has been consolidation going on, consolidation where there's actual acquisitions happening. Kandla, of course, y ou' ve seen we've done 2 or 3 key acquisitions. Kochi, we've just done a small acquisition. Proposals come to us all the time, but we won't pay top rupee. We will pay because we can build it cheaper than what the market expectations are. So I'm extremely bullish on the prospects for liquids. There will be announcements as I've already mentioned to you that in Haldia, we are -- and overall, we are expanding next year, probably another 300,000 kiloliters all over different ports and so on, and it may be more than that. And that is because we are clearly becoming the market leader in all these ports. Secondly, I think the technical aspects of this industry. There are products that we are handling, which are very complex and difficult for -- unless you are technically sophisticated, which we combined forces of Aegis and Vopak, they're not easy to handl e and -- safely and even from a quality perspective. So customers, international customers, domestic customers are coming to us rather than choosing to go with competitors. So I think definitely in that area, we are very, very bullish and I'm happy with th e way things are going. And on the LPG side, at least in the -- we know that we have competition. We know, of course, you mentioned the A word many times, people have mentioned another group, which is very powerful and so on. But at least from our perspective, with the five terminals that we are, fourterminals operating and another two coming up, and more opportunities that we are exploring, we are pretty confident that we are certainly a leading player in this business.

Sounds great. Sounds good. And sir, when we look at an acquisition that's happening in India, what sort of turnaround time for that business to be integrated to our own set of values and processes? And also given that we have an international partner invol ved where the processes are much more aligned at a higher level. So how do you look at that?
Murad, I'm going to ask you because he's involved in...

Asset , integrity has to be examined before we acquire. So it's not that any trash can will be acquired and it would take a lot of time for it to turnaround. So we have our due diligence process. And in fact, being in the business, we know what kind of assets are on ground. And when we do take up or acquire those assets, I think bec ause of our expertise and because more Aegis Logistics Limited February 02, 2024 so of our EPC expertise that we construct our own terminals, we are able to turn those around very, very quickly. So it could take 3 months, 6 months, a year, maybe. So -- but what best is in these cases is nothing comes to a standstill. So what you do is you start off with low -value, low -risk products to handle. And then as you upgrade your terminal, you move on to more value -added products. So it's not that it takes time and everything is zero till the time you upgrade. So our expertise on EPC, our expertise in operating and our marketing strength that we can get products which suits the infrastructure we acquire and thenWe upgrade and move to higher value products as the upgradation happens.

Yes. And in answer to your question, our agreement with Vopak is very clear that both partners must be satisfied that the operating asset adheres to their standards and our standards. And they operate globally. We operate, of course, all over India. And basically, we' ve aligned completely on our safety standards and operating standards, emission standards and everything. So whenever we are going in for acquisitions and so on, basically, these are the boxes that we have to check. They send their people over from Singapore and so on, and we send our teams. It's one team actually, which adheres to the common standard now. So I think we're pretty good. I mean the acquisitions we have done so far have learned -- have taught us a lot. And so it's a pretty seamless process now.

We also delivered record volumes in our LPG logistics business of 4.1 million metric tons and distribution volumes of 0.56 million tons. And our profits for FY '24 amounted to INR672 crores, marking a 32% year-over-year growth. The outstanding performance aligns with our guidance of achieving a 25% cumulative average growth in earnings per share over the next 3 years. And I'm pleased to note that we have maintained, in fact, an EPS of 25% since 2022 after our joint venture with Vopak. So I think you'll agree with me that these results are consistent with our quarterly updates during the past Aegis Logistics Limited May 24, 2024 year. The main drivers for this have been the continued growth of the volumes in our Kandla terminal, growth in our distribution business, and continued growth in liquids through the addition of new capacity and full utilization of newly commissioned tanks. Furthermore, as the new projects that are now being implemented are commissioned, we are confident that the positive momentum we saw in FY '24 will be sustained in FY '25 and onwards. […] Moving on then to Mangalore. We successfully acquired a specialized storage terminal with a capacity of 44,168 KL in this last year. This acquisition meets the growing demand for specialized storage with the heating arrangements of up to 230 degrees centigrade in our Liquid division. This expands our facilities at Mangalore under the Aegis-Vopak Terminals Limited. The newly acquired capacity is already operational and with additional capacity under construction, expected to come online in phases by the end of FY '25. Following these expansions, our total liquid capacity at Mangalore will reach 154,000 KL and we are constructing an additional 71,000 KL in liquids that will be operational in the next 12 to 15 months. Our cryogenic LPG project, the 85,000 ton cryogenic LPG project is proceeding well on schedule and expected to be definitely commissioned on time.

So this will remain with the Listco. And secondly, sir, just a request. Given that we have sort of one subsidiary, which is the JV and then a bunch of others which are part of the Mumbai business or a step-down subsidiary which is a holdco for the JV or some other assets. If perhaps you could just in your presentation, just help us understand the breakup of the financials to the extent possible. Because like this quarter, for example, if we see your stand- alone net profit is actually higher than your consolidated net profit and this sort of just leads to a lot of confusion as to how the assets are doing. So while you may not -- obviously, I appreciate for competitive reasons, we want to disclose asset level information, but at least if you could club it as JV assets versus, let's say, all the assets which are under Aegis, the listed company, I think it would go a long way for us to understand the business better and how things are progressing on the various segments?

Thank you for raising this. Very good question. And I request you to refer to our annual report for all the breakups that are there between the standalones, the subsidiaries, etc. But regarding the stand-alone Aegis profit being more than the consolidated profit, let me just highlight here Aegis Logistics Limited July 31, 2024 one more event which happened in Q1 was that we realized INR180 crores by -- as envisage in our JV by selling our compulsorily convertible preference shares in our subsidiary AVTL to Royal Vopak as it was envisaged in the JV. Now this INR180 crores does not come into consolidated profits because of the Indian accounting standard, therefore, it goes and directly sits into results, even though we have realized it in cash. I wish it would have been reflected in P&L to give the correct picture of what we have earned in the quarter. But that's how Indian accounting standards require you to do so. And therefore, you will see it reflected in the stand-alone, but not so i n console.

Let me repeat that. Out of the total capital expenditure program of Rs. 4,500 crores by FY27, approximately already 50% is complete and or currently in progress and we anticipate that the Pipavav and Mangalore projects will be commissioned soon with the revenue expected to start in Q1 of FY26. The pace of capital spending is expected to persist beyond FY27 as we explore further opportunities which are in our pipeline. Before I hand over the call to our CFO to brief you on the “Financial Performance” of the company in more detail, let me update you on the developments at Aegis-Vopak Terminals Limited subsidiary. Yesterday, let me announce that this company has filed a DRHP for an IPO and the document has been uploaded on the SEBI website and it's also available on the website of Aegis-Vopak Terminals Limited. The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes. So, to summarize, the coming year should see higher revenues and profitability led by the additional capacities which are already under construction and set to come online in phases by the end of FY25-26. The continuing ramp up of the Kandla LPG terminal along with the improved utilization at our existing terminals and leveraging the terminals and supporting infrastructure to increase our distribution business.

And one bookkeeping question, how the profit from this JV currently flows into Aegis Logistics? That is question one. And second, a request, once we have spent, let's say one week, all of us can go through DRHP, we can have a call just to discuss that and then nuances of that like you discussed one when we had the Vopak JV that would be great?

So, the JV consolidation happens line by line on account of it being a subsidiary. Even after the IPO as and when it happens, we will have management control and it will still get consolidated line by line. So, there will be no change whatsoever. Secondly, DRHP, we are very near because this time we did earnings call a little late on account of Diwali and certain we were also a little occupied. So, we will have our next call very soon and I think that will be end of January. So, we'll discuss more at that time.
And post the IPO of Aegis Vopak, the standalone will be left with a lot of cash. So, what do you plan and have you already planned anything or can you give some idea over here?

Yes, we are always holding a lot of cash for a lot of opportunities that we believe are there. As and when these opportunities crystallize and we are ready to undertake, we will do the disclosures and talk about it. But there are always opportunities that we look at, but only when they mature and we are ready to undertake, we then disclose and discuss with our investors. As of now, whatever we have disclosed, the CAPEX coming up are the ones that we are doing.

Murad Moledina and Ms. Payal Dave from our Investor Relations Team. We will be presenting the performance for the 1st Quarter ended June ‘25. So, I am sure most of you would have attended the Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited; AVTL maiden earnings call earlier this afternoon. We are pleased to share that our subsidiary AVTL was successfully listed in June, 2025. Aegis Logistics continues to hold 44.71% equity in AVTL and it is important to note that given Aegis Logistics management control over the company, AVTL financials continue to be consolidated into Aegis Logistics financial statement. So, before we dive into the business overview, I am just pleased to announce that our ESG rating from MSCI has been upgraded from (A) to (AA) in this calendar year. […] We participated in various tenders to get additional land at Haldia to expand our capacity and the Haldia LPG terminal continues to do well and increase its utilization slowly and steadily. We are looking to extend our presence to a seventh port and once we are allotted some land, at the moment we are not able to disclose where we are bidding, but once we are allotted some Aegis Logistics Limited August 08, 2025 land, we will of course be able to set up some additional capacity in the liquid side there soon and we will be informing everybody. So, in summary, Aegis possesses really strong in which we have demonstrated in-house expertise in identifying opportunities and executing infrastructure projects that are cost effective, fast and flexible while at the same time maintaining the highest quality standards that ensure the long-term durability of these assets and we have also constructed them at the lowest cost for designated number of throughput terms. All these projects are housed and operated under Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited and we will already reach a Capex of US$ 1.2 billion by the end of next year and we expect to reach US$ 5 billion aggregate Capex by 2030 which would be funded by a mix of internal accruals and utilization of debt with a prudent debt gearing ratio of 0.6X capped to a 3.5X of EBITDA. With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded. Coming to the distribution side, this is of course a key focus for us as we utilize our existing terminal facilities and infrastructure to reach the end customers. In the case of LPG, we manage the entire value chain from sourcing, storage to distribution across India and since distribution is a B2C segment it offers significantly higher earnings per ton compared to our other segments while requiring relatively little investment.

Maybe just one last question. On JNPT, as I understand, actually one of our competitions has announced a LPG terminal and I think they have started construction in February this year. So, with that in mind, do we anticipate an overcapacity situation over there? Are there any assumptions on their capacity build? Because after all, I think if you combine the two capacities that we have announced and the peer has announced, there seems to be a lot of capacity in JNPT. I don't know. Any color from that.

Yes. So, JNPA, please keep in mind that there are two partners involved in the JNPA infrastructure, which we are setting up, Aegis and Vopak. Both are very experienced infrastructure players in storage business, one a leader in India and one world over. We have examined all the macro market conditions, competition, everything and after having confidence Aegis Logistics Limited August 08, 2025 on all the parameters, we have decided to go ahead. Another thing which you can notice that the so-called LPG infrastructure that you have referred to, there are news items saying that BW has, of course, withdrawn. So, we don't know the fate of that particular infrastructure. In spite of that, like I said, we do our own calculations, and we are confident of what we are doing at JNPA. We expect good and solid utilization going forward as far as JNPA is concerned. It is in Western India and near to the high consumption north of India.
Sure, sir. Secondly, apart from the expansions already announced in AVTL, do you plan to enter any new terminal or have any product or service in this company in the near future?

Yash, please understand. Aegis Logistics Limited is a consolidated financial statement that we are talking about. It's inclusive of AVTL. It does not exclude AVTL. So, all of the CAPEX of AVTL are included line by line into this company. So, it's inclusive of whatever Aegis Vopak will house. So, it's like we have Mumbai Terminal No. 2 housed in Sealord. We have our packed cylinder business housed in Aegis Gas. We have Liquid and LPG Terminal housed in Aegis Vopak. So, all of these get combined and consolidated. So, Aegis Logistics is a whole, is what includes everything. And like we have said, in addition to Rs. 2,500 crores projects that we are doing, which will be housed in Aegis Vopak, another Rs. 250 crores of Mumbai expansion in Liquid will be housed in our parent - individual standalone company. But we will be inclusive of all of it.
Sure, sir. So, that means if you enter any new product, let's say hydrogen, that will be housed in Aegis Vopak only or any other sort of product, sir?

Let me say it this way, that as and when the opportunity comes in any new energy, any new port, or any other infrastructure, the company will decide whether it falls within our benchmark returns that we expect. Aegis Logistics Limited August 08, 2025

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is GAIL's own directly-authorised city gas distribution (CGD) retail business — the six geographical areas Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum (Jamshedpur), Cuttack and Khordha (Bhubaneswar) — which the Board resolved to hive down into its 100% subsidiary GAIL Gas Limited as a slump sale on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027, with the subsidiary then to be listed via IPO diluting up to 25% of GAIL's equity. Management's stated reason was structural, not financial distress: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta said it was 'in order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach' — i.e. GAIL group CGD was split across GAIL's own balance sheet (six GAs, 0.36–0.55 MMSCMD, 195→215 CNG stations and 3.53→4.64 lakh DPNG connections over FY25–Q3FY26, volumes up ~25% in FY25 but 'currently in their early stages of development'), GAIL Gas (16 GAs plus 9 JVs, 7.0→7.8 MMSCMD, 12.46 lakh DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations, FY25 turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore up 42%, PAT Rs 451 crore up 40%) and 72 group GAs in all. A pipeline-and-marketing parent was also an awkward owner of a retail business: management said 'we are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies', and segment reporting of the CGD/marketing split was itself confusing analysts (the Rs 400 crore standalone-to-consolidated regrouping queried in Jul 2025). The upside case cited was CGD demand: a PNGRB projection of consumption rising '2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY 24' (~15% CAGR), PNGRB capping CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion lowering CGD input costs. For the IPO, the argument was scale and timing — 'GAIL Gas is one of the biggest company in the country in terms of city gas distribution... now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas' — with a consultant already selected and a roughly one-year timeline. The impetus came largely from sell-side investors (Citi's Saurabh Handa on restructuring CGD investments in Nov 2024; Alliance Services' Balaji Das on the IPO consultant in Oct 2025); the only external consent management named was CCEA, 'since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA' — no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. Running in the opposite direction, GAIL simultaneously pulled Konkan LNG Limited in: it bought out MSEB Holding's 7,40,55,220 shares via a NCLT-approved capital reduction (paid 06.07.2026, GAIL to 100%) and then merged KLL (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into GAIL to 'create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure'.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced only as an unprompted analyst question on the Nov 06, 2024 Q2 FY25 call, where R.K. Jain said no call had been taken on restructuring GAIL Gas — 'this is in our mind, but nothing concrete' — while adding that GAIL was 'looking for listing one or two JVs'; the Jan 30, 2025 call did not touch it. It became concrete at the May 14, 2025 annual analyst meet, where the CMD disclosed the Board's recommendation (passed 13.05.2025) to transfer the six GAs to GAIL Gas for a 'single entity... retail focused business approach', subject to CCEA. On Oct 31, 2025 the second leg appeared: GAIL confirmed it had started the GAIL Gas listing process, had selected a consultant, and expected 'a one year time line or so'; the Feb 02, 2026 Q3 FY26 call was silent on both. The filings then executed it: 31.07.2026 KLL merger into GAIL, and 30.10.2026 Board approval of the six-GA slump sale effective 01.01.2027 plus in-principle approval of a GAIL Gas IPO diluting up to 25%.

points.point: Citi's Saurabh Handa raised the split of CGD investments between GAIL standalone and GAIL Gas and asked whether GAIL would restructure them — the first time the idea appears in the record.
points.quote: On your City Gas investments, whether they are at the standalone entity or in GAIL Gas? Is there any thought process to look at restructuring these streamline these investments?

points.point: Director (Finance) R.K. Jain confirmed restructuring was under internal consideration but that no decision existed, while separately flagging that GAIL was working on listing one or two JVs with an update promised in Q3.
points.quote: As a company about GAIL Gas has not yet taken any call for restructuring of GAIL Gas. This is in our mind, but nothing concrete I can share with you right now.

points.point: Alongside CGD restructuring, Jain said listing of group entities was already in progress and at 'a good stage', promising an update in Q3 FY25.
points.quote: So also, we are looking for listing one or two JVs, which we are in the process and once we move forward and we take a call, we'll come back to you, but that we are certainly working and we are in a good stage.

points.point: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta disclosed the Board's 13.05.2025 recommendation to transfer GAIL's six directly-held CGD geographical areas to wholly-owned GAIL Gas Limited — the core rationale being one single, synergistic, retail-focused CGD entity.
points.quote: In order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach, the Board has recommended to transfer six geographical areas of GAIL to its wholly owned subsidiary, GAIL Gas Limited.

points.point: The only approval condition management named was CCEA, because the six GAs (Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack) had been awarded to GAIL by CCEA rather than won by GAIL Gas.
points.quote: This is subject to approval of CCEA since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA.

points.point: The six GAs were described as early-stage but fast-growing (volumes up ~25% in FY25, then ~0.4–0.45 MMSCMD) and under continuous cost review — the sub-scale retail assets being pushed into the dedicated CGD vehicle.
points.quote: In the Financial Year 24-25, these six GAs have shown impressive growth with volumes increasing by approximately 25%. We are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies.

points.point: The growth case for a standalone CGD entity rested on PNGRB's demand projection, supplemented by PNGRB's proposal to cap CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion to cut CGD input costs.
points.quote: the CGD sector is anticipated to be the key driver of growth, with consumption expected to increase 2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY '24

points.point: GAIL Gas's own FY25 numbers framed the receiving entity as a scaled, improving business: turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore (+42%), PAT Rs 451 crore (+40%), 16 GAs owned plus 9 JVs.
points.quote: During the current financial year, that is FY '25, GAIL Gas Limited's turnover stood at Rs. 12,231 crores as against Rs. 10,944 crores in FY '24. PBT increased by 42% and stood at Rs. 615 crores as against Rs. 434 crores in FY '24.

points.point: On the other entity later consolidated in, management said Konkan LNG (Dabhol) would swing to profit once the all-weather breakwater let it run 34–36 cargoes versus 21, worth roughly Rs 300 crore.
points.quote: So this year certainly we were not in positive because of the breakwater issue. But going forward, we will have positive bottom line from KLL.

points.point: An investor (Balaji Das) pressed on the GAIL Gas IPO and the consultant being hired for listing analysis, confirming the second leg of the plan was investor-driven.
points.quote: And the second question is on, we had like on the listing of the GAIL Gas IPO actually. So, any further progress on consultant and when are the future plans actually for GAIL Gas actually, because we heard that we are hiring consultants for analysis of listing.

points.point: Jain confirmed the listing process had begun — consultant selected, order imminent — and justified it on GAIL Gas's scale: 7.72 MMSCMD of volume and more GAs than any peer, with Bangalore alone at 1 MMSCMD.
points.quote: And we in GAIL believe that now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas, in that regard we have already started the process of hiring of consultant.

points.point: He put a roughly one-year timeline on the listing, contingent on the consultant's study — the only timing guidance given on the IPO.
points.quote: So, we are on a path to study about listing of GAIL Gas and after conclusion of that study, certainly that study is very important for us, we expect a one year time line or so should be good enough.

points.point: The last call in the record discussed the six GAs and GAIL Gas purely operationally (0.55 MMSCMD, 215 CNG stations, 4.64 lakh DPNG; GAIL Gas 7.8 MMSCMD, PBT Rs 143 crore) with no mention of the transfer or the IPO.
points.quote: GAIL has direct authorization of 6 GAs and has an infrastructure of 215 CNG stations and 4.64 lakh DPNG connections.

points.point: Filing 30.10.2026: Board approved the carve-out of the six named CGD GAs to GAIL Gas as a slump sale, via Business Transfer Agreement on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027.
points.quote: GAIL Board in its meeting held today i.e. 30.10.2026 accorded approval for Transfer of Six CGD Geographical Areas of GAIL India Ltd. viz. Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum, Cuttack and Khordha to GAIL Gas Ltd. (wholly owned Subsidiary of GAIL) through slump sale by Execution of Business Transfer Agreement on going concern basis, with effective date of transfer as 01.01.2027.

points.point: Same-day filing: in-principle Board approval to list GAIL Gas on Indian exchanges via IPO, diluting GAIL's stake by up to 25%, with valuation, price band and final dilution left to BRLM recommendations and a later Board approval.
points.quote: accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through Initial Public Offering (IPO) route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%.

points.point: Filing 31.07.2026: in the opposite direction, GAIL approved absorbing wholly-owned Konkan LNG (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into itself under Section 233, with KLL's shares cancelled and no change in GAIL's shareholding.
points.quote: To create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure which will enhance operational efficiencies.

points.point: Filing 10.07.2026: the KLL merger was preceded by an NCLT-approved capital reduction (order 03.06.2026) buying out partner MSEB Holding, taking GAIL from 50% to 100% of Konkan LNG before the absorption.
points.quote: an aggregate of 14,81,10,440 equity shares of ₹10 each, including 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by GAIL and 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by MSEB in KLL stand cancelled and extinguished i.e. MSEB holding in KLL reduced to Nil and GAIL shareholding increased to 100% of the equity share capital of KLL.

rationale.what_management_expects: One consolidated, retail-focused CGD entity with business synergy and efficiency; the six early-stage GAs (0.55 MMSCMD) folded into GAIL Gas's 7.8 MMSCMD platform (674 CNG stations, 12.46 lakh DPNG) to capture CGD demand rising 2.5–3.5x by 2030, aided by Zone-1 tariff capping and expected GST; price discovery and capital via an IPO of up to 25%. Parent keeps transmission/marketing; Konkan LNG's merger simplifies the group and adds its cargo-driven profit.
rationale.gaps: No valuation, slump-sale consideration, IPO size or use of proceeds, standalone margin/ROCE or capex targets, CCEA timing, or why 25%; calls after Oct 2025 went silent.

judge.what_is_spun: Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), IEX's 47.3%-held natural gas spot exchange associate, partly sold via IPO
judge.reason: PNGRB regulations require IEX to cut its 47.3% IGX holding to 25% within five years; the five-year period ended December 2025, a one-year extension was taken, so 22.3% is offered in the IPO.

listing.short: IPO DRHP filed — Indian Gas Exchange Limited
listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO DRHP FILED — Indian Gas Exchange Limited; At the IEX Analyst Meet held July 24, 2026 the CFO said "the good part is that they filed the DRHP in this month and hopefully (would be) getting listed soon";

rationale.rationale: The separation here is not a demerger of IEX's own operations but the carve-out of its gas arm, Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), via an offer-for-sale IPO, driven purely by PNGRB's exchange ownership rules, which cap any single shareholder at 25% and any trading member at 5%. IEX held 47.3%-47.5% of IGX and had to cut that to 25% within five years; that five-year window expired in December 2025, so IEX took a one-year extension from PNGRB, now running to 31 December 2026. Management said the original slippage was commercial, not strategic: 'there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange' and the 'business ramp-up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it' (Nov 2025). With IGX now scaled - FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28% YoY, over 40% CAGR), PAT Rs 41.9-42 crore (+35%), roughly 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 23 delivery points versus 4 in FY22 and 10 contract types versus 6 - IEX chose the IPO over other divestment options and formally asked IGX to proceed. The DRHP was filed on 14 July 2026 with SEBI and BSE as a pure offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 shares by IEX, i.e. the 22.3% it must shed; no fresh issue, proceeds or valuation was discussed. The same ownership-cap logic makes IEX house each new commodity in its own company: Indian Coal Exchange Ltd was incorporated in June 2026 with board approval, a mineral exchange company is planned, and its shareholding rules are 'similar to what has been notified for the power exchange and the gas exchange.' The only parties asking for the separation were regulators (PNGRB; the Ministry of Coal rules for the coal exchange) - not investors, lenders or partners; investors asked only about timing and for a proportionate reservation in the IGX IPO, which Goel refused because it is 'an independent IPO'. Separately, management rejected the analyst suggestion that the exchange's clearing and settlement function must be hived into its own entity, saying the PSS Act requires registration, not separation, with no financial impact.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2025 call (31 Oct 2025), where Goel disclosed the 25% PNGRB deadline of December 2025, blamed the slow gas-market ramp-up for the delay, said the regulator had assured an extension (IEX asked for eighteen months), and that IEX was 'considering different options for divestment'. By the Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) the option had narrowed to an IPO: IEX had asked IGX to proceed, targeting completion within the year subject to SEBI clearance. On the Apr 2026 call (24 Apr 2026) the extension was confirmed to 31 December 2026 and the process was 'progressing well'. The DRHP followed on 14 July 2026, and at the Jul 2026 analyst meet (24 Jul 2026) Goel sized it as a 22.3% sell-down while also disclosing that Indian Coal Exchange Ltd had been incorporated in June 2026 as a separate company.

points.point: First disclosure of the mandated sell-down: IEX's 47.5% stake in IGX must fall to 25% by December 2025 under PNGRB regulations, with an extension requested (one and a half years asked) and the regulator supportive.
points.quote: As per the PNGRB regulations, we have to bring down the equity to 25% by December 2025.

points.point: Reason the deadline could not be met on the original schedule was weak gas-exchange ramp-up, and the route was still undecided at this point.
points.quote: So we have applied to PNGRB and the regulator was quite supportive, and they have assured that they will give time extension. And we are also working out option s, we are considering different options for divestment and complying with the regulatory provisions.

points.point: Goel attributed the shortfall explicitly to gas market conditions rather than any strategic choice.
points.quote: because in the past, there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange. The business ramp -up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it.

points.point: The divestment route is fixed as an IPO; IEX directs its associate to execute it, with timing dependent on SEBI clearances.
points.quote: As far as IPO is concerned, basically, as per the regulations, our holding in the gas exchange is 47.5% and w e have to bring it out to 25% as per regulations. So , we have requested IGX to proceed with the IPO for this.

points.point: The PNGRB extension is confirmed as running to end-December 2026, setting the hard deadline for the sell-down.
points.quote: PNGRB has given us time up to 31st of December 2026.

points.point: Process underway but CMD gave no detail on status, pricing or structure.
points.quote: I think IGX IPO process is we have initiated the process.

points.point: The filing confirms the structure: a pure offer for sale by IEX of up to 16,710,000 IGX shares, no fresh issue, filed with SEBI and BSE on 14 July 2026.
points.quote: The Offer comprise s of an offer for  sale of up to 16,710,000 equity shares by IEX, and remains  subject to receipt of applicable approvals, market conditions, and other relevant considerations .

points.point: Goel quantifies the stake being sold - 22.3% of IGX, taking IEX from 47.3% to the 25% regulatory ceiling - and ties it directly to the expired five-year PNGRB window.
points.quote: As you may be aware that we have already filed a DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) for IPO of IGX as we today hold 47.3% in IGX.

points.point: The compliance driver and the one-year extension are restated as the sole rationale for the share sale.
points.quote: In fact, this 5 -year period was over in the month of December 2025. So , we took an extension of one year from the PNGRB. And therefore, to sell this 22.3% equity, we have offered that in the IPO.

points.point: An investor (Paresh Sanghani) asked for a proportionate reservation of IGX shares for IEX shareholders; Goel refused, treating IGX as a standalone issuer, and offered a buyback instead.
points.quote: The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback , yes definitely , we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market .

points.point: IGX's scale-up is presented as what makes the listing viable: 76.8 million MMBtu at over 40% CAGR and Rs 42 crore profit, within consolidated FY26 PAT of Rs 493 crore (IEX standalone Rs 474 crore).
points.quote: it was a very new concept when it was started in 2019 and it reached with CAGR growth of over 40% a volume of 76.8 million MM Btu and reported profit of 42 crores .

points.point: The same separate-entity logic is applied to new commodities: a dedicated coal exchange company was incorporated with board approval in June 2026, with a mineral exchange company to follow.
points.quote: And we with the approval of the (IEX) B oard have al ready incorporated Indian Coal Exchange Ltd – a separate company for this purpose .

points.point: Why each exchange must be a separate company with diluted ownership: identical shareholding caps apply across power, gas and coal exchanges.
points.quote: Nobody can hold more than 25 percent, and no trading member can hold more than 5% .

points.point: Management explicitly rejected a second possible separation - hiving off clearing and settlement into its own entity - saying the PSS Act demands registration, not a separate company, with no financial impact.
points.quote: There is no question of any separation because this narrative is coming where SEBI requires the separation of the clearing and settlement function for the stock exchanges .

rationale.what_management_expects: Compliance first: IEX falls to 25% of IGX, keeping an associate stake in a business they expect to grow volumes 25-30% annually as gas prices fall; IGX gets its own listing and price. Each new commodity (coal, minerals) sits in its own company under the same 25%/5% ownership caps. No margin, capital or valuation benefit for IEX was claimed.
rationale.gaps: No price band, valuation, IGX stake-sale proceeds or gain, no post-IPO accounting/control impact, no use of cash, and no plan if the 31 December 2026 deadline is missed.

listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO BOARD APPROVAL — NLC India Renewables Limited; date not fixed

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is NLC India Ltd's renewable energy (solar/wind) portfolio, carved out of the lignite-mining and thermal-power parent into NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary. The filings state the reason explicitly as policy-driven monetisation, not a strategic idea originated by management: the 31.10.2025 intimation says the hive-off of 7 RE assets totalling 1,430 MW is 'under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry', and the Q2 FY27 accounts repeat that it is 'In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal'. Scale cited: the 7 assets earned Rs 701.61 crore of revenue in FY25 (4.59% of consolidated revenue of Rs 15,282.96 crore) but carried net worth of Rs 3,869.26 crore (20.67% of owners' equity of Rs 18,722.97 crore) — i.e. a capital-heavy, low-revenue block being moved off the parent's balance sheet at book value, with consideration by equity shares/acknowledgement of debt, and Government of India approval already received. Execution was phased: Phase I (1,430 MW) transferred w.e.f. 01.01.2026; a second addendum dated 03.09.2026 added 708.96 MW (including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, assets at various stages of construction/operation) for Rs 853.97 crore, contributing only Rs 41.16 crore of FY26 revenue (0.24%) and Rs 925.08 crore of net worth (4.30%). The separate vehicle is visibly being used to raise third-party capital and partners that the parent could not house: a maiden green loan with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) under the ECB framework 'to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL', a PTC India JV for 2,000 MW, an OREDA MoU/JV, a DIPAM-approved JV with MAHAPREIT, an SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA and an NCRTC LoA for 110 MW captive solar — now sitting as step-down subsidiaries NARL, NRRL, NNRL, NORL and NPRL. The end state is a listing: the Board gave in-principle approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026 and on 04.11.2026 approved an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each held by NLCIL in NIRL as part of NIRL's proposed IPO, after NLCIL injected a further Rs 2,000 crore of equity on 12.10.2026 taking its NIRL investment to Rs 5,119.75 crore.
rationale.evolution: The seven earnings calls tagged Feb 2024, Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025 and Feb 2026 (held 10.02.2026) contain no extractable transcript text — six are scanned images and the Feb 2026 item is only the covering letter — so the idea cannot be traced call by call from these documents. From the filings the sequence is: in-principle approval for the Business Transfer Agreement to hive off the RE assets on 07.08.2025 (referenced in the 31.10.2025 intimation), BTA signed 31.10.2025 for 7 assets/1,430 MW under the Ministry of Coal's Asset Monetization Plan, transfer effected 01.01.2026, in-principle Board approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026, an addendum on 03.09.2026 adding 708.96 MW plus a 4 MW green hydrogen project, and OFS/IPO approval on 04.11.2026. The plan therefore widened from a one-off intra-group asset transfer at book value into a phased carve-out plus an IPO of the subsidiary, with the scope growing to include under-construction and green-hydrogen assets and five new partner-funded step-down subsidiaries.

points.point: The separation is a Ministry of Coal-mandated monetisation: 7 renewable assets of 1,430 MW hived off from NLCIL to wholly owned subsidiary NIRL under the approved Asset Monetization Plan, with Government of India approval already obtained.
points.quote: we write to inform that the Company has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement with NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company on 31st October, 2025, for proposed Hived off of the 7 Renewable Energy Assets with total Capacity of 1,430 MW from the Company to its Wholly Owned Subsidiary, NIRL, under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry.

points.point: The disclosed economics show a capital-heavy, low-revenue block: 4.59% of consolidated revenue but 20.67% of owners' equity, transferred at book value with consideration in shares or acknowledgement of debt.
points.quote: Net worth of 7 RE assets is Rs. 3,869.26 Crore, which is 20.67% of Net-worth of NLCIL i.e., Rs. 18,722.97 Crore (Total equity attributable to owners) based on Audited Financial Statements of 31st March, 2025.

points.point: Q2 FY27 accounts restate the driver as the National Monetization Pipeline and set out the two-phase mechanics, Phase II being 708.96 MW for Rs 853.97 crore under a second addendum.
points.quote: In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) with NLC India Renewables Limited on 31st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy assets.

points.point: The scope later widened beyond operating plants to assets still being built, including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, contributing only 0.24% of FY26 revenue and 4.30% of net worth.
points.quote: Addendum to the Business Transfer Agreement with NIRL is signed on 03rd September, 2026 for proposed hiving off 708.96 MW of Renewable Energy Assets including a 4 MW Green Hydrogen Project which are at various stages of construction/ operation.

points.point: The first transfer actually completed on 1 January 2026, converting the plan from intimation to executed carve-out.
points.quote: The aforesaid transfer has been effected on 01st January, 2026, in terms of the Business Transfer Agreement executed between the Company and NIRL on 31st October, 2025.

points.point: The end-point is an IPO of NIRL with NLCIL selling down: OFS of up to 10 crore shares approved on 04.11.2026, following in-principle listing approval on 12.01.2026.
points.quote: Offer for Sale (OFS) of up to 10,00,00,000 (Ten Crore) equity shares of face value of Rs.10 each held by the Company in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), Wholly Owned Subsidiary, as part of the proposed Initial Public Offering (IPO) of NIRL, subject to compliance with the applicable provisions of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, and other applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.

points.point: Lenders and partners are transacting with the subsidiary, not the parent: a maiden offshore green loan of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) from SMBC under the ECB framework is explicitly routed through NIRL.
points.quote: Signed its maiden Green Loan agreement with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) under the ECB framework , amounting to JPY 15.464 billion (USO 100 million), to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL.

points.point: NIRL has become the JV platform for state and PSU partners (PTC India 2,000 MW, OREDA, MAHAPREIT with DIPAM approval, SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA, NCRTC 110 MW captive solar), now held as step-down subsidiaries.
points.quote: NIRL signed a JV agreement with PTC India Ltd, for development of 2000 MW of green energy capacity and formation of JV company is in progress.

points.point: The parent is funding the vehicle ahead of the IPO, taking its NIRL equity to Rs 5,119.75 crore, while renewables segment assets roughly doubled to Rs 10,881.76 crore from Rs 5,470.15 crore a year earlier.
points.quote: The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 2,000 crore on 12th October 2026.

points.point: The structure deliberately avoids a merger/demerger scheme: it is a related-party slump sale at book value between holding company and wholly owned subsidiary, so Regulation 37A does not apply.
points.quote: No amalgamation/ merger is envisaged. Hence compliance w.r.t. Regulation 37A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, is not applicable as the transaction is being entered between the Company and its Wholly Owned Subsidiary i.e. NIRL.

rationale.what_management_expects: Not stated in words. The documents imply only: a dedicated, separately capitalised renewables vehicle (NIRL equity Rs 5,119.75 crore) able to raise third-party green debt (SMBC USD 100 million ECB) and partner equity via JVs with PTC, OREDA, MAHAPREIT, SJVNL and NCRTC, monetising assets per the Ministry of Coal plan and realising value through an NIRL IPO/OFS, leaving NLCIL focused on mining and thermal.
rationale.gaps: No call transcripts were extractable, so no management commentary, margin, valuation, capital-allocation or focus rationale; IPO size, pricing, timing, use of proceeds and residual NLCIL stake are unstated.

judge.what_is_spun: STL's Global Services Business (system integration / services arm), demerged out of Sterlite Technologies into a separate company
judge.reason: Not stated in the scheme filing; on the Jul 2026 call management said it had "consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses" and demerged system integration to be "very, very focused on the optical fibre cable connectivity side"
judge.insiders: Not stated for STL Networks. In the parent, promoter Twin Star Overseas Limited held 42.90%, rising to 47.75% fully diluted on exercise of 4,53,00,000 warrants at Rs.110; ultimate beneficial owner Mr. Anil Agarwal
judge.hidden_value: Leaves a pure-play optical parent: Q2 FY27 record revenue INR 2,529 Cr, EBITDA INR 846 Cr, PAT INR 517 Cr, order book INR 35,274 Cr, net debt-free, CRISIL AA/Stable. Any Kakinada writ contingent gain now belongs to STL Networks, not STL
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents give no size, shareholding, index or float details for STL Networks Limited
judge.listing_timeline: No listing date stated; the August 21, 2026 filing says the demerger was "effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025" under the NCLT Mumbai order dated February 14, 2025, and that STL Networks Limited "has filed a requisite disclosure ... on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited on August 20, 2026"
judge.read_next: STL Networks Limited's own August 20, 2026 exchange disclosure and its standalone financials

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is STL's Global Services (system integration / network-deployment) business, demerged out of Sterlite Technologies Limited (STLTECH) into a separate listed entity, STL Networks Limited, rebranded 'Invenia', leaving STL as a pure optical business (optical fibre, fibre cable, specialty cable, optical connectivity) plus the small STL Digital IT-services arm. Management's stated reason was portfolio simplification and focus: Ankit Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that the demerger 'aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses,' and in Jul 2026 placed it in a multi-year clean-up in which STL exited, sold or shut down wireless solutions, OSS/BSS, active components and other businesses to be 'very, very focused on the optical fiber cable connectivity side.' The second reason was capital and working-capital drag: the services business was a project business with large net fund involvement, and on the Jan 2025 call management's stated priority for it was 'select projects intake to improve the profitability and optimize the net fund involvement,' with Tushar Shroff conceding receivables and contract assets in state-government projects like T-Fiber and MahaNet were liquidating slower than planned because they depended on state budgetary allocation. The scale difference management cited: Global Services did INR 289 crores of revenue in Q3 FY25 at only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8% margin), versus the optical business at INR 924 crores and INR 119 crores (12.9%); consolidated net debt was INR 2,195 crores at Q3 FY25 and the retained (post-demerger) business reported net debt of about INR 1,350 crores at Q4 FY25, with a stated target of taking net debt/EBITDA from ~3x to 2x. Structurally, management wanted a clean break rather than a carve-out on paper: in Nov 2025 Ajay Jhanjhari said 'the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company,' and 'No relationship between STL and STL networks from that perspective.' The INR 2,600 crore BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package (3-year build plus 10-year maintenance) went with the demerged entity, and STL now supplies cable to it on an arm's-length basis — in Jan 2026 described as 'our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.' Each entity also got its own leadership and identity: Pankaj Malik as CEO of STL Networks under the Invenia brand, with shareholders receiving a 1:1 share entitlement on holdings as of April 24, 2025. Across the calls, no investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the only shareholder pressure visible is generic complaints about poor equity returns and past cash burn (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 calls), which management answered by pointing to the business exits, the ~INR 1,000 crore QIP of April 2024, and the demerger as portfolio simplification.
rationale.evolution: The idea is already in execution by the Jan 23, 2025 call, where it appears as a standing FY26 priority ('work towards completing the demerger of the services business') with the NCLT timeline laid out — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors July 10, 2024, petition admitted October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025, listing targeted by Q1 FY26. On the May 16, 2025 call Ankit Agarwal declared it done, effective March 31, 2025, named the new entity STL Networks, the new brand Invenia, Pankaj Malik as CEO and the 1:1 share entitlement, and reported the retained business separately at INR 1,350 crores net debt. By Jul 25, 2025 the plan had slipped only on listing (NCLT approval received Feb 2025, shares expected to list 'by the end of August'), and by Nov 6, 2025 the emphasis shifted to completing the operational separation — no intercompany guarantees, a roughly year-long transition to transfer everything. Thereafter it is treated as finished history: Jan 23, 2026 references Invenia only as a BharatNet customer served at arm's length, and Jul 24, 2026 cites 'we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity' purely as evidence of focus.

points.point: The Aug 2026 filing records the legal mechanics: the Scheme of Arrangement was approved by NCLT Mumbai by order dated February 14, 2025, and the Global Services Business demerged into STL Networks Limited from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025, with litigation outcomes of that business (e.g. the Kakinada Smart City writ petition) now accruing to STL Networks.
points.quote: Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.

rationale.what_management_expects: Focused growth in each entity: STL becomes a pure optical manufacturer chasing global top-3, 70-80% utilisation and 20% EBITDA versus ~13-14%, with net debt/EBITDA cut from ~3x to 2x (net debt INR 1,350 crores post-demerger versus INR 2,195 crores consolidated), no intercompany guarantees, and less capital tied up in project/working-capital-heavy services. Invenia gets its own brand, CEO and large-project mandate.
rationale.gaps: No standalone Invenia financials, valuation, debt split, separation costs, or capital allocation given; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it; listing-date slippage unexplained.

deal.size_statement: Annexure P2 - Consolidated balance sheet as on March 31, 2023 (all figures are in INR crores): "Revenue From Operations" STL (Demerged Co) Pre Demerger 7,020 / STL (Demerged Co) Post Demerger 5,403 / STL Networks (Resulting Co) Post Demerger 1,617; "PAT" 127 / 107 / 19; "Total Assets" 8,864 / 5,830 / 3,034; "Total Equity" 2,095 / 972 / 1,123. Apportionment of cost of acquisition of equity shares consequent upon demerger: "1. Sterlite Technologies Limited 42.23" and "2. STL Networks Limited 57.77" (% of Cost of Acquisition of Equity Shares).
deal.promoter_holding_parent: "Pursuant to the QIP issue promoter's shareholding in the Company has been reduced from 53.98% to 44.18%." (disclosed in the audited financial results for the year ended March 31, 2025, filed May 16, 2025); no promoter and promoter group holding percentage as of any specific date is otherwise stated.
deal.promoter_holding_after: Mirror shareholding, stated as: "Further, pursuant to the Scheme, the shareholders of the Company on the record date have been issued equity shares of STL Networks Limited in the same proportion as their holding in The Company." and "Pursuant to the Scheme, all the shareholders of Demerged Company will get new shares in the Resulting Company, in the ratio of 1:1 i.e. 1 share of the Resulting Company for 1 share held in the Demerged Company, and there would be no change in the economic interest for any shareholder of Demerged Company pre and post Scheme in the Demerged Undertaking." The specific promoter percentage in STL Networks Limited is not stated.
deal.public_shareholders_get: "1 (one) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 2 (Two Rupees Only) each of the Resulting Company for every 1 (one) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 2 (Two Rupees Only) each held in the Demerged Company", issued to shareholders "whose names were recorded in the register of members and / or records of the depository as on the Record Date (i.e. April 24, 2025)"; "with shareholders receiving 1:1 share entitlement based on holdings as of April 24, 2025"; shares "shall be issued in dematerialised form"; and "the demerger is tax neutral in the hands of shareholders of the Demerged Company under the IT Act in view of the exemption granted under Section 47(vid) of the IT Act."
deal.management_incentives: not stated (the documents disclose only "Employee stock option expenses 0" (FY25) and "(3)" (FY24) in the consolidated cash flow statement, and "Employee stock option expenses 1" (FY25) / "(6)" (FY24) standalone; no treatment of existing grants under the Scheme, no new plan in STL Networks Limited, no exercise price or pricing date, and no management or insider shareholding is stated. Managerial remuneration of INR 6 crores is stated as requiring approval: "The Company has paid/ provided for managerial remuneration in accordance with the requisite approvals mandated by the provisions of Section 197 read with Schedule V to the Act except for managerial remuneration aggregating to INR 6 crores.")
deal.insider_actions: No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging around the separation is stated. The documents state only dilution through capital raising: "During the year ended March 31, 2025, the Company has issued 88,456,435 equity shares of face value 2 each at an issue price of INR 113.05 per equity share pursuant to Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP)... Pursuant to the QIP issue promoter's shareholding in the Company has been reduced from 53.98% to 44.18%. The management does not expect any material impact on account of the change in the promoter's shareholding." A later raise is reported on the Q1 FY27 call (July 24, 2026): "STL successfully completed a landmark QIP of INR 1,500 crores... strengthening our institutional holdings to a fresh historic high of 33%."

This is an imp ortant slide which shows how the global data consumption across traffic categories is expected to rise multi fold in coming years and there's simply no alternative than to expand fiber networks to support such massive traffic expansion. Be It network param eters such as bandwidth offered , latency, data loss or energy savings, and in fact even environmental friendliness and reliability , fiber is undoubtedly the most efficient and reliable data transfer technolog y. With the growing use of fiber in various applications, such as fib er to the home, AI in data centers, edge data centers, smart cities, small cells, and the smart enterprises, fiber demand is bound to increase manifold going forward. On optical networking business , we shall continue to grow the optical business by increasing OFC market share and connectivity attach rate. […] No wonder various industry reports suggesting 2/3rd of network traffic sh all involve AI by 2030 , for this high growth of AI and technology users who sustain and succeed the technology backbone shall need massive data center capacities with fiber rich interconnections that smoothly manage the data explosion. To access these AI data centers and applications at the front end users shall need reliable connectivity through FT Tx or 5G or future generation like 6 G but fiber again shall be at the core of the connectivity. As we digest this further our belie f get stronger every day that denser fiber networks will be necessity for the success of the futuristic AI led digital society. rationale.rationale: On the documentary record available, Edelweiss is not executing a demerger scheme but a sequence of subsidiary-level separations that convert a holding-company conglomerate into separately capitalised, separately owned businesses — described in its own press release as "seven independent and well-governed businesses" each with "dedicated management teams and strong boards." The clearest stated reason is the Alternative Asset Management arm, EAAA India Alternatives: management said the IPO was "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform," i.e. separating the fastest-growing, fee-income business (FPAUM INR 41,920 Cr, +33% YoY; nine-month fund raise INR 7,576 Cr, +67% YoY; total income Rs 963.76 Cr in FY26 versus Rs 584.25 Cr in FY24; net worth Rs 1,075.54 Cr) from the credit-heavy parent so it can be valued and institutionalised on its own. Critically, the EAAA listing was a pure offer for sale by holdco subsidiary ESIPL (originally up to Rs 15,000 mn, cut to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP, finally Rs 1,200 Cr gross / Rs 1,120.63 Cr net at Rs 1,665 per share) — no primary money went to EAAA, so the cash accrues to the Edelweiss holding structure, which fits the stated priority of "focused reduction in corporate net debt" (down 15% to INR 6,520 Cr over two years, with consolidated net debt INR 11,390 Cr and a 3.46x debt-equity ratio). The second separation is Housing Finance: Nido Home Finance was handed to a strategic majority investor, CA Sardo Investments (The Carlyle Group) with Salisbury Investments (Aditya Puri's family vehicle), investing ~INR 2,100 Cr — Rs 580.68 Cr of secondary for 45% plus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of primary equity and warrants at INR 193 — taking them to 58.26% immediately and 72.70% fully diluted within 18 months, so Nido "ceased to be a subsidiary" and Edelweiss fell to 38.91% (25.46% diluted). Here the separation solves a growth-capital problem Edelweiss itself was not funding: a business contributing only 5.47% of consolidated income (Rs 520.63 Cr) but consuming 13.99% of net worth (Rs 828.2 Cr) was recapitalised with third-party primary money, with Edelweiss retaining upside via a minority stake and "an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments." The same template was applied to the Mutual Fund arm, where a 15% sale of Edelweiss Asset Management and Edelweiss Trusteeship to WestBridge moved both into joint control, crystallising a Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised and Rs 281 Cr realised gain (and a Rs 389 Cr deferred tax charge) — evidence that the separations are also being used to mark up carrying value and lift reported net worth/PAT (nine-month PAT Rs 549 Cr, +45% YoY). Taken together, the stated logic is: each business reaches scale, then gets its own owner, its own capital and its own valuation, while the parent de-levers.
rationale.evolution: This cannot be traced call by call: all ten earnings-call transcripts supplied (Nov 2023, May/Aug/Oct/Nov 2024, May/Aug/Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026) contained no extractable text, so no dated management commentary is available. From the filings, the sequence is: EAAA's DRHP filed 19–20 January 2026 (OFS up to Rs 15,000 mn by ESIPL); on 10 February 2026 the Q3FY26 release framed it as "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform" and the same day the Carlyle/Salisbury definitive agreements for a majority of Nido were announced, with WestBridge's Mutual Fund investment consummated in that quarter; SEBI observations came 23 April 2026, the Nido transaction closed 25 September 2026 (versus a 31 July 2026 expectation), and the EAAA IPO was repriced down to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP of 19 October 2026 before listing on 2 November 2026 at Rs 1,665. So the plan visibly scaled down in size (Rs 1,500 Cr to Rs 1,200 Cr) and slipped in timing, while widening from one business to three.

points.point: The EAAA IPO is explicitly positioned as the first step in separating the alternatives business into a self-standing institutional platform, announced alongside the DRHP filing in January 2026.
points.quote: We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA’s DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.

points.point: The structural end-state management describes for the group is a set of separately governed operating companies rather than an integrated financial conglomerate.
points.quote: Edelweiss is a diversified financial services company with seven independent and well-governed businesses.

points.point: The separations sit directly under the stated priority of de-levering the holding company, with corporate net debt the metric management tracks.
points.quote: Corporate net debt continues to be on path to reduction, with a 15% decline to INR 6,520 Cr over the last two years

points.point: Housing Finance was separated by bringing in Carlyle and Aditya Puri's family vehicle as strategic majority owners with roughly INR 2,100 crores of new money.
points.quote: has entered into definitive agreements (the Agreements) with CA Sardo Investments (an affiliate of The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG)) and Salisbury Investments Private Limited (an investment vehicle of Aditya Puri and his family) (collectively Buyers) for the Buyers to invest approximately INR 2,100 crores to acquire a strategic majority stake in Nido.

points.point: The Nido deal is a true deconsolidation, not a minority stake sale — Edelweiss gives up control of the housing finance book.
points.quote: Consequent to the transaction, Nido will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Nido was absorbing far more of the group's capital than it contributed in income — 13.99% of net worth for 5.47% of income — which the recapitalisation by third parties addresses.
Most of the Carlyle money is primary capital into Nido's balance sheet rather than cash out to Edelweiss: Rs 580.68 Cr secondary versus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of fresh equity and warrants.
points.quote: Further, in accordance with the Agreements, Nido has also issued 2,59,06,736 equity shares and 5,18,13,472 warrants, to the Buyers, for an aggregate amount of INR 14,46,13,99,102.56.

points.point: Edelweiss retains economic upside in the separated housing business through a retained minority stake and a contingent payment linked to Carlyle's realised returns.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Agreements and subject to applicable laws, the Sellers (Edelweiss) may also receive an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments from its investment in Nido.

points.point: Control of Nido passes progressively to the buyers — 58.26% on closing rising to 72.70% fully diluted — while Edelweiss falls to 25.46%.
points.quote: the Buyers now hold 58.26% shareholding of Nido which would be increased to 72.70% within 18 months, on a fully diluted basis post conversion of the warrants.

points.point: The Mutual Fund business was separated on the same template, with a 15% strategic sale converting EAML and ETCL into jointly controlled entities.
points.quote: Additionally, the WestBridge investment in Mutual Fund received its final approval from the regulators, and the deal has been consummated this quarter.

points.point: That Mutual Fund separation crystallised very large accounting gains — Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised plus Rs 281 Cr realised — showing the separations also re-rate carrying values inside the consolidated accounts.
points.quote: Pursuant to the terms of the SHA, the Group now has joint control for both of these Entities with the new investor, and consequently, in accordance with Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28, these entities are now classified as jointly controlled entities under Ind AS accounting principles.

points.point: The EAAA listing raised no primary capital for EAAA itself; proceeds went to the holding-company subsidiary ESIPL, consistent with using separation to fund parent de-leveraging.
points.quote: The IPO comprises an offer for sale (“OFS”) for an amount not exceeding Rs. 12,000 million, which is proposed to be undertaken by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited (“ESIPL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The alternatives business being separated had tripled income over three years, supporting the argument that it deserves its own valuation.
points.quote: FY 2025-26: Rs 963.76 crores FY 2024-25: Rs 786.54 crores. FY 2023-24: Rs 584.25 crores.

points.point: On completion Edelweiss kept overwhelming ownership of EAAA — 83.88% across subsidiaries — so this is a listing and institutionalisation step, not an exit.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company, through all its subsidiaries, hold 54,233,039 equity shares of EAAA representing 83.88% of the total paid-up equity share capital of EAAA.

points.point: The separations are set against an insurance drag and a credit book being wound down, including a Rs 920 Cr discretionary overlay on discontinued security receipts and a 34% YoY cut in the wholesale book.
points.quote: the Group has recognised a discretionary management overlay provision of 920 crores on its discontinued Security Receipts (Purchased or Originated Credit-Impaired (POCI) loans) in the consolidated financial results as at 31 December 2025.

rationale.what_management_expects: EAAA becomes a listed, "standalone institutionalized platform" with its own valuation; Nido gets Carlyle/Puri growth capital and majority ownership while Edelweiss keeps 25–39% plus a returns-linked earn-out; Mutual Fund gains a strategic partner and a Rs 2,440 Cr value mark; the parent frees capital (Rs 1,120.63 Cr net OFS proceeds) to push corporate net debt below INR 6,520 Cr.
rationale.gaps: All ten earnings-call transcripts were unextractable, so management's spoken rationale, investor/lender demands, use of proceeds, valuation targets, and any formal demerger scheme are absent.

judge.what_is_spun: Chemicals Business Undertaking — adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals — into Astral Chemie, merging with its paints/coatings business
judge.reason: Dedicated leadership and sector expertise, independent capital allocation, consolidating chemicals with paints under one platform, eliminating conglomerate discount and unlocking distinct equity value for each vertical.
judge.insiders: Promoters and Promoter Group hold 100% of Resulting Company pre-Scheme, 54.22% post-Scheme (mirror of parent); MD Sandeep Engineer's son Saumya runs adhesives and paints.
judge.hidden_value: Chemicals turnover ₹12,663 million, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076 million; adhesive India EBITDA 15.1%, UK turned 6.5% positive, paints still loss-making (₹6 crore in Q4) — yet consultant said scale insufficient to stand alone.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Board withdrew the Scheme on July 29, 2026; no shares of the Resulting Company will be issued or listed.
judge.listing_timeline: June 25, 2026: "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme and subject to receipt of regulatory approvals, the New Shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges" — no date given; Scheme withdrawn July 29, 2026, so no listing
judge.read_next: Independent Consultant's scale findings on the Chemical Business; next quarterly segment numbers for adhesives and paints.
judge.quote: Accordingly, the Board has decided to withdraw the Composite Scheme of Arrangement now, and no further steps will be undertaken in relation to the proposed the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.

turns: The second question is around, we 've seen how George Fisher involves and we have seen how Jubirit has created value in the insulation piping business. I think I remember last time in the last analyst meet, you spoke highly about the aluminum coated insulation pipe for the hot water segmen t. So could you just throw a little bit light on that space as to how would you want to capture that theme? Because that product is a very premium product, but eventually you want to bring unit economics to India. So that would be really helpful as to ho w would that market eventually evolve. The third question is around adhesives and sealant business. Look, honestly, you have been very strong in the piping business over the last 15, 16 years. But to replicate that similar kind of a distribution, the kind of a reach, the just -in-time product to the market, it requires a little dedicated effort in which I'm honestly seeing great effort from the team. But do you think that creating a separately listed company with a very dedicated, separate distribution netw ork, still relying on the cross synergies of the parent business can support your expansion because your vision is very big, the addressable market is huge but probably the ability to cater to it in the right time at the right moment might be the influenc ing factor around the growth. So that was one question and the fourth question is on we've seen how some regional players like Sera Chem in Chennai or in Tamil Nadu segment having a really dominant position in the niche silicon sealant space, where DAO is really a significant player. So how would you want to really work on this space going forward? Because I think the regional players are having a lo t of impact on the industrial applications. So I think a little bit light on that aspect would really help. Thank you for that. Mr. Kairav Engineer: So, I will answer the piping side of the questions that you raised. So gas piping, yes, you are correct that there will be a shift. See, Europe, they use polyethylene and polybutylene pipes for gas applications. And India is still using metals. So gas side, t here will be a move to usage of polymer pipes. It is still in a very nascent phase. And we are actively keeping a watch on the developments on this side. It's too soon to commit to any sort of a capex till there are proper standards and proper uses and pro per authorities willing to accept these products for the gas transfer application . Because India, the thing is that, you know, foreign and all, they have set of standards. So they are very comfortable using polymer products. But in India, you know, people are always scared that it's a polymer pipe and we are using it for gas. What if there is breakage? What if someone drills through it? What if there is a leak of gas? So all these things come up in people's minds. So we are actively watching this space. We are not saying that, you know, if tomorrow this space develops, that we will not enter it. We will definitely enter it. But it is still in a very nascent phase. So, we are just keeping a watch. And you asked about the aluminum composite pipes.
